units.title: Greetings & Everyday Phrases
units.description: First words in Spanish — Core greetings and polite phrases.

questions.prompt: How do you say "hello" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Hola" is the everyday Spanish word for "hello" and works with anyone at any time of day. "Mucho gusto" means "nice to meet you", not "hello".

questions.prompt: How do you say "good morning" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Buenos días" is the greeting for the morning, until about midday. "Buenas tardes" is used later, in the afternoon.

questions.prompt: How do you say "good afternoon" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Buenas tardes" is the greeting from midday until it gets dark. After dark you switch to "Buenas noches".

questions.prompt: How do you say "good evening" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Buenas noches" is the greeting once it gets dark, so it covers "good evening"; before dusk you would say "Buenas tardes".

questions.prompt: How do you say "goodbye" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Adiós" is the standard way to say "goodbye" when you leave. "Bienvenido" means "welcome", which is what you say when someone arrives.

questions.prompt: How do you say "see you soon" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Hasta pronto" means "until soon", so it is the Spanish way to say "see you soon" when you expect to meet again before long.

questions.prompt: How do you say "see you tomorrow" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Hasta mañana" means "until tomorrow", so it is how you say "see you tomorrow". "Buenas noches" is a greeting or a good-night, not a plan to meet.

questions.prompt: How do you say "please" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Por favor" is how you say "please" when you ask for something, for example "Un café, por favor."

questions.prompt: How do you say "thank you" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Gracias" is how you say "thank you" in Spanish, and people often reply "De nada" (you're welcome).

questions.prompt: How do you say "you're welcome" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: You reply "De nada" (literally 'of nothing') after someone thanks you; "Bienvenido" only greets a person arriving.

questions.prompt: How do you say "excuse me" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Perdón" is a short, polite "excuse me" for getting someone's attention or squeezing past them. "Por favor" means "please", not "excuse me".

questions.prompt: How do you say "sorry" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Lo siento" means "I'm sorry" and is what you say to apologize or to show sympathy.

questions.prompt: How do you say "yes" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Sí" means "yes". It needs the accent: without it, "si" means "if".

questions.prompt: A friend asks "¿Hablas francés?" and you don't speak French. You answer: "___, hablo español."
questions.explanation: "No" is the Spanish word for "no", spelled the same as in English. Here it turns down the question about speaking French.

questions.prompt: How do you say "how are you?" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¿Cómo estás?" uses estar, the verb for how someone is feeling, in the friendly tú form. "¿Cómo te llamas?" asks for a name instead.

questions.prompt: How do you say "I'm fine, thanks" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Estoy bien, gracias" uses estoy (from estar) to say how you feel right now, and gracias for thanks. "Sí, gracias" only means "yes, thanks".

questions.prompt: How do you say "what is your name?" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¿Cómo te llamas?" literally means "What do you call yourself?", which is how Spanish asks someone's name. "¿Cómo estás?" asks how someone is.

questions.prompt: How do you say "my name is..." in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Me llamo..." (literally 'I call myself') is how you tell someone your name; "¿Cómo te llamas?" is the question that asks for it.

questions.prompt: How do you say "nice to meet you" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Mucho gusto" (literally "much pleasure") is what you say when you meet someone for the first time. "Hasta pronto" means "see you soon".

questions.prompt: How do you say "welcome" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Bienvenido" means welcome and agrees with the person welcomed: bienvenida for a woman, bienvenidos for a group.

units.title: Numbers 1-20
units.description: Counting in Spanish — Numbers one through twenty.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "one" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "uno" is the number one. Before a masculine noun it shortens to "un", as in un libro.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "two" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "dos" is the number two. Don't confuse it with doce, which is twelve.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "three" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "tres" is the number three. Trece, which looks similar, is thirteen.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "four" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cuatro" is the number four. Catorce, which sounds similar, is fourteen.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "five" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cinco" is the number five. Don't mix it up with quince, which is fifteen.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "six" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: The number six in Spanish is "seis"; "ocho" is eight, "dos" is two and "quince" is fifteen.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "seven" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "siete" is the number seven. Diecisiete (17) is diez y siete, "ten and seven", written as one word.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "eight" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "ocho" is the number eight. Dieciocho (18) is diez y ocho, "ten and eight", written as one word.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "nine" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "nueve" is the number nine. Diecinueve (19) is diez y nueve, "ten and nine", written as one word.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "ten" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Ten is "diez". It is also the base of 16 to 19: dieci- means 'ten and'.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "eleven" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Eleven is "once", the first of the special -ce words for 11 to 15. It is not built as 'diez y uno', and it is not the English word 'once'.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "twelve" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Twelve is "doce". It looks like dos (two) plus the -ce ending used for 11 to 15.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "thirteen" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Thirteen is "trece" in Spanish; don't confuse it with "catorce", which is fourteen.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "fourteen" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Fourteen is "catorce". It comes from cuatro (four) plus the -ce ending used for 11 to 15.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "fifteen" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Fifteen is "quince", the last of the special -ce words for 11 to 15. From 16 on, numbers start with dieci-.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "sixteen" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Sixteen is "dieciséis": dieci- (ten and) plus seis (six), written as one word with an accent on the final é.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "seventeen" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Seventeen is "diecisiete": dieci- (ten and) plus siete (seven), written as one word.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "eighteen" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Eighteen is "dieciocho": dieci- (ten and) plus ocho (eight), written as one word.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "nineteen" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Nineteen is "diecinueve": dieci- (ten and) plus nueve (nine), written as one word.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "twenty" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Twenty is "veinte". It is a new word and is not built from diez like 16 to 19.

units.title: Colors & Basic Adjectives
units.description: Describing things — Common colors and simple descriptive words.

questions.prompt: How do you say "red" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Red is "rojo". Like most colors ending in -o, it changes to roja with feminine nouns.

questions.prompt: How do you say "blue" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Blue is "azul". It ends in -l, so the same form works with masculine and feminine nouns.

questions.prompt: How do you say "green" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "verde" means green; it ends in -e, so it stays the same for masculine and feminine nouns (un coche verde, una casa verde).

questions.prompt: How do you say "yellow" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "amarillo" means yellow; like most colors ending in -o, it changes to "amarilla" with feminine nouns.

questions.prompt: How do you say "black" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "negro" means black; it becomes "negra" with feminine nouns (una camisa negra).

questions.prompt: How do you say "white" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "blanco" means white; it becomes "blanca" with feminine nouns (una casa blanca).

questions.prompt: How do you say "big" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "grande" means big; it ends in -e, so it is the same for masculine and feminine nouns (un perro grande, una casa grande).

questions.prompt: How do you say "small" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "pequeño" means small; don't confuse it with its opposite grande (big).

questions.prompt: How do you say "new" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "nuevo" means new; its opposite in the list is viejo (old).

questions.prompt: How do you say "old" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "viejo" means old (for people and things); it becomes "vieja" with feminine nouns.

questions.prompt: How do you say "good" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "bueno" means good; its opposite is "malo" (bad), and it becomes "buena" with feminine nouns.

questions.prompt: How do you say "bad" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "malo" means bad; it is the opposite of "bueno" and becomes "mala" with feminine nouns.

questions.prompt: How do you say "happy" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "feliz" means happy; it is the same for masculine and feminine (él es feliz, ella es feliz), and its plural is "felices".

questions.prompt: How do you say "sad" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "triste" means sad; feliz, also in the list, is its opposite (happy).

questions.prompt: How do you say "beautiful" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "hermoso" means beautiful; the other options mean old, fast and black.

questions.prompt: How do you say "tall" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "alto" means tall; its opposite bajo means short in height.

questions.prompt: How do you say "short" (in height) in Spanish?
questions.explanation: For a person's height, short is "bajo"; pequeño means small in general size.

questions.prompt: How do you say "fast" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "rápido" means fast; remember the accent on the a (rá-pi-do), and it becomes "rápida" with feminine nouns.

questions.prompt: How do you say "slow" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "lento" means slow; it is the opposite of "rápido" and becomes "lenta" with feminine nouns.

questions.prompt: How do you say "easy" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "fácil" means easy; it needs the accent on the a, and it is the same for masculine and feminine nouns.

units.title: Family Members
units.description: Talking about family — Immediate and extended family vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "mother" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Mother" in Spanish is "madre" (la madre). In everyday speech people often say "mamá".

questions.prompt: How do you say "father" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Father" in Spanish is "padre" (el padre). Careful: the plural "padres" usually means "parents".

questions.prompt: How do you say "sister" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Sister" in Spanish is "hermana". The -a ending marks a female sibling, and "hermano" is brother.

questions.prompt: How do you say "brother" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Brother" in Spanish is "hermano". Change the -o to -a and you get "hermana", sister.

questions.prompt: How do you say "daughter" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Daughter" in Spanish is "hija" (the h is silent). The -a ending marks female, and "hijo" is son.

questions.prompt: How do you say "son" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "hijo" means son, a male child; for a daughter you say hija.

questions.prompt: How do you say "grandmother" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "abuela" is your mother's or father's mother; esposa means wife, not grandmother.

questions.prompt: How do you say "grandfather" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A grandfather is a man, so you use the masculine form "abuelo". "Abuela" ends in -a and means grandmother.

questions.prompt: How do you say "aunt" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: An aunt is a woman, so you need the feminine form "tía". "Tío" ends in -o and means uncle.

questions.prompt: How do you say "uncle" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: An uncle is a man, so you use the masculine form "tío". The feminine form, "tía", means aunt.

questions.prompt: How do you say "cousin" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "primo" means cousin and is the form used for a male cousin. A female cousin is "prima".

questions.prompt: How do you say "wife" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A wife is a woman, so you use the feminine form "esposa". The masculine form, "esposo", means husband.

questions.prompt: How do you say "husband" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A husband is a man, so you use the masculine form "esposo". The feminine form, "esposa", means wife.

questions.prompt: How do you say "family" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "familia" names the whole group of relatives. "Padres" means only the parents, and the other options are single family members.

questions.prompt: How do you say "baby" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "bebé" means baby. Words ending in a vowel are normally stressed on the second-to-last syllable, so the tilde on the final é shows that this word is stressed on the last syllable.

questions.prompt: How do you say "parents" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "padres" is the plural of "padre" (father). In the plural it covers the mother and the father together, so it means parents.

questions.prompt: How do you say "friend (male)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: The clue says male, so you need the -o form "amigo". "Amiga" means a female friend.

questions.prompt: How do you say "friend (female)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: The clue says female, so you need the -a form "amiga". "Amigo" means a male friend.

questions.prompt: How do you say "child" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "niño" means a child, especially a young boy; a young girl is "niña". The other options mean aunt, father and family.

questions.prompt: How do you say "grown-up" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "adulto" means a grown-up person; "hermana" is sister, "tío" is uncle and "amigo" is friend.

units.title: Common Verbs (yo form)
units.description: Present tense, first person — Present-tense "yo" conjugation of common verbs.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (hablar) español.
questions.explanation: The subject "Yo" needs the first-person ending -o on the stem of hablar, giving "hablo"; "hablas", "habla" and "hablan" belong to tú, he/she and they.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (comer) una manzana.
questions.explanation: With "Yo", regular -er verbs like comer take the ending -o, giving "como"; "comes" is tú, "come" is he/she and "comemos" is we.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (tener) un gato.
questions.explanation: Tener has an irregular yo form with -g-, so "Yo" takes "tengo"; "tiene", "tienen" and "tenemos" match other subjects.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (estar) cansado.
questions.explanation: Estar is irregular in the yo form: "Yo" goes with "estoy", and it fits here because tiredness is a temporary state; "estás", "están" and "estamos" belong to other subjects.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (ser) estudiante.
questions.explanation: Ser is irregular and its yo form is "soy", used here to say what you are (a student); "eres", "es" and "son" go with tú, he/she and they.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (ir) al mercado.
questions.explanation: Ir is completely irregular and its yo form is "voy"; "vas" is tú, "va" is he/she and "vamos" is we.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (hacer) mi tarea.
questions.explanation: Hacer has an irregular yo form with -g-, so "Yo" takes "hago"; "hace", "hacen" and "hacemos" match other subjects.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (querer) un café.
questions.explanation: Querer changes e to ie in the stem for yo, so "Yo" takes "quiero"; "quieres", "quieren" and "queremos" belong to other subjects.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (poder) ayudarte.
questions.explanation: Poder changes o to ue in the stem for yo, so "Yo" takes "puedo"; "puedes" is tú, "puede" is he/she and "pueden" is they.
questions.meaning: I can, I am able to

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (saber) la respuesta.
questions.explanation: Saber has a unique irregular yo form, "sé", written with an accent; "sabes", "sabe" and "sabemos" belong to other subjects.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (tomar) el autobús.
questions.explanation: Regular -ar verbs like tomar take -o for yo, giving "tomo"; "tomas", "toma" and "tomamos" match other subjects.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (ver) el mar.
questions.explanation: Ver has an irregular yo form, "veo", which keeps the e and adds -o; "ve", "ven" and "vemos" belong to he/she, they and we.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (venir) mañana.
questions.explanation: The subject is "Yo", so venir takes its irregular first-person form "vengo" (with a g), unlike "vienes" or "vienen".

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (decir) la verdad.
questions.explanation: With "Yo" as the subject, decir has an irregular first-person form, "digo", not the stem-changed "dices" or "dice".

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (vivir) en Madrid.
questions.explanation: "Yo" takes the -o ending on the regular -ir verb vivir, giving "vivo"; "vive" and "vives" are for él and tú.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (dormir) ocho horas.
questions.explanation: Dormir changes o to ue in the stem for "yo", giving "duermo"; "dormimos" keeps the o because it is the nosotros form.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (beber) agua.
questions.explanation: Regular -er verbs end in -o for "yo", so beber becomes "bebo"; "bebes" and "beben" belong to tú and ellos.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (leer) un libro.
questions.explanation: The "yo" form of the regular -er verb leer is "leo"; "lees" is tú, "lee" is él, and "leen" is ellos.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (escribir) una carta.
questions.explanation: For "yo", the regular -ir verb escribir drops -ir and adds -o, giving "escribo"; "escribe" and "escribes" fit other subjects.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (abrir) la puerta.
questions.explanation: The subject "Yo" needs the -o ending, so abrir becomes "abro"; "abre", "abren" and "abrimos" belong to other subjects.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (necesitar) tiempo.
questions.explanation: Regular -ar verbs take -o with "yo", so necesitar becomes "necesito"; "necesita" is él/ella and "necesitan" is ellos.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (trabajar) mucho.
questions.explanation: With "Yo", the regular -ar verb trabajar ends in -o: "trabajo"; "trabaja" and "trabajas" do not agree with yo.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (estudiar) español.
questions.explanation: The "yo" form of the regular -ar verb estudiar ends in -o, giving "estudio"; "estudia" and "estudias" are for él and tú.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (llegar) tarde.
questions.explanation: Regular -ar verbs end in -o for "yo", so llegar becomes "llego"; "llegas" and "llegan" don't match the subject yo.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (empezar) ahora.
questions.explanation: "empiezo" is the yo form of empezar, which changes e to ie in the stem and ends in -o. The other options belong to él, nosotros or ellos.

units.title: Days & Time Expressions
units.description: Talking about when — Days of the week and common time words.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Monday" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Monday" in Spanish is "lunes". Spanish days of the week are written in lowercase.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Tuesday" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Tuesday" in Spanish is "martes". Like most weekdays, it ends in -s and does not change in the plural.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Wednesday" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Wednesday" in Spanish is "miércoles". Note the accent on the first e and the lowercase spelling.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Thursday" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Thursday" in Spanish is "jueves". Don't confuse it with "viernes", which is Friday.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Friday" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Friday" in Spanish is "viernes". It comes right after "jueves" (Thursday).

questions.prompt: How do you say "Saturday" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Saturday" in Spanish is "sábado", with an accent on the first a. Its plural is "sábados".

questions.prompt: How do you say "Sunday" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Sunday" in Spanish is "domingo". Like all days, it is written in lowercase.

questions.prompt: How do you say "today" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "hoy" means "today". "Ahora" means "now", "luego" means "later" and "temprano" means "early".

questions.prompt: How do you say "tomorrow" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "mañana" means "tomorrow" (it can also mean "morning"); "temprano" is early, "luego" is later and "tarde" is late or afternoon.

questions.prompt: How do you say "yesterday" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "ayer" means "yesterday"; "hoy" is today, "mañana" is tomorrow and "tarde" is late or afternoon.

questions.prompt: How do you say "now" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "ahora" means "now"; "ayer" is yesterday, "temprano" is early and "mañana" is tomorrow.

questions.prompt: How do you say "later" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "luego" means "later"; "tarde" on its own means late or afternoon, "hoy" is today and "ahora" is now.

questions.prompt: How do you say "week" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "semana" means "week"; "día" is day, "mes" is month and "minuto" is minute.

questions.prompt: How do you say "month" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "mes" means "month"; "año" is year, "hora" is hour and "semana" is week.

questions.prompt: How do you say "year" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "año" means "year" (mind the ñ); "día" is day, "semana" is week and "minuto" is minute.

questions.prompt: How do you say "in the morning" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "por la mañana" means "in the morning"; "por la tarde" is in the afternoon, "por la noche" is at night and "al mediodía" is at noon.

questions.prompt: How do you say "in the afternoon" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "por la tarde" means "in the afternoon"; "por la mañana" is in the morning, "por la noche" is at night and "a medianoche" is at midnight.

questions.prompt: How do you say "at night" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "por la noche" means "at night"; "a medianoche" is only at midnight, "por la mañana" is in the morning and "al mediodía" is at noon.

questions.prompt: How do you say "early" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "temprano" means early; its opposite is "tarde" (late), and "mañana" means morning or tomorrow.

questions.prompt: How do you say "late" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "tarde" means late (it also means afternoon); its opposite is "temprano", early.

units.title: Household Objects
units.description: Around the house — Common household nouns.

questions.prompt: How do you say "house" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "casa" means "house" or "home", the whole building. "Dormitorio" is only one room in it, the bedroom.

questions.prompt: How do you say "room" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "habitación" is a room in a house; the other options are objects: a pen, a table and a mirror.

questions.prompt: How do you say "kitchen" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cocina" is the room where you cook, the kitchen. The same word can also mean the stove.

questions.prompt: How do you say "bathroom" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "baño" is the bathroom; "casa" is the whole house and "puerta" is a door.

questions.prompt: How do you say "bedroom" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "dormitorio" is the bedroom, the room where you sleep; in much of Latin America you will also hear "cuarto" or "recámara".

questions.prompt: How do you say "table" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "mesa" means "table". Don't confuse it with "silla", which is the chair you sit on at the table.

questions.prompt: How do you say "chair" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "silla" means "chair", the seat you pull up to a "mesa" (table). Remember that "ll" here sounds like the English "y".

questions.prompt: How do you say "bed" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cama" is the bed itself; "habitación" is the room the bed is in.

questions.prompt: How do you say "door" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "puerta" means "door", what you open to go into a room or a house. "Baño" is the bathroom itself.

questions.prompt: How do you say "window" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ventana" means "window", the glass opening in a wall. "Espejo" is a mirror, which reflects instead of letting you see outside.

questions.prompt: How do you say "key" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "llave" means "key", the thing you use to open a door. It is a feminine word: "la llave".

questions.prompt: How do you say "lamp" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "lámpara" means "lamp". Note the accent on the first "a": lám-pa-ra.

questions.prompt: How do you say "mirror" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "espejo" means "mirror", the glass you look at yourself in. "Televisor" is a TV, and "habitación" is a room.

questions.prompt: How do you say "clock" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "reloj" means "clock", and the same word is used for a wristwatch. The final "j" is a soft h-like sound that many speakers drop in casual speech.

questions.prompt: How do you say "television" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "televisor" is the TV set in your living room. "Televisión" usually means the medium or the programs.

questions.prompt: How do you say "telephone" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "teléfono" means telephone. It is masculine (el teléfono), like most nouns ending in -o, and it has a written accent on the second e.

questions.prompt: How do you say "book" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "libro" means book (el libro). Don't confuse it with "librería", which means bookstore; a library is "biblioteca".

questions.prompt: How do you say "pen" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "bolígrafo" means pen (el bolígrafo). In much of Latin America you will also hear "pluma" (Mexico) or "lapicero" (Peru).

questions.prompt: How do you say "paper" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "papel" means paper. It is masculine (el papel), even though it does not end in -o.

questions.prompt: How do you say "bag" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "bolsa" means bag, such as a shopping or plastic bag (la bolsa). It is a feminine noun ending in -a.

units.title: Body Parts
units.description: The human body — Basic body-part vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "head" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cabeza" means head (la cabeza). For example, "Me duele la cabeza" means "My head hurts."

questions.prompt: How do you say "hair" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "pelo" means hair on your head (el pelo). "cabello" is a more formal word with the same meaning.

questions.prompt: How do you say "eye" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ojo" means eye (el ojo). The plural is "ojos", as in "ojos azules" (blue eyes).

questions.prompt: How do you say "ear" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "oreja" means ear, the outer part you can see (la oreja). "oído" means the inner ear or the sense of hearing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "nose" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "nariz" means nose. It is feminine (la nariz), even though it does not end in -a.

questions.prompt: How do you say "mouth" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "boca" means mouth (la boca). It is a feminine noun ending in -a.

questions.prompt: How do you say "tooth" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "diente" means tooth (el diente). The plural is "dientes", as in "cepillarse los dientes" (to brush your teeth).

questions.prompt: How do you say "neck" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Neck" in Spanish is "cuello". It is a masculine noun: el cuello.

questions.prompt: How do you say "shoulder" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Shoulder" in Spanish is "hombro" (el hombro). The h is silent.

questions.prompt: How do you say "arm" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Arm" in Spanish is "brazo" (el brazo). Don't mix it up with "pie" (foot) or "pelo" (hair).

questions.prompt: How do you say "hand" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Hand" in Spanish is "mano". It is feminine even though it ends in -o: la mano.

questions.prompt: How do you say "finger" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Finger" in Spanish is "dedo" (el dedo). The same word is also used for a toe.

questions.prompt: How do you say "leg" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Leg" in Spanish is "pierna". It is a feminine noun: la pierna.

questions.prompt: How do you say "knee" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Knee" in Spanish is "rodilla" (la rodilla). In Latin America the double l sounds like the English y.

questions.prompt: How do you say "foot" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Foot" in Spanish is "pie" (el pie). Don't confuse it with "piel", which means skin.

questions.prompt: How do you say "back" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Back" (the body part) in Spanish is "espalda". It is a feminine noun: la espalda.

questions.prompt: How do you say "stomach" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Stomach" in Spanish is "estómago" (el estómago), with an accent on the first o.

questions.prompt: How do you say "heart" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Heart" in Spanish is "corazón" (el corazón), with an accent on the last o.

questions.prompt: How do you say "skin" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Skin" in Spanish is "piel". It is feminine (la piel); don't confuse it with "pie", which means foot.

questions.prompt: How do you say "face" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cara" means face, the front of the head. It is feminine, so you say "la cara".

units.title: Numbers 21-100
units.description: Bigger numbers — Numbers from twenty-one to one hundred, including the tens.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "twenty-one" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Twenty-one is "veintiuno", written as one word like every number from 21 to 29.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "twenty-five" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Twenty-five is "veinticinco": veinte and cinco are joined into one word, as with all numbers from 21 to 29.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "thirty" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Thirty is "treinta". Do not confuse it with "trece", which is thirteen.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "thirty-five" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: From 31 upward, Spanish joins the tens and the units with "y", so thirty-five is "treinta y cinco".

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "forty" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Forty is "cuarenta". "Catorce" is fourteen and "cuatrocientos" is four hundred.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "forty-five" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Forty-five is "cuarenta y cinco": cuarenta (40) plus "y" plus cinco (5).

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "fifty" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cincuenta" is fifty. It comes from cinco (five) plus the -enta ending used for the tens.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "sixty" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "sesenta" is sixty. It is built on seis (six) plus the -enta ending used for the tens, and it is spelled with s, unlike the English "sixty".

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "seventy" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Seventy is "setenta", built from siete (seven) plus -enta; don't mix it up with sesenta (60).

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "eighty" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Eighty is "ochenta", built from ocho (eight) plus -enta; setenta is 70 and noventa is 90.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "ninety" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "noventa" is ninety. It is built on nueve (nine), while setenta (seventy) comes from siete.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "one hundred" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cien" is exactly one hundred. Before other numbers it becomes ciento (ciento uno = 101), and mil means a thousand.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "two hundred" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Two hundred is "doscientos": dos (two) plus -cientos, written as one word.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "five hundred" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Five hundred is "quinientos", an irregular form: Spanish does not say cincocientos.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number "one thousand" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: One thousand is simply "mil"; Spanish does not put un in front of it.

units.title: Animals
units.description: Pets and wildlife — Common pets and wild animals.

questions.prompt: How do you say "dog" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "perro" means dog. Pronounce the double rr with a strong roll, which sets it apart from pero (but).

questions.prompt: How do you say "cat" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "gato" means cat. A female cat is una gata.

questions.prompt: How do you say "bird" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: The general word for bird is "pájaro", with an accent on the first a: el pájaro.

questions.prompt: How do you say "fish" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "pez" is a living fish, for example in a river or an aquarium. Fish as food on your plate is pescado.

questions.prompt: How do you say "horse" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "caballo" means horse. In Latin America the ll sounds like the y in yes.

questions.prompt: How do you say "cow" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "vaca" means cow. In Spanish b and v sound the same, so remember to spell it with v ("baca" is a car roof rack).

questions.prompt: How do you say "pig" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cerdo" means pig and is understood everywhere. In many Latin American countries you will also hear chancho or puerco.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sheep" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "oveja" means sheep. It is feminine: la oveja.

questions.prompt: How do you say "lion" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "león" is the Spanish word for lion. It is masculine (el león) and keeps its accent on the o.

questions.prompt: How do you say "tiger" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "tigre" is the Spanish word for tiger. It is masculine: el tigre.

questions.prompt: How do you say "bear" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "oso" is the Spanish word for bear. It is masculine: el oso.

questions.prompt: How do you say "elephant" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "elefante" is the Spanish word for elephant. It is masculine (el elefante) and starts with e, not the English el-ph spelling.

questions.prompt: How do you say "monkey" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "mono" is the Spanish word for monkey. It is masculine: el mono.

questions.prompt: How do you say "rabbit" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "conejo" is the Spanish word for rabbit. It is masculine: el conejo.

questions.prompt: How do you say "mouse" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ratón" is the Spanish word for mouse. It is masculine (el ratón) and has an accent on the o.

questions.prompt: How do you say "snake" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "serpiente" is the Spanish word for snake. It is feminine: la serpiente.

questions.prompt: How do you say "frog" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "rana" is the Spanish word for frog. It is feminine: la rana.

questions.prompt: How do you say "turtle" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Turtle (or tortoise) is "tortuga" in Spanish, a feminine noun: la tortuga.

questions.prompt: How do you say "duck" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "pato" is the Spanish word for duck. It is masculine: el pato.

questions.prompt: How do you say "wolf" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Wolf is "lobo", a masculine noun: el lobo.

units.title: Weather
units.description: Talking about the weather — Weather-related vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sun" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "sol" is the Spanish word for sun. It is masculine: el sol, as in hace sol (it's sunny).

questions.prompt: How do you say "rain" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "lluvia" is the Spanish word for rain. It is feminine (la lluvia), and the verb is llover.

questions.prompt: How do you say "snow" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Snow is "nieve" (la nieve). Don't confuse it with "niebla", which means fog.

questions.prompt: How do you say "wind" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Wind is "viento" (el viento), as in "Hace viento" (It's windy).

questions.prompt: How do you say "cloud" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Cloud is "nube" (la nube). Don't mix it up with "nieve" (snow), which looks similar.

questions.prompt: How do you say "storm" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Storm is "tormenta" (la tormenta). A storm can bring "relámpago" (lightning) and "viento" (wind), but those are different words.

questions.prompt: How do you say "fog" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Fog is "niebla" (la niebla). In much of Latin America you'll also hear "neblina" for light fog.

questions.prompt: How do you say "ice" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Ice is "hielo" (el hielo). "Nieve" is snow, which is soft and falls from the sky.

questions.prompt: How do you say "heat" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Heat is "calor" (el calor), as in "Hace calor" (It's hot). Its opposite is "frío" (cold).

questions.prompt: How do you say "cold" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Cold is "frío", as in hace frío (it's cold); its opposite, calor, means heat.

questions.prompt: How do you say "humidity" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: humidity → humedad. Weather-related vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "rainbow" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Rainbow is "arcoíris", from arco (arc) plus iris; the other options mean fog, thunder and snow.

questions.prompt: How do you say "thunder" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Thunder, the sound, is "trueno" (el trueno). The flash of light is "relámpago".

questions.prompt: How do you say "lightning" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Lightning, the flash of light, is "relámpago" (el relámpago). The sound that follows is "trueno" (thunder).

questions.prompt: How do you say "temperature" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Temperature" is "temperatura" in Spanish, a close cognate; "calor" is heat, "relámpago" is lightning and "viento" is wind.

units.title: Clothing
units.description: What are you wearing? — Common clothing items.

questions.prompt: How do you say "shirt" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A shirt with buttons and a collar is "camisa" (la camisa). A t-shirt is "camiseta".

questions.prompt: How do you say "t-shirt" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A t-shirt is "camiseta", a little "camisa" (shirt). In Mexico you'll often hear "playera", and in Argentina "remera".

questions.prompt: How do you say "pants" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Pants are "pantalones" (los pantalones). Like in English, the word is usually plural.

questions.prompt: How do you say "dress" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A dress is "vestido", a masculine noun: el vestido. A camiseta is a T-shirt, a bufanda a scarf and zapatos are shoes.

questions.prompt: How do you say "skirt" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A skirt is "falda", a feminine noun: la falda. Pantalones are trousers, calcetines socks and a cinturón a belt.

questions.prompt: How do you say "jacket" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: jacket → chaqueta. Common clothing items.

questions.prompt: How do you say "coat" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A coat is "abrigo" (el abrigo), the heavy outer layer you wear in cold weather. A suéter is a sweater, not a coat.

questions.prompt: How do you say "shoes" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Shoes are "zapatos", plural like the English word: one shoe is un zapato. Calcetines are socks, the ones you wear inside your shoes.

questions.prompt: How do you say "socks" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "calcetines" means socks; it is plural (el calcetín, los calcetines) because socks come in pairs.

questions.prompt: How do you say "hat" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "sombrero" is the word for a hat you wear on your head; it is masculine (el sombrero).

questions.prompt: How do you say "gloves" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "guantes" means gloves, the ones you wear on your hands; it is plural because gloves come in pairs (el guante, los guantes).

questions.prompt: How do you say "scarf" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "bufanda" is the scarf you wrap around your neck in cold weather; it is feminine (la bufanda).

questions.prompt: How do you say "belt" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cinturón" is the belt you wear around your waist; note the accent on the last syllable (el cinturón).

questions.prompt: How do you say "sweater" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "suéter" is the common Latin American word for a sweater; it comes from English and is written with an accent on the e.

questions.prompt: How do you say "pajamas" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "pijama" means pajamas; Spanish usually uses it in the singular (el pijama), even though English says pajamas.

units.title: School & Classroom
units.description: In the classroom — School and classroom objects.

questions.prompt: How do you say "school" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "escuela" is the whole school, the building or institution where children study; "salón de clase" is only one room in it.

questions.prompt: How do you say "classroom" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "salón de clase" is the room where lessons take place; "escuela" is the whole school.

questions.prompt: How do you say "teacher (primary school)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "maestro" is the word for a primary school teacher; for a woman you say "maestra".

questions.prompt: How do you say "student" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "estudiante" means student and has the same form for men and women; only the article changes (el estudiante, la estudiante).

questions.prompt: How do you say "desk" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "escritorio" is a desk, the table where a student or teacher sits to write and work.

questions.prompt: How do you say "notebook" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A notebook is "cuaderno" (el cuaderno), the book you write your class notes in.

questions.prompt: How do you say "pencil" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A pencil is "lápiz", with an accent on the first a. The plural is lápices.

questions.prompt: How do you say "eraser" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: An eraser is "goma" (la goma, short for goma de borrar). In many Latin American countries you will also hear borrador.

questions.prompt: How do you say "backpack" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A backpack is "mochila" (la mochila), the bag you carry your school things in.

questions.prompt: How do you say "blackboard" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A blackboard is "pizarra" (la pizarra). In Mexico and much of Latin America you will also hear pizarrón.

questions.prompt: How do you say "ruler" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A ruler is "regla" (la regla), the tool for measuring and drawing straight lines. The same word also means a rule.

questions.prompt: How do you say "scissors" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Scissors are "tijeras", plural like the English word: las tijeras.

questions.prompt: How do you say "glue" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Glue is "pegamento" (el pegamento), from the verb pegar, to stick.

questions.prompt: How do you say "homework" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Homework is "tarea" in Latin America, often used in the plural: "hacer las tareas". "Mochila" is a backpack and "examen" is an exam.

questions.prompt: How do you say "exam" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: An exam is "examen" (el examen). Note that the plural takes an accent: "exámenes".

units.title: Professions
units.description: What do you do? — Common jobs and professions.

questions.prompt: How do you say "doctor" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "médico" is the Spanish word for a doctor who treats patients; a woman is "médica". People also say "doctor" when speaking to one.

questions.prompt: How do you say "nurse" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A nurse is "enfermero" (feminine enfermera); "conductor" is a driver, "bombero" a firefighter and "abogado" a lawyer.

questions.prompt: How do you say "teacher" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "profesor" means teacher, for a man; a woman is "profesora".

questions.prompt: How do you say "lawyer" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "abogado" means lawyer, for a man; a woman is "abogada".

questions.prompt: How do you say "engineer" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "ingeniero" means engineer, for a man; a woman is "ingeniera".

questions.prompt: How do you say "cook" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cocinero" means cook, someone who prepares food, for a man; a woman is "cocinera".

questions.prompt: How do you say "police officer" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "policía" means police officer, and the word is the same for a man or a woman (el/la policía).

questions.prompt: How do you say "firefighter" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "bombero" means firefighter, for a man; a woman is "bombera".

questions.prompt: How do you say "farmer" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "granjero" means farmer, someone who runs a farm; in Latin America you will also often hear "agricultor".

questions.prompt: How do you say "artist" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "artista" means artist, and the word is the same for a man or a woman (el/la artista).

questions.prompt: How do you say "musician" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "músico" means musician; note the written accent on the first syllable.

questions.prompt: How do you say "writer" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "escritor" means writer, for a man; a woman is "escritora".

questions.prompt: How do you say "driver" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "conductor" means driver, someone who drives a vehicle; a woman is "conductora".

questions.prompt: How do you say "waiter" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "camarero" means waiter (a waitress is "camarera"); in much of Latin America, such as Mexico, people more often say "mesero".

questions.prompt: How do you say "scientist" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A scientist is "científico", with an accent on the í. A female scientist is "científica".

units.title: Opposites
units.description: Qualities and textures — Common opposite adjectives.

questions.prompt: How do you say "hot" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Hot is "caliente", and its opposite is "frío". For hot weather Spanish says "hace calor" instead.

questions.prompt: How do you say "rough" (to the touch) in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "áspero" describes a rough surface, like sandpaper, and its opposite is "suave" (smooth).

questions.prompt: How do you say "sweet" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Sweet is "dulce". Its opposites are "salado" (salty) and "amargo" (bitter).

questions.prompt: How do you say "salty" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Salty is "salado", from "sal" (salt). Its opposite is "dulce" (sweet).

questions.prompt: How do you say "hard" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "duro" means hard as in firm, not soft (the opposite of "blando"); hard meaning difficult is "difícil".

questions.prompt: How do you say "soft" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "blando" means soft as in not hard, like a pillow or a ripe fruit, and it is the opposite of "duro".

questions.prompt: How do you say "clean" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "limpio" means "clean"; its opposite in this lesson is "sucio" (dirty).

questions.prompt: How do you say "dirty" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Dirty is "sucio". Its opposite is "limpio" (clean), so don't mix up the pair.

questions.prompt: How do you say "full" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Full is "lleno", and its opposite is "vacío" (empty).

questions.prompt: How do you say "empty" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Empty is "vacío", with an accent on the í. Its opposite is "lleno" (full).

questions.prompt: How do you say "open" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Open is "abierto", and its opposite is "cerrado" (closed).

questions.prompt: How do you say "closed" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Closed is "cerrado", and its opposite is "abierto" (open).

questions.prompt: How do you say "wet" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Wet is "mojado", and its opposite is "seco" (dry).

questions.prompt: How do you say "dry" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "seco" means dry, as in "La ropa está seca"; its opposite is "mojado" (wet).

questions.prompt: How do you say "heavy" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "pesado" means heavy; its opposite is "ligero" (light). "fuerte" means strong, not heavy.

questions.prompt: How do you say "light (weight)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ligero" means light in weight, the opposite of "pesado" (heavy); in much of Latin America "liviano" is also very common.

questions.prompt: How do you say "strong" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "fuerte" means strong, the opposite of "débil" (weak).

questions.prompt: How do you say "weak" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "débil" means weak and is the opposite of "fuerte" (strong); it has the same form for masculine and feminine.

questions.prompt: How do you say "loud" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "ruidoso" means loud or noisy, the opposite of "silencioso" (quiet).

questions.prompt: How do you say "quiet" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "silencioso" means quiet (making no noise) and is the opposite of "ruidoso" (noisy).

units.title: Emotions
units.description: How do you feel? — Common emotion words.

questions.prompt: How do you say "happy (content)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "contento" means happy or pleased and is used with estar: "Estoy contento".

questions.prompt: How do you say "grateful" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "agradecido" means grateful and comes from the verb agradecer (to thank).

questions.prompt: How do you say "angry" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "enojado" means angry and is the usual word in Latin America: "Estoy enojado".

questions.prompt: How do you say "scared" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "asustado" means scared and comes from susto (a fright): "Estoy asustado".

questions.prompt: How do you say "surprised" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "sorprendido" means surprised and looks like the English word: "Estoy sorprendido".

questions.prompt: How do you say "bored" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "aburrido" means bored with estar ("Estoy aburrido"), but boring with ser ("Es aburrido").

questions.prompt: How do you say "excited" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "emocionado" means excited, as in "Estoy emocionado por el viaje"; it does not mean emotional in a sad way.

questions.prompt: How do you say "nervous" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Nervous" is "nervioso" (nerviosa for a woman); "tranquilo" means calm, "enojado" angry and "celoso" jealous.

questions.prompt: How do you say "calm" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "tranquilo" means calm and is the opposite of "nervioso" or "preocupado" (worried).

questions.prompt: How do you say "in love" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "enamorado" means "in love", as in "Estoy enamorado". "contento" means happy, "aburrido" means bored and "preocupado" means worried.

questions.prompt: How do you say "tired" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cansado" means "tired", as in "Estoy cansado". "emocionado" means excited, "orgulloso" means proud and "enojado" means angry.

questions.prompt: How do you say "worried" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "preocupado" means "worried", as in "Estoy preocupado". "nervioso" is nervous, which is close but not the same feeling.

questions.prompt: How do you say "proud" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "orgulloso" means "proud", as in "Estoy orgulloso de ti". "celoso" means jealous and "enojado" means angry.

questions.prompt: How do you say "jealous" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "celoso" means "jealous", as in "Él está celoso". "asustado" means scared and "orgulloso" means proud.

questions.prompt: How do you say "confused" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "confundido" means "confused" and looks like the English word. "contento" means happy, "aburrido" means bored and "cansado" means tired.

units.title: Question Words
units.description: Asking questions — The core interrogative words.

questions.prompt: How do you say "what" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "qué" means "what" and takes an accent in questions, as in "¿Qué es?". "quién" means who.

questions.prompt: How do you say "who" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "quién" means "who" and takes an accent in questions, as in "¿Quién es?". "dónde" means where and "cuándo" means when.

questions.prompt: How do you say "when" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cuándo" asks about time (when), and it takes a written accent because it is a question word.

questions.prompt: How do you say "where" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "dónde" asks about place (where), as in "¿Dónde está el baño?".

questions.prompt: How do you say "why" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "por qué" means why and is written as two words with an accent; "porque", one word with no accent, means because.

questions.prompt: How do you say "how" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cómo" asks about manner or way (how), as in "¿Cómo estás?"; "qué" means what.

questions.prompt: How do you say "which" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cuál" means which (one) and is used to choose among options; "quién" asks who and "de quién" asks whose.

questions.prompt: How do you say "how much" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cuánto" means "how much" and asks about an amount, as in "¿Cuánto cuesta?"; the plural "cuántos" means "how many".

questions.prompt: How do you say "how many" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cuántos" is the plural form, used to count things, so it means "how many", as in "¿Cuántos libros tienes?"

questions.prompt: How do you say "whose" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Spanish has no single word for "whose"; it says "de quién" (literally "of whom"), as in "¿De quién es este libro?"

units.title: Telling Time
units.description: What time is it? — Basic time-telling expressions.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué hora ___?
questions.explanation: Spanish asks the time with "es": ¿Qué hora es? The question uses the verb ser, not hay, tener or estar.

questions.prompt: Es la ___ (one o'clock).
questions.explanation: One o'clock is singular and "la" is feminine because it agrees with "hora", so the number must be "una", not uno. Only one o'clock uses "Es"; other hours use "Son las".

questions.prompt: Son las ___ (two o'clock).
questions.explanation: From two o'clock on, Spanish uses plural "Son las" plus the number, so two o'clock is "dos". "Una" would need "Es la".

questions.prompt: Son las tres y ___ (half).
questions.explanation: Half past is "y media", with the feminine "media" agreeing with the understood word "hora". "Medio" is masculine and "mitad" is not used for telling time.

questions.prompt: Son las cuatro y ___ (quarter).
questions.explanation: A quarter past is "y cuarto", using the masculine noun "cuarto" (a fourth of an hour). "Cuarta" is not used in this expression.

questions.prompt: Es ___ (midnight).
questions.explanation: Midnight is "medianoche" (literally half-night), as in "Es medianoche". "Mediodía" means noon, while "tarde" and "mañana" are parts of the day.

questions.prompt: Es ___ (noon).
questions.explanation: Noon is "mediodía" (literally half-day), as in "Es mediodía". "Medianoche" is midnight, and "mañana" and "tarde" are parts of the day.

questions.prompt: Son las cinco en ___ (exactly).
questions.explanation: "punto" is correct here. Basic time-telling expressions.

questions.prompt: Son las seis menos ___ (quarter).
questions.explanation: "cuarto" is correct here. Basic time-telling expressions.

questions.prompt: Llego a las siete de la ___ (morning).
questions.explanation: "mañana" is correct here. Basic time-telling expressions.

questions.prompt: Ceno a las nueve de la ___ (night).
questions.explanation: "noche" is correct here. Basic time-telling expressions.

questions.prompt: Trabajo por la ___ (afternoon).
questions.explanation: The English clue says "afternoon", and "tarde" is the Spanish word for it; "por la tarde" means 'in the afternoon'.

questions.prompt: Son las ocho y ___ (ten minutes).
questions.explanation: The clue says ten minutes, and "diez" is ten, so the time is 'las ocho y diez' (8:10).

questions.prompt: Llega a las once y ___ (twenty).
questions.explanation: The clue says twenty minutes, and "veinte" is twenty, so the time is 'las once y veinte' (11:20).

questions.prompt: El tren sale a la una y ___ (five).
questions.explanation: The clue says five minutes, and "cinco" is five, so the train leaves at 'la una y cinco' (1:05).

units.title: Basic Prepositions
units.description: Where is it? — Common location prepositions.

questions.prompt: How do you say "in" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "en" means "in", as in "El gato está en la caja"; the other options mean around, near and next to.

questions.prompt: How do you say "on" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "sobre" means "on" (on top of a surface), as in "El libro está sobre la mesa"; Spanish also often uses "en" for this. The other options mean around, next to and far from.

questions.prompt: How do you say "under" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "debajo de" means "under", as in "debajo de la mesa". "encima de" and "sobre" mean the opposite, on top of.

questions.prompt: How do you say "next to" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "al lado de" means "next to" (right beside), as in "al lado de la puerta". "cerca de" only means near.

questions.prompt: How do you say "between" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "entre" means "between", as in "entre la casa y el parque". "al lado de" means next to and "dentro de" means inside.

questions.prompt: How do you say "in front of" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "delante de" means "in front of", as in "delante de la casa"; in Latin America you will also hear "enfrente de". "dentro de" means inside.

questions.prompt: How do you say "behind" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "detrás de" means behind, at the back of something: "El gato está detrás de la puerta." Don't confuse it with "debajo de" (under).

questions.prompt: How do you say "near (to)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cerca de" means near (to): "La tienda está cerca de mi casa." Its opposite is "lejos de" (far from).

questions.prompt: How do you say "far from" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "lejos de" means far from: "El aeropuerto está lejos de la ciudad." Its opposite is "cerca de" (near).

questions.prompt: How do you say "inside" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "dentro de" means inside, in the interior of something: "Las llaves están dentro de la caja." Its opposite is "fuera de" (outside).

questions.prompt: How do you say "outside" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "fuera de" means outside (of): "El perro está fuera de la casa." Its opposite is "dentro de" (inside).

questions.prompt: How do you say "above" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "encima de" means "above" or "on top of", as in "La lámpara está encima de la mesa"; "debajo de" is its opposite, below.

questions.prompt: How do you say "around" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "alrededor de" means around, on every side of something: "Hay árboles alrededor de la casa."

questions.prompt: How do you say "through" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "a través de" means through, from one side to the other: "Caminamos a través del parque."

questions.prompt: How do you say "against" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "contra" means against, touching or pushing on something: "La bicicleta está contra la pared." Unlike "delante de" and "fuera de", it takes no "de".

units.title: Nature & Outdoors
units.description: The world outside — Basic nature vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "coral reef" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "arrecife de coral" is the Spanish for "coral reef" ("arrecife" means reef); playa, roca and flor mean beach, rock and flower.

questions.prompt: How do you say "moon" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "luna" means moon. It is feminine: "la luna", as in "La luna está llena."

questions.prompt: How do you say "star" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "estrella" means "star", as in "Hay muchas estrellas en el cielo"; flor and lago mean flower and lake.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sky" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cielo" means sky. It is masculine: "el cielo", as in "El cielo está azul."

questions.prompt: How do you say "tree" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "árbol" means tree. It is masculine and has a written accent on the a: "el árbol".

questions.prompt: How do you say "flower" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "flor" means flower. It is feminine: "la flor", and its plural is "flores".

questions.prompt: How do you say "grass" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "hierba" means grass (la hierba). In much of Latin America people also say "pasto" for the grass in a lawn or field.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sea" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "mar" means sea (el mar). "Arena" is the sand on the beach and "cielo" is the sky above it.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sand" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "arena" means sand (la arena), as in la arena de la playa. "Isla" means island, not sand.

questions.prompt: How do you say "rock" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "roca" means rock (la roca), a big piece of stone. "Flor" is a flower and "luna" is the moon.

questions.prompt: How do you say "lake" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "lago" means lake (el lago), a body of fresh water surrounded by land. "Isla" is an island, which is land surrounded by water.

questions.prompt: How do you say "island" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "isla" means "island", land with water all around it; lago is a lake and arrecife de coral is a coral reef.

questions.prompt: How do you say "leaf" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "hoja" means leaf (la hoja de un árbol); the h is silent. "Hierba" is grass, not a leaf.

questions.prompt: How do you say "mountain" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "montaña" means mountain (la montaña); note the ñ. "Lago" is a lake.

questions.prompt: How do you say "beach" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "playa" means beach (la playa). "Mar" is the sea next to it, not the beach itself.

units.title: Fruits & Vegetables
units.description: At the market — Common fruits and vegetables.

questions.prompt: How do you say "apple" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "manzana" means apple (la manzana). "Sandía" is a watermelon and "coco" is a coconut.

questions.prompt: How do you say "banana" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "plátano" is a common word for "banana", for example in Mexico; in some countries it means plantain, and you may also hear "banano" or "guineo".

questions.prompt: How do you say "orange (fruit)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "naranja" means orange, the fruit (la naranja); it is also the word for the color orange. "Pera" is a pear.

questions.prompt: How do you say "strawberry" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "fresa" means "strawberry"; in Chile and Argentina people also say "frutilla".

questions.prompt: How do you say "grape" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "uva" means grape (la uva); a bunch of grapes is un racimo de uvas. "Limón" is a lemon or lime.

questions.prompt: How do you say "watermelon" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "sandía" means watermelon (la sandía); note the accent on the í. "Papa" is a potato.

questions.prompt: How do you say "pineapple" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "piña" is the Spanish word for pineapple, the tropical fruit with spiky leaves; note the ñ, which sounds like the 'ny' in 'canyon'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "pear" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "pera" means "pear"; cebolla is an onion, calabaza is a squash and piña is a pineapple.

questions.prompt: How do you say "cherry" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cereza" means "cherry"; sandía is a watermelon, pepino is a cucumber and kiwi is a kiwi.

questions.prompt: How do you say "lemon" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "limón" means "lemon"; note the accent on the o, and don't confuse it with lechuga (lettuce).

questions.prompt: How do you say "peach" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "durazno" is the Latin American word for "peach"; in Spain people say "melocotón".

questions.prompt: How do you say "mango" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: mango → mango. Common fruits and vegetables.

questions.prompt: How do you say "coconut" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "coco" is the Spanish word for coconut; don't confuse it with "aguacate" (avocado) or "zanahoria" (carrot).

questions.prompt: How do you say "kiwi" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: kiwi → kiwi. Common fruits and vegetables.

questions.prompt: How do you say "tomato" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "tomate" means "tomato" and looks almost like the English word; "papa" is a potato, "maíz" is corn and "uva" is a grape.

questions.prompt: How do you say "potato" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "papa" is the Latin American word for "potato"; in Spain people say "patata".

questions.prompt: How do you say "carrot" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "zanahoria" means "carrot"; coco is a coconut, pepino is a cucumber and naranja is an orange.

questions.prompt: How do you say "onion" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cebolla" is the Spanish word for onion; watch the double l, which sounds like the y in 'yes' in most of Latin America.

questions.prompt: How do you say "garlic" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ajo" is the Spanish word for garlic; the j sounds like a strong English h.

questions.prompt: How do you say "lettuce" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "lechuga" means lettuce, the green leafy vegetable used in salads, as in "una ensalada de lechuga".

questions.prompt: How do you say "cucumber" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "pepino" means cucumber, the long green vegetable often sliced into salads.

questions.prompt: How do you say "pepper (vegetable)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "pimiento" is the bell pepper (the vegetable, not the spice); you may also hear "morrón" or "pimentón" in some countries, and "chile" for hot peppers.

questions.prompt: How do you say "corn" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "maíz" is the general word for corn; corn on the cob is often called "elote" in Mexico and "choclo" in South America.

questions.prompt: How do you say "avocado" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "aguacate" means avocado and is used in Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean; in much of South America people say "palta".

questions.prompt: How do you say "pumpkin" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "calabaza" means pumpkin or squash; in Argentina and Uruguay you will also hear "zapallo".

units.title: Kitchen Verbs
units.description: Cooking actions — Present-tense "yo" conjugation of common cooking verbs.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (cortar) las verduras.
questions.explanation: The subject "yo" (I) takes the present-tense ending -o, so cortar becomes "corto"; -as, -an and -amos belong to tú, ellos and nosotros.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (mezclar) los ingredientes.
questions.explanation: With "yo" (I), -ar verbs end in -o, so mezclar becomes "mezclo"; the other forms match él, nosotros or ellos.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (hervir) el agua.
questions.explanation: Hervir changes its stem e to ie in the yo form and takes -o, giving "hiervo"; "hervimos" (we) keeps the plain stem but doesn't match "yo".

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (freír) el pescado.
questions.explanation: Freír takes -o with "yo" and keeps a written accent on the í, giving "frío"; "fríe", "fríes" and "fríen" are for él, tú and ellos.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (hornear) un pastel.
questions.explanation: The subject "yo" (I) takes -o on -ar verbs, so hornear becomes "horneo"; "horneas", "hornean" and "horneamos" fit tú, ellos and nosotros.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (lavar) los platos.
questions.explanation: With "yo" (I), -ar verbs end in -o, so lavar becomes "lavo"; the other options match nosotros, ellos or él.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (verter) la leche.
questions.explanation: Verter changes e to ie in the yo form and ends in -o, giving "vierto"; "vertemos" keeps the plain stem and belongs to nosotros.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (añadir) sal a la sopa.
questions.explanation: The subject "yo" (I) takes -o on -ir verbs, so añadir becomes "añado"; "añade", "añades" and "añaden" match él, tú and ellos.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (calentar) la comida.
questions.explanation: With "yo" the present-tense ending is -o, and calentar changes its stem e to ie in this form, giving "caliento". Only "calentamos" keeps the plain stem, and that form is for "nosotros".
questions.meaning: I heat up, I warm up

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (servir) la cena.
questions.explanation: The subject "yo" takes the ending -o, and servir changes its stem e to i, so the form is "sirvo". The other options end in -e, -es or -en, which belong to él, tú or ellos.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (probar) la salsa.
questions.explanation: After "yo" the verb ends in -o, and probar changes its stem o to ue, giving "pruebo". "Pruebas", "prueba" and "prueban" are the tú, él and ellos forms.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (pelar) las papas.
questions.explanation: Pelar is a regular -ar verb, so "yo" takes the ending -o and the form is "pelo". The endings -a, -as and -amos go with él, tú and nosotros.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (picar) la cebolla.
questions.explanation: Picar is a regular -ar verb, so "yo" takes the ending -o, giving "pico". "Pican", "pica" and "picamos" match ellos, él and nosotros.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (batir) los huevos.
questions.explanation: Batir is an -ir verb, and the "yo" form drops -ir and adds -o, giving "bato". The options "bates", "baten" and "batimos" are for tú, ellos and nosotros.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (asar) el pollo.
questions.explanation: Asar is a regular -ar verb, so the "yo" form ends in -o: "aso". The forms with -a, -an and -as belong to él, ellos and tú.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (colar) la pasta.
questions.explanation: With "yo" the ending is -o, and colar changes its stem o to ue, so the form is "cuelo". "Colamos" keeps the plain stem because it is the nosotros form.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (rallar) el queso.
questions.explanation: Rallar is a regular -ar verb, so "yo" takes the ending -o, giving "rallo". "Rallan", "rallamos" and "ralla" are the ellos, nosotros and él forms.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (exprimir) un limón.
questions.explanation: Exprimir is a regular -ir verb, and the "yo" form ends in -o: "exprimo". The endings -es, -en and -imos go with tú, ellos and nosotros.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (revolver) el arroz.
questions.explanation: The subject "yo" takes the ending -o, and revolver changes its stem o to ue, giving "revuelvo". The other options end in -e, -en or -es, which match él, ellos and tú.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (tapar) la olla.
questions.explanation: Tapar is a regular -ar verb, so the "yo" form ends in -o: "tapo". The forms with -a, -amos and -as are for él, nosotros and tú.
questions.meaning: I cover, I put the lid on

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (encender) la estufa.
questions.explanation: The subject "yo" takes the "-o" ending, and encender changes e to ie in the stem, so it is "enciendo". "Enciende", "enciendes" and "encendemos" match other subjects.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (apagar) el horno.
questions.explanation: With "yo", a regular -ar verb like apagar ends in -o, giving "apago". "Apaga", "apagan" and "apagamos" go with él, ellos and nosotros.
questions.meaning: I turn off, I switch off

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (medir) la harina.
questions.explanation: Medir changes e to i in the stem and takes the "-o" ending for "yo", so it is "mido". "Mides", "miden" and "medimos" belong to tú, ellos and nosotros.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (untar) mantequilla en el pan.
questions.explanation: Untar is a regular -ar verb, so "yo" takes the "-o" ending: "unto". "Unta", "untas" and "untan" are for él, tú and ellos.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (enfriar) el postre.
questions.explanation: Enfriar takes a written accent in the "yo" form, "enfrío", to keep the í stressed. "Enfría" and "enfrías" are for él and tú, and "enfriamos" for nosotros.

units.title: Quantifiers
units.description: How much, how many — Common quantity words.

questions.prompt: How do you say "more" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "más" means more, as in "quiero más agua"; it needs the accent, because "mas" without it is a rare word meaning 'but'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "less" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "menos" means less, as in "más o menos"; "poco" means a little, not less.

questions.prompt: How do you say "a lot" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "mucho" means a lot, as in "Me gusta mucho."

questions.prompt: How do you say "little (not much)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "poco" means little or not much, as in "tengo poco dinero" (I have little money).

questions.prompt: How do you say "several" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "varios" means several and agrees with the noun, as in "varios libros" or "varias casas".

questions.prompt: How do you say "enough" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "suficiente" means enough, as in "Tengo suficiente dinero."

questions.prompt: How do you say "too much" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "demasiado" means too much, as in "Hay demasiado ruido"; "pocos" means few.

questions.prompt: How do you say "each" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cada" means each and never changes form, as in "cada día" (each day) or "cada persona".

questions.prompt: How do you say "none" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "ninguno" means none or not one, as in "No hay ninguno."

questions.prompt: How do you say "half" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "mitad" is the noun for half, as in "la mitad de la pizza"; "cuarto" is a quarter and "parte" is just a part.

questions.prompt: How do you say "some" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "algunos" means "some" before a plural masculine noun, as in "algunos amigos"; with feminine nouns it becomes "algunas".

questions.prompt: How do you say "many" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "muchos" means "many" before a plural masculine noun, as in "muchos libros"; with feminine nouns it becomes "muchas".

questions.prompt: How do you say "few" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "pocos" means "few" before a plural masculine noun, as in "pocos días"; it is the opposite of "muchos".

questions.prompt: How do you say "most" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "mayoría" means "majority", and "most" is said as "la mayoría de", as in "la mayoría de los estudiantes".

questions.prompt: How do you say "only" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "solo" means "only" when it modifies a word, as in "Solo tengo un hermano"; it is written without an accent.

questions.prompt: How do you say "almost" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "casi" means almost and goes before the word it softens, as in "casi todo" (almost everything). "Solo" means only and "cada" means each.

questions.prompt: How do you say "nothing" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "nada" means nothing. After a verb, Spanish also keeps "no", as in "No quiero nada" (I don't want anything).

questions.prompt: How do you say "double" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "doble" means double (twice as much) and has the same form for masculine and feminine, as in "un café doble". "Extra" only means additional.

questions.prompt: How do you say "three times as much" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "triple" means "three times as much", just as "doble" means "twice as much", as in "el triple de trabajo".

questions.prompt: How do you say "only (the one and only)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "único" means "the only one" or "single", as in "Es mi único hermano" (He is my only brother).

questions.prompt: How do you say "additional (more than usual)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "extra" means "additional" and does not change for gender, as in "una hora extra".

questions.prompt: How do you say "entire" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "entero" means "entire" or "whole" and agrees with its noun, as in "Comí la pizza entera".

questions.prompt: How do you say "partial" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "parcial" means "partial", the opposite of "entero" (whole), as in "un pago parcial".

questions.prompt: How do you say "approximately" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "aproximadamente" means "approximately", as in "aproximadamente diez personas"; in speech, "más o menos" is also common.

questions.prompt: How do you say "exactly" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "exactamente" means "exactly", the opposite of "aproximadamente", as in "Son exactamente las tres".

units.title: Basic Conversation Phrases
units.description: Everyday small talk — Common small-talk and reaction phrases.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Make yourself at home" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Siéntete como en casa" literally means 'feel as if at home'. It uses the friendly tú command, so say it to a friend or family guest.

questions.prompt: How do you say "How's it going?" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¿Qué tal?" is the short, friendly way to ask how things are going. Note the opening ¿ and the accent on "qué" in a question.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Long time no see" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Cuánto tiempo sin verte" literally means 'how much time without seeing you'. "Verte" is the tú form, so use it with friends.

questions.prompt: How do you say "See you later" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Hasta luego" literally means 'until later'. It is the everyday goodbye when you expect to see someone again.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Take care" in Spanish?
