questions.explanation: "Cuídate" is the friendly tú command of cuidarse (to look after yourself), and people say it when parting from someone. The other options mean "congratulations", "I don't know" and "I agree".

questions.prompt: How do you say "Have a good day" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Que tengas un buen día" is the set phrase for wishing a friend a good day, so learn it as one chunk. The other options ask someone to repeat, ask how things are, and say "make yourself at home".

questions.prompt: How do you say "Welcome back" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Bienvenido de vuelta" greets someone who has returned. Say "bienvenida" to a woman, and note that "bienvenido de nuevo" is also common.

questions.prompt: How do you say "I don't understand" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "No entiendo" is the yo form of "entender" (the e changes to ie) with "no" in front. No subject is needed because the ending already shows 'I'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Can you repeat that?" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¿Puedes repetirlo?" literally asks "Can you repeat it?" with the verb repetir. "Habla despacio, por favor" asks someone to speak slowly, not to repeat.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Speak slowly, please" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Habla despacio, por favor" uses "despacio" (slowly), while "más alto" would mean louder. This is the tú command; to a stranger, say "Hable despacio, por favor".

questions.prompt: How do you say "What does that mean?" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¿Qué significa eso?" uses "significar" (to mean) and "eso" (that). "Qué" takes an accent because it is a question word.

questions.prompt: How do you say "I don't know" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "No sé" comes from "saber" (to know). "Sé" needs the accent to mean 'I know' and not the pronoun "se".

questions.prompt: How do you say "Of course" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Claro" (literally "clear") is the everyday way to say "of course" when agreeing to something. The other options mean "I don't know", "likewise" and "take care".

questions.prompt: How do you say "No problem" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "No hay problema" literally means 'there is no problem', using "hay" (there is). It is the usual friendly reply to thanks or a request.

questions.prompt: How do you say "That's okay" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Está bien" means "it's fine" and is used to accept an apology or agree to something. The other options mean "congratulations", "I don't understand" and "see you later".

questions.prompt: How do you say "I agree" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Estoy de acuerdo" literally means "I am in agreement": Spanish uses estar + de acuerdo where English uses the verb "agree".

questions.prompt: How do you say "I disagree" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "No estoy de acuerdo" is the negative of "Estoy de acuerdo": put "no" before the verb to say you disagree.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Good luck" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Buena suerte" means "good luck"; suerte is feminine, so the adjective is buena, not bueno.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Congratulations" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Felicidades" is what you say for a birthday, a new job or any good news; in much of Latin America you will also hear Felicitaciones.

questions.prompt: How do you say "I'm sorry" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Perdón" is a quick apology for a small mistake, like bumping into someone. For deeper regret, "lo siento" is also used.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Excuse me (getting attention)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Disculpe" is the polite usted form you use to get a stranger's attention, such as a waiter or someone on the street.

questions.prompt: How do you say "It's a pleasure" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Es un placer" means "it's a pleasure"; you can say it when you meet someone or after you help them.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Same to you" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Igualmente" means "likewise" and is the usual reply when someone wishes you something, like ¡Buen fin de semana!

questions.prompt: How do you say "Take it easy" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Tómalo con calma" literally means "take it calmly". It is the friendly tú way to tell someone to relax or not stress.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Good job" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Buen trabajo" means "good job"; trabajo is masculine, and bueno shortens to buen before a masculine noun.

units.title: Colors & Shapes
units.description: More colors, and basic shapes — Additional colors and basic geometric shapes.

questions.prompt: How do you say "pink" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "rosa" means pink; in much of Latin America you will also hear rosado.

questions.prompt: How do you say "purple" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "morado" is purple; "dorado" is gold, "naranja" is orange and "gris" is grey.

questions.prompt: How do you say "gray" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "gris" means gray and keeps the same form for masculine and feminine nouns: un gato gris, una casa gris.

questions.prompt: How do you say "brown" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "marrón" means brown; in much of Latin America "café" is also very common for brown.

questions.prompt: How do you say "turquoise" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "turquesa" is turquoise, the blue-green color; "dorado" is gold and "plateado" is silver.

questions.prompt: How do you say "gold" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "dorado" means gold, the color; "azul marino" is navy blue and "rosa" is pink.

questions.prompt: How do you say "silver" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "plateado" means silver; it comes from plata, the metal silver. With feminine nouns it changes to plateada (una llave plateada).

questions.prompt: How do you say "beige" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: beige → beige. Additional colors and basic geometric shapes.

questions.prompt: How do you say "navy blue" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "azul marino" is navy blue, literally 'marine blue', while azul claro is light blue. It does not change form: pantalones azul marino.

questions.prompt: How do you say "circle" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "círculo" means circle; it carries an accent on the first i because the stress falls on the third-to-last syllable.

questions.prompt: How do you say "square" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cuadrado" means square; it also works as an adjective, as in una mesa cuadrada.

questions.prompt: How do you say "triangle" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "triángulo" is the three-sided shape (tri- means three, as in English). Note the accent on the first a.

questions.prompt: How do you say "rectangle" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "rectángulo" is the four-sided shape with two long and two short sides; "cuadrado" is a square, with all sides equal.

questions.prompt: How do you say "star (shape)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "estrella" means star, both the shape and the one in the sky; it is feminine: una estrella.

questions.prompt: How do you say "heart (shape)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "corazón" means heart, both the organ and the shape. It has an accent on the last o.

questions.prompt: How do you say "oval" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "óvalo" is the egg-like shape, a stretched circle; note the accent on the first ó.

questions.prompt: How do you say "diamond (shape)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: diamond (shape) → diamante. Additional colors and basic geometric shapes.

questions.prompt: How do you say "line" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "línea" means line and is feminine (una línea); the written accent goes on the í: lí-ne-a.

questions.prompt: How do you say "dot" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "punto" means a dot or point, a very small round mark; it is masculine: un punto.

questions.prompt: How do you say "curve" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "curva" is a curved line; "línea" on its own usually means a straight line.

questions.prompt: How do you say "striped" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "rayado" means striped, from raya (stripe); it agrees with the noun, as in una camisa rayada.

questions.prompt: How do you say "spotted" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "con manchas" literally means 'with spots' and is the usual way to describe a spotted pattern, as in un perro con manchas.

questions.prompt: How do you say "light (color shade)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "claro" goes after a color to make it light, as in azul claro (light blue).

questions.prompt: How do you say "dark (color shade)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "oscuro" goes after a color to make it dark, as in verde oscuro (dark green); it is the opposite of claro.

questions.prompt: How do you say "bright" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "brillante" means bright or shiny; it has the same form for masculine and feminine: un color brillante, una luz brillante.

units.title: Directions & Commands
units.description: Basic instructions — Basic imperative instructions and directions.

questions.prompt: How do you say "turn left" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "gira a la izquierda" uses the tú command of girar plus izquierda (left); derecha would mean right.

questions.prompt: How do you say "turn right" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "gira a la derecha" combines the tú command gira (turn) with a la derecha (to the right). Sigue derecho means 'go straight' and a la izquierda means 'to the left'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "go straight" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "sigue derecho" is the tú command of seguir (to keep going) plus derecho (straight), the usual way to say "go straight" in Latin America; "para" means "stop".

questions.prompt: How do you say "stop" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "para" is the tú command of parar, 'to stop'. Don't confuse it with the preposition para, 'for'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "walk" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "camina" is the tú command of caminar, 'to walk'. Cruza means 'cross', apúrate means 'hurry up' and entra means 'come in'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "cross the street" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cruza la calle" is the tú command of cruzar, 'to cross', plus la calle, 'the street'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "go up" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "sube" is the tú command of subir, 'to go up'. Its opposite is baja, 'go down'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "go down" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "baja" is the tú command of bajar, 'to go down'. Its opposite is sube, 'go up'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "come here" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ven aquí" uses ven, the irregular tú command of venir (to come), plus aquí (here); "ve allá" would mean 'go there'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "go there" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "ve allá" uses ve, the irregular tú command of ir (to go), plus allá (there); it is the opposite of 'ven aquí' (come here).

questions.prompt: How do you say "wait here" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "espera aquí" is espera, the tú command of esperar (to wait), plus aquí (here).

questions.prompt: How do you say "follow me" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "sígueme" is sigue, the tú command of seguir (to follow), with me attached; the written accent keeps the stress on the first syllable, SÍ-gue-me. 'Sigue derecho' means 'go straight ahead'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "hurry up" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "apúrate" is the tú command of apurarse (to hurry), with the reflexive te attached; it is the usual way to say 'hurry up' in Latin America.

questions.prompt: How do you say "be careful" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ten cuidado" uses ten, the irregular tú command of tener, so it literally means 'have care', that is, 'be careful'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "slow down" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "más despacio" literally means 'more slowly'; on its own it is the common way to tell someone to slow down.

questions.prompt: How do you say "look here" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "mira aquí" is mira, the tú command of mirar (to look), plus aquí (here).

questions.prompt: How do you say "listen" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "escucha" is the tú command of escuchar (to listen); the other options mean go down, stand up and turn left.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sit down" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "siéntate" is the tú command of sentarse (to sit down), with the reflexive te attached and an accent to keep the stress on sién.

questions.prompt: How do you say "stand up" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "levántate" is the tú command of levantarse (to stand up), with the reflexive te attached and an accent to keep the stress on ván.

questions.prompt: How do you say "come in" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "entra" is the tú command of entrar (to enter), so it is what you say to invite someone to come in.

questions.prompt: How do you say "go out" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "sal" is the tú command of salir (to go out). It is irregular: it is not "sale", it is just "sal".

questions.prompt: How do you say "close the door" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cierra la puerta" means close the door: "cierra" is the tú command of cerrar (e→ie), and "la puerta" is the door.

questions.prompt: How do you say "open the window" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "abre la ventana" means open the window: "abre" is the tú command of abrir, and "la ventana" is the window.

questions.prompt: How do you say "be quiet" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cállate" is the tú command of callarse (to be quiet), with -te attached and a written accent. It sounds blunt, so use it only with people you know well.

questions.prompt: How do you say "pay attention" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "presta atención" is the tú command of prestar atención, literally "lend attention". It is the usual way to say pay attention.

units.title: Speaking: Basic Everyday Phrases
units.description: Say it out loud — Short everyday greetings and phrases to practise saying.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Hola, ¿cómo estás?" is the friendly tú way to say "Hi, how are you?" to a friend; the question mark ¿ opens where the question starts, after the comma.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Buenos días." means "Good morning" and is used until about noon; Spanish uses the plural días here.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Buenas noches." means "Good evening" or "Good night" and works both as a greeting and as a goodbye after dark.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "¿Cómo te llamas?" is the tú way to ask "What's your name?"; it literally means "How do you call yourself?".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Me llamo Ana." means "My name is Ana"; it literally means "I call myself Ana" and answers ¿Cómo te llamas?

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Mucho gusto." means "Nice to meet you" and is said when you are introduced to someone.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "¿De dónde eres?" means "Where are you from?"; it uses ser (eres) because it asks about origin, in the tú form for someone your age or a friend.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "Soy de España." It means "I'm from Spain": use soy de + a country to say where you are from.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Tengo hambre." means "I'm hungry"; Spanish says "I have hunger" with tener, not ser or estar.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Tengo sed." means "I'm thirsty"; like hambre, sed goes with tener ("I have thirst").

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "¿Dónde está el baño?" means "Where is the bathroom?"; it uses estar because it asks about location, and baño is the everyday Latin American word.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Muchas gracias." means "Thank you very much"; it is muchas, not muchos, because gracias is feminine plural.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "De nada." means "You're welcome". Say it when someone thanks you; the d in "nada" is soft, almost like the th in "this".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Por favor." means "please". Add it to any request to sound polite; tap the r in "por" once, lightly.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "Lo siento." It means "I'm sorry" and is used to apologize or to show sympathy.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "¿Qué hora es?" It means "What time is it?" and is the standard way to ask the time.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "Hasta luego." It means "See you later" and is a very common everyday goodbye.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "Hasta mañana." It means "See you tomorrow" and is used when you will see the person the next day.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "¿Habla usted inglés?" It means "Do you speak English?" and uses polite usted, which is right for a stranger.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "No entiendo." It means "I don't understand" and is useful when you can't follow what someone says.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "¿Puede repetir, por favor?" means "Can you repeat that, please?". "Puede" is the polite usted form, so it suits strangers, shop staff and teachers.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Tengo dos hermanos." means "I have two brothers" (or two siblings, if mixed). "Tengo" is the yo form of "tener", the verb used to talk about family.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Tengo tres hermanas." means "I have three sisters". "Hermanas" ends in -as because the sisters are female and there is more than one.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Son las cinco." means "It's five o'clock". Spanish uses plural "son las" for every hour except one o'clock ("Es la una").

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Vivo aquí." means "I live here". "Vivo" is the yo form of "vivir", and "aquí" carries an accent on the í.

units.title: Write It Yourself: Everyday Needs
units.description: Say it your own way — Greetings, needs and everyday small talk. More than one wording can be right.

questions.prompt: Ask someone their name.
questions.explanation: "¿Cómo te llamas?" is the friendly tú way to ask someone's name. With a stranger or an older person, use the usted form "¿Cómo se llama usted?".

questions.prompt: Say your name is Ana.
questions.explanation: "Me llamo Ana." literally means "I call myself Ana" and is the most common way to give your name. "Mi nombre es Ana." and "Soy Ana." are also correct.

questions.prompt: Ask how someone is doing.
questions.explanation: "¿Cómo estás?" uses estar because it asks about a passing state, and it is the friendly tú form. With a stranger, say "¿Cómo está?" instead.

questions.prompt: Say you are fine, thanks.
questions.explanation: "Estoy bien, gracias." uses estar because how you feel is a temporary state. In everyday speech you can also just say "Bien, gracias."

questions.prompt: Say good morning.
questions.explanation: "Buenos días." is the standard morning greeting and is always plural. In many Latin American countries people also say "Buen día.".

questions.prompt: Ask where the bathroom is.
questions.explanation: "¿Dónde está el baño?" uses estar because Spanish uses estar to give the location of things. "Baño" is the usual word for bathroom in Latin America.

questions.prompt: Say you don't understand.
questions.explanation: "No entiendo." puts "no" right before the verb; the yo form "entiendo" already means "I understand", so you don't need "yo".

questions.prompt: Ask someone to repeat that.
questions.explanation: "¿Puedes repetir eso?" uses poder plus an infinitive to make a request, here in the friendly tú form. With a stranger, say "¿Puede repetir, por favor?"

questions.prompt: Say you are hungry.
questions.explanation: "Tengo hambre." is the everyday way to say "I'm hungry": Spanish uses "tener" (to have) with the noun hambre. "Estoy hambriento" also works but sounds stronger and less common.

questions.prompt: Say you are thirsty.
questions.explanation: "Tengo sed." is how Spanish says "I'm thirsty": you "have" thirst with "tener", just as with "tengo hambre".

questions.prompt: Ask for a coffee.
questions.explanation: "Quiero un café, por favor." is a simple, polite way to order: "quiero" means "I want", and "por favor" keeps it courteous. At a counter, "¿Me da un café, por favor?" is also very common.

questions.prompt: Say thank you very much.
questions.explanation: "Muchas gracias." uses "muchas" (feminine plural) because it agrees with "gracias", a feminine plural noun.

questions.prompt: Say you're welcome.
questions.explanation: "De nada." (literally "for nothing") is the standard reply when someone thanks you. "Con gusto" is also very common in Latin America.

questions.prompt: Ask what time it is.
questions.explanation: "¿Qué hora es?" uses the singular "es" because you are asking about the hour itself; the answer changes to "son" for most times, as in "Son las tres".

questions.prompt: Say it's five o'clock.
questions.explanation: For any hour except one o'clock, Spanish uses the plural "son las" plus the number, so "Son las cinco." means it's five o'clock.

questions.prompt: Ask where someone lives.
questions.explanation: "¿Dónde vives?" uses "vives", the tú form of vivir (to live), for a friend; with a stranger say "¿Dónde vive usted?"

questions.prompt: Say you live in Mexico.
questions.explanation: "Vivo en México." uses "vivo" (I live) with "en" for the place. "México" keeps its accent on the first syllable.

questions.prompt: Ask someone's age.
questions.explanation: Spanish asks age with tener (to have), literally 'how many years do you have', so "¿Cuántos años tienes?" is the informal question.

questions.prompt: Say you are twenty years old.
questions.explanation: Spanish gives age with tener, not ser, so you say "Tengo veinte años." (literally 'I have twenty years').

questions.prompt: Say goodbye to a friend.
questions.explanation: "Adiós." is the standard goodbye; with a friend you can also say "Nos vemos." or the very common Latin American "Chao."

questions.prompt: Say see you tomorrow.
questions.explanation: "Hasta mañana." combines hasta (until) with mañana (tomorrow) and is the set phrase for 'see you tomorrow'.

questions.prompt: Ask for the check at a restaurant.
acceptableAnswers: ¿Nos puede traer la cuenta, por favor?
questions.explanation: In a restaurant the check is la cuenta, and "La cuenta, por favor." is the short, polite way to ask the waiter for it.

questions.prompt: Say you like the food.
questions.explanation: With gustar the thing you like is the subject, so "Me gusta la comida." literally means 'the food pleases me'.

questions.prompt: Ask how much something costs.
questions.explanation: "¿Cuánto cuesta?" means "How much does it cost?"; use "¿Cuánto cuestan?" for more than one thing. Note the accent on "cuánto" in questions.

questions.prompt: Say good night.
questions.explanation: "Buenas noches." is used both as a greeting in the evening and to say good night before bed; it is always plural.

units.title: Minimal Pairs
units.description: Listen closely — Sentences built around sounds that merge for most Spanish speakers: seseo (casa/caza), b/v (basto/vasto, botar/votar), yeísmo (pollo/poyo), and silent h (onda/honda).

questions.prompt: ¿Qué escuchaste?
questions.audioText: Hablamos de la casa toda la tarde.
choices: Decidieron botar ayer por la tarde.
Decidieron votar ayer por la tarde.
Nunca había visto una casa tan grande.
Hablamos de la casa toda la tarde.
questions.answer: Hablamos de la casa toda la tarde.
questions.explanation: You heard "Hablamos de la casa toda la tarde." It is the only option that starts with "Hablamos" and ends with "toda la tarde"; the others are about a decision made yesterday or a big house.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué escuchaste?
questions.audioText: Hablamos de la caza toda la tarde.
choices: Decidieron botar ayer por la tarde.
Decidieron votar ayer por la tarde.
Nunca había visto una caza tan grande.
Hablamos de la caza toda la tarde.
questions.answer: Hablamos de la caza toda la tarde.
questions.explanation: You heard "Hablamos de la caza toda la tarde." It is the only option with "Hablamos de" and "toda la tarde"; here "caza" means hunting, and it sounds just like "casa".

questions.prompt: ¿Qué escuchaste?
questions.audioText: Nunca había visto una casa tan grande.
choices: Nadie esperaba una onda tan fuerte.
Nadie esperaba una honda tan fuerte.
Nunca había visto una casa tan grande.
Hablamos de la casa toda la tarde.
questions.answer: Nunca había visto una casa tan grande.
questions.explanation: You heard "Nunca había visto una casa tan grande." The other options start with "Nadie esperaba" or "Hablamos", so only this one matches "Nunca había visto... tan grande".

questions.prompt: ¿Qué escuchaste?
questions.audioText: Nunca había visto una caza tan grande.
choices: Nadie esperaba una onda tan fuerte.
Nunca había visto una caza tan grande.
Nadie esperaba una honda tan fuerte.
Hablamos de la caza toda la tarde.
questions.answer: Nunca había visto una caza tan grande.
questions.explanation: You heard "Nunca había visto una caza tan grande." It is the only option that starts with "Nunca había visto"; "caza" (a hunt) sounds the same as "casa".

questions.prompt: ¿Qué escuchaste?
questions.audioText: Vimos la onda desde la playa.
choices: Vimos la onda desde la playa.
Vimos el poyo en el patio.
Se podía ver el cerro desde la ventana.
Vimos el pollo en el patio.
questions.answer: Vimos la onda desde la playa.
questions.explanation: You heard "Vimos la onda desde la playa." It is the only option that ends with "desde la playa"; the others mention a patio or a window.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué escuchaste?
questions.audioText: Vimos la honda desde la playa.
choices: Nadie esperaba una honda tan fuerte.
Vimos la honda desde la playa.
Vimos el poyo en el patio.
Vimos el pollo en el patio.
questions.answer: Vimos la honda desde la playa.
questions.explanation: You heard "Vimos la honda desde la playa." It is the only option that starts with "Vimos la" and ends with "desde la playa"; the h in "honda" is silent, so it sounds like "onda".

questions.prompt: ¿Qué escuchaste?
questions.audioText: Nadie esperaba una onda tan fuerte.
choices: Nadie esperaba una onda tan fuerte.
Nunca había visto una caza tan grande.
Vimos la onda desde la playa.
Nunca había visto una casa tan grande.
questions.answer: Nadie esperaba una onda tan fuerte.
questions.explanation: You heard "Nadie esperaba una onda tan fuerte." It is the only option that starts with "Nadie esperaba"; the others start with "Nunca" or "Vimos".

questions.prompt: ¿Qué escuchaste?
questions.audioText: Nadie esperaba una honda tan fuerte.
choices: Nunca había visto una caza tan grande.
Nadie esperaba una honda tan fuerte.
Vimos la honda desde la playa.
Nunca había visto una casa tan grande.
questions.answer: Nadie esperaba una honda tan fuerte.
questions.explanation: You heard "Nadie esperaba una honda tan fuerte." It is the only option that starts with "Nadie esperaba"; the silent h makes "honda" sound like "onda".

questions.audioText: Vimos el pollo en el patio.

units.title: Food & Dining
units.description: Ordering and talking about food — Everyday food and restaurant vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "bread" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "pan" means bread; pescado is fish, menú is menu and arroz is rice.

questions.prompt: How do you say "water" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "agua" means water; it is feminine but takes el in the singular (el agua) because it starts with a stressed a.

questions.prompt: How do you say "coffee" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "café" means coffee; note the accent on the final é, which carries the stress.

questions.prompt: How do you say "milk" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "leche" means milk; it is feminine (la leche), while cena means dinner and arroz means rice.

questions.prompt: How do you say "rice" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "arroz" means rice; it is a masculine noun (el arroz), as in arroz con pollo.

questions.prompt: How do you say "chicken" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "pollo" is chicken, both the bird and the meat you eat, as in arroz con pollo.

questions.prompt: How do you say "fish (as food)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "pescado" is fish as food on your plate; a live fish swimming in water is "pez".

questions.prompt: How do you say "vegetables" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "verduras" means vegetables and is usually used in the plural; in many Latin American countries you will also hear "vegetales".

questions.prompt: How do you say "fruit" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "fruta" means fruit; it is a feminine noun (la fruta).

questions.prompt: How do you say "breakfast" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "desayuno" is breakfast, the first meal of the day; the verb for eating it is desayunar.

questions.prompt: How do you say "lunch" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "almuerzo" is lunch, the midday meal, in most of Latin America; the verb for eating it is almorzar.

questions.prompt: How do you say "dinner" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cena" is dinner, the evening meal; the verb for eating it is cenar.

questions.prompt: How do you say "the bill" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "la cuenta" is the bill you ask for at a restaurant, as in "La cuenta, por favor".

questions.prompt: How do you say "menu" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "menú" means menu; note the written accent on the ú.

questions.prompt: How do you say "delicious" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "delicioso" means delicious, as in La comida está deliciosa; "picante" means spicy and "caliente" means hot.

questions.prompt: How do you say "hungry" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "hambriento" is the adjective for hungry, but in everyday speech people usually say Tengo hambre (I'm hungry).

questions.prompt: How do you say "thirsty" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "sediento" is the adjective for thirsty, but in everyday speech people usually say Tengo sed (I'm thirsty).

questions.prompt: How do you say "spoon" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cuchara" means spoon; it is a feminine noun (la cuchara), used for soup.

questions.prompt: How do you say "fork" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "tenedor" means fork; it is a masculine noun (el tenedor).

questions.prompt: How do you say "knife" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A knife is "cuchillo" (el cuchillo), the utensil you cut with; "cuenta" is the bill and "pollo" is chicken.

units.title: Past Tense (yo form)
units.description: Preterite, first person — Simple past ("yo" form) of common regular and irregular verbs.

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (hablar) con mi madre.
questions.explanation: "Ayer" calls for the simple past, and the "yo" form of an -ar verb ends in -é: "hablé". "Habló" is él, "hablaste" is tú and "hablaron" is ellos.

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (comer) en un restaurante.
questions.explanation: "Ayer" calls for the simple past, and the "yo" form of an -er verb ends in -í: "comí". "Comió" is él, "comiste" is tú and "comimos" is nosotros.

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (vivir) una gran aventura.
questions.explanation: "Ayer" calls for the simple past, and the "yo" form of an -ir verb ends in -í: "viví". "Vivió", "vivieron" and "vivimos" match other subjects.

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (ir) al cine.
questions.explanation: Ir has an irregular simple past, and its "yo" form is "fui" (it is the same as ser). "Fuiste", "fueron" and "fuimos" belong to tú, ellos and nosotros.

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (ser) muy feliz.
questions.explanation: Ser has an irregular simple past, and its "yo" form is "fui". "Fue", "fuiste" and "fueron" belong to él, tú and ellos.

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (tener) una reunión.
questions.explanation: Tener has an irregular simple past stem, tuv-, and "yo" takes the unaccented ending -e: "tuve". "Tuvo", "tuviste" and "tuvimos" match other subjects.

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (hacer) la cena.
questions.explanation: Hacer has an irregular simple past stem, hic-, and "yo" takes the ending -e: "hice". "Hizo", "hicimos" and "hicieron" match other subjects.

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (ver) una película.
questions.explanation: The subject "yo" and "Ayer" call for the preterite, and "ver" has the irregular yo form "vi" (no accent). "viste", "vieron" and "vimos" belong to tú, ellos and nosotros.

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (dar) un regalo.
questions.explanation: With "yo" and "Ayer", the preterite of "dar" is "di" (an irregular form with no accent). "dio", "dieron" and "diste" go with él, ellos and tú.
questions.example: Ayer le di un regalo a mi hermana.

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (decir) la verdad.
questions.explanation: The preterite of "decir" has an irregular stem dij-, and the yo ending is a plain "-e", giving "dije". The forms "dijo", "dijimos" and "dijiste" match other subjects, not "yo".

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (poder) terminar el trabajo.
questions.explanation: "Poder" has the irregular preterite stem pud-, and the yo ending is "-e", so "yo" takes "pude". "Pudo", "pudimos" and "pudiste" match él, nosotros and tú.
questions.meaning: I could, I was able to

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (venir) temprano.
questions.explanation: "Venir" has the irregular preterite stem vin-, and the yo ending is "-e", giving "vine". "Viniste", "vino" and "vinieron" belong to tú, él and ellos.

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (querer) descansar.
questions.explanation: "Querer" has the irregular preterite stem quis-, and the yo ending is "-e", so "yo" takes "quise". The other options are the tú, ellos and nosotros forms.
questions.example: Ayer quise descansar, pero no pude.

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (poner) la mesa.
questions.explanation: "Poner" has the irregular preterite stem pus-, and the yo ending is "-e", giving "puse". "Pusimos", "puso" and "pusieron" go with nosotros, él and ellos.

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (traer) el postre.
questions.explanation: "Traer" has the irregular preterite stem traj-, and the yo ending is "-e", so "yo" takes "traje". "Trajo", "trajimos" and "trajiste" fit other subjects.

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (estar) en casa.
questions.explanation: "Estar" has the irregular preterite stem estuv-, and the yo ending is "-e" with no accent, giving "estuve". "Estuviste", "estuvieron" and "estuvo" go with tú, ellos and él.

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (llegar) a tiempo.
questions.explanation: In the yo preterite of "-gar" verbs, g becomes gu before "-é" to keep the hard g sound, giving "llegué". "Llegaste", "llegaron" and "llegamos" match other subjects.

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (empezar) el proyecto.
questions.explanation: In the yo preterite of "-zar" verbs, z becomes c before "-é", so "empezar" gives "empecé". "Empezó", "empezamos" and "empezaron" match él, nosotros and ellos.

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (buscar) mis llaves.
questions.explanation: In the yo preterite of "-car" verbs, c becomes qu before "-é" to keep the hard k sound, giving "busqué". "Buscó", "buscamos" and "buscaste" match other subjects.

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (leer) el periódico.
questions.explanation: "Ayer" signals a completed past action, and the subject is "yo", so leer takes the first-person preterite ending: "leí" (the i carries an accent).

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (escribir) un correo.
questions.explanation: With "ayer" and the subject "yo", regular -ir verbs take the preterite ending -í: "escribí".

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (dormir) muy bien.
questions.explanation: The subject is "yo" and the action is finished ("ayer"), so dormir takes the first-person preterite: "dormí". The stem change to "durmió" happens only in the third person.

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (pedir) ayuda.
questions.explanation: For "yo" in the preterite, pedir keeps its regular stem and takes -í: "pedí". The e-to-i stem change appears only in the third person ("pidió", "pidieron").

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (viajar) a Madrid.
questions.explanation: "Yo" with a regular -ar verb in the preterite takes -é, with an accent on the final vowel: "viajé".

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (comprar) un regalo.
questions.explanation: "Yo" with a regular -ar verb in the past takes -é: "compré". "Compró" is he/she and "compramos" is we.

units.title: Directions & Places
units.description: Getting around town — Places in town and basic direction words.

questions.prompt: How do you say "street" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Street is "calle" (la calle), as in "Vivo en esta calle"; "parque" is park and "banco" is bank.

questions.prompt: How do you say "city" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: City is "ciudad" (la ciudad); note that it is feminine, like most nouns ending in -dad.

questions.prompt: How do you say "bank" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "banco" is the place where you keep money (it can also mean a park bench).

questions.prompt: How do you say "hospital" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "hospital" is spelled the same as in English, but in Spanish the h is silent and the stress falls on the last syllable (os-pi-TAL).

questions.prompt: How do you say "bridge" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Bridge is "puente" (el puente), a masculine noun; "iglesia" is church and "calle" is street.

questions.prompt: How do you say "store" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "tienda" is a store or shop; "estación" is a station and "esquina" is a corner.

questions.prompt: How do you say "market" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "mercado" is a market with many stalls or vendors, while "tienda" is a single store.

questions.prompt: How do you say "park" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Park is "parque" (el parque); "mercado" is market and "semáforo" is traffic light.

questions.prompt: How do you say "church" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Church is "iglesia" (la iglesia); "estación" is station and "hospital" is hospital.

questions.prompt: How do you say "station" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Station is "estación" (la estación), with an accent on the ó; it is feminine, like most nouns ending in -ción.

questions.prompt: How do you say "airport" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Airport is "aeropuerto" (el aeropuerto), literally an 'air port': aero + puerto.

questions.prompt: How do you say "left" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Left is "izquierda", as in "a la izquierda" (on the left); don't confuse it with "derecho", which means straight ahead.

questions.prompt: How do you say "right" in "Turn right at the corner"? Gire a la ___ en la esquina.
questions.explanation: "derecha" is the right-hand direction and is feminine, so it follows a la in Gire a la derecha; "derecho" means straight ahead.

questions.prompt: How do you say "straight ahead" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "derecho" means straight ahead, as in Siga derecho; do not confuse it with "derecha", which means right.

questions.prompt: How do you say "near" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Near is "cerca", as in "cerca de la plaza"; its opposite is "lejos" (far).

questions.prompt: How do you say "far" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "lejos" means far, as in El banco está lejos; its opposite is cerca (near).

questions.prompt: How do you say "here" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Here is "aquí", with an accent on the í; "allí" means there.

questions.prompt: How do you say "there" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "allí" means there, a place away from the speaker, as in El mercado está allí.

questions.prompt: How do you say "corner" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A street corner is "esquina" (la esquina), as in "en la esquina" (on the corner).

questions.prompt: How do you say "traffic light" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A traffic light is "semáforo", a masculine noun (el semáforo), as in "Gire a la derecha en el semáforo". The other options are places: church, hospital and airport.

units.title: Adjective Agreement
units.description: Matching gender and number — Adjectives agree in gender and number with the noun they describe.

questions.prompt: La casa es muy ___ (bonito).
questions.explanation: "Casa" is feminine singular, so the adjective must be feminine singular too: "bonita".

questions.prompt: El coche es muy ___ (fast).
questions.explanation: "Coche" is masculine singular, so the adjective takes the masculine singular form: "rápido".
questions.example: El carro es muy rápido.

questions.prompt: Las flores son muy ___ (bonito).
questions.explanation: "Flores" is feminine plural, so the adjective needs both feminine and plural endings: "bonitas".

questions.prompt: Los libros son muy ___ (interesante).
questions.explanation: "Libros" is plural, and adjectives ending in -e only add -s for the plural: "interesantes". "Interesados" is a different word, meaning interested.

questions.prompt: La chica es muy ___ (alto).
questions.explanation: "Chica" is feminine singular, so "alto" changes to its feminine form: "alta".

questions.prompt: El chico es muy ___ (tall).
questions.explanation: "Chico" is masculine singular, so the adjective stays in the masculine singular form: "alto".

questions.prompt: Las mesas son ___ (nuevo).
questions.explanation: "nuevas" is feminine plural to agree with "las mesas" (feminine, plural), so the adjective needs both the -a and the -s.

questions.prompt: El problema es ___ (difficult).
questions.explanation: "difícil" means difficult and is singular to match "el problema"; adjectives ending in -l or -e have one form for masculine and feminine, so only the number changes.

questions.prompt: La sopa está ___ (hot).
questions.explanation: "caliente" means hot and is singular to match "la sopa"; it ends in -e, so it has the same form for masculine and feminine, and the plural "calientes" would not fit one soup.

questions.prompt: Los perros son ___ (pequeño).
questions.explanation: "pequeños" is masculine plural to agree with "los perros": the -o shows masculine and the -s shows plural.

questions.prompt: La película fue ___ (aburrido).
questions.explanation: "aburrida" is feminine singular to agree with "la película", so the -o ending changes to -a.

questions.prompt: El examen fue ___ (easy).
questions.explanation: "fácil" means easy and stays singular for "el examen"; it ends in -l, so it has one form for masculine and feminine.

questions.prompt: Las camisas son ___ (blanco).
questions.explanation: "blancas" is feminine plural to agree with "las camisas": -a for feminine and -s for plural.

questions.prompt: El agua está ___ (frío).
questions.explanation: "fría" is feminine singular because "agua" is a feminine noun even though it takes "el" in the singular; the adjective must agree with the noun's gender, not the article.
questions.example: La bebida está fría.

questions.prompt: La ciudad es ___ (big).
questions.explanation: "grande" means big and is singular to match "la ciudad"; it ends in -e, so it is the same for masculine and feminine.

questions.prompt: Los estudiantes están ___ (cansado).
questions.explanation: "cansados" is masculine plural to agree with "los estudiantes": -o for masculine and -s for plural.

questions.prompt: La profesora es ___ (kind).
questions.explanation: "amable" means kind and is singular to match "la profesora"; it ends in -e, so it has the same form for feminine and masculine. "simpático" is masculine, so it does not agree with "la profesora".

questions.prompt: El edificio es ___ (old).
questions.explanation: "viejo" is masculine singular to agree with "el edificio", so it keeps the -o with no -s.

questions.prompt: Las manzanas están ___ (verde).
questions.explanation: "verdes" is correct because "Las manzanas" is feminine plural, and "verde" has one form for both genders, so only the plural -s is added.

questions.prompt: El café está ___ (tasty).
questions.explanation: "rico" is correct because "El café" is masculine singular, so the adjective takes the masculine singular ending -o.

questions.prompt: La habitación es ___ (oscuro).
questions.explanation: "oscura" is correct because "La habitación" is feminine singular, so the adjective changes -o to -a.

questions.prompt: Los zapatos son ___ (cómodo).
questions.explanation: "cómodos" is correct because "Los zapatos" is masculine plural, so the adjective takes -os.

questions.prompt: La tarea es ___ (largo).
questions.explanation: "larga" is correct because "La tarea" is feminine singular (a feminine noun ending in -a), so the adjective ends in -a.

questions.prompt: El cielo está ___ (cloudy).
questions.explanation: "nublado" is correct because "El cielo" is masculine singular, so the adjective takes -o with estar.

questions.prompt: Las noticias son ___ (importante).
questions.explanation: "importantes" is correct because "Las noticias" is plural, and an adjective ending in -e only adds -s for the plural.

units.title: Comparisons
units.description: más / menos / tan... como — Comparative and superlative structures.

questions.prompt: Este libro es ___ interesante que ese. (more)
questions.explanation: "más" is correct because "más + adjective + que" is the pattern for 'more ... than', matching the clue (more).

questions.prompt: Mi hermano es ___ alto que yo. (more)
questions.explanation: "más" is correct because "más alto que" means 'taller than', as the clue (more) and "que" show.

questions.prompt: Ella es ___ inteligente como su hermana. (as)
questions.explanation: "tan" is correct because equality uses "tan + adjective + como" ('as ... as'), and "como" in the sentence signals it.

questions.prompt: Este coche es ___ caro que aquel. (less)
questions.explanation: "menos" is correct because "menos caro que" means 'less expensive than', matching the clue (less).

questions.prompt: Juan corre ___ rápido que Pedro. (more)
questions.explanation: "más" is correct because "más rápido que" means 'faster than', as the clue (more) and "que" indicate.

questions.prompt: Esta ciudad es la ___ grande del país. (most)
questions.explanation: The superlative is built with "la más" + adjective + de, so "más" gives 'the biggest in the country'.

questions.prompt: Hoy hace ___ calor que ayer. (more)
questions.explanation: The sentence compares today with yesterday using 'que', and the clue says 'more', so "más" calor que ayer.

questions.prompt: Mi casa es ___ pequeña que la tuya. (more)
questions.explanation: Unequal comparisons use más + adjective + que; the clue 'more' and the "que la tuya" point to "más".

questions.prompt: Ana es ___ paciente como su madre. (as)
questions.explanation: Equality with an adjective uses tan + adjective + como ('as... as'), so "tan" goes before 'paciente'; "tanto" is only for nouns or verbs.

questions.prompt: Este examen es el ___ difícil de todos. (most)
questions.explanation: The superlative 'el más + adjective + de todos' means 'the most difficult of all', so the word needed is "más".

questions.prompt: Tu perro es ___ grande que el mío. (more)
questions.explanation: 'Más + adjective + que' compares two dogs and the clue says 'more', so "más" fits before 'grande que el mío'.

questions.prompt: Este plato es ___ picante que el otro. (less)
questions.explanation: The clue 'less' plus 'que el otro' calls for menos + adjective + que, so the answer is "menos".

questions.prompt: Ellos son ___ trabajadores que nosotros. (more)
questions.explanation: Comparing 'ellos' and 'nosotros' with 'que' and the clue 'more' needs "más" before 'trabajadores'.

questions.prompt: Esta calle es la ___ larga de la ciudad. (most)
questions.explanation: After the article 'la', the superlative is formed with más + adjective + de, so "más" gives 'the longest street in the city'.

questions.prompt: El tren es ___ rápido que el autobús. (more)
questions.explanation: The train is compared to the bus with 'que', and the clue 'more' makes it "más" rápido que.

questions.prompt: Mi café está ___ caliente que el tuyo. (less)
questions.explanation: The clue 'less' with 'que el tuyo' needs menos + adjective + que, so "menos" caliente que.

questions.prompt: Esta película es la ___ interesante del año. (most)
questions.explanation: The superlative 'la más + adjective + del año' means 'the most interesting of the year', so "más" is needed.

questions.prompt: Su casa es ___ bonita como la nuestra. (as)
questions.explanation: The equal-comparison pattern is "tan" + adjective + "como" (as pretty as). "Tan" goes before the adjective "bonita", while "tanto" would be used with nouns.
questions.meaning: as, so (as in 'tan... como', as... as)

questions.prompt: El invierno aquí es ___ frío que allá. (more)
questions.explanation: The clue says "more", and "más" + adjective + "que" forms the comparative of superiority (more cold than). "Menos" would mean less.

questions.prompt: Esta tienda es la ___ barata de todas. (most)
questions.explanation: "más" is correct here. Comparative and superlative structures.

questions.prompt: Mi trabajo es ___ estresante que el tuyo. (less)
questions.explanation: The clue says "less", and "menos" + adjective + "que" compares two things (less stressful than yours). "Tan" needs "como", not "que".

questions.prompt: Este edificio es el ___ alto de la ciudad. (most)
questions.explanation: After "el", the superlative is formed with "más" + adjective + "de" (the tallest in the city). "Más" matches the clue "most".

questions.prompt: La comida aquí es ___ rica como en casa. (as)
questions.explanation: The "como" at the end signals an equal comparison: "tan" + adjective + "como" (as tasty as). "Tan" goes before the adjective "rica".
questions.meaning: as, so (as in 'tan... como', as... as)

questions.prompt: Este camino es ___ corto que el otro. (more)
questions.explanation: The clue says "more", and "más" + adjective + "que" is the comparative of superiority (shorter than the other). "Menos" would give the opposite meaning.

questions.prompt: Su idea es la ___ original de todas. (most)
questions.explanation: "más" is correct here. Comparative and superlative structures.

units.title: Common Verbs (tú form)
units.description: Present tense, informal you — Present-tense "tú" conjugation of common verbs.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (hablar) muy bien español.
questions.explanation: The subject "Tú" takes the -as ending for -ar verbs in the present, so hablar becomes "hablas". "Habla" is for él/ella, "hablan" for ellos.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (comer) mucha fruta.
questions.explanation: The subject "Tú" takes the -es ending for -er verbs in the present, so comer becomes "comes". "Como" is for yo and "come" for él/ella.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (vivir) en Madrid.
questions.explanation: The subject "Tú" takes the -es ending for -ir verbs in the present, so vivir becomes "vives". "Vivo" is for yo and "vive" for él/ella.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (tener) razón.
questions.explanation: Tener changes its stem in the tú form, e→ie, giving "tienes". "Tengo" is the yo form and "tienen" is for ellos.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (ser) muy amable.
questions.explanation: The subject "Tú" needs the second-person singular of ser, which is "eres"; "somos", "es" and "son" belong to nosotros, usted/él and ustedes/ellos.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (estar) cansado.
questions.explanation: With the subject "Tú", estar takes the ending -s: "estás". "está" is for él/usted, "estoy" for yo and "estamos" for nosotros.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (ir) a la escuela.
questions.explanation: The irregular verb ir uses "vas" for "tú"; "voy" is yo, "va" is él/usted and "van" is ustedes/ellos.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (hacer) la tarea.
questions.explanation: Hacer is irregular only in the yo form; for "tú" it follows the regular -er pattern, stem hac- plus -es, giving "haces". "Hago" is yo, "hacen" ustedes/ellos and "hacemos" nosotros.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (querer) un café.
questions.explanation: Querer changes e to ie in the stem and takes -es for "tú": "quieres". "quiere" is él/usted and "quieren" is ustedes/ellos.
questions.example: ¿Tú quieres un café?

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (poder) ayudarme.
questions.explanation: Poder changes o to ue and takes -es for "tú", giving "puedes"; "puedo" is yo, "puede" is él/usted and "podemos" is nosotros.
questions.meaning: you can, you are able to

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (saber) la respuesta.
questions.explanation: Saber is regular for "tú": stem plus -es gives "sabes". "sé" is only the yo form, and "sabe"/"sabemos" belong to other subjects.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (tomar) el autobús.
questions.explanation: Regular -ar verbs end in -as for "tú", so tomar becomes "tomas"; "tomo" is yo, "toma" is él/usted and "toman" is ustedes/ellos.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (ver) la película.
questions.explanation: Ver takes -s for "tú", giving "ves" (no accent, one syllable); "veo" is yo, "ven" is ustedes/ellos and "vemos" is nosotros.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (venir) a la fiesta.
questions.explanation: Venir changes e to ie and takes -es for "tú": "vienes". "viene" is él/usted, "vienen" ustedes/ellos and "venimos" nosotros.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (decir) la verdad.
questions.explanation: Decir changes e to i in the stem and takes -es for "tú", giving "dices"; "digo" is yo, "dice" is él/usted and "decimos" is nosotros.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (dormir) bien.
questions.explanation: Dormir changes o to ue and takes -es for "tú": "duermes". "duermo" is yo, "duerme" is él/usted and "duermen" is ustedes/ellos.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (beber) agua.
questions.explanation: The subject "Tú" takes the -es ending for -er verbs, so beber becomes "bebes". "bebo" is for yo, "beben" for ellos, "bebemos" for nosotros.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (leer) el periódico.
questions.explanation: With "Tú", the -er verb leer takes the -es ending, giving "lees". "lee" is for él/ella and "leen" for ellos.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (escribir) una carta.
questions.explanation: The subject "Tú" requires the -ir verb escribir to end in -es, giving "escribes". "escribe" is for él/ella and "escribo" for yo.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (jugar) al fútbol.
questions.explanation: Jugar changes u to ue in the stem (juego, juegas), and "Tú" takes -s, so the form is "juegas". "juega" is for él/ella and "juegan" for ellos.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (trabajar) mucho.
questions.explanation: The subject "Tú" takes the -as ending for -ar verbs, so trabajar becomes "trabajas". "trabajo" is for yo and "trabaja" for él/ella.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (estudiar) español.
questions.explanation: With "Tú", the -ar verb estudiar takes -as, giving "estudias". "estudia" is for él/ella and "estudio" for yo.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (llegar) tarde.
questions.explanation: The subject "Tú" calls for the -as ending on the -ar verb llegar, so it is "llegas". "llega" is for él/ella and "llegan" for ellos.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (empezar) el proyecto.
questions.explanation: Empezar changes e to ie in the stem, and "Tú" takes -s, giving "empiezas". "empezamos" (nosotros) keeps the plain stem.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (pedir) ayuda.
questions.explanation: Pedir changes e to i in the stem, and "Tú" takes -es, giving "pides". "pide" is for él/ella and "pido" for yo.

units.title: Shopping & Money
units.description: At the store — Shopping and money vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "money" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "dinero" is money in general; "moneda" is a coin (or a currency) and "cambio" is change.

questions.prompt: How do you say "price" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Price is "precio" (el precio), as in "¿Cuál es el precio?". Do not confuse it with "factura", the bill or invoice, or "dinero", money.

questions.prompt: How do you say "expensive" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Expensive is "caro", which changes to cara, caros or caras to agree with the noun. Its opposite, barato, means cheap.

questions.prompt: How do you say "cheap" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "barato" means cheap (low in price); its opposite is "caro" (expensive).

questions.prompt: How do you say "cashier" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cajero" is the person who takes your payment at the register (a woman is a "cajera").

questions.prompt: How do you say "to buy" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "comprar" means to buy; "pagar" is to pay, "costar" is to cost and "cobrar" is to charge.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to sell" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "vender" means to sell; it is the opposite of "comprar" (to buy).

questions.prompt: How do you say "cash" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "efectivo" is cash (bills and coins), as in "pagar en efectivo"; "cambio" is change and "moneda" is a coin.

questions.prompt: How do you say "credit card" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "tarjeta de crédito" is a credit card, as in "pagar con tarjeta de crédito"; "recibo" is a receipt.

questions.prompt: How do you say "receipt" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "recibo" is the receipt you get after paying, as in "¿Me da el recibo?"

questions.prompt: How do you say "discount" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "descuento" is a discount (a lower price); "factura" is an invoice or bill.

questions.prompt: How do you say "size" (of clothes) in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "talla" is the size of clothes, as in "¿Qué talla usa?"; for the general size of an object, Spanish uses "tamaño".

questions.prompt: How do you say "change (money)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cambio" is the money you get back when you pay more than the price, as in "Aquí tiene su cambio." "Precio" is the price and "descuento" is a discount.

questions.prompt: How do you say "wallet" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cartera" is the wallet where you keep money and cards; in much of Latin America people also say "billetera", and in some countries "cartera" means a handbag.

questions.prompt: How do you say "free (no cost)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "gratis" means free of charge and never changes its ending, as in "La entrada es gratis." "Caro" means expensive and "pagado" means paid.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sale" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "rebaja" is a sale where a shop lowers its prices, as in "Hay rebajas en enero." "Recibo" is a receipt and "factura" is an invoice.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to pay" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "pagar" means to pay, as in "Voy a pagar con tarjeta." "Comprar" is to buy, "gastar" is to spend and "ahorrar" is to save.

questions.prompt: How do you say "customer" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cliente" is the person who buys in a shop or restaurant, as in "El cliente paga en la caja." "Precio" is price and "cartera" is wallet.

questions.prompt: How do you say "bill (invoice)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "factura" is the invoice or bill you get for a purchase or a service; a banknote is a "billete", and "moneda" is a coin.

questions.prompt: How do you say "coin" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A coin is "moneda" (la moneda). "Cambio" is the change you get back, "dinero" is money in general and "efectivo" is cash.

units.title: Hobbies & Free Time
units.description: What do you like to do? — Hobbies and leisure-activity vocabulary.

lessons.title: Hobbies & Free Time 1
lessons.subtitle: What do you like to do?

questions.prompt: How do you say "to read" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: To read is "leer", as in "Me gusta leer novelas". Its yo form is leo.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to swim" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: To swim is "nadar", as in "Nado en la piscina los sábados". A swimming pool is la piscina, or la alberca in Mexico.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to dance" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: To dance is "bailar", as in "Me gusta bailar salsa". A dance is el baile.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to sing" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: To sing is "cantar", as in "Ella canta muy bien". A song is la canción.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to paint" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "pintar" means to paint, as in "Me gusta pintar paisajes." "Correr" is to run, "nadar" is to swim and "acampar" is to camp.

lessons.title: Hobbies & Free Time 2
lessons.subtitle: What do you like to do?

questions.prompt: How do you say "to cook" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: To cook is "cocinar", as in "Mi papá cocina los domingos". Be careful not to mix it up with caminar, which means to walk.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to travel" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: To travel is "viajar", as in "Quiero viajar a Perú". A trip is el viaje.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to run" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "correr" means to run, as in "Corro en el parque." "Cocinar" is to cook, "pescar" is to fish and "leer" is to read.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to walk" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "caminar" means to walk, as in "Camino al trabajo." "Correr" is to run, so it is faster than walking.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to draw" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "dibujar" means to draw pictures with a pencil or pen, as in "Mi hijo dibuja animales." "Cantar" is to sing and "nadar" is to swim.

lessons.title: Hobbies & Free Time 3
lessons.subtitle: What do you like to do?

questions.prompt: How do you say "music" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "música" means music and needs an accent on the first syllable, as in "Escucho música." "Película" is a movie and "fotografía" is photography.

questions.prompt: How do you say "movie" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "película" means "movie" (a film). The other words mean soccer (fútbol), garden (jardín) and game (juego).

questions.prompt: How do you say "game" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "juego" means "game", as in a board game or video game. "deporte" means "sport", a different word.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sport" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "deporte" is the general word for "sport"; "fútbol" is only one particular sport.

questions.prompt: How do you say "soccer" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "fútbol" is the Spanish word for "soccer", the game Americans call soccer. American football is "fútbol americano".

lessons.title: Hobbies & Free Time 4
lessons.subtitle: What do you like to do?

questions.prompt: How do you say "guitar" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "guitarra" is the instrument "guitar". "música" is music in general, not the instrument.

questions.prompt: How do you say "photograph" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "fotografía" means "photograph" and also the hobby of photography. In speech it is often shortened to "foto".

questions.prompt: How do you say "garden" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "jardín" means "garden", for example the place where you do gardening. Remember the accent on the í.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to fish" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "pescar" means "to fish" (to catch fish). The other verbs mean to swim (nadar), to walk (caminar) and to sing (cantar).

questions.prompt: How do you say "to camp" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "acampar" means "to camp", to sleep outdoors in a tent; it comes from "campo" (countryside). The other verbs mean to fish, to draw and to paint.

units.title: Weather Expressions
units.description: hacer, estar, and weather — Common weather expressions using hacer/estar/haber.

questions.prompt: ___ calor hoy.
questions.explanation: Spanish describes weather with hacer, so heat is "Hace" calor. "Es" and "Está" do not work here, and "Tiene" is used for people (tengo calor).
questions.meaning: it is (weather: hace calor = it's hot)

questions.prompt: ___ frío en invierno.
questions.explanation: Weather uses the impersonal verb hacer, so cold is "Hace" frío. "Tiene" would describe a person, and "Es"/"Está" are not used for weather.

questions.prompt: ___ mucho viento.
questions.explanation: Wind is expressed with hacer, just like hace calor and hace frío, so the answer is "Hace" mucho viento. "Está", "Es" and "Tiene" are not used with viento.

questions.prompt: ___ sol esta tarde.
questions.explanation: Weather with sun, heat or cold uses "Hace" (hacer): Hace sol means it is sunny. Tiene, Está and Es do not describe the weather this way.

questions.prompt: Está ___ (raining) ahora.
questions.explanation: Right now needs the present progressive: estar + gerund, so "lloviendo" (from llover) completes Está lloviendo. "Llueve" or "llover" cannot follow Está.

questions.prompt: Está ___ (snowing) en las montañas.
questions.explanation: After Está you need a gerund, and the clue is "snowing": "nevando" comes from nevar. "Lloviendo" means raining, and "nieva" or "nevar" are not gerunds.

questions.prompt: Está muy ___ (cloudy) hoy.
questions.explanation: After "Está muy" you need an adjective meaning cloudy: "nublado". "Despejado" means clear and "soleado" means sunny, while "nubes" is a noun and cannot follow muy.

questions.prompt: ___ niebla esta mañana.
questions.explanation: Fog is expressed with the impersonal "Hay" (there is): Hay niebla. Hace, Está and Es are not used with niebla.

questions.prompt: ___ buen tiempo hoy.
questions.explanation: The fixed weather phrase is hacer + buen/mal tiempo, so "Hace" buen tiempo means the weather is nice. Está, Tiene and Va do not work here.
questions.meaning: it is (weather: hace buen tiempo = nice weather)

questions.prompt: ___ mal tiempo este fin de semana.
questions.explanation: Spanish says the weather is bad with hacer: "Hace" mal tiempo. Tiene, Va and Está cannot take tiempo in this meaning.

questions.prompt: La temperatura ___ de veinte grados.
questions.explanation: To state a measured value we use ser with de: La temperatura "es" de veinte grados. Hace and Hay describe weather conditions, not the temperature as a subject.

questions.prompt: ___ humedad hoy.
questions.explanation: Humidity is expressed with impersonal "Hay" (there is): Hay humedad. Está, Es and Tiene do not fit with humedad.

questions.prompt: En verano ___ mucho calor.
questions.explanation: Heat uses the weather idiom hacer calor, so "hace" mucho calor means it is very hot. Tiene or está would describe a person or thing, not the weather.
questions.meaning: it is (weather: hace calor = it's hot)

questions.prompt: En invierno ___ mucho frío.
questions.explanation: Cold weather uses hacer frío, so "hace" mucho frío means it is very cold. Es, está and tiene do not describe the weather this way.

questions.prompt: A veces ___ tormentas fuertes.
questions.explanation: Storms are things that exist or occur, so Spanish uses impersonal "hay" (there are): hay tormentas. Es, está and hace do not take tormentas.

units.title: Restaurant Phrases
units.description: Ordering food — Common restaurant phrases.

questions.prompt: How do you say "I would like..." in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Quisiera..." is a soft, polite form of querer, used for ordering, as in "Quisiera un café, por favor". The other options ask about service, takeaway and vegetarian food.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Could I have the menu?" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¿Me da el menú?" literally means 'Will you give me the menu?', a polite everyday way to ask the waiter for it. You can also say "la carta".

questions.prompt: How do you say "What do you recommend?" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¿Qué me recomienda?" uses the usted form, recomienda, because you are speaking politely to a waiter. With a friend you would say ¿Qué me recomiendas?

questions.prompt: How do you say "I'm allergic to..." in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Soy alérgico a..." means 'I'm allergic to...'; it uses ser because an allergy is a permanent trait. A woman says "alérgica".

questions.prompt: How do you say "The check, please" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "La cuenta, por favor" is how you ask for the bill: "la cuenta" means "the check", and "por favor" means "please".

questions.prompt: How do you say "Is service included?" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¿Está incluido el servicio?" uses "estar" + "incluido" to ask whether service (the tip) is already included in the bill.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Table for two, please" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Mesa para dos, por favor" is what you say when you arrive: "mesa" means "table" and "para dos" means "for two".

questions.prompt: How do you say "I'll have the same" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Yo quiero lo mismo" means 'I want the same', used to order what the other person just ordered. The "yo" stresses 'me too'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "It was delicious" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Estaba delicioso" uses the past form "estaba" ("it was") because you are describing a meal you have just finished.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Can I get this to go?" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¿Me lo da para llevar?" asks for your food to go: "para llevar" means "to take away", and "me lo da" (usted) keeps it polite with the server.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Do you have vegetarian options?" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¿Tienen opciones vegetarianas?" uses "tienen" (ustedes) because you are asking the restaurant and its staff, not one person.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Enjoy your meal" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Buen provecho" is the fixed phrase you say to someone who is about to eat or is eating, like "Enjoy your meal".

questions.prompt: How do you say "Is this dish spicy?" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¿Este plato es picante?" uses "picante" for chili-hot food and "es" because spiciness is a feature of the dish.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Water, please" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Agua, por favor" is the simplest polite way to order: name the item, "agua" (water), then add "por favor".

questions.prompt: How do you say "Nothing else, thanks" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Nada más, gracias" literally means "nothing more, thanks" and tells the server you don't want anything else; "Un poco más" would ask for more.

units.title: At the Doctor
units.description: Health and illness — Health and doctor's-visit vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "doctor's office" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "consultorio" is the room or office where a doctor sees patients; "farmacia" is where you buy medicine.

questions.prompt: How do you say "appointment" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cita" is a scheduled appointment, as in "Tengo una cita con el doctor"; "receta" is a prescription.

questions.prompt: How do you say "symptom" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "síntoma" is a sign of illness, like fever or cough; note the written accent on the i, because the stress falls on the first syllable (SÍN-to-ma).

questions.prompt: How do you say "fever" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "fiebre" means a high body temperature, as in "Tengo fiebre"; "tos" is a cough.

questions.prompt: How do you say "headache" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "dolor de cabeza" literally means "pain of head"; Spanish names aches with "dolor de" plus the body part.

questions.prompt: How do you say "cough" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "tos" is the noun for a cough, used with tener: "Tengo tos" means "I have a cough".

questions.prompt: How do you say "medicine" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "medicina" is the everyday word for medicine you take when you are sick; it looks like the English word but ends in -a.

questions.prompt: How do you say "prescription" (from the doctor) in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A doctor's prescription is a "receta"; the same word also means a cooking recipe, so context tells you which one is meant.

questions.prompt: How do you say "pharmacy" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "farmacia" is the shop where you buy medicine; a "consultorio" is the doctor's office, not a pharmacy.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sick" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "enfermo" means "sick" or "ill"; "herido" means "injured" and "débil" means "weak", so they describe different conditions.

questions.prompt: How do you say "healthy" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "sano" means "healthy", the opposite of sick; "cansado" means "tired" and "débil" means "weak".

questions.prompt: How do you say "injury" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "lesión" means an injury, such as a sprain or a hurt knee; note the written accent on the last syllable.

questions.prompt: How do you say "allergy" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "alergia" is the Spanish word for "allergy"; it is spelled with a g, and the word is feminine ("la alergia").

questions.prompt: How do you say "nurse (female)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "enfermera" ends in -a because the nurse is female; a male nurse is "enfermero".

questions.prompt: How do you say "patient" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "paciente" is the person a doctor treats; the same form is used for men and women ("el paciente", "la paciente").

units.title: Clothing & Shopping
units.description: Trying things on — Clothes-shopping phrases and vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "fitting room" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: The "probador" is the room where you try on clothes; it comes from "probarse", to try on.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Can I try this on?" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¿Puedo probarme esto?" uses "probarme" ("to try on myself") after "puedo" ("can I") to ask to try on the item.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Do you have a smaller size?" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Más pequeña" means smaller ("más grande" means bigger), so "¿Tiene una talla más pequeña?" asks for a smaller size.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Do you have a bigger size?" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Talla" is clothing size and "más grande" means bigger, so "¿Tiene una talla más grande?" asks the clerk for a bigger size.

questions.prompt: How do you say "It fits well" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Queda" describes how clothes fit you, and "bien" means well, so "Me queda bien" means it fits well.

questions.prompt: How do you say "It's too tight" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Apretado" means tight ("flojo" means loose), so "Me queda apretado" says the item fits you too tightly.

questions.prompt: How do you say "It's too loose" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Flojo" means loose (the opposite of "apretado", tight), so "Me queda flojo" says it is too loose on you.

questions.prompt: How do you say "What size do you wear?" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Usar" means to wear here, and a clerk speaks to a customer with usted, so the question is "¿Qué talla usa?".

questions.prompt: How do you say "I'm just looking" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Solo" means just and "estoy mirando" means I am looking, so "Solo estoy mirando" tells a clerk you are only browsing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Where are the fitting rooms?" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¿Dónde están los probadores?" uses "están" because it asks where things are located, and "los probadores" are the fitting rooms in a clothes shop.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Does it come in another color?" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¿Viene en otro color?" uses "venir en" (to come in) plus "otro color" (another color, with no article) to ask whether the item is available in a different color.

questions.prompt: How do you say "I'll take it" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Me lo llevo" literally means "I take it with me". Shoppers use "llevarse" with "lo" (it) to say they will buy the item.

questions.prompt: How do you say "How much does it cost?" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¿Cuánto cuesta?" combines "cuánto" (how much), with its accent because it is a question word, and "cuesta" from "costar" (to cost) to ask the price of one item.

questions.prompt: How do you say "It's on sale" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Está de rebaja" uses "estar" for the item's current state and "rebaja" (discount) to say it is on sale. You will also hear "está en oferta" in Latin America.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Do you accept cards?" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¿Aceptan tarjetas?" uses the "ustedes" form "aceptan" because you are asking the store, meaning its staff, whether they take card payments.

units.title: Places in the City II
units.description: More around town — More places found around a city.

questions.prompt: How do you say "post office" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "oficina de correos" means post office, since "correos" refers to the mail service. In much of Latin America people also just say "el correo".

questions.prompt: How do you say "clinic" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "clínica" is the Spanish word for clinic. It is feminine ("la clínica") and has an accent on the first "i".

questions.prompt: How do you say "supermarket" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "supermercado" is "super" plus "mercado" (market), the large store where you buy groceries, while "panadería" only sells bread.

questions.prompt: How do you say "library" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "biblioteca" is the place where you borrow books. Don't confuse it with "librería", which is a bookstore.

questions.prompt: How do you say "museum" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "museo" means museum and is masculine ("el museo"), like most Spanish nouns ending in -o.

questions.prompt: How do you say "theater" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "teatro" is a cognate of theater: same meaning, Spanish spelling with a final -o.

questions.prompt: How do you say "gym" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: English "gym" is short for gymnasium, and Spanish uses the full word, "gimnasio".

questions.prompt: How do you say "hotel" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Spanish uses the same word, "hotel", but the h is silent: say it like "o-TEL".

questions.prompt: How do you say "restaurant" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A restaurant is "restaurante" in Spanish, with an extra -e at the end and the stress on "-RAN-".

questions.prompt: How do you say "bakery" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "panadería" comes from "pan" (bread) plus the ending "-ería", which names a shop, so it is the place that sells bread.

questions.prompt: How do you say "bookstore" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A bookstore, where you buy books, is a "librería". Don't confuse it with "biblioteca", which means library, where you borrow books.

questions.prompt: How do you say "gas station" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A gas station is a "gasolinera", the place where you buy gasolina (gas). Some countries also say "estación de servicio".

questions.prompt: How do you say "police station" in Spanish?
