questions.explanation: A police station is "comisaría", the place where you go to report a crime; in some countries you will also hear "estación de policía".

questions.prompt: How do you say "town hall" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Town hall is "ayuntamiento", the city government and its building. In much of Latin America you will also hear "municipalidad", "alcaldía" or "palacio municipal".

questions.prompt: How do you say "courthouse" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A courthouse building is often called "palacio de justicia"; the court itself is usually called "juzgado".

units.title: Technology & Devices
units.description: Everyday tech vocabulary — Common technology vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "phone" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Phone is "teléfono". Note the accent on the second e. A cell phone is a "teléfono celular", or just "celular", in Latin America.

questions.prompt: How do you say "computer" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: In Latin America a computer is "computadora"; in Spain people say "ordenador".

questions.prompt: How do you say "internet" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Spanish also says "internet", usually without an article and with the stress at the end: "Busco información en internet".

questions.prompt: How do you say "email" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Email is "correo electrónico", literally "electronic mail". In everyday speech people often shorten it to "correo".

questions.prompt: How do you say "password" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Password is "contraseña", the secret word you type to log in. Remember the ñ.

questions.prompt: How do you say "screen" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Screen is "pantalla", the part of a phone, computer or TV where you see images.

questions.prompt: How do you say "keyboard" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Keyboard is "teclado", from "tecla" (key), because it is the set of keys you type on.

questions.prompt: How do you say "mouse (device)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: The computer mouse is "ratón", the same word as the animal. In much of Latin America people also just say "mouse".

questions.prompt: How do you say "application" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Application is "aplicación", with an accent on the ó. For phone apps people often shorten it to "app".

questions.prompt: How do you say "charger" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Charger is "cargador", from the verb "cargar" (to charge), so it is the thing that charges your device.

questions.prompt: How do you say "battery" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: The battery of a phone or laptop is "batería". Small disposable batteries are usually called "pilas".

questions.prompt: How do you say "wifi" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Spanish uses "wifi" too, often pronounced "GÜI-fi" and used with "el" or "la": "¿Hay wifi aquí?".

questions.prompt: How do you say "file" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A computer "file" is "archivo" in Latin America (Spain also says "fichero"); "ratón" is the mouse, not a file.

questions.prompt: How do you say "video call" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "videollamada" joins "video" and "llamada" (call) into one word, so it means a video call; "teclado" is a keyboard.

questions.prompt: How do you say "a download" (noun) in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: The noun "a download" is "descarga"; the verb "to download" is "descargar".

units.title: Frequency Adverbs
units.description: How often? — Adverbs of frequency for describing routines.

questions.prompt: How do you say "always" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "siempre" means always, every time; "nunca" is its opposite (never), and "a veces" means only sometimes.

questions.prompt: How do you say "usually" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Usually" is "generalmente", which describes what you do most of the time; "normalmente" means the same thing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "often" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "a menudo" means often, many times; "a veces" is less frequent (sometimes), and "siempre" is always.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sometimes" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "a veces" means sometimes; don't confuse it with "otra vez", which means again.

questions.prompt: How do you say "rarely" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Rarely" is "raramente", for things that almost never happen; don't confuse it with "generalmente", which means usually.

questions.prompt: How do you say "never" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "nunca" means never, not even once; "siempre" is the opposite (always).

questions.prompt: How do you say "every day" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "todos los días" is literally "all the days", which is how Spanish says every day.

questions.prompt: How do you say "once a week" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "una vez a la semana" is literally "one time to the week": "vez" counts the times and "a la semana" means per week.

questions.prompt: How do you say "from time to time" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "de vez en cuando" means from time to time, now and then; "otra vez" means again.

questions.prompt: How do you say "again" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Again" (one more time) is "otra vez"; it is not a routine word like "a menudo" (often).

units.title: Ir a + Infinitive
units.description: Near future tense — "Ir a + infinitive" for talking about the near future.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (ir) a estudiar esta noche.
questions.explanation: The subject "Yo" takes the first-person form of ir, "voy", and it is followed by a + infinitive to talk about the near future.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (ir) a llamar a tu madre.
questions.explanation: The subject "Tú" takes the second-person singular form of ir, "vas", before a + infinitive ("vas a llamar").

questions.prompt: Ella ___ (ir) a viajar mañana.
questions.explanation: The subject "Ella" is third-person singular, so ir becomes "va" before a + infinitive ("va a viajar").

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (ir) a comer pronto.
questions.explanation: The subject "Nosotros" takes the we-form of ir, "vamos", before a + infinitive ("vamos a comer").

questions.prompt: Ellos ___ (ir) a llegar tarde.
questions.explanation: The subject "Ellos" is third-person plural, so ir becomes "van" before a + infinitive ("van a llegar").

questions.prompt: Yo voy a ___ (to buy) un regalo.
questions.explanation: After "voy a" the verb must stay in the infinitive, so "to buy" is "comprar", not a conjugated or -ado/-ando form.

questions.prompt: Tú vas a ___ (to visit) a tus abuelos.
questions.explanation: After "vas a" Spanish uses the bare infinitive, so "to visit" is "visitar".

questions.prompt: Ella va a ___ (to start) un nuevo trabajo.
questions.explanation: After "va a" the next verb is an infinitive, so "to start" is "empezar", not a conjugated form.

questions.prompt: Nosotros vamos a ___ (to see) una película.
questions.explanation: After "vamos a" you need the infinitive, so "to see" is "ver".

questions.prompt: Ellos van a ___ (to have, to hold) una fiesta.
questions.explanation: After "van a" you need an infinitive, and the natural verb for throwing a party is "hacer" (hacer una fiesta).

questions.prompt: ¿___ (ir) tú a venir con nosotros?
questions.explanation: The subject "tú" takes the second-person form of ir, "Vas", which starts the question "¿Vas a venir...?"
questions.example: ¿Vas a venir con nosotros?

questions.prompt: Yo no ___ (ir) a poder ir.
questions.explanation: The subject "Yo" takes "voy", and "no voy a poder" means 'I am not going to be able to'.

questions.prompt: Nosotros vamos a ___ (to leave) temprano.
questions.explanation: After "vamos a" the verb must be an infinitive, so the future plan is "salir"; the other forms are conjugated or participle forms that cannot follow "ir a".

questions.prompt: Ella va a ___ (to call) más tarde.
questions.explanation: The near future is built as "va a" plus an infinitive, so "llamar" is needed after "va a" to say she will call later.

questions.prompt: Ellos van a ___ (to study) juntos.
questions.explanation: "van a" must be followed by an infinitive, so "estudiar" completes the plan to study together; conjugated forms and participles do not work here.

units.title: Possessive Adjectives
units.description: my, your, his, her... — Possessive adjectives agreeing with the noun they modify.

questions.prompt: Este es ___ (my) libro.
questions.explanation: "libro" is masculine singular and the clue says 'my', so the singular possessive "mi" is needed; "mis" is plural and "nuestra" means 'our'.

questions.prompt: Esta es ___ (your, informal) casa.
questions.explanation: The clue says informal 'your', which is "tu" before a singular noun like "casa"; "tus" is plural, and "su" would be formal or 'his/her'.

questions.prompt: Ese es ___ (his) coche.
questions.explanation: 'His' before the singular noun "coche" is "su"; "sus" is for plural nouns and "suya" is a form used after the noun.

questions.prompt: Esa es ___ (her) mochila.
questions.explanation: 'Her' before the singular noun "mochila" is "su"; "mi" means 'my', "mis" is plural and "nuestra" means 'our'.

questions.prompt: Estos son ___ (our) amigos.
questions.explanation: 'Our' with the masculine plural noun "amigos" must be "nuestros", agreeing in gender and number with the noun.

questions.prompt: Esas son ___ (their) ideas.
questions.explanation: 'Their' with the plural noun "ideas" is "sus"; the possessive agrees in number with the thing owned, so singular "su" is wrong here.

questions.prompt: ___ (my) padres viven aquí.
questions.explanation: 'My' before the plural noun "padres" is "Mis", capitalized because it starts the sentence; "tu" and "su" do not mean 'my'.

questions.prompt: ¿Dónde está ___ (your, formal) oficina?
questions.explanation: The clue says formal 'your' (usted), which is "su" before the singular noun "oficina"; "tu" is informal and "mi" means 'my'.

questions.prompt: ___ (our) casa es grande.
questions.explanation: 'Our' before the feminine singular noun "casa" is "Nuestra", capitalized because it starts the sentence.

questions.prompt: Ellos perdieron ___ (their) llaves.
questions.explanation: The possessive must agree in number with the thing owned, and "llaves" is plural, so the plural form "sus" is needed for 'their keys'. 'Su' is singular and 'tu' means 'your'.

questions.prompt: Ella olvidó ___ (her) teléfono.
questions.explanation: 'Her' phone is one thing owned by a third person, so Spanish uses "su" before "teléfono"; "sus" is plural, "tu" means 'your' and "nuestro" means 'our'.

questions.prompt: Nosotros amamos ___ (our) ciudad.
questions.explanation: 'Our' is nuestro, and it agrees with "ciudad", which is feminine singular, so the form is "nuestra"; "nuestro" is masculine and "nuestros" is plural.

questions.prompt: ¿Son ___ (yours, informal) estas llaves?
questions.explanation: After ser, Spanish uses the long possessive, and it agrees with "llaves" (feminine plural), so informal "yours" is "tuyas".

questions.prompt: Ese perro es ___ (mine).
questions.explanation: After 'ser' the long possessive form is used, and 'mine' for masculine singular "perro" is "mío". 'Tuyas' is feminine plural and means 'yours'.

questions.prompt: Esa idea fue ___ (his).
questions.explanation: After 'ser' the long possessive form is used, and it must agree with "idea" (feminine singular), so 'his' becomes "suya". 'Sus' and 'mi' are short forms that only go before a noun.

units.title: Common Irregular Verbs
units.description: Yo-form irregulars — Verbs with an irregular "yo" form in the present tense.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (poner) la mesa todos los días.
questions.explanation: With 'yo', the verb 'poner' has an irregular present form that adds a g: "pongo". The other options belong to él, nosotros and tú.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (salir) de casa a las ocho.
questions.explanation: With 'yo', the verb 'salir' adds a g in the present tense: "salgo". 'Sales', 'sale' and 'salen' go with tú, él and ellos.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (traer) el postre a la fiesta.
questions.explanation: With 'yo', the verb 'traer' has the irregular present form "traigo" (with ig). The other options belong to tú, ellos and nosotros.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (conducir) al trabajo.
questions.explanation: Verbs ending in -ducir change to -zco with 'yo', so 'conducir' becomes "conduzco". The other options are forms for él, nosotros and ellos.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (conocer) a mucha gente aquí.
questions.explanation: Verbs ending in a vowel + -cer change to -zco with 'yo', so 'conocer' becomes "conozco". The other options belong to él, nosotros and tú.

questions.prompt: Yo les ___ (caer) bien a mis compañeros.
questions.explanation: Caer has an irregular yo form with -ig-, so after "Yo" the verb is "caigo"; "Yo les caigo bien a mis compañeros" means 'My classmates like me'.
questions.example: A veces me caigo cuando corro muy rápido.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (valer) mucho para este equipo.
questions.explanation: Valer adds -g- in the yo form of the present tense, so with "Yo" the verb is "valgo".
questions.meaning: I am worth, I have value
questions.example: Yo valgo mucho para este equipo.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (hacer) ejercicio cada mañana.
questions.explanation: The subject "Yo" needs the irregular first-person form of hacer, which adds -g-: "hago". The other options are forms for él, ellos and nosotros.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (dar) consejos a mis amigos.
questions.explanation: Dar has an irregular "yo" form ending in -y: "doy". "Da", "das" and "damos" belong to él, tú and nosotros.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (ver) las noticias por la noche.
questions.explanation: For "yo", ver keeps its e before the -o ending, giving "veo" (not "vo"). "Ves", "ve" and "ven" are the tú, él and ellos forms.

units.title: Months & Seasons
units.description: The calendar — Months of the year and the four seasons.

questions.prompt: How do you say "January" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "enero" is January, the first month; like all Spanish months it is written with a lowercase letter.

questions.prompt: How do you say "February" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "febrero" is February, the second month; it is written in lowercase and spelled without the extra "u" of English.

questions.prompt: How do you say "March" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "marzo" is March, the third month; it is written in lowercase, and the z is pronounced like an s in Latin America.

questions.prompt: How do you say "April" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: April is "abril" in Spanish. Like every month name in Spanish, it is written with a lowercase letter.

questions.prompt: How do you say "May" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: May is "mayo" in Spanish. Note the -o ending, and remember that Spanish month names are not capitalized.

questions.prompt: How do you say "June" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: June → junio. Months of the year and the four seasons.

questions.prompt: How do you say "July" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: July is "julio" in Spanish. The j sounds like an English h, and it is easy to mix up with junio (June).

questions.prompt: How do you say "August" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: August is "agosto" in Spanish. It is written in lowercase, like all Spanish month names.

questions.prompt: How do you say "September" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: September is "septiembre" in Spanish. Some countries, such as Peru and Uruguay, also write it setiembre.

questions.prompt: How do you say "October" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: October is "octubre" in Spanish. It ends in -ubre, while the other autumn months end in -iembre (septiembre, noviembre).

questions.prompt: How do you say "November" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: November is "noviembre" in Spanish. It is spelled with a v and comes just before diciembre.

questions.prompt: How do you say "December" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: December is "diciembre" in Spanish. In Latin America the c before i sounds like an s.

questions.prompt: How do you say "spring" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Spring is "primavera" in Spanish; "verano" is summer, "invierno" is winter and "calendario" is calendar.

questions.prompt: How do you say "summer" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: summer → verano. Months of the year and the four seasons.

questions.prompt: How do you say "autumn" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Autumn (fall) is "otoño" in Spanish, written with ñ. Verano means summer.

questions.prompt: How do you say "winter" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Winter is "invierno" in Spanish, which is the opposite of verano (summer).

questions.prompt: How do you say "season" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Season is "estación" in Spanish. It is feminine (la estación) and can also mean a station.

questions.prompt: How do you say "calendar" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Calendar is "calendario" in Spanish, a masculine noun (el calendario). Siglo means century.

questions.prompt: How do you say "century" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: century → siglo. Months of the year and the four seasons.

questions.prompt: How do you say "decade" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: decade → década. Months of the year and the four seasons.

units.title: Weekend Activities
units.description: What do you do on weekends? — Common weekend and leisure activities.

lessons.title: Weekend Activities 1
lessons.subtitle: What do you do on weekends?

questions.prompt: How do you say "to relax" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: to relax → relajarse. Common weekend and leisure activities.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to sleep in" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: to sleep in → dormir hasta tarde. Common weekend and leisure activities.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to go shopping" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: to go shopping → ir de compras. Common weekend and leisure activities.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to visit friends" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: to visit friends → visitar a amigos. Common weekend and leisure activities.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to watch a movie" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: to watch a movie → ver una película. Common weekend and leisure activities.

lessons.title: Weekend Activities 2
lessons.subtitle: What do you do on weekends?

questions.prompt: How do you say "to go for a walk" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: to go for a walk → dar un paseo. Common weekend and leisure activities.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to clean the house" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Limpiar means "to clean" and la casa is "the house", so the phrase is "limpiar la casa".

questions.prompt: How do you say "to go to the gym" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Ir takes a for destination, and a + el gimnasio contracts to "ir al gimnasio".

questions.prompt: How do you say "to have a picnic" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Spanish uses hacer (to make/do), not tener, for this activity, so "to have a picnic" is "hacer un picnic".

questions.prompt: How do you say "to go out to eat" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Salir means "to go out", and a + infinitive gives the purpose, so "to go out to eat" is "salir a comer".

lessons.title: Weekend Activities 3
lessons.subtitle: What do you do on weekends?

questions.prompt: How do you say "to go to bed late" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Acostarse is the reflexive verb for "to go to bed" and tarde means "late", so the phrase is "acostarse tarde".

questions.prompt: How do you say "to do nothing" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Spanish needs a double negative here: "no hacer nada" is literally 'not do nothing', with no before the verb and nada after it.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to read a book" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "leer un libro" is the verb leer (to read) plus un libro (a book); libro is masculine, so it takes un.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to cook a big meal" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cocinar una gran comida" is cocinar (to cook) plus una gran comida (a big meal); grande shortens to gran before a singular noun.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to go to the beach" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ir a la playa" uses ir (to go) with the preposition a for the destination; playa is feminine, so it is la playa.

units.title: Household Appliances
units.description: Around the house — Home appliances and cleaning tools.

questions.prompt: How do you say "refrigerator" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "refrigerador" is the fridge, the appliance that keeps food cold; you will also hear nevera in Colombia and the Caribbean and heladera in Argentina.

questions.prompt: How do you say "stove" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "estufa" is the stove you cook on in Mexico and Central America; in Argentina or Chile people say cocina, and estufa there means a heater.

questions.prompt: How do you say "oven" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "horno" is the oven, the appliance you bake or roast food in; it is masculine, el horno.

questions.prompt: How do you say "microwave" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: microwave → microondas. Home appliances and cleaning tools.

questions.prompt: How do you say "washing machine" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: washing machine → lavadora. Home appliances and cleaning tools.

questions.prompt: How do you say "dryer" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: dryer → secadora. Home appliances and cleaning tools.

questions.prompt: How do you say "dishwasher" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: dishwasher → lavavajillas. Home appliances and cleaning tools.

questions.prompt: How do you say "vacuum cleaner" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A vacuum cleaner is "aspiradora" (feminine: la aspiradora), from aspirar, 'to suck in'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "iron" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A clothes iron is "plancha" (la plancha), and 'to iron' is planchar.

questions.prompt: How do you say "blender" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: In Latin America a blender is "licuadora" (la licuadora), from licuar, 'to liquefy'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "toaster" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A toaster is "tostadora" (la tostadora), the machine that makes pan tostado, 'toast'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "fan" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: An electric fan is "ventilador" (el ventilador), related to ventilar, 'to air out'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "air conditioner" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: An air conditioner is "aire acondicionado" (el aire acondicionado), literally 'conditioned air'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "heater" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A room heater is "calefactor" (el calefactor); in some countries people also say calentador or estufa.

questions.prompt: How do you say "coffee maker" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cafetera" comes from café (coffee) and is the machine that makes coffee.

questions.prompt: How do you say "mop" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "trapeador" is the mop for cleaning floors, from trapear (to mop); in Colombia you will also hear trapero.

questions.prompt: How do you say "broom" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A broom is "escoba" (la escoba), and 'to sweep' is barrer.

questions.prompt: How do you say "bucket" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: bucket → cubo. Home appliances and cleaning tools.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sponge" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A sponge is "esponja" (la esponja), a close cognate of the English word.

questions.prompt: How do you say "detergent" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Detergent is "detergente" (el detergente), almost the same as the English word.

questions.prompt: How do you say "hanger" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "percha" is the hanger you hang clothes on; in Mexico people usually say gancho.

questions.prompt: How do you say "drawer" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A drawer is "cajón" (el cajón), with an accent on the o; it comes from caja, 'box'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "shelf" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A shelf is "estante" (el estante); in Latin America a single wall shelf is also often called repisa.

questions.prompt: How do you say "closet" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: closet → armario. Home appliances and cleaning tools.

questions.prompt: How do you say "curtain" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: curtain → cortina. Home appliances and cleaning tools.

units.title: Emotions & Feelings
units.description: ponerse / sentirse + adjective — "Ponerse" and "sentirse" with emotion adjectives.

questions.prompt: Ella se pone ___ (nervous) antes de un examen.
questions.explanation: The clue "(nervous)" points to "nerviosa", and it is feminine to agree with the subject "Ella" after "se pone". The other words mean curious, bored and angry.

questions.prompt: Yo me siento ___ (happy) hoy.
questions.explanation: The clue "(happy)" gives "feliz", which works for any speaker after "me siento". The other options mean nervous, embarrassed and bored.

questions.prompt: Nos ponemos ___ (sad) cuando llueve.
questions.explanation: "Nos ponemos" has a plural subject, and the clue "(sad)" gives "tristes". The other plural options mean excited, calm and jealous.

questions.prompt: Él se siente ___ (tired) después del trabajo.
questions.explanation: The clue "(tired)" gives "cansado", masculine singular to agree with "Él". "Relajado", "triste" and "emocionado" mean relaxed, sad and excited.

questions.prompt: Te pones ___ (angry) fácilmente.
questions.explanation: The clue "(angry)" gives "enojado", masculine singular after "Te pones". The others mean sure, nervous and happy.

questions.prompt: Me siento ___ (confused) con esta pregunta.
questions.explanation: The clue "(confused)" gives "confundido" after "Me siento". The others mean angry, sad and grateful.

questions.prompt: Se ponen ___ (excited) antes del viaje.
questions.explanation: "Se ponen" has a plural subject, and the clue "(excited)" gives "emocionados". The others mean impatient, sad and relaxed.

questions.prompt: Nos sentimos ___ (proud) de nuestro equipo.
questions.explanation: "Nos sentimos" takes a plural adjective, and the clue "(proud)" gives "orgullosos". The others mean bored, excited and curious.

questions.prompt: Te sientes ___ (nervous) por la entrevista.
questions.explanation: "nervioso" means nervous, as the clue says, and agrees with the singular "te sientes" (one person, masculine). The other options are other feelings or are plural.

questions.prompt: Ella se pone ___ (worried) cuando no la llamas.
questions.explanation: The clue says worried, which is "preocupada"; it is feminine singular to agree with "ella". The other options mean excited, motivated and calm.
questions.example: Ella se siente preocupada cuando no la llamas.

questions.prompt: Me siento ___ (relaxed) en la playa.
questions.explanation: The clue says relaxed, which is "relajado"; it is singular to agree with the speaker in "me siento". The other options mean excited, motivated and tired.

questions.prompt: Se sienten ___ (surprised) por la noticia.
questions.explanation: The clue says surprised, which is "sorprendidos"; it is plural because "se sienten" refers to more than one person. The others mean tired, relaxed and confident.

questions.prompt: Te pones ___ (sad) cuando pierdes.
questions.explanation: The clue says sad, which is "triste", and it is singular like "te pones". The others mean disappointed, embarrassed and angry.

questions.prompt: Nos ponemos ___ (happy) en las fiestas.
questions.explanation: "Nos ponemos" has a plural subject (we), so happy must be plural: "felices". "Feliz" is singular, and the others mean calm and nervous.

questions.prompt: Se siente ___ (bored) los domingos.
questions.explanation: The clue says bored, which is "aburrido", and it is singular to agree with "se siente". The others mean angry, surprised and grateful.

questions.prompt: Me pongo ___ (embarrassed) fácilmente.
questions.explanation: The clue says embarrassed, which is "avergonzado", singular to match "me pongo". The other words mean proud, confident and nervous.
questions.example: Me siento avergonzado cuando hablo en público.

questions.prompt: Él se siente ___ (calm) antes de dormir.
questions.explanation: "tranquilo" means calm, as the clue says, and is masculine singular for "él se siente". "Felices" and "emocionados" are plural, and "curioso" means curious.

questions.prompt: Ellas se ponen ___ (excited) con la música.
questions.explanation: "ellas" is feminine plural, so the adjective must be "emocionadas" (excited, as the clue says). "Preocupada" and "impaciente" are singular, and "tristes" means sad.

questions.prompt: Te sientes ___ (confident) hoy.
questions.explanation: The clue says confident, which is "seguro" with "te sientes". The other options mean nervous, proud and bored.
questions.example: Hoy me siento muy seguro.

questions.prompt: Nos sentimos ___ (grateful) por su ayuda.
questions.explanation: "nos sentimos" has a plural subject (we), and "agradecidos" (grateful, as the clue says) is the plural form that fits. "Feliz" and "seguro" are singular.

questions.prompt: Se pone ___ (impatient) en las filas.
questions.explanation: The clue says impatient, which is "impaciente"; "se pone" refers to one person (he or she), and "impaciente" has the same form for both genders. The others mean surprised, angry and disappointed.

questions.prompt: Me siento ___ (curious) sobre esto.
questions.explanation: The clue says 'curious', and "curioso" is the only option with that meaning; it is masculine singular, agreeing with "Me siento" (I feel).
questions.example: Mi hijo es muy curioso y siempre pregunta todo.

questions.prompt: Se sienten ___ (disappointed) con el resultado.
questions.explanation: "Se sienten" has a plural subject (they), so the adjective must be plural: "decepcionados" means 'disappointed' and is the only plural option matching the clue.

questions.prompt: Te pones ___ (jealous) a veces.
questions.explanation: The clue says jealous, which is "celoso" after "te pones". The other options mean excited, relaxed and nervous.

questions.prompt: Nos sentimos ___ (motivated) para empezar.
questions.explanation: "Nos sentimos" (we feel) needs a plural adjective, and the clue says 'motivated': "motivados" is the only plural option that fits.

units.title: Banking & Post Office
units.description: Money and mail — Banking and post-office vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "bank account" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: bank account → cuenta bancaria. Banking and post-office vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "ATM" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: ATM → cajero automático. Banking and post-office vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "deposit" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: deposit → depósito. Banking and post-office vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "withdrawal" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: withdrawal → retiro. Banking and post-office vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "savings" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: savings → ahorros. Banking and post-office vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "loan" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: loan → préstamo. Banking and post-office vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "interest rate" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: interest rate → tasa de interés. Banking and post-office vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "balance" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: balance → saldo. Banking and post-office vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "envelope" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: envelope → sobre. Banking and post-office vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "stamp" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "estampilla" is the postage stamp you stick on a letter; in some countries people also say "timbre" or "sello".

questions.prompt: How do you say "package" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: package → paquete. Banking and post-office vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "mailbox" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "buzón" is the box where you drop or receive letters, so it means "mailbox".

questions.prompt: How do you say "address" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: address → dirección. Banking and post-office vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "zip code" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "código postal" is the number code for an address, the Spanish for "zip code".

questions.prompt: How do you say "to send" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: to send → enviar. Banking and post-office vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to mail" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: to mail → enviar por correo. Banking and post-office vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "signature" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "firma" is your signature, the name you write by hand to sign a form or check; the verb is "firmar" (to sign).

questions.prompt: How do you say "form (document)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "formulario" is a form you fill out, like a bank or post-office form; don't confuse it with "forma", which means shape or way.

questions.prompt: How do you say "identification" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "identificación" is the ID you show at a bank or post office, such as a passport; it ends in -ción, like English -tion words.

questions.prompt: How do you say "teller" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: teller → cajero. Banking and post-office vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "branch (bank)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: branch (bank) → sucursal. Banking and post-office vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "transfer" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: transfer → transferencia. Banking and post-office vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "currency" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: currency → moneda. Banking and post-office vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "exchange rate" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: exchange rate → tipo de cambio. Banking and post-office vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "safe (strongbox)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "caja fuerte" is a safe, a strong locked box for money or valuables; a bank's rented safe-deposit box is usually "caja de seguridad".

units.title: Common Adverbs
units.description: Describing how — Common manner and degree adverbs.

questions.prompt: How do you say "quickly" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: quickly → rápidamente. Common manner and degree adverbs.

questions.prompt: How do you say "slowly" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: slowly → lentamente. Common manner and degree adverbs.

questions.prompt: How do you say "well" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "bien" is the irregular adverb for "well" (as in "Hablo bien"); it is not formed with -mente like the other options.

questions.prompt: How do you say "badly" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "mal" is the short irregular adverb for "badly" (as in "Duermo mal"), the opposite of "bien".

questions.prompt: How do you say "easily" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "fácilmente" is built from "fácil" (easy) plus -mente, the Spanish equivalent of English -ly, and it keeps the accent of "fácil".

questions.prompt: How do you say "carefully" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cuidadosamente" comes from the feminine adjective "cuidadosa" (careful) plus -mente, so it means "carefully".

questions.prompt: How do you say "suddenly" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "de repente" is the fixed phrase for 'suddenly', when something happens without warning; "de nuevo" means 'again'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "finally" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "finalmente" means 'finally' or 'in the end' ("final" + -mente); "en realidad" means 'actually', not 'finally'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "immediately" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "inmediatamente" means 'immediately', right away; "rápidamente" means 'quickly', which describes speed, not timing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "especially" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "especialmente" means 'especially'; it is the adjective "especial" plus -mente, just as English adds -ly.

questions.prompt: How do you say "probably" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "probablemente" means 'probably'; it is "probable" plus -mente, while "aparentemente" means 'apparently'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "certainly" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "ciertamente" means 'certainly' (for sure), from "cierto" (true) plus -mente; "probablemente" only means 'probably'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "unfortunately" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "desafortunadamente" means 'unfortunately'; the prefix des- turns "afortunadamente" (fortunately) into its opposite.

questions.prompt: How do you say "fortunately" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "afortunadamente" means 'fortunately'; it comes from "afortunado" (lucky) plus -mente.

questions.prompt: How do you say "obviously" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "obviamente" means "obviously": it is the adjective obvio (feminine obvia) plus -mente, the Spanish ending for English -ly.

questions.prompt: How do you say "simply" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "simplemente" means "simply" or "just": it is simple plus -mente. "directamente" means "directly", which is a different idea.

questions.prompt: How do you say "completely" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "completamente" means "completely": it is completa (from completo) plus -mente. "claramente" means "clearly" and "obviamente" means "obviously".

questions.prompt: How do you say "totally" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "totalmente" means "totally": it is total plus -mente, as in "Estoy totalmente de acuerdo" (I totally agree).

questions.prompt: How do you say "generally" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "generalmente" means "generally" or "usually": it is general plus -mente. "en realidad" means "actually", and "de repente" means "suddenly".

questions.prompt: How do you say "personally" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "personalmente" means "personally": it is personal plus -mente, as in "Personalmente, prefiero el té".

questions.prompt: How do you say "seriously" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "en serio" is the everyday way to say "seriously" or "for real", as in "¿En serio?". It is a phrase, not a -mente word.

questions.prompt: How do you say "actually" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "en realidad" means "actually" or "in fact". Be careful: "actualmente" means "currently", not "actually".

questions.prompt: How do you say "apparently" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "aparentemente" means "apparently": it is aparente plus -mente. Note that Spanish spells it with one p.

questions.prompt: How do you say "clearly" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "claramente" means "clearly": it is clara (from claro) plus -mente, as in "Habla claramente".

questions.prompt: How do you say "directly" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "directamente" means "directly": it is directa (from directo) plus -mente, as in "Voy directamente a casa".

units.title: Prepositions of Time
units.description: When things happen — Prepositions and expressions for talking about time.

questions.prompt: How do you say "before" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "antes de" means "before", as in "antes de la clase". "desde" means "since", and "hace" means "ago".

questions.prompt: How do you say "after" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "después de" means 'after' and goes before a noun or infinitive (después de la clase, después de comer); "durante" means 'during' and "dentro de" means 'within'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "during" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "durante" means 'during' and goes straight before a noun (durante la película); "antes de" means 'before', "dentro de" 'within' and "desde" 'since'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "since" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "desde" means 'since' or 'from' a starting point in time (desde 2020, desde el lunes); "antes de" means 'before'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "until" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "hasta" means 'until' and marks the end point of a period (hasta las cinco); "durante" means 'during' and "antes de" means 'before'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "for (duration)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "por" can express how long something lasts (Estudié por dos horas); "para" is used for deadlines and purposes, not for length of time.

questions.prompt: How do you say "at (time)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Clock times use "a las" for "at" because the hour is feminine and plural, as in "a las tres" (with "a la" only for one o'clock).

questions.prompt: How do you say "on (day)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Spanish uses no preposition for "on" with days; you put the article "el" before the day instead, as in "el lunes" (on Monday).

questions.prompt: How do you say "in (month/year)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Months and years take "en", just like English "in": "en mayo", "en 2020".

questions.prompt: How do you say "within" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "dentro de" means "within" or "in" a period of time from now, as in "dentro de una hora" (within an hour).

questions.prompt: How do you say "throughout" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "a lo largo de" literally means "along the length of", so it expresses "throughout" a period: "a lo largo del año".

questions.prompt: How do you say "by (deadline)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "para" marks a deadline (Necesito el informe para el viernes = by Friday); "dentro de" means 'in/within' a stretch of time, not 'by' a date.

questions.prompt: How do you say "from...to" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "desde...hasta" marks the start and end of a span, as in "desde las nueve hasta las cinco" (from nine to five).

questions.prompt: How do you say "ago" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "hace" means "ago" but comes before the amount of time, not after it: "hace dos años" (two years ago).

questions.prompt: How do you say "soon" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "pronto" means 'soon', in a short time from now (Llego pronto); "mientras tanto" means 'meanwhile' and "anteriormente" means 'previously'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "meanwhile" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "mientras tanto" means 'meanwhile', at the same time as something else is happening; "hoy en día" means 'nowadays' and "de ahora en adelante" means 'from now on'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "eventually" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "con el tiempo" means 'eventually, over time', when something happens after a long while; "posteriormente" just means 'later, subsequently'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "nowadays" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "hoy en día" is a fixed phrase meaning 'nowadays, these days'; the other options mean 'subsequently', 'often' and 'over time'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "previously" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "anteriormente" means 'previously, before now'; its opposite is "posteriormente" ('subsequently, later').

questions.prompt: How do you say "subsequently" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "posteriormente" means 'subsequently, afterwards' and is the opposite of 'anteriormente'; "pronto" means 'soon' and "hoy en día" means 'nowadays'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "briefly" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "brevemente" is the adverb formed from "breve" (short) + -mente, so it means "briefly"; "pronto" means "soon", not "briefly".

questions.prompt: How do you say "frequently" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "frecuentemente" comes from "frecuente" (frequent) + -mente, so it means "frequently"; "ocasionalmente" means the opposite, only now and then.

questions.prompt: How do you say "occasionally" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ocasionalmente" comes from "ocasional" + -mente and means "from time to time", which is "occasionally"; "anteriormente" means "previously".

questions.prompt: How do you say "right now" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "ahora mismo" adds "mismo" to "ahora" to stress this very moment, which is "right now"; "de ahora en adelante" means "from now on".

questions.prompt: How do you say "from now on" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "de ahora en adelante" literally means "from now forward", so it is used for a change that starts now and continues; "hoy en día" means "nowadays".

units.title: Common Verbs (nosotros form)
units.description: Present tense, we form — Present-tense "nosotros" conjugation, including stem-changing and irregular verbs.

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (empezar) el proyecto mañana.
questions.explanation: With "nosotros" the present of "empezar" ends in -amos and has no stem change, so it is "empezamos"; the stem change e→ie only appears in the other persons.

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (terminar) el trabajo a las cinco.
questions.explanation: "Nosotros" (we) requires the -amos ending for -ar verbs, so "terminar" becomes "terminamos"; the other forms belong to yo, ellos or él.

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (entender) la lección.
questions.explanation: "Entender" changes e→ie in most forms, but not in "nosotros", which keeps the plain stem: "entendemos".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (pensar) viajar pronto.
questions.explanation: "Pensar" changes e→ie except in "nosotros", where the stress falls on the ending: "pensamos".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (perder) el autobús a veces.
questions.explanation: "Perder" has a stem change e→ie in other persons, but "nosotros" keeps the plain stem and takes -emos: "perdemos".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (encontrar) las llaves.
questions.explanation: "Encontrar" changes o→ue in most persons, but "nosotros" keeps the o and takes -amos: "encontramos".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (dormir) ocho horas.
questions.explanation: "Dormir" changes o→ue in most persons, but "nosotros" keeps the o and takes -imos: "dormimos".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (pedir) ayuda cuando la necesitamos.
questions.explanation: "Nosotros" takes the ending -imos, and in the nosotros form pedir keeps its e (no e→i change), so the verb is "pedimos" rather than "pidimos".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (seguir) las instrucciones.
questions.explanation: The subject "nosotros" needs the -imos ending, and seguir keeps its e in this form (the e→i change only happens in yo, tú, él and ellos), giving "seguimos".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (repetir) la pregunta.
questions.explanation: With "nosotros", -ir verbs end in -imos, and repetir does not change its stem in this form, so it is "repetimos".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (preferir) el té al café.
questions.explanation: Preferir changes e→ie in most forms, but not in "nosotros", which takes the plain -imos ending: "preferimos".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (cerrar) la tienda a las nueve.
questions.explanation: Cerrar changes e→ie in yo, tú, él and ellos, but "nosotros" keeps the stem and takes -amos, giving "cerramos".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (mostrar) el camino a los turistas.
questions.explanation: Mostrar changes o→ue in other forms, but "nosotros" keeps the stem o and takes -amos: "mostramos".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (recordar) su cumpleaños.
questions.explanation: Recordar changes o→ue in the other forms, but "nosotros" keeps the stem o and ends in -amos, so it is "recordamos".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (volver) a casa tarde.
questions.explanation: Volver changes o→ue in yo, tú, él and ellos, but "nosotros" keeps the o and takes -emos, giving "volvemos".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (conseguir) boletos para el concierto.
questions.explanation: Conseguir changes e→i in yo, tú, él and ellos, but "nosotros" keeps the e and takes -imos: "conseguimos".
questions.meaning: we get, we manage to get

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (elegir) el mejor restaurante.
questions.explanation: Elegir changes e→i in other forms, but "nosotros" keeps the e and takes -imos, so it is "elegimos".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (construir) una casa nueva.
questions.explanation: Construir adds a y before the ending in most forms (construyo, construyen), but "nosotros" takes plain -imos, giving "construimos".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (destruir) los documentos viejos.
questions.explanation: Destruir adds a y in forms like destruyo and destruyen, but "nosotros" takes plain -imos, so it is "destruimos".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (incluir) a todos en el plan.
questions.explanation: "incluimos" is right because "nosotros" takes the -imos ending. Incluir has no stem change in the nosotros form (the y only appears in incluyo, incluyes, incluyen).

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (huir) del peligro.
questions.explanation: "huimos" is right because "nosotros" takes -imos. The y of huir (huyo, huyes, huyen) does not appear in the nosotros form.

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (concluir) la reunión temprano.
questions.explanation: "concluimos" is right because "nosotros" takes -imos. Concluir keeps its regular form here, with no y.

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (sonreír) mucho.
questions.explanation: "sonreímos" is right because "nosotros" takes the -imos ending on the plain stem sonre- (no e→i change), with an accent on the í to split the vowels, while forms like sonríes change the stem to sonrí-.

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (reír) con sus chistes.
questions.explanation: "reímos" is right because the subject is "nosotros". Reír uses the accented -ímos ending, unlike río, ríes, ríe, which go with other subjects.

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (freír) las papas.
questions.explanation: "freímos" is right because the subject is "nosotros". Freír keeps the e and takes -ímos here, unlike fríes, fríe, fríen.

units.title: Speaking: Daily Routine & Plans
units.description: Say it out loud — Everyday routine and near-future plans to practise saying.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "Me levanto a las siete." Everyday routine and near-future plans to practise saying.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Desayuno a las ocho." means "I have breakfast at eight." "Desayunar" is a verb, so "desayuno" alone means "I have breakfast", and clock times use "a las".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Voy al trabajo en autobús." means "I go to work by bus." "A" + "el" contracts to "al", and Spanish uses "en" for means of transport.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Trabajo hasta las cinco." means "I work until five." "Hasta" means "until" and marks when the activity ends.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Vuelvo a casa cansado." means "I come home tired." "Volver" changes o to ue in "vuelvo", and a woman would say "cansada".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Ceno con mi familia." means "I have dinner with my family." "Cenar" is a verb meaning "to have dinner", and in Latin America the "ce" sounds like "se".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Veo la televisión un rato." means "I watch TV for a while." "Un rato" means "a little while".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Me acuesto a las diez." means "I go to bed at ten." "Acostarse" is reflexive, so it takes "me", and it changes o to ue in "acuesto".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Los fines de semana descanso." means "On weekends I rest." Spanish uses "los" with days and weekends to describe a habit.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "A veces voy al cine." means "Sometimes I go to the movies." "A veces" means "sometimes" and usually comes at the start of the sentence.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Me gusta cocinar los domingos." means "I like cooking on Sundays." "Gusta" is singular because the thing you like is an action ("cocinar"), and "los domingos" means "on Sundays".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Prefiero el té al café." means "I prefer tea to coffee." "Preferir" changes e to ie in "prefiero", and "al" (a + el) works like English "to" in this comparison.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Necesito comprar leche." means "I need to buy milk." "Necesitar" is followed directly by an infinitive, with no extra word in between.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Say "Voy al mercado los sábados." to describe a weekly habit: "los sábados" means "on Saturdays", and "al" is "a + el".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Say "Hoy hace mucho calor." to talk about the weather: Spanish uses "hace" + "calor" ("it's hot"), not "es" or "está".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Say "Mañana va a llover." to predict the weather: "va a" + infinitive is the everyday way to talk about the near future.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "El invierno aquí es frío." Use "es" (ser) because being cold is what winter is like here; keep the stress on "frío" and "aquí".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Say "Me encanta la primavera." to say you love spring: "encantar" works like "gustar", so the thing you love ("la primavera") is the subject.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Tengo una reunión a las nueve.
questions.explanation: Say "Tengo una reunión a las nueve." to give a time for a plan: Spanish uses "a las" + hour for "at nine".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Say "Llego tarde a veces." to describe an occasional habit: "a veces" means "sometimes", and the "ll" in "llego" sounds like an English "y" in most of Latin America.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Say "Estudio español todos los días." to describe a daily routine: "todos los días" means "every day".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Say "Practico con mis amigos." to say who you practise with: stress the second syllable, "prac-TI-co".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Say "Quiero viajar el próximo año." to talk about a wish for the future: "quiero" + infinitive means "I want to", and "el próximo año" is "next year".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Voy a visitar a mis abuelos.
questions.explanation: Say "Voy a visitar a mis abuelos." to state a plan: "voy a" + infinitive gives the near future, and "a" comes before people as objects ("a mis abuelos").

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Say "Espero verte pronto." to say "I hope to see you soon": "te" attaches to the end of the infinitive "ver".

units.title: Write It Yourself: Asking and Arranging
units.description: Say it your own way — Practice asking, arranging and explaining; more than one wording can be right.

lessons.title: Write It Yourself: Asking and Arranging 1
lessons.subtitle: Say it your own way

questions.prompt: Ask a friend if they are free tonight.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "¿Estás libre esta noche?" Use "estar libre" for being free at a given time, and tú because you are talking to a friend.

questions.prompt: Suggest meeting tomorrow.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "¿Nos vemos mañana?" A question with "vernos" (to see each other) is a friendly way to suggest meeting.

questions.prompt: Say you have to leave now.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Tengo que irme ahora." Use "tener que" + infinitive for something you must do, and "irme" for "leave".

questions.prompt: Ask for directions to the station.
acceptableAnswers: ¿Por dónde se va a la estación?
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "¿Cómo llego a la estación?" "¿Cómo llego a...?" (How do I get to...?) is the standard way to ask for directions.

questions.prompt: Tell a friend to turn left at the corner.
acceptableAnswers: Gira a la izquierda en la esquina.
Dobla a la izquierda en la esquina.
En la esquina, gira a la izquierda.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Gira a la izquierda en la esquina." "Gira" (or "dobla") is the tú command for "turn", and "en la esquina" means "at the corner".

lessons.title: Write It Yourself: Asking and Arranging 2
lessons.subtitle: Say it your own way

questions.prompt: Ask if the store is open.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "¿Está abierta la tienda?" Use "estar" for the store's current state, and "abierta" is feminine to agree with "la tienda".

questions.prompt: Say you would like to reserve a table.
questions.explanation: "Quisiera reservar una mesa." uses "quisiera", a polite form of "querer" that means 'I would like', followed by the infinitive "reservar" (to reserve).

questions.prompt: Ask if there is a room available.
questions.explanation: "¿Hay una habitación disponible?" uses "hay" for 'is there', and "disponible" means 'available'.

questions.prompt: Ask what time the train leaves.
questions.explanation: "¿A qué hora sale el tren?" uses "a qué hora" to ask for a clock time, and "sale" (from "salir") means 'leaves' or 'departs'.

questions.prompt: Say you need to see a doctor.
acceptableAnswers: Tengo que consultar a un médico.
questions.explanation: "Necesito ver a un médico." puts "necesito" (I need) before the infinitive "ver", and "ver" takes the personal "a" because a doctor is a person.

lessons.title: Write It Yourself: Asking and Arranging 3
lessons.subtitle: Say it your own way

questions.prompt: Say you don't feel well.
questions.explanation: "No me siento bien." uses the reflexive verb "sentirse" (to feel), so "me" goes before the verb and "no" goes before both.

questions.prompt: Ask a friend what they are doing this weekend.
acceptableAnswers: ¿Qué vas a hacer este fin de semana?
¿Tienes planes para el fin de semana?
questions.explanation: "¿Qué vas a hacer este fin de semana?" uses "ir a" plus an infinitive to ask about plans, with informal "vas" because you are talking to a friend.

questions.prompt: Say you work in an office.
acceptableAnswers: Mi trabajo es en una oficina.
questions.explanation: "Trabajo en una oficina." uses "trabajo" (I work), where the ending already shows the subject, and "en" gives the place.

questions.prompt: Say you have been studying Spanish for two years.
acceptableAnswers: Estudio español desde hace dos años.
Hace dos años que estudio español.
questions.explanation: "Llevo dos años estudiando español." uses "llevar" plus a length of time plus a gerund to say how long you have been doing something that is still going on.

questions.prompt: Say you have lived here for a long time.
acceptableAnswers: Vivo aquí desde hace mucho tiempo.
Hace mucho tiempo que vivo aquí.
questions.explanation: "Vivo aquí desde hace mucho tiempo." uses the present tense with "desde hace" because the living here started in the past and still continues.

lessons.title: Write It Yourself: Asking and Arranging 4
lessons.subtitle: Say it your own way

questions.prompt: Say she arrives in ten minutes.
questions.explanation: "Ella llega en diez minutos." uses the present tense for a near-future event, and "en diez minutos" means 'in ten minutes'.

questions.prompt: Say he left last night.
questions.explanation: "Él se fue anoche." uses the preterite "se fue" (from "irse", to leave) for an action finished "anoche", last night.

questions.prompt: Ask a friend if they can come with us.
questions.explanation: "¿Puedes venir con nosotros?" uses informal "puedes" (from "poder") because you are asking a friend, followed by the infinitive "venir".

questions.prompt: Say that's a good idea.
questions.explanation: "Es una buena idea." uses "es" (ser) to describe the idea, and "buena" comes before "idea" and is feminine to agree with it.

questions.prompt: Say you agree with someone.
questions.explanation: Spanish says "estar de acuerdo" for 'to agree', and "contigo" means 'with you', so "Estoy de acuerdo contigo." is the natural way to say it.

lessons.title: Write It Yourself: Asking and Arranging 5
lessons.subtitle: Say it your own way

questions.prompt: Say you don't agree.
questions.explanation: Put "no" before the verb to negate "estar de acuerdo": "No estoy de acuerdo."

questions.prompt: Suggest meeting in front of the station.
acceptableAnswers: Nos vemos frente a la estación.
questions.explanation: "Nos vemos frente a la estación." proposes a meeting place, with "frente a" meaning 'in front of'; it also works as a question: "¿Nos vemos frente a la estación?"

questions.prompt: Ask someone to call you back.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Llámame, por favor." Asking, arranging and explaining, and more than one wording is right.

questions.prompt: Say you'll be there in five minutes.
questions.explanation: "Llego en cinco minutos." uses the present tense of "llegar" for a near future, the usual way to say you'll be there soon; "en cinco minutos" means 'in five minutes'.

questions.prompt: Ask someone to speak more slowly.
questions.explanation: "¿Puedes hablar más despacio?" is a polite tú request with "poder", and "más despacio" means 'more slowly'.

questions.prompt: Ellos ___ (querer) verte pronto.
questions.explanation: "Ellos" is third-person plural, so the irregular stem querr- takes -án, giving "querrán".

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (poner) la mesa más tarde.
questions.explanation: "Tú" takes the ending -ás, and poner has the irregular stem pondr-, giving "pondrás".
questions.meaning: you will put, you will set

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (ser) felices allí.
questions.explanation: "Nosotros" takes the future ending -emos added to the whole infinitive ser, giving "seremos".

questions.prompt: Ella ___ (ir) al médico la próxima semana.
questions.explanation: "Ella" is third-person singular, so the future ending -á is added to the infinitive ir, giving "irá".

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (estar) listo a tiempo.
questions.explanation: "Yo" takes the ending -é added to the whole infinitive estar, giving "estaré" (with the written accent).

questions.prompt: Ellos ___ (tener) que estudiar más.
questions.explanation: The subject "Ellos" is third-person plural, so the future of tener takes the irregular stem "tendr-" plus -án: "tendrán".

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (ver) los resultados mañana.
questions.explanation: The subject "Tú" needs the second-person singular future ending -ás, added to the whole infinitive ver: "verás".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (venir) a visitarte pronto.
questions.explanation: The subject "Nosotros" takes the ending -emos, and venir has the irregular future stem "vendr-": "vendremos".

questions.prompt: Él ___ (hacer) la cena esta noche.
questions.explanation: The subject "Él" takes the ending -á, and hacer has the irregular future stem "har-" (not "hacer-"): "hará".
questions.meaning: he will make, he will do

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (dar) una charla el lunes.
questions.explanation: The subject "Yo" takes the first-person singular future ending -é, added to the infinitive dar: "daré".

questions.prompt: Ella ___ (saber) la respuesta pronto.
questions.explanation: The subject "Ella" takes the ending -á, and saber has the irregular future stem "sabr-": "sabrá".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (poder) terminar a tiempo.
questions.explanation: The subject "Nosotros" takes the ending -emos, and poder has the irregular future stem "podr-": "podremos".

questions.prompt: Ellos ___ (llegar) mañana por la tarde.
questions.explanation: The subject "Ellos" is third-person plural, so llegar takes the regular future ending -án after the full infinitive: "llegarán".

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (ser) un gran médico.
questions.explanation: The subject "Tú" needs the second-person singular future ending -ás added to the infinitive ser: "serás".

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (volver) el próximo mes.
questions.explanation: The subject "Yo" takes the first-person singular future ending -é, added to the infinitive volver: "volveré".
questions.meaning: I will return, I will come back

units.title: Reflexive Verbs
units.description: Daily routine actions — Reflexive verbs for daily routine, present tense.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (levantarse) a las siete.
questions.explanation: The subject "Yo" requires the reflexive pronoun me and the first-person present ending -o: "me levanto".

questions.prompt: Ella ___ (despertarse) temprano.
questions.explanation: The subject "Ella" is third-person singular, so it takes se and the singular verb with the e→ie stem change: "se despierta".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (ducharse) por la mañana.
questions.explanation: The subject "Nosotros" (we) takes the reflexive pronoun "nos" and the "-amos" ending, so the form is "nos duchamos".
questions.meaning: we shower, we take a shower

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (vestirse) rápido.
questions.explanation: "Tú" pairs with the reflexive pronoun "te", and vestirse changes e to i in the stem, giving "te vistes".

questions.prompt: Ellos ___ (acostarse) tarde.
questions.explanation: "Ellos" is third person plural, so the pronoun is "se" and the verb ends in -n; acostarse also changes o to ue, giving "se acuestan".

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (lavarse) las manos.
questions.explanation: "Yo" takes the reflexive pronoun "me" and the "-o" ending, so washing my own hands is "me lavo".

questions.prompt: Él ___ (peinarse) antes de salir.
questions.explanation: "Él" is third person singular, so the pronoun is "se" and the verb ends in -a, giving "se peina".

questions.prompt: Nosotras ___ (sentarse) a la mesa.
questions.explanation: "Nosotras" (we) requires the pronoun "nos" and the "-amos" ending; sentarse keeps its regular stem in the nosotros form, so it is "nos sentamos".

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (cepillarse) los dientes.
questions.explanation: "Tú" takes the reflexive pronoun "te" and the "-as" ending, so brushing your teeth is "te cepillas".

questions.prompt: Ella ___ (maquillarse) para la fiesta.
questions.explanation: "Ella" is third person singular, so the pronoun is "se" and the verb ends in -a, giving "se maquilla".

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (bañarse) todos los días.
questions.explanation: "Yo" takes the reflexive pronoun "me" and the "-o" ending, so the form is "me baño".
questions.meaning: I take a bath, I bathe

questions.prompt: Ellos ___ (dormirse) fácilmente.
questions.explanation: "Ellos" is third person plural, so it needs "se" and an -n ending; dormirse also changes o to ue, giving "se duermen".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (relajarse) los fines de semana.
questions.explanation: "Nosotros" (we) takes the pronoun "nos" and the "-amos" ending, so the form is "nos relajamos".

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (preocuparse) demasiado.
questions.explanation: "Tú" takes the reflexive pronoun "te" and the "-as" ending, so "you worry" is "te preocupas".

questions.prompt: Él ___ (afeitarse) cada mañana.
questions.explanation: The subject Él is third person singular, so the reflexive pronoun is "se" and the verb ends in -a: "se afeita". The other options belong to different subjects.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (quedarse) en casa hoy.
questions.explanation: The subject Yo takes the reflexive pronoun "me" and the -o ending: "me quedo" (I stay).

questions.prompt: Ella ___ (sentirse) mejor ahora.
questions.explanation: Ella is third person singular, so we need "se" plus the stem-changing e→ie form: "se siente". "se sienten" would be plural.

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (divertirse) mucho aquí.
questions.explanation: Nosotros requires the reflexive pronoun "nos" and the -imos ending: "nos divertimos". Only this option matches 'we'.
questions.meaning: we have fun, we enjoy ourselves

questions.prompt: Ellos ___ (mudarse) el próximo mes.
questions.explanation: Ellos is third person plural, so the verb ends in -an after "se": "se mudan". "se muda" is singular.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (equivocarse) a veces.
questions.explanation: Tú goes with the reflexive pronoun "te" and the -as ending: "te equivocas" (you make a mistake).
questions.meaning: you make a mistake, you are wrong

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (cansarse) rápido.
questions.explanation: Yo takes "me" and the -o ending, so the first-person form is "me canso" (I get tired).

questions.prompt: Ella ___ (enojarse) fácilmente.
questions.explanation: Ella is third person singular, so "se" plus the -a ending gives "se enoja". "se enojan" would be plural.

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (aburrirse) sin planes.
questions.explanation: Nosotros requires "nos" and the -imos ending of -ir verbs: "nos aburrimos" (we get bored).

questions.prompt: Ellos ___ (casarse) en junio.
questions.explanation: Ellos is third person plural, so the reflexive form is "se casan" (they get married). The other options match yo, nosotros or tú.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (olvidarse) de las llaves a veces.
questions.explanation: Yo takes "me" and the -o ending: "me olvido" (I forget). The other options match other subjects.
questions.example: Yo me olvido de las llaves a veces.

units.title: Subjunctive Basics
units.description: Wishes, doubts, and recommendations — Present subjunctive after expressions of wish, doubt, or recommendation.

questions.prompt: Espero que tú ___ (venir) mañana.
questions.explanation: "Espero que" expresses a wish and triggers the present subjunctive; for tú, venir becomes "vengas". "vienes" is indicative and "venga" is the usted form.

questions.prompt: Dudo que ella ___ (saber) la verdad.
questions.explanation: "sepa" is right because "Dudo que" expresses doubt and triggers the subjunctive, and "ella" needs the third-person singular form of saber. "Sabe" is indicative, and "sepas" and "sepan" are the wrong person.

questions.prompt: Es importante que nosotros ___ (llegar) a tiempo.
questions.explanation: "lleguemos" is right because "Es importante que" triggers the subjunctive, and "nosotros" needs the "nosotros" form. "Llegamos" is indicative, and "llegue" and "llegan" are the wrong person.

questions.prompt: Quiero que tú ___ (ser) feliz.
questions.explanation: "seas" is right because "Quiero que" expresses a wish and triggers the subjunctive, and "tú" needs the second-person form of ser. "Sea" is for él/ella, "sean" for ellos, and "seamos" for nosotros.

questions.prompt: Recomiendo que usted ___ (descansar) más.
questions.explanation: "descanse" is right because "Recomiendo que" triggers the subjunctive, and "usted" takes the third-person singular form. "Descanses" is the tú form, "descansemos" is nosotros, and "descansen" is plural.

questions.prompt: Ojalá que ellos ___ (ganar) el partido.
questions.explanation: "ganen" is right because "Ojalá que" expresses a wish and triggers the subjunctive, and "ellos" needs the third-person plural form. "Gane" is singular, "ganes" is tú, and "ganemos" is nosotros.

questions.prompt: Es necesario que yo ___ (estudiar) más.
questions.explanation: "estudie" is right because "Es necesario que" triggers the subjunctive, and "yo" takes the first-person singular form, which is the same as the él/ella form. "Estudies" is tú, "estudien" is plural, and "estudiemos" is nosotros.

questions.prompt: No creo que él ___ (tener) razón.
questions.explanation: "tenga" is right because "No creo que" expresses doubt and triggers the subjunctive, and "él" needs the third-person singular form. "Tengas" is tú, "tengan" is plural, and "tengamos" is nosotros.

questions.prompt: Espero que ustedes ___ (disfrutar) el viaje.
questions.explanation: "disfruten" is right because "Espero que" expresses a wish and triggers the subjunctive, and "ustedes" needs the third-person plural form. "Disfrute" is singular, "disfrutes" is tú, and "disfrutemos" is nosotros.
questions.meaning: you all enjoy (subjunctive form of disfrutar)

questions.prompt: Es posible que ella ___ (venir) hoy.
questions.explanation: "venga" is right because "Es posible que" expresses possibility and triggers the subjunctive, and "ella" needs the third-person singular form of venir. "Vengan", "vengas" and "vengamos" are other persons.

questions.prompt: Prefiero que tú ___ (hacer) la tarea ahora.
questions.explanation: "hagas" is right because "Prefiero que" expresses a preference and triggers the subjunctive, and "tú" needs the second-person form of hacer. "Haces" is indicative, "haga" is él/ella, and "hagan" is plural.

questions.prompt: Es raro que él no ___ (contestar).
questions.explanation: "conteste" is right because "Es raro que" expresses a reaction to a fact and triggers the subjunctive, and "él" needs the third-person singular form. "Contestes" is tú, "contesten" is plural, and "contestemos" is nosotros.

questions.prompt: Sugiero que nosotros ___ (esperar) un poco.
questions.explanation: "esperemos" is right because "Sugiero que" expresses a recommendation and triggers the subjunctive, and "nosotros" needs the "nosotros" form. "Espere", "esperes" and "esperen" are other persons.

questions.prompt: Ojalá que tú ___ (poder) venir.
questions.explanation: "Ojalá que" always takes the subjunctive, and the subject is "tú", so poder becomes "puedas" (-er verbs take -as, with o→ue in the stem).

questions.prompt: Dudo que ellos ___ (decir) la verdad.
questions.explanation: "Dudo que" expresses doubt, so the verb is subjunctive, and "ellos" needs the third-person plural: decir becomes "digan" (stem dig-, -an).

questions.prompt: Es bueno que ustedes ___ (aprender) español.
questions.explanation: "Es bueno que" is an evaluation phrase that triggers the subjunctive, and "ustedes" takes the plural ending: aprender becomes "aprendan".
questions.meaning: you all learn (subjunctive form of aprender)

questions.prompt: Espero que ella ___ (estar) bien.
questions.explanation: "Espero que" expresses a wish, so the verb is subjunctive, and for "ella" estar becomes "esté" (with an accent on the final syllable).

questions.prompt: Es una lástima que tú no ___ (ir).
questions.explanation: "Es una lástima que" expresses an emotional reaction and triggers the subjunctive; with "tú", ir becomes "vayas".

questions.prompt: Quiero que ellos ___ (ser) puntuales.
questions.explanation: "Quiero que" (a wish with a new subject) requires the subjunctive, and with "ellos" ser becomes "sean".

questions.prompt: Es probable que nosotros ___ (perder) el tren.
questions.explanation: "Es probable que" expresses possibility and triggers the subjunctive; with "nosotros", perder becomes "perdamos" (the nosotros form keeps the plain stem, no e→ie change).

questions.prompt: Recomiendo que tú ___ (leer) ese libro.
questions.explanation: "Recomiendo que" is a recommendation and triggers the subjunctive; with "tú", leer becomes "leas", whereas "lees" is the indicative.

questions.prompt: Espero que él ___ (recuperarse) pronto.
questions.explanation: "Espero que" triggers the subjunctive, and the reflexive pronoun must match "él", so the form is "se recupere".

questions.prompt: No pienso que ella ___ (mentir).
questions.explanation: "No pienso que" expresses doubt, so the verb is subjunctive, and for "ella" mentir becomes "mienta" (e→ie stem change, -a ending).

questions.prompt: Es mejor que ustedes ___ (salir) temprano.
questions.explanation: "Es mejor que" is a recommendation that triggers the subjunctive, and "ustedes" takes the plural: salir becomes "salgan" (stem salg-).
questions.meaning: you all leave, you all go out (subjunctive)

questions.prompt: Ojalá que nosotros ___ (encontrar) una solución.
questions.explanation: "Ojalá que" always takes the subjunctive, and "nosotros" needs the nosotros form: encontrar becomes "encontremos" (no stem change, -emos).

units.title: Connectors & Conjunctions
units.description: Linking ideas — Common linking words for more complex sentences.

questions.prompt: How do you say "however" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "sin embargo" means "however": it introduces a contrast with the previous idea, as in "Quería ir; sin embargo, no tenía tiempo."

questions.prompt: How do you say "although" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "aunque" means "although" and is followed by a full clause, as in "Aunque llueve, salgo." Note that "a pesar de" means "despite" and goes before a noun.

questions.prompt: How do you say "because" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "porque" (one word, no accent) introduces a reason, like "because"; don't confuse it with "por qué" (why) in questions.

questions.prompt: How do you say "therefore" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "por lo tanto" means "therefore": it introduces the result of what was just said, as in "Llovía; por lo tanto, no salimos."

questions.prompt: How do you say "since (cause)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "ya que" means "since" in the sense of "because": it gives a reason, often at the start of the sentence, as in "Ya que estás aquí, ayúdame."

questions.prompt: How do you say "in spite of" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "a pesar de" means "in spite of" and is followed by a noun or an infinitive, as in a pesar de la lluvia.

questions.prompt: How do you say "on the other hand" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "por otro lado" literally means "by the other side" and introduces a second point or contrast, just like "on the other hand".

questions.prompt: How do you say "in addition" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "además" means "in addition": it adds one more point to what you just said, as in "Es barato; además, es rápido."

questions.prompt: How do you say "for example" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "por ejemplo" means "for example": it introduces an example, as in "Me gustan las frutas, por ejemplo, el mango."

questions.prompt: How do you say "in other words" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "es decir" (literally "that is to say") introduces a rephrasing of what was just said, like "in other words".

questions.prompt: How do you say "otherwise" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "de lo contrario" means "otherwise" and tells what happens if the condition isn't met, as in Estudia; de lo contrario, no aprobarás.

questions.prompt: How do you say "likewise" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "asimismo" means "likewise" or "in the same way": it adds a similar point, mostly in formal writing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "in fact" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "de hecho" literally means "of fact" and adds a stronger or confirming point, like "in fact".

questions.prompt: How do you say "as soon as" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "tan pronto como" means "as soon as"; when it refers to the future it takes the subjunctive, as in tan pronto como llegues.

questions.prompt: How do you say "unless" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "a menos que" means "unless" and is always followed by the subjunctive, as in a menos que llueva.

questions.prompt: How do you say "even though (formal)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "aun cuando" means "even though" or "even if": it is a more formal way of introducing a concession than "aunque".

questions.prompt: How do you say "so that" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "para que" expresses purpose, like "so that", and is followed by the subjunctive, as in Te lo digo para que lo sepas.

questions.prompt: How do you say "as long as" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "siempre que" means "as long as": it sets a condition and takes the subjunctive, as in "Puedes ir siempre que vuelvas temprano."
