questions.prompt: How do you say "consequently" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "en consecuencia" means "consequently": it introduces the result of what was just said, while the other options express contrast or time.

questions.prompt: How do you say "nevertheless" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "no obstante" means "nevertheless": it introduces a contrast with what was just said, like a more formal "sin embargo".

units.title: Idiomatic Expressions
units.description: Everyday sayings — Common idiomatic expressions used in everyday Spanish.

questions.prompt: What does "tener hambre" mean?
questions.explanation: "tener hambre" means "to be hungry": Spanish uses "tener" (to have) where English uses "to be", as in "Tengo hambre."

questions.prompt: What does "tener sueño" mean? ___
questions.explanation: Spanish uses "tener" (to have) for physical states where English uses "to be": "tener sueño" is literally "to have sleep," so it means "to be sleepy".

questions.prompt: What does "tener prisa" mean?
questions.explanation: "Tener prisa" is literally "to have hurry"; Spanish uses "tener" where English uses "to be," so it means "to be in a hurry".

questions.prompt: What does "tener razón" mean? ___
questions.explanation: "Tener razón" is literally "to have reason"; like other tener expressions, it uses "to be" in English, so it means "to be right".

questions.prompt: What does "echar de menos" mean?
questions.explanation: "Echar de menos" literally means 'to throw as less', so it means "to miss (someone)": Echo de menos a mi familia. In Latin America you will also often hear "extrañar" with the same meaning.

questions.prompt: What does "darse cuenta" mean? ___
questions.explanation: "Darse cuenta" (often with 'de') means "to realize", that is, to become aware of something: Me di cuenta de que era tarde.

questions.prompt: What does "hacer caso" mean?
questions.explanation: hacer caso → to pay attention. Common idiomatic expressions used in everyday Spanish.

questions.prompt: What does "tomar el pelo" mean? ___
bank: to hit the nail on the head
questions.explanation: "Tomar el pelo" literally means 'to take the hair', but it means "to tease someone" or pull their leg: ¿Me estás tomando el pelo?

questions.prompt: What does "costar un ojo de la cara" mean?
questions.explanation: "Costar un ojo de la cara" literally means 'to cost an eye from the face', so it means "to cost a fortune": Ese carro cuesta un ojo de la cara.

questions.prompt: What does "estar en las nubes" mean? ___
questions.explanation: "Estar en las nubes" is literally "to be in the clouds," describing someone whose mind is elsewhere, so it means "to be daydreaming".

questions.prompt: What does "meter la pata" mean? ___
questions.explanation: "Meter la pata" is literally "to put your paw in it," like the English "put your foot in it," so it means "to make a mistake".

questions.prompt: What does "no tener pelos en la lengua" mean?
questions.explanation: "No tener pelos en la lengua" is literally "to have no hairs on your tongue": nothing holds back what you say, so it means "to speak bluntly".

questions.prompt: What does "ser pan comido" mean? ___
questions.explanation: "Ser pan comido" is literally "to be eaten bread": something already done, with no effort left, so it means "to be very easy".

questions.prompt: What does "tirar la toalla" mean?
questions.explanation: "Tirar la toalla" comes from boxing, where throwing in the towel concedes the fight, so it means "to give up".

questions.prompt: What does "ponerse las pilas" mean? ___
bank: to hit the nail on the head
questions.explanation: "Ponerse las pilas" is literally "to put your batteries in": to recharge and start making an effort, so it means "to get one's act together".

questions.prompt: What does "más vale tarde que nunca" mean?
questions.explanation: "Más vale tarde que nunca" says late is worth more than never, matching the English proverb "better late than never".

questions.prompt: What does "dar en el clavo" mean? ___
bank: to hit the nail on the head
questions.answer: to hit the nail on the head
questions.explanation: "Dar en el clavo" is literally "to strike the nail," meaning to get something exactly right, just like "to hit the nail on the head".

questions.prompt: What does "estar como pez en el agua" mean?
questions.explanation: A fish in water is completely in its element, so "estar como pez en el agua" means "to feel right at home".

questions.prompt: What does "no dar pie con bola" mean? ___
questions.explanation: "No dar pie con bola" pictures someone who can never get foot to ball, so it means "to keep getting it wrong".

questions.prompt: What does "tomar cartas en el asunto" mean?
questions.explanation: "Tomar cartas en el asunto" means stepping in to deal with a problem yourself, so it means "to take action".

units.title: Present Perfect
units.description: haber + past participle — Present perfect tense across several subjects.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (comer) ya.
questions.explanation: The subject "Yo" takes the auxiliary "he", and the participle of comer is comido, so "he comido" is right.
questions.example: Ya he comido.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (terminar) el trabajo.
questions.explanation: The subject "Tú" takes the auxiliary "has", and terminar gives the participle terminado, so "has terminado" is right.

questions.prompt: Ella ___ (llegar) tarde.
questions.explanation: The subject "Ella" (she) takes the auxiliary "ha", and llegar gives llegado, so "ha llegado" is right.

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (viajar) mucho.
questions.explanation: The subject "Nosotros" (we) takes the auxiliary "hemos", and viajar gives viajado, so "hemos viajado" is right.

questions.prompt: Ellos ___ (ver) esa película.
questions.explanation: The subject "Ellos" (they) takes the auxiliary "han", and the irregular participle of ver is visto, so "han visto" is right.

questions.prompt: Yo ya ___ (hacer) mi tarea.
questions.explanation: The subject "Yo" takes "he", and hacer has the irregular participle hecho (not "hacido"), so "he hecho" is right.
questions.meaning: I have done, I have made

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (escribir) la carta.
questions.explanation: The subject "Tú" takes "has", and escribir has the irregular participle escrito (not "escribido"), so "has escrito" is right.

questions.prompt: Él ___ (abrir) la puerta.
questions.explanation: The subject "Él" takes "ha", and abrir has the irregular participle abierto (not "abrido"), so "ha abierto" is right.

questions.prompt: Nosotras ___ (decir) la verdad.
questions.explanation: The subject "Nosotras" (we) takes "hemos", and decir has the irregular participle dicho, so "hemos dicho" is right.
questions.meaning: we have said, we have told

questions.prompt: Ellas ___ (poner) la mesa.
questions.explanation: The subject "Ellas" (they) takes "han", and poner has the irregular participle puesto (not "ponido"), so "han puesto" is right.
questions.meaning: they have put, they have set

questions.prompt: Yo nunca ___ (estar) en España.
questions.explanation: The subject "Yo" takes "he", and the verb is estar (to be somewhere), so the participle is estado, giving "he estado"; "he sido" would come from ser.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (romper) el vaso.
questions.explanation: The subject "Tú" takes "has", and romper has the irregular participle roto (not "rompido"), so "has roto" is right.

questions.prompt: Ella ___ (volver) a casa.
questions.explanation: "ha vuelto" is right because the subject "Ella" needs "ha", and volver has an irregular participle (vuelto), not "volvido".
questions.meaning: she has returned, has come back

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (resolver) el problema.
questions.explanation: "hemos resuelto" is right because "Nosotros" takes "hemos", and resolver has an irregular participle (resuelto), not "resolvido".

questions.prompt: Ellos ___ (descubrir) la verdad.
questions.explanation: "han descubierto" is right because "Ellos" takes "han", and descubrir has an irregular participle (descubierto), not "descubrido".

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (vivir) en tres países.
questions.explanation: "he vivido" is right because "Yo" takes "he", and the regular -ir participle is "vivido"; the present perfect fits life experience.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (leer) ese libro.
questions.explanation: "has leído" is right because "Tú" takes "has", and leer's participle is "leído" with an accent on the í, not "leyido".

questions.prompt: Él ___ (cubrir) la mesa.
questions.explanation: "ha cubierto" is right because "Él" takes "ha", and cubrir has an irregular participle (cubierto), not "cubrido".
questions.example: Él ha cubierto la mesa con un mantel.

questions.prompt: Nosotras ___ (freír) el pollo.
questions.explanation: "hemos freído" is right because "Nosotras" takes the auxiliary "hemos"; freír has two accepted participles, freído (written with an accent on the í) and the more common frito.

questions.prompt: Ellos ___ (imprimir) el documento.
questions.explanation: "han impreso" is right because "Ellos" takes "han", and imprimir has an irregular participle (impreso).

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (ganar) el partido.
questions.explanation: "he ganado" is right because "Yo" takes "he", followed by the regular participle of ganar.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (perder) las llaves.
questions.explanation: "has perdido" is right because "Tú" takes "has", and the participle of perder is "perdido", not a gerund form.

questions.prompt: Ella ___ (aprender) mucho.
questions.explanation: "ha aprendido" is right because "Ella" takes "ha", and the participle is "aprendido", not the gerund "aprendiendo".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (comprar) una casa.
questions.explanation: "hemos comprado" is right because "Nosotros" takes "hemos"; "habemos" is not standard as an auxiliary.

questions.prompt: Ellos ___ (llegar) temprano.
questions.explanation: "han llegado" is right because "ellos" (they) takes the third-person plural form of haber in the present perfect: han + past participle.

units.title: Ser vs. Estar
units.description: Two verbs for 'to be' — Ser (identity/traits) vs. estar (state/location), present tense.

questions.prompt: Ella ___ doctora.
questions.explanation: "es" is right because "ella" is a singular third-person subject and a profession is described with ser, so ser becomes "es".

questions.prompt: Él ___ enfermo hoy.
questions.explanation: "está" is right because being ill today is a temporary state, which uses estar, and "él" takes the third-person singular form.

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ de México.
questions.explanation: "somos" is right because origin ("de México") is expressed with ser, and "nosotros" takes the first-person plural form.

questions.prompt: Ellos ___ en la playa.
questions.explanation: "están" is right because location ("en la playa") uses estar, and "ellos" takes the third-person plural form.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ alto, como mi padre.
questions.explanation: "soy" is right because height is a lasting trait described with ser, and "yo" takes the first-person singular form.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ muy feliz hoy.
questions.explanation: "estás" is right because a feeling like being happy is a temporary state (estar), and "tú" takes the second-person singular form.

questions.prompt: Cuidado, el café ___ caliente.
questions.explanation: "está" is right because the coffee's temperature is a temporary condition, which uses estar, and "el café" is singular third person.

questions.prompt: La casa ___ grande y tiene cinco cuartos.
questions.explanation: "es" is right because size is an inherent characteristic described with ser, and "la casa" is singular third person.

questions.prompt: Nosotras ___ cansadas.
questions.explanation: "estamos" is right because being tired is a temporary state (estar), and "nosotras" takes the first-person plural form.

questions.prompt: Ellas ___ profesoras.
questions.explanation: "son" is right because a profession is identity, which uses ser, and "ellas" takes the third-person plural form.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ en casa.
questions.explanation: "estoy" is right because location ("en casa") uses estar, and "yo" takes the first-person singular form.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ una persona muy inteligente.
questions.explanation: The subject is "Tú" (you, informal), so ser takes the form "eres". Ser is used here because intelligence is a lasting trait, not a temporary state.

questions.prompt: El cielo ___ (estar) nublado.
questions.explanation: "El cielo" is a singular third-person subject, so estar becomes "está". Estar is used because being cloudy is a temporary condition of the sky.

questions.prompt: La fiesta ___ (ser) el sábado.
questions.explanation: "La fiesta" is singular, so ser takes the form "es". Ser is used to say when or where an event takes place, as in "es el sábado".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (estar) listos.
questions.explanation: "Nosotros" (we) requires the form "estamos". Estar is used because being ready is a temporary state.

questions.prompt: Ellos ___ (ser) argentinos.
questions.explanation: "Ellos" (they) requires the form "son". Ser is used because nationality is part of a person's identity.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (ser) profesor.
questions.explanation: "Yo" (I) requires the form "soy". Ser is used to state a profession, which is part of who you are.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (estar) preocupado.
questions.explanation: "Tú" (you, informal) requires the form "estás". Estar is used because being worried is a temporary feeling, not a lasting trait.

questions.prompt: El libro ___ (ser) interesante.
questions.explanation: "El libro" is a singular third-person subject, so ser becomes "es". Ser is used because "interesante" describes a characteristic of the book.

questions.prompt: La sopa ___ (estar) fría.
questions.explanation: "La sopa" is singular, so estar becomes "está". Estar is used because being cold is the soup's current condition, which can change.

questions.prompt: Nosotras ___ (ser) hermanas.
questions.explanation: "Nosotras" (we) requires the form "somos". Ser is used because being sisters is an identity or relationship, not a passing state.

questions.prompt: Ellas ___ (estar) ocupadas.
questions.explanation: "Ellas" (they, feminine) requires the form "están". Estar is used because being busy is a temporary state.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (estar) aburrido.
questions.explanation: "Yo" (I) requires the form "estoy". Estar is used because being bored is a temporary feeling, not a permanent trait.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (ser) muy simpático.
questions.explanation: The subject is "Tú", so ser takes the second-person form "eres"; "es" goes with él/ella/usted and "soy" with yo. Ser fits because simpático describes a personality trait.

questions.prompt: El examen ___ (ser) difícil.
questions.explanation: The subject "El examen" is third person singular, so ser is "es". Ser is used because difícil describes a characteristic of the exam.

units.title: Travel & Transportation
units.description: Getting from A to B — Travel and transportation vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "airplane" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "avión" is the noun for an airplane and is masculine (el avión). Do not confuse it with "volar", which is the verb 'to fly'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "train" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "tren" is the Spanish noun for a train and is masculine (el tren), as in Tomamos el tren a las ocho.

questions.prompt: How do you say "bus" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "autobús" means bus and keeps its accent on the ú. In parts of Latin America you will also hear camión (Mexico) or colectivo (Argentina).

questions.prompt: How do you say "car" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "coche" means car; in much of Latin America you will also hear carro or auto for the same thing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "ship" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "barco" is the word for a ship or boat that travels on water; "avión" flies and "coche" goes on roads.

questions.prompt: How do you say "bicycle" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "bicicleta" means bicycle and is feminine (la bicicleta). People often shorten it to la bici.

questions.prompt: How do you say "ticket" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "boleto" is the Latin American word for a travel ticket, such as a bus or train ticket (in Spain it is billete).

questions.prompt: How do you say "passport" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A passport is "pasaporte"; "tren" is train, "viaje" is trip and "equipaje" is luggage.

questions.prompt: How do you say "suitcase" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "maleta" is the bag you pack clothes in for a trip, so it means suitcase. Aduana means customs and barco means boat.

questions.prompt: How do you say "trip" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "viaje" is the noun for a trip or journey, as in ¡Buen viaje! The related verb is viajar, 'to travel'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to fly" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "volar" is the verb 'to fly', for both birds and planes. It is a stem-changing verb: vuelo, vuelas, vuela.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to arrive" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "llegar" means to arrive, that is, to reach a place; "salir" is to leave and "regresar" is to go back.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to depart" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "partir" means to depart or set off on a journey; "llegar" is its opposite (to arrive).

questions.prompt: How do you say "schedule" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "horario" is the schedule or timetable, for example the times when trains or buses leave.

questions.prompt: How do you say "platform" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "andén" is the platform where you wait for a train or bus, as in El tren sale del andén tres.

questions.prompt: How do you say "seat" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "asiento" is the seat where you sit on a bus, train or plane.

questions.prompt: How do you say "luggage" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "equipaje" means luggage, all the bags you take with you when you travel.

questions.prompt: How do you say "customs" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: At a border or airport, "customs" is the checkpoint where officers inspect your luggage, and in Spanish that is "aduana" (la aduana).

questions.prompt: How do you say "tourist" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A person who travels for pleasure is a "turista"; it ends in -a but is used for both men and women (el turista, la turista).

questions.prompt: How do you say "map" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: The Spanish word for map is "mapa"; note that it is masculine even though it ends in -a, so you say el mapa.

units.title: Commands
units.description: Affirmative and negative tú commands — Informal (tú) imperative mood, affirmative and negative.

questions.prompt: ¡___ (hablar, tú) más despacio!
questions.explanation: An affirmative tú command uses the third-person present form of the verb, so hablar becomes "Habla". "Hables" is the negative command form.

questions.prompt: ¡No ___ (hablar, tú) tan rápido!
questions.explanation: After "No", a tú command switches to the subjunctive form, so hablar becomes "hables". The affirmative "habla" is not used in negative commands.

questions.prompt: ¡___ (comer) tus verduras!
questions.explanation: A positive tú command uses the third-person present form, so comer becomes "Come". "Comas" is the form used after "no".

questions.prompt: ¡No ___ (comer, tú) tanto azúcar!
questions.explanation: A negative tú command uses the subjunctive, so comer becomes "comas" after "No". "Come" is only for affirmative commands.

questions.prompt: ¡___ (abrir, tú) la ventana!
questions.explanation: The affirmative tú command of abrir is the same as the él form of the present tense: "Abre". "Abras" is reserved for negative commands.

questions.prompt: ¡No ___ (abrir, tú) la puerta!
questions.explanation: After "No", the tú command uses the subjunctive form, so abrir becomes "abras". "Abre" would only work without the "no".

questions.prompt: ¡___ (venir, tú) aquí!
questions.explanation: Venir has an irregular affirmative tú command, "Ven", not the regular-looking "Vienes" or the negative form "Vengas". This is a verb to memorize.

questions.prompt: ¡No ___ (venir, tú) tarde!
questions.explanation: A negative tú command uses the subjunctive, so venir becomes "vengas" after "No". The irregular "ven" is only for affirmative commands.

questions.prompt: ¡___ (hacer) tu tarea!
questions.explanation: "Haz" is correct here. Informal (tú) imperative mood, affirmative and negative.

questions.prompt: ¡No ___ (hacer, tú) ruido!
questions.explanation: With "No", the tú command uses the subjunctive, so hacer becomes "hagas". The affirmative "haz" cannot follow "no".

questions.prompt: ¡___ (salir, tú) de aquí!
questions.explanation: The affirmative tú command of "salir" is irregular: it drops the ending and becomes "Sal". "Sales" is the present tense, and "Salgas" and "Salga" are subjunctive forms used for negative or formal commands.

questions.prompt: ¡No ___ (salir, tú) sin abrigo!
questions.explanation: "salgas" is correct here. Informal (tú) imperative mood, affirmative and negative.

questions.prompt: ¡___ (ser, tú) paciente!
questions.explanation: "Sé" is the irregular affirmative tú command of "ser" (with an accent to tell it from "se"). "Seas" is for negative commands, and "Eres" is just the present tense.

questions.prompt: ¡No ___ (ser, tú) grosero!
questions.explanation: After "No", a tú command takes the subjunctive, so "No seas grosero" uses "seas". The affirmative "sé" and the present "eres" do not work in a negative command.

questions.prompt: ¡___ (poner, tú) la mesa!
questions.explanation: The affirmative tú command of "poner" is the irregular short form "Pon". "Pones" is the present tense, and "Pongas" and "Ponga" are subjunctive forms.

questions.prompt: ¡No ___ (poner, tú) los pies en la mesa!
questions.explanation: "pongas" is correct here. Informal (tú) imperative mood, affirmative and negative.

questions.prompt: ¡___ (decir, tú) la verdad!
questions.explanation: The affirmative tú command of "decir" is the irregular one-syllable form "Di". "Dices" is the present tense, and "Digas" is the negative-command (subjunctive) form.

questions.prompt: ¡No ___ (decir, tú) mentiras!
questions.explanation: Negative tú commands use the present subjunctive, so "No digas mentiras" needs "digas". The affirmative "di" and the present "dices" do not fit after "no".

questions.prompt: ¡___ (ir) a tu cuarto!
questions.explanation: The affirmative tú command of "ir" is the irregular "Ve". "Vas" is the present tense, and "Vayas" is the negative-command (subjunctive) form.

questions.prompt: ¡No ___ (ir, tú) solo!
questions.explanation: "vayas" is correct here. Informal (tú) imperative mood, affirmative and negative.

units.title: Direct Object Pronouns
units.description: lo, la, los, las — Direct object pronouns replacing a previously mentioned noun.

questions.prompt: ¿Compraste el pan? Sí, ___ compré.
questions.explanation: "El pan" is masculine singular, so the direct object pronoun that replaces it is "lo". "Los" is plural and "la" is feminine.

questions.prompt: ¿Viste la película? Sí, ___ vi.
questions.explanation: "La película" is feminine singular, so the pronoun that replaces it is "la". "Lo" is masculine, "las" is plural, and "te" means you.

questions.prompt: ¿Tienes los boletos? Sí, ___ tengo.
questions.explanation: The noun being replaced is "los boletos", which is masculine plural, so the object pronoun must be "los".

questions.prompt: ¿Leíste las noticias? Sí, ___ leí.
questions.explanation: "las noticias" is feminine plural, so the pronoun that replaces it is "las".

questions.prompt: ¿Quieres el café? Sí, ___ quiero.
questions.explanation: "el café" is masculine singular, so the pronoun that replaces it is "lo".

questions.prompt: ¿Conoces a María? Sí, ___ conozco.
questions.explanation: "María" is one woman, so the feminine singular pronoun "la" replaces her as the object of "conozco".

questions.prompt: ¿Compraste los zapatos? No, no ___ compré.
questions.explanation: "los zapatos" is masculine plural, so the pronoun before the verb is "los".

questions.prompt: ¿Escribiste las cartas? No, no ___ escribí.
questions.explanation: "las cartas" is feminine plural, so the pronoun that replaces it is "las".

questions.prompt: ¿Puedes ayudarme? Sí, puedo ayudar___.
questions.explanation: The asker says "ayudarme" (help me), so in reply you are helping that person, "you", and the pronoun attaches to the infinitive as "ayudarte" with "te".

questions.prompt: ¿Me llamas mañana? Sí, ___ llamo.
questions.explanation: The question says "Me llamas" (you call me), so the answer is "I call you", and the pronoun for "you" is "te".

questions.prompt: ¿Nos ves el sábado? Sí, ___ veo.
questions.explanation: The askers are a group ("nos" = us), so the reply means "I see you all", and the object pronoun for ustedes is "los".

questions.prompt: ¿Me esperas aquí? Sí, ___ espero.
questions.explanation: The question "¿Me esperas?" means you wait for me, so the answer is "I wait for you", and "you" as an object is "te".

questions.prompt: ¿Trajiste las llaves? Sí, ___ traje.
questions.explanation: "las llaves" is feminine plural, so the pronoun that replaces it is "las".

questions.prompt: ¿Compraste el regalo? No, no ___ compré.
questions.explanation: "el regalo" is masculine singular, so the pronoun placed before "compré" is "lo".

questions.prompt: ¿Terminaste la tarea? Sí, ya ___ terminé.
questions.explanation: "la" replaces "la tarea", which is feminine singular, so the direct object pronoun must be "la" and it goes before the verb "terminé".

units.title: Gustar & Indirect Object Pronouns
units.description: me/te/le/nos/les gusta — "Gustar" and similar verbs (encantar, molestar, interesar) with indirect object pronouns.

questions.prompt: A mí ___ gusta el chocolate.
questions.explanation: "me" matches "A mí": the indirect object pronoun must agree with the person who likes the chocolate, which is "I".

questions.prompt: A ti ___ gusta bailar.
questions.explanation: "te" matches "A ti": with gustar the indirect object pronoun must agree with the person who likes something, here "you" (informal).

questions.prompt: A ella ___ gusta leer.
questions.explanation: "le" matches "A ella": third person singular takes "le" as the indirect object pronoun with gustar.
questions.meaning: to him, to her, to you (formal)

questions.prompt: A nosotros ___ gusta viajar.
questions.explanation: "nos" matches "A nosotros": the pronoun must agree with the people who like something, here "we".

questions.prompt: A ellos ___ gustan los deportes.
questions.explanation: "les" matches "A ellos": third person plural takes "les" as the indirect object pronoun with gustar.

questions.prompt: A mí ___ encanta esta canción.
questions.explanation: "me" matches "A mí": encantar works like gustar, so the pronoun agrees with the person who loves the song, "I".

questions.prompt: A ti ___ molesta el ruido.
questions.explanation: "te" matches "A ti": molestar works like gustar, so the pronoun agrees with the person who is bothered, "you".

questions.prompt: A él ___ interesa la historia.
questions.explanation: "le" matches "A él": interesar works like gustar, and third person singular takes "le".

questions.prompt: A nosotras ___ gustan las películas.
questions.explanation: "nos" matches "A nosotras": the pronoun must agree with "we", while "gustan" agrees with the plural "las películas".

questions.prompt: A ustedes ___ importa el medio ambiente.
questions.explanation: "les" matches "A ustedes": ustedes is third person plural, so it takes "les" as the indirect object pronoun.
questions.meaning: to you all, for you all

questions.prompt: A mí me ___ (gustar) mucho los perros.
questions.explanation: "gustan" agrees with the plural subject "los perros": gustar matches the thing liked, not the person, and "me" is already in the sentence.

questions.prompt: A ella le ___ (encantar) la música clásica.
questions.explanation: The thing loved, "la música clásica", is singular, so encantar agrees with it: "encanta". The pronoun "le" marks who loves it.

questions.prompt: A nosotros nos ___ (faltar) tiempo.
questions.explanation: With faltar, the verb agrees with the thing that is lacking, "tiempo", which is singular: "falta". The "nos" only shows who is short of it.

questions.prompt: A ellos les ___ (quedar) poco dinero.
questions.explanation: Quedar agrees with what is left, "poco dinero", which is singular, so the verb is "queda". The "les" refers to "ellos" but does not change the verb.

questions.prompt: A ti te ___ (doler) la cabeza.
questions.explanation: What hurts is "la cabeza", a singular noun, so doler takes "duele". The "te" shows whose head hurts; it is not the subject.

units.title: Preterite vs. Imperfect
units.description: Choosing the right past tense — Preterite (completed action) vs. imperfect (ongoing/habitual past).

questions.prompt: Cuando era niño, ___ (jugar) todos los días.
questions.explanation: "Cuando era niño" and "todos los días" describe a habit in the past, so you need the imperfect: "jugaba". The preterite would suggest a single completed event.

questions.prompt: Ayer yo ___ (jugar) al fútbol con mis amigos.
questions.explanation: "Ayer" points to one finished event, so the preterite is needed, and "yo" requires the first-person form "jugué". "Jugaba" would suggest a habit, and "jugó" is the he/she form.

questions.prompt: Mientras yo ___ (cocinar), sonó el teléfono.
questions.explanation: "Mientras" sets up an action in progress that was interrupted by the phone ringing ("sonó"), so the background action takes the imperfect: "cocinaba".

questions.prompt: Ella ___ (llamar) a las tres en punto.
questions.explanation: "A las tres en punto" marks one specific completed moment, so the preterite is used, and "ella" needs the third-person singular form "llamó".

questions.prompt: De pequeños, nosotros ___ (vivir) en el campo.
questions.explanation: "De pequeños" describes an ongoing past situation, so the imperfect is needed, and "nosotros" requires the we-form "vivíamos".

questions.prompt: El año pasado, nosotros ___ (mudarnos) a la ciudad.
questions.explanation: "El año pasado" marks a single completed event, so the preterite is needed, and "nosotros" requires the reflexive "nos mudamos". "Nos mudábamos" would describe a repeated or ongoing action.

questions.prompt: Todos los veranos, ellos ___ (visitar) a sus abuelos.
questions.explanation: "Todos los veranos" signals a repeated habit in the past, so the imperfect is needed, and "ellos" requires the they-form "visitaban".

questions.prompt: El verano pasado, ellos ___ (viajar) a Perú.
questions.explanation: "El verano pasado" refers to one completed trip, so the preterite is needed, and "ellos" takes the they-form "viajaron".

questions.prompt: Hacía sol cuando yo ___ (salir) de casa.
questions.explanation: The subject is "yo" and leaving home is a single completed action interrupting the sunny background, so the preterite "salí" (yo form) is needed.

questions.prompt: Eran las diez cuando ___ (empezar) la película.
questions.explanation: The film's start is a single completed event at a point in time, so the preterite is used, and "la película" is singular, giving "empezó".

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (tener) diez años en esa foto.
questions.explanation: Age in a past description ("en esa foto") uses the imperfect, and the subject "yo" takes "tenía".

questions.prompt: De repente, ___ (escuchar) un ruido extraño.
questions.explanation: "De repente" signals a sudden, completed event, so the preterite is needed; the form "escuché" matches the speaker as "yo".

questions.prompt: Todos los días ella ___ (caminar) al trabajo.
questions.explanation: "Todos los días" marks a habitual past action, so the imperfect is used, and "ella" takes "caminaba".

questions.prompt: Anoche nosotros ___ (cenar) en un restaurante nuevo.
questions.explanation: "Anoche" points to one completed event last night, so the preterite is used, and "nosotros" takes "cenamos".

questions.prompt: Mientras ellos ___ (hablar), yo escribía notas.
questions.explanation: "Mientras" with a parallel past action ("yo escribía") calls for the imperfect, and "ellos" takes "hablaban".

units.title: Work & Professions
units.description: Talking about your job — Workplace and profession-related vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "job" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "trabajo" means job or work, as in "Busco trabajo". "Oficina" is the place where you work, and "entrevista" is an interview.

questions.prompt: How do you say "career" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "carrera" means career, as in "una carrera profesional". In Latin America it also often means a university degree program.

questions.prompt: How do you say "company" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "empresa" is the usual word for a company or business, as in "Trabajo en una empresa grande". "Contrato" is a contract.

questions.prompt: How do you say "office" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "oficina" is the room or building where people work at desks; "carrera" means career or degree, and "currículum" is the resume.

questions.prompt: How do you say "boss" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "jefe" means boss; for a woman you say "jefa". "Oficina" is the office and "contrato" is a contract.

questions.prompt: How do you say "colleague" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "colega" means colleague and keeps the same form for men and women: "el colega", "la colega".

questions.prompt: How do you say "salary" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "salario" is the regular money you are paid for your job ("sueldo" is a common synonym); "trabajo" is the job itself, and "horas extra" means overtime.

questions.prompt: How do you say "meeting" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "reunión" means a meeting, as in "Tengo una reunión a las tres". "Entrevista" is an interview.

questions.prompt: How do you say "overtime" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Overtime is "horas extra", literally extra hours, as in "Hoy trabajé horas extra".

questions.prompt: How do you say "resume" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "currículum" is the document listing your experience that you send to employers (in some countries also "hoja de vida"); "entrevista" is the interview, and "empresa" is the company.

questions.prompt: How do you say "interview" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "entrevista" is a formal conversation, such as a job interview; "oficina" is the office, and "contrato" is the contract.

questions.prompt: How do you say "contract" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "contrato" is the written agreement between an employer and an employee; "colega" is a coworker, and "fecha límite" is a deadline.

questions.prompt: How do you say "promotion" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ascenso" means moving up to a higher position at work (from "ascender", to go up); "colega" is a coworker, and "fecha límite" is a deadline.

questions.prompt: How do you say "deadline" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "fecha límite" literally means 'limit date', the last day to finish something; "horas extra" means overtime, and "carrera" means career.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to hire" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "contratar" means to give someone a job; "despedir" is to fire someone, and "renunciar" is to quit.

units.title: Expressions with Tener
units.description: tener que, tener ganas de... — "Tener" idiomatic expressions common in everyday Spanish.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (tener) que estudiar hoy.
questions.explanation: The subject "yo" takes the irregular form "tengo", and "tengo que" + infinitive means 'I have to'.
questions.meaning: I have (tengo que = I have to)

questions.prompt: Ella ___ (tener) ganas de bailar.
questions.explanation: The subject "ella" is third person singular, so "tiene" is used in "tiene ganas de" (feels like).
questions.meaning: she has (tiene ganas de = feels like)

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (tener) miedo de las alturas.
questions.explanation: The subject "nosotros" takes "tenemos", used in "tenemos miedo de" (we are afraid of).

questions.prompt: Ellos ___ (tener) prisa esta mañana.
questions.explanation: The subject "ellos" is third person plural, so "tienen" is used in "tienen prisa" (they are in a hurry).
questions.meaning: they have (tienen prisa: they're in a hurry)

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (tener) razón, como siempre.
questions.explanation: The subject "tú" takes "tienes", used in "tienes razón" (you are right).
questions.meaning: you have; tener razón = to be right

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (tener) sueño después de comer.
questions.explanation: The subject "Yo" takes the first-person form of tener, which is "tengo". The idiom tener sueño means to be sleepy.
questions.meaning: I have; tener sueño = to be sleepy

questions.prompt: Él ___ (tener) éxito en su trabajo.
questions.explanation: "Él" is third-person singular, so tener becomes "tiene". The idiom tener éxito means to be successful.
questions.meaning: he has; tener éxito = to be successful

questions.prompt: Nosotras ___ (tener) suerte hoy.
questions.explanation: "Nosotras" is first-person plural, so tener becomes "tenemos". The idiom tener suerte means to be lucky.
questions.meaning: we have; tener suerte = to be lucky

questions.prompt: Ellas ___ (tener) cuidado con el perro.
questions.explanation: "Ellas" is third-person plural, so tener becomes "tienen". The idiom tener cuidado con means to be careful with.
questions.meaning: they have; tener cuidado = to be careful

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (tener) veinte años.
questions.explanation: "Yo" takes "tengo". Spanish uses tener for age (tener veinte años), where English uses 'to be'.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (tener) que llegar a tiempo.
questions.explanation: "Tú" takes the second-person form "tienes". Tener que plus an infinitive expresses obligation (you have to arrive on time).
questions.meaning: you have; tener que = to have to

questions.prompt: Ella ___ (tener) ganas de un café.
questions.explanation: "Ella" is third-person singular, so tener becomes "tiene". Tener ganas de means to feel like having something.
questions.meaning: she has (tener ganas de: to feel like)

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (tener) que salir ya.
questions.explanation: "Nosotros" takes the first-person plural "tenemos". Tener que plus an infinitive means to have to do something.
questions.meaning: we have; tener que = to have to

questions.prompt: Ellos ___ (tener) frío en invierno.
questions.explanation: "Ellos" is third-person plural, so tener becomes "tienen". The idiom tener frío means to be cold, with tener where English uses 'to be'.
questions.meaning: they have; tener frío = to be cold

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (tener) calor en verano.
questions.explanation: "Yo" takes "tengo". The idiom tener calor means to be hot, with tener where English uses 'to be'.
questions.meaning: I have; tener calor = to be hot

units.title: Technology Verbs
units.description: Using devices and the internet — Verbs for using technology and the internet.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to upload" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "subir" literally means to go up, and online it means to upload a file or photo. Its opposite is "descargar", which means to download.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to download" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "descargar" means to download, as in "descargar una aplicación". To upload is "subir".

questions.prompt: How do you say "to browse" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "navegar" literally means to sail, and it is used for browsing the internet: "navegar por internet".

questions.prompt: How do you say "to search" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "To search" is "buscar", as in buscar en internet; "eliminar" means to delete and "cargar" means to load or charge.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to click" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: To click is "hacer clic", as in "Haz clic aquí". In Mexico you will also hear "dar clic".

questions.prompt: How do you say "to save (a file)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "guardar" means to save a file, as in "Guarda el documento". It also means to keep or put away.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to delete" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "eliminar" means to delete, as in removing a file, photo or message. "cerrar sesión" means to log out, and "hacer clic" means to click.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to share" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "compartir" means to share, for example a post or a link, as in "compartir una foto". "eliminar" means to delete, and "respaldar" means to back up.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to install" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "instalar" means to install a program or app; it looks like the English word. "conectar" means to connect, and "navegar" means to browse.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to update" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "actualizar" means to update software or an app, as in "actualizar el teléfono". "hacer clic" means to click, and "cerrar sesión" means to log out.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to connect" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "conectar" means to connect, as in "conectar a internet". "cargar" means to charge, and "guardar" means to save.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to log in" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "iniciar sesión" means entering an app or website with your username and password; "conectar" is to connect, and "buscar" is to search.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to log out" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cerrar sesión" means to log out; literally it is "to close the session". "descargar" means to download, and "instalar" means to install.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to charge (a device)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cargar" means to charge a phone or laptop, as in "cargar el celular". "respaldar" means to back up, and "eliminar" means to delete.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to back up (data)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: In Latin America, "respaldar" means to back up data, as in "respaldar tus fotos". "cargar" means to charge, and "eliminar" means to delete.

units.title: Household Chores
units.description: hay que / se debe — Impersonal expressions of obligation for household tasks.

questions.prompt: ___ que lavar los platos.
questions.explanation: "Hay" is correct here. Impersonal expressions of obligation for household tasks.
questions.meaning: there is; hay que: one must

questions.prompt: ___ que limpiar la casa.
questions.explanation: "Hay" is correct here. Impersonal expressions of obligation for household tasks.

questions.prompt: Se ___ (deber) sacar la basura.
questions.explanation: With impersonal "se", deber agrees with the thing to be done: "la basura" is singular, so "debe" is right. "Deben" would need a plural noun, and "debes" and "debemos" do not go with "se".
questions.meaning: must, should (se debe = one must, one should)

questions.prompt: Se ___ (deber) barrer el piso.
questions.explanation: With impersonal "se", deber agrees with the thing to be done: "el piso" is singular, so "debe" fits. "Deben" would need a plural noun, and "debes" and "debemos" do not go with "se".

questions.prompt: Hay que ___ la ropa. (iron)
questions.explanation: "Hay que" is always followed by an infinitive, never a conjugated verb, so the blank needs "planchar". "Plancha" and "planchamos" are conjugated forms and do not work after "hay que".

questions.prompt: Hay que ___ la aspiradora. (vacuum)
questions.explanation: "Hay que" must be followed by an infinitive, and the set phrase for vacuuming is "pasar la aspiradora", so "pasar" is right. "Pasa" and "pasamos" are conjugated and cannot follow "hay que".

questions.prompt: Se debe ___ el cuarto. (tidy up)
questions.explanation: After "se debe" the main action must be an infinitive, so the blank takes "ordenar". "Ordena" and "ordenamos" are conjugated forms, which cannot follow the verb deber.
questions.meaning: to tidy up, to put in order

questions.prompt: Hay que ___ la ropa hoy. (wash)
questions.explanation: "Hay que" is followed by an infinitive, so "lavar" completes "hay que lavar la ropa hoy". "Lava" and "lavamos" are conjugated forms that do not fit after "hay que".

questions.prompt: Se deben ___ (regar) las plantas.
questions.explanation: After "se deben" the verb that follows is an infinitive, so the blank needs "regar". "Riega" and "riegan" are conjugated forms and cannot follow deber.
questions.example: Se deben regar las plantas.

questions.prompt: Hay que ___ las camas. (make)
questions.explanation: "Hay que" takes an infinitive, so "hacer" completes "hay que hacer las camas", the usual way to say making the beds. "Hace" and "hacen" are conjugated forms that cannot follow "hay que".

questions.prompt: Se deben ___ (sacudir) los muebles.
questions.explanation: "Se deben" is followed by an infinitive, so the blank takes "sacudir". "Sacude" and "sacuden" are conjugated forms, which cannot follow deber.
questions.example: Se deben sacudir los muebles.

questions.prompt: Hay que ___ los platos. (wash)
questions.explanation: "Hay que" must be followed by an infinitive, so the verb stays unconjugated: "fregar" los platos. "Friega" and "friegan" are conjugated forms and cannot follow "hay que".
questions.example: Hay que fregar el piso.

questions.prompt: Hay que ___ (organizar) el armario.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase "hay que" takes an infinitive, so "organizar" completes "hay que organizar el armario". "Organiza" and "organizan" are conjugated and cannot follow it.

questions.prompt: Se deben ___ (limpiar) las ventanas.
questions.explanation: "Se deben" agrees with the plural "las ventanas" and is followed by an infinitive, so the blank takes "limpiar". "Limpia" and "limpian" are conjugated forms that cannot follow deber.
questions.example: Se deben limpiar las ventanas.

questions.prompt: Hay que ___ la ropa. (hang out to dry)
questions.explanation: After "hay que" Spanish uses the infinitive, so the verb stays unconjugated: "tender". The conjugated forms "tiende" and "tienden" cannot follow this impersonal expression of obligation.

units.title: Sports & Competition
units.description: Games and matches — Sports and competition vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "team" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A team is "equipo"; "árbitro" is referee and "medalla" is medal.

questions.prompt: How do you say "match" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "partido" is a sports match or game, as in "un partido de fútbol". "estadio" is the stadium, and "marcador" is the scoreboard or score.

questions.prompt: How do you say "champion" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "campeón" means champion; the accent goes on the last syllable. "partido" is a match, and "derrota" is a defeat.

questions.prompt: How do you say "championship" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A "championship" is the whole competition that decides the champion, which is "campeonato" (related to "campeón"); a "partido" is just one match.

questions.prompt: How do you say "score" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: In sports, the "score" is the running count of points or goals in a game, which Spanish calls "marcador" (it is also the word for the scoreboard).

questions.prompt: How do you say "goal" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "gol" is a goal scored in a game, borrowed from English. "marcador" is the score, and "uniforme" is the uniform.

questions.prompt: How do you say "referee" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "árbitro" is the referee who enforces the rules in a game; note the accent on the first a. "empate" is a tie, and "campeón" is the champion.

questions.prompt: How do you say "coach" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A sports coach is "entrenador" (from entrenar, to train); it is masculine, el entrenador, and a female coach is la entrenadora.

questions.prompt: How do you say "victory" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "victoria" means a victory or win in a match; "equipo" is team and "entrenador" is coach.

questions.prompt: How do you say "defeat" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A defeat in a game or competition is "derrota" (la derrota), from derrotar, to defeat; its opposite is la victoria.

questions.prompt: How do you say "tie" (a game that ends level) in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A game where both teams finish with the same score is an "empate" (from "empatar"); a necktie would be "corbata".

questions.prompt: How do you say "stadium" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "estadio" is the stadium where a match is played; "campeón" is champion and "derrota" is defeat.

questions.prompt: How do you say "uniform" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A uniform is "uniforme", a cognate; "empate" means a draw or tie and "campeonato" means championship.

questions.prompt: How do you say "medal" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A medal is "medalla" (la medalla), spelled with a double l, as in medalla de oro, gold medal.

questions.prompt: How do you say "tournament" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "torneo" is the word for a tournament, a competition with several rounds of matches; "árbitro" is the referee and "medalla" is a medal.

units.title: Making Plans & Invitations
units.description: Suggesting and agreeing — Phrases for making plans and invitations.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Do you want to go out?" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¿Quieres salir?" uses querer + infinitive to invite a friend; "salir" means to go out, and "quieres" is the friendly tú form.

questions.prompt: How do you say "What are you doing this weekend?" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¿Qué haces este fin de semana?" asks about someone's plans; Spanish uses the simple present "haces" where English says "are you doing".

questions.prompt: How do you say "Want to grab a coffee?" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¿Quieres tomar un café?" is the natural way to invite someone for coffee; Spanish uses "tomar" (to have) for drinks where English says "grab".

questions.prompt: How do you say "I'm free on Saturday" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Estoy libre el sábado" uses estar because being free is a temporary state, and "el sábado" means "on Saturday" with no word for "on".

questions.prompt: How do you say "Sounds good" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Suena bien" is the usual reply to accept a plan; it is literally "it sounds good", from the verb sonar.

questions.prompt: How do you say "I can't, I'm busy" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "No puedo, estoy ocupado" turns down an invitation; it uses estar for a temporary state, and a woman would say "ocupada".

questions.prompt: How do you say "Maybe another time" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Quizás otro día" softly declines while leaving the door open; "quizás" means maybe and "otro día" is literally "another day".

questions.prompt: How do you say "Let's meet at eight" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Nos vemos a las ocho" sets the meeting time: "nos vemos" means "we'll see each other" and "a las ocho" means "at eight".

questions.prompt: How do you say "Where should we meet?" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¿Dónde nos encontramos?" asks where to meet up; "dónde" asks about a place and "nos encontramos" means "we meet".

questions.prompt: How do you say "I'll pick you up" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Paso por ti" uses pasar por (to come by for someone) to mean "I'll pick you up"; the present tense here refers to the near future.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Count me in" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Cuenta conmigo" comes from contar con (to count on) and is the usual way to say you're in on a plan.

questions.prompt: How do you say "I'll think about it" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Lo voy a pensar" uses ir a + infinitive for a near-future intention, and "lo" stands for the invitation, so it means "I'll think about it."

questions.prompt: How do you say "See you then" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Nos vemos entonces" uses "entonces" for "then", pointing back to a time already agreed; "Nos vemos a las ocho" names a specific time instead.

questions.prompt: How do you say "I'll text you" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Te escribo un mensaje" uses the present tense for a near-future promise, and te means "(to) you"; Te mando un mensaje is also common.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Let's do it another day" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Lo hacemos otro día" uses the present tense of hacer with nosotros to suggest a plan, and lo means "it"; otro día means another day, with no un before otro.

units.title: Life Events
units.description: Milestones — Vocabulary for major life events.

questions.prompt: How do you say "birth" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Birth is "nacimiento" (el nacimiento), from nacer, to be born; aniversario means anniversary and infancia means childhood.

questions.prompt: How do you say "childhood" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Childhood is "infancia" (la infancia), a false friend that covers all of childhood, not only infancy.

questions.prompt: How do you say "graduation" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Graduation is "graduación" (la graduación); like most -ción words, it is feminine and carries an accent on the ó.

questions.prompt: How do you say "wedding" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A wedding is "boda" (la boda), the celebration; the marriage itself is el matrimonio.

questions.prompt: How do you say "engagement" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: An engagement to marry is "compromiso" (el compromiso), and the same word also means commitment; embarazo is pregnancy, a false friend.

questions.prompt: How do you say "divorce" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: divorce → divorcio. Vocabulary for major life events.

questions.prompt: How do you say "retirement" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: retirement → jubilación. Vocabulary for major life events.

questions.prompt: Which Spanish word names the ceremony held after someone dies?
questions.explanation: "funeral" is the ceremony for someone who has died (it is spelled the same as in English); "boda" is a wedding and "madrastra" a stepmother.

questions.prompt: How do you say "anniversary" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: anniversary → aniversario. Vocabulary for major life events.

questions.prompt: How do you say "pregnancy" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: pregnancy → embarazo. Vocabulary for major life events.

questions.prompt: How do you say "in-laws" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: in-laws → suegros. Vocabulary for major life events.

questions.prompt: How do you say "stepmother" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "madrastra" means "stepmother"; "padrastro" is stepfather and "hijastra" is stepdaughter.

questions.prompt: How do you say "stepfather" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: stepfather → padrastro. Vocabulary for major life events.

questions.prompt: How do you say "widow" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: widow → viuda. Vocabulary for major life events.

questions.prompt: How do you say "adulthood" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: adulthood → adultez. Vocabulary for major life events.

units.title: Emotional Reactions
units.description: Reacting to news — Phrases for reacting emotionally to news or events.

questions.prompt: How do you say "What great news!" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¡Qué buena noticia!" follows the pattern ¡Qué + adjective + noun! to react to good news; "¡Qué alivio!" means 'What a relief!' instead.

questions.prompt: How do you say "I'm so sorry" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: I'm so sorry → Lo siento mucho. Phrases for reacting emotionally to news or events.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Congratulations!" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Congratulations! → ¡Felicidades!. Phrases for reacting emotionally to news or events.

questions.prompt: How do you say "That's terrible" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Eso es terrible" is the word-for-word match for 'That's terrible' (eso = that, es = is); "¡Qué lástima!" is softer and means 'What a shame'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "I can't believe it" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "No puedo creerlo" is word for word "I can't believe it": poder + creer, with "lo" (it) attached to the end of the infinitive.

questions.prompt: How do you say "How exciting!" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Spanish says "¡Qué emoción!" (literally "What excitement!"), using qué + noun where English uses "How" + adjective.

questions.prompt: How do you say "That's a relief" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: That's a relief → Qué alivio. Phrases for reacting emotionally to news or events.

questions.prompt: How do you say "I'm speechless" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Spanish reacts with the preterite "Me quedé sin palabras" (literally "I was left without words"), which is the everyday way to say "I'm speechless."

questions.prompt: How do you say "What a shame" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: What a shame → Qué lástima. Phrases for reacting emotionally to news or events.

questions.prompt: How do you say "I'm thrilled for you" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Estoy feliz por ti" uses estar for a feeling and "por ti" for "for you", so it shares someone's good news; "Qué lástima" and "Lo siento mucho" react to bad news.

questions.prompt: How do you say "That worries me" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Eso me preocupa" works like gustar: "eso" (that) is the subject that worries, and "me" is the person who is worried.

questions.prompt: How do you say "It doesn't matter" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "No importa" means "It doesn't matter"; Spanish drops the subject "it" and just uses no + importa.

questions.prompt: How do you say "That makes sense" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Spanish says "Eso tiene sentido" (literally "that has sense"), with tener, not hacer, for "makes sense".

questions.prompt: How do you say "I'm proud of you" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Estoy orgulloso de ti" uses estar + orgulloso de for "proud of"; a woman says "orgullosa" because the adjective agrees with the speaker.

questions.prompt: How do you say "What a surprise!" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¡Qué sorpresa!" means "What a surprise!": qué + noun forms the exclamation, and "sorpresa" is surprise.

units.title: Furniture & Home Structure
units.description: Around the house, part 2 — Furniture and parts of a house.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sofa" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "sofá" is the long padded seat in a living room; note the written accent on the final á.

questions.prompt: How do you say "cushion" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cojín" is a soft cushion you put on a sofa or chair; it is written with an accent on the í.

questions.prompt: How do you say "rug" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "alfombra" is the floor covering for a rug or carpet; "almohada" is a pillow, "timbre" a doorbell and "pared" a wall.

questions.prompt: How do you say "doorbell" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "timbre" is the bell at the front door; to ring it is "tocar el timbre".

questions.prompt: How do you say "windowsill" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "alféizar" is the ledge at the bottom of a window; note the accent on the é.

questions.prompt: How do you say "fireplace" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A fireplace is "chimenea" (the same word also means chimney). Don't confuse it with "tejado", which is the roof.

questions.prompt: How do you say "wardrobe" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A wardrobe is "armario"; in much of Latin America you will also hear "clóset" or "ropero" for the same piece of furniture.

questions.prompt: How do you say "nightstand" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A nightstand is "mesita de noche", the small table beside the bed; many Latin Americans also say "mesa de noche" (or "buró" in Mexico).

questions.prompt: How do you say "mattress" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A mattress is "colchón", the soft part of the bed you sleep on; note the accent on the final -ón.

questions.prompt: How do you say "blanket" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "manta" is the warm cover for a bed or sofa (in much of Latin America people also say "cobija" or "frazada"); "cojín" is a cushion.

questions.prompt: How do you say "pillow" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "almohada" is the pillow you rest your head on in bed; "colchón" is the mattress and "sábana" the sheet.

questions.prompt: How do you say "towel" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A towel is "toalla", spelled with -ll-; it is a household item you dry yourself with, not furniture.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sink" (in the kitchen) in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A kitchen sink is "fregadero"; the bathroom sink is a different word, "lavabo" or "lavamanos".

questions.prompt: How do you say "faucet" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "grifo" is the faucet where water comes out; in much of Latin America people also say "llave" (Mexico, Colombia) or "canilla" (Argentina).

questions.prompt: How do you say "stairs" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Stairs are "escalera" (often used in the plural, "escaleras"); "ascensor" is the elevator, not the stairs.

questions.prompt: How do you say "ceiling" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: The ceiling is "techo"; "tejado" is the outside tiled roof, although in Latin America "techo" is used for both.

questions.prompt: How do you say "floor" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: The floor you walk on is "suelo"; in most of Latin America people more often say "piso" for the same thing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "wall" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A wall of a room or house is "pared", a feminine noun (la pared).

questions.prompt: How do you say "roof" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "tejado" is the outer roof of a house, usually covered with tiles; in Latin America "techo" is also very common for roof.

questions.prompt: How do you say "fence" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A fence is "cerca" (la cerca); don't confuse it with the adverb cerca meaning "near". You may also hear "valla" or "reja".

questions.prompt: How do you say "garage" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A garage is "garaje", spelled with a j (not g) before the final -e.

questions.prompt: How do you say "balcony" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: balcony → balcón. Furniture and parts of a house.

questions.prompt: How do you say "elevator" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: elevator → ascensor. Furniture and parts of a house.

questions.prompt: How do you say "basement" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: basement → sótano. Furniture and parts of a house.

questions.prompt: How do you say "attic" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ático" is the space under the roof at the top of a house; in Spain it can also mean a top-floor apartment, and "desván" is a synonym.

units.title: Reflexive Verbs of Emotion
units.description: More reflexive verbs of feeling — Reflexive verbs describing emotional reactions.

questions.prompt: Yo me ___ (enamorarse) fácilmente.
questions.explanation: The subject "yo" (with "me") takes the first-person singular ending -o, giving "enamoro". The other forms belong to nosotros, tú and ella.

questions.prompt: Tú te ___ (frustrarse) cuando algo no funciona.
questions.explanation: "Tú te" requires the second-person singular ending -as, so frustrarse becomes "frustras". The other endings match yo, nosotros or ella.

questions.prompt: Ella se ___ (calmarse) después de respirar.
questions.explanation: "Ella se" is third-person singular, so the -ar verb takes -a: "calma". "Calman" would need a plural subject like "ellos".

questions.prompt: Nosotros nos ___ (emocionarse) con las buenas noticias.
questions.explanation: "Nosotros nos" calls for the first-person plural ending -amos, giving "emocionamos". The other forms match yo, ellos and tú.

questions.prompt: Ellos se ___ (aburrirse) en clases largas.
questions.explanation: "Ellos se" is third-person plural, so the -ir verb ends in -en: "aburren". "Aburre" would go with a singular subject.

questions.prompt: Yo me ___ (preocuparse) por mi familia.
questions.explanation: "Yo me" takes the first-person singular ending -o, so preocuparse becomes "preocupo". The other forms are for tú, ella and ellos.

questions.prompt: Tú te ___ (sorprenderse) con los regalos.
questions.explanation: "Tú te" needs the second-person singular ending of an -er verb, -es: "sorprendes". "Sorprendo" would go with "yo".
questions.meaning: you are surprised, you get surprised

questions.prompt: Ella se ___ (entristecerse) con las despedidas.
questions.explanation: "Ella se" is third-person singular, so entristecerse takes -e: "entristece". "Entristezco" is the yo form and "entristecen" is plural.
questions.meaning: she gets sad, she is saddened

questions.prompt: Nosotros nos ___ (alegrarse) de verte.
questions.explanation: "Nosotros nos" requires the first-person plural ending -amos, giving "alegramos". The other forms match ellos, tú and ella.
questions.meaning: we are glad, we are happy

questions.prompt: Ellos se ___ (enojarse) por pequeñas cosas.
questions.explanation: "Ellos se" is third-person plural, so the -ar verb ends in -an: "enojan". The other endings fit nosotros, tú and yo.

questions.prompt: Yo me ___ (sentirse) mejor ahora.
questions.explanation: "Yo me" takes the first-person singular form of sentirse, which changes its stem to ie and ends in -o: "siento". "Sentimos" is the nosotros form.

questions.prompt: Tú te ___ (relajarse) los fines de semana.
questions.explanation: The subject "Tú" and the pronoun "te" call for the second-person singular ending -as, so the verb is "relajas".

questions.prompt: Ella se ___ (avergonzarse) fácilmente.
questions.explanation: "Ella se" needs the third-person singular, and avergonzarse changes o to üe in the stem, giving "avergüenza".
questions.meaning: she gets embarrassed, she is ashamed

questions.prompt: Nosotros nos ___ (divertirse) en las fiestas.
questions.explanation: "Nosotros nos" takes the -imos ending, and in the nosotros form divertirse keeps its stem (no e to ie change), so it is "divertimos".
questions.meaning: we have fun, we enjoy ourselves

questions.prompt: Ellos se ___ (cansarse) rápido.
questions.explanation: "Ellos se" needs the third-person plural ending -an, giving "cansan".

questions.prompt: Yo me ___ (estresarse) antes de los exámenes.
questions.explanation: "Yo me" takes the first-person singular ending -o, so estresarse becomes "estreso".

questions.prompt: Tú te ___ (acostumbrarse) a la rutina.
questions.explanation: "Tú te" needs the second-person singular ending -as, so acostumbrarse becomes "acostumbras".

questions.prompt: Ella se ___ (interesarse) por el arte.
questions.explanation: "Ella se" is third-person singular, so interesarse takes the ending -a: "interesa".
questions.meaning: she is interested, she takes an interest

questions.prompt: Nosotros no nos ___ (arrepentirse) de nada.
questions.explanation: "Nosotros nos" takes -imos, and arrepentirse does not change its stem in the nosotros form, so it is "arrepentimos".
questions.meaning: we regret, we are sorry for
questions.example: Nosotros nos arrepentimos de lo que dijimos.

questions.prompt: Ellos se ___ (quejarse) del clima.
questions.explanation: "Ellos se" needs the third-person plural ending -an, so quejarse becomes "quejan".

questions.prompt: Yo me ___ (impacientarse) en las filas.
questions.explanation: "Yo me" takes the first-person singular ending -o, so impacientarse becomes "impaciento".

questions.prompt: Tú te ___ (asustarse) con las películas de terror.
questions.explanation: "Tú te" needs the second-person singular ending -as, so asustarse becomes "asustas".
questions.meaning: you get scared, you are frightened

questions.prompt: Ella se ___ (concentrarse) al estudiar.
questions.explanation: "Ella se" is third-person singular, so concentrarse takes the ending -a: "concentra".

questions.prompt: Nosotros nos ___ (esforzarse) para mejorar.
questions.explanation: The subject "Nosotros" and the reflexive "nos" call for the nosotros form of esforzarse, which keeps its o in the stem: "esforzamos".
questions.meaning: we make an effort, we try hard

questions.prompt: Ellos se ___ (motivarse) antes del partido.
questions.explanation: The subject "Ellos" and the reflexive "se" need the third-person plural ending -an, giving "motivan".
questions.meaning: they get motivated, they psych themselves up

units.title: Nature & Landscape
units.description: Geographic features — Landscape and geography vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "valley" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: valley → valle. Landscape and geography vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "cliff" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "acantilado" means "cliff": a steep, high rock face, usually beside the sea.

questions.prompt: How do you say "cave" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: cave → cueva. Landscape and geography vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "waterfall" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cascada" means "waterfall": water falling from a height, as in a river.

questions.prompt: How do you say "volcano" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: volcano → volcán. Landscape and geography vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "desert" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "desierto" means "desert", a very dry area with little rain; a "duna" is only a sand hill inside it.

questions.prompt: How do you say "jungle" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: jungle → selva. Landscape and geography vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "swamp" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "pantano" means "swamp": low, wet land covered with shallow water and plants.

questions.prompt: How do you say "glacier" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "glaciar" means "glacier", a huge mass of ice that moves slowly down a mountain; note the Spanish spelling ends in -ar.

questions.prompt: How do you say "canyon" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: canyon → cañón. Landscape and geography vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "plain" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: plain → llanura. Landscape and geography vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "hill" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: hill → colina. Landscape and geography vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "peninsula" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Peninsula" is "península". Note the written accent on the í, because the stress falls on the third-to-last syllable (pe-NÍN-su-la).

questions.prompt: How do you say "bay" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: bay → bahía. Landscape and geography vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "coast" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Coast" is "costa", a feminine noun (la costa), as in "vivimos en la costa".

questions.prompt: How do you say "cape (geography)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: cape (geography) → cabo. Landscape and geography vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "reef" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "arrecife" is the Spanish word for a reef, a ridge of rock or coral near the surface of the sea; the other words mean swamp, archipelago and coast.

questions.prompt: How do you say "dune" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Dune" is "duna", a feminine noun (la duna), a hill of sand formed by the wind.

questions.prompt: How do you say "meadow" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "prado" means a meadow, a grassy field; the other words mean swamp, dune and valley.

questions.prompt: How do you say "stream" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "arroyo" means a stream, a small natural flow of water; the other words mean volcano, hill and meadow.

questions.prompt: How do you say "pond" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "estanque" means a pond, a small body of still water; the other words mean volcano, hill and meadow.

questions.prompt: How do you say "plateau" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "meseta" means a plateau, a high area of flat land; the other words mean cape, desert and delta.

questions.prompt: How do you say "archipelago" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Archipelago" is "archipiélago". It carries a written accent on the é because the stress falls on the third-to-last syllable.

questions.prompt: How do you say "bay" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Bay" is "bahía". The accent on the í splits the vowels into separate syllables (ba-hí-a).

questions.prompt: How do you say "tundra" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Spanish uses the same word, "tundra" (la tundra), for the cold, treeless plains of the Arctic.

units.title: Common Reactions
units.description: Interjections and exclamations — Common interjections and reaction phrases.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Wow!" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¡Guau!" is the Spanish way to say "Wow!" when you are impressed. ¡Uy! is closer to "Oops!" and ¡No puede ser! to "No way!"

questions.prompt: How do you say "Ouch!" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¡Ay!" is what Spanish speakers say when something hurts, like "Ouch!"; "¡Guau!" expresses amazement instead.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Oh no!" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Oh no! → ¡Oh no!. Common interjections and reaction phrases.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Really?" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¿En serio?" (literally "Seriously?") is how you react with surprise or doubt, like "Really?"; note the question marks.

questions.prompt: How do you say "No way!" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¡No puede ser!" literally means "It can't be!" and expresses disbelief, just like "No way!"

questions.prompt: How do you say "Come on!" (cheering someone on) in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¡Vamos!" (literally "let's go") is what you shout to encourage someone, like "Come on!" at a game.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Watch out!" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¡Cuidado!" (literally "care!") warns someone of danger, like "Watch out!".

questions.prompt: How do you say "Hurry!" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¡Rápido!" ("Quick!") is how you tell someone to hurry. ¡Cuidado! is a warning and ¡Claro! means "Of course!"

questions.prompt: How do you say "Wait!" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¡Espera!" is the tú command of esperar (to wait), used to tell a friend to stop and wait.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Help!" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¡Ayuda!" comes from ayudar (to help) and is how you call for help; "¡Socorro!" is also used in emergencies.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Cheers! (toast)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¡Salud!" (literally "health!") is what you say when raising a glass for a toast; it is also said after someone sneezes.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Bless you! (sneeze)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: When someone sneezes, Spanish speakers say "¡Salud!" (literally "Health!"), the equivalent of "Bless you!"

questions.prompt: How do you say "Good grief!" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¡Vaya!" is the everyday Spanish reaction of mild surprise or exasperation, like "Good grief!"; "¡Ay!" is more for pain or worry.

questions.prompt: How do you say "That's enough!" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¡Ya basta!" comes from bastar (to be enough) and is used to tell someone to stop, like "That's enough!".

questions.prompt: How do you say "Of course!" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¡Claro!" (literally "clear!") is the everyday way to say "Of course!" when agreeing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Exactly!" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¡Exacto!" is how you strongly agree that something is right, like "Exactly!"; "¡No me digas!" shows surprise instead.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Not again!" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¡Otra vez no!" is literally "another time, no!", which is how Spanish speakers complain that something bad is happening again. "¡Basta ya!" means "enough!", not "again".

questions.prompt: How do you say "Finally!" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¡Por fin!" (literally "at last!") is the set phrase for relief when something you waited for finally happens.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Look out!" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¡Ojo!" literally means "Eye!" and is a quick informal warning to pay attention, like "Look out!".

questions.prompt: How do you say "What a mess!" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¡Qué desastre!" uses "qué" + noun to make an exclamation ("what a disaster!"), the usual way to react to a mess.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Poor thing!" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¡Pobrecito!" shows sympathy for someone, like "Poor thing!"; say "¡Pobrecita!" for a girl or woman.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Yikes!" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¡Uy!" is a short wince of alarm or embarrassment, like "Yikes!"; "¡Guau!" expresses admiration instead.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Well done!" (applauding someone) in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¡Bravo!" is what Spanish speakers shout to applaud a good performance, like "Well done!".

questions.prompt: How do you say "Enough already!" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¡Basta ya!" comes from "bastar" (to be enough), so it says "that's enough already!". "¡Otra vez no!" means "not again!".

questions.prompt: How do you say "No kidding!" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¡No me digas!" literally means "Don't tell me!" and is the usual reaction of surprise, like "No kidding!".

units.title: Cooking & Recipes
units.description: Kitchen vocabulary, advanced — Vocabulary for recipes and cooking technique.

questions.prompt: How do you say "recipe" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A recipe is "receta", the same word used for a doctor's prescription; "caldo" is broth.

questions.prompt: How do you say "ingredient" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "ingrediente" is the Spanish word for each item a recipe uses; it is masculine: el ingrediente.

questions.prompt: How do you say "portion" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "porción" means a serving or share of food, like "portion"; it is feminine: una porción.

questions.prompt: How do you say "teaspoon" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cucharadita" is the small diminutive of "cucharada" (tablespoon), so it means teaspoon in recipes.

questions.prompt: How do you say "tablespoon" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cucharada" is a spoonful measured with a full spoon, the tablespoon in recipes; the small one is "cucharadita".

questions.prompt: How do you say "cup (measure)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "taza" means cup, both the drinking cup and the cup used as a measure in recipes, as in "una taza de harina".

questions.prompt: How do you say "oven-safe" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "apto para horno" literally means "suitable for the oven", the label on dishes that can go in the oven.

questions.prompt: How do you say "boiling" (as in boiling point) in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "ebullición" is the noun for boiling, as in punto de ebullición (boiling point); the verb is hervir.

questions.prompt: How do you say "simmer" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: simmer → fuego lento. Vocabulary for recipes and cooking technique.

questions.prompt: How do you say "marinate" in Spanish? ___
