questions.explanation: "marinar" is the verb for soaking food in a seasoned liquid before cooking, like English "marinate".

questions.prompt: How do you say "season (verb)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "sazonar" is the verb for adding salt, pepper or spices to food; "hornear" means to bake, "rallar" to grate and "picar" to chop.

questions.prompt: How do you say "garnish" (a dish, verb) in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "decorar" is the verb recipes use for garnishing a dish, as in decorar con perejil (garnish with parsley).

questions.prompt: How do you say "dough" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Dough is "masa", the soft mix of flour and water used for bread, pizza or tortillas (masa de maíz).

questions.prompt: How do you say "broth" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Broth is "caldo", the liquid made by simmering meat, bones or vegetables, as in caldo de pollo.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sauce" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Sauce is "salsa"; in Latin America it means any sauce, not only the spicy dip English calls salsa.

questions.prompt: How do you say "spice" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Spice is "especia", like cinnamon or cumin; don't confuse it with "especie", which means species.

questions.prompt: How do you say "herb" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Herb is "hierba", as in hierbas aromáticas such as basil or parsley; the h is silent.

questions.prompt: How do you say "flavor" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Flavor is "sabor", a masculine noun: el sabor, as in ¿Qué sabor tiene?

questions.prompt: How do you say "texture" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Texture is "textura", a feminine noun: la textura, as in una textura suave.

questions.prompt: How do you say "crispy" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Crispy is "crujiente", from crujir (to crunch); it has the same form for masculine and feminine nouns.

questions.prompt: How do you say "tender" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "tierno" describes food that is soft and easy to cut or chew, like tender meat; "bien cocido" only means cooked through.

questions.prompt: How do you say "well-done (meat)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Well-done meat is "bien cocido", literally well cooked; it agrees with the noun, so you say la carne bien cocida.

questions.prompt: How do you say "rare (meat)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "poco cocido" describes meat cooked only briefly so it stays red inside, which is rare; "término medio" means medium.

questions.prompt: How do you say "medium (meat)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Medium meat is "término medio", the standard Latin American way to order a steak cooked halfway.

questions.prompt: How do you say "leftovers" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Leftovers are "sobras", the food left after a meal; like the English word, it is normally plural.

units.title: Adjective + Preposition Combos
units.description: Fixed adjective-preposition pairings — Common adjectives paired with a specific preposition.

questions.prompt: Estoy interesado ___ (in) la música.
questions.explanation: The adjective interesado takes the preposition "en" (interesado en = interested in), so you say interesado en la música.

questions.prompt: Estoy cansado ___ (of) trabajar tanto.
questions.explanation: Cansado is followed by "de" to mean tired of something (cansado de trabajar), not a, por or en.

questions.prompt: Estoy contento ___ (with) los resultados.
questions.explanation: Contento takes "con" to say what you are happy with (contento con los resultados).

questions.prompt: Ella está enamorada ___ (of) él.
questions.explanation: Enamorada is followed by "de" for the person you love (enamorada de él), never en or a.

questions.prompt: Estamos preocupados ___ (about) el examen.
questions.explanation: Preocupado takes "por" for the thing that worries you (preocupados por el examen).

questions.prompt: Él es responsable ___ (for) el proyecto.
questions.explanation: Responsable takes "de" for what you are in charge of (responsable del proyecto, with de + el contracting to del).
questions.example: Él es responsable del proyecto.

questions.prompt: Estoy seguro ___ (of) mi decisión.
questions.explanation: Seguro takes "de" to say what you are sure about (seguro de mi decisión).

questions.prompt: Ella está orgullosa ___ (of) su hijo.
questions.explanation: Orgulloso/a is followed by "de" for the source of pride (orgullosa de su hijo).

questions.prompt: Estamos listos ___ (for) el viaje.
questions.explanation: Listo pairs with "para" to mean ready for something (listos para el viaje); para marks the purpose or event you are ready for, unlike por.

questions.prompt: Él es bueno ___ (at) matemáticas.
questions.explanation: Bueno takes "en" for a skill or subject (bueno en matemáticas), not a, de or por.

questions.prompt: Estoy acostumbrado ___ este clima.
questions.explanation: The adjective "acostumbrado" takes the preposition "a" (acostumbrado a = used to), so the sentence reads "Estoy acostumbrado a este clima."

questions.prompt: Ella es diferente ___ (from) su hermana.
questions.explanation: "diferente" is paired with "de" to mean different from, so you say "diferente de su hermana".

questions.prompt: Estamos emocionados ___ (about) las vacaciones.
questions.explanation: "emocionado" is followed by "por" when you are excited about something, so you say "emocionados por las vacaciones".

questions.prompt: Él es amable ___ (with) todos.
questions.explanation: "amable" takes "con" for the person you are kind to, so "amable con todos" means kind to everyone.

questions.prompt: Estoy harto ___ (of) esperar.
questions.explanation: "harto" is followed by "de" to mean fed up with, so you say "harto de esperar" before an infinitive.

questions.prompt: Ella es capaz ___ (of) hacerlo sola.
questions.explanation: "capaz" is followed by "de" before an infinitive, so "capaz de hacerlo sola" means capable of doing it alone.

questions.prompt: Estamos agradecidos ___ (for) su ayuda.
questions.explanation: "agradecido" uses "por" to introduce what you are grateful for, so you say "agradecidos por su ayuda".

questions.prompt: Él es fiel ___ (to) sus principios.
questions.explanation: "fiel" takes "a" for the thing you stay loyal to, so you say "fiel a sus principios".

questions.prompt: Estoy dispuesto ___ (to) ayudar.
questions.explanation: "dispuesto" is followed by "a" plus an infinitive to mean willing to, so you say "dispuesto a ayudar".

questions.prompt: Ella es similar ___ (to) su madre.
questions.explanation: "similar" takes "a" for the thing being compared, so you say "similar a su madre" for similar to her mother.

questions.prompt: Estamos preocupados ___ (about) los resultados.
questions.explanation: "Preocupado" takes "por" to introduce what you are worried about, so you say "preocupados por los resultados".

questions.prompt: Él es alérgico ___ (to) los gatos.
questions.explanation: "alérgico" takes "a" for the thing that causes the allergy, so you say "alérgico a los gatos".

questions.prompt: Estoy libre ___ (of) compromisos.
questions.explanation: The adjective "libre" takes the preposition "de" to mean 'free of' something, so "libre de compromisos" means free of commitments.

questions.prompt: Ella es amable ___ (with) los niños.
questions.explanation: The adjective "amable" takes "con" before the people you are kind to, so "amable con los niños" means kind to the children.

questions.prompt: Estamos satisfechos ___ (with) el servicio.
questions.explanation: "Satisfecho" is followed by "con" for the thing you are happy about, so we say "satisfechos con el servicio".

units.title: Speaking: Opinions & Feelings
units.description: Say it out loud — Opinions, feelings, and hypotheticals to practise saying.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "Creo que tienes razón." Opinions, feelings, and hypotheticals to practise saying.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: En mi opinión, es una buena idea.
questions.explanation: "En mi opinión, es una buena idea." means "In my opinion, it's a good idea"; "En mi opinión" is a neutral way to introduce what you think.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Me parece interesante." means "I find it interesting"; "me parece" works like gustar, with the thing as the subject and "me" for the person giving the opinion.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "No estoy de acuerdo contigo." means "I don't agree with you"; it uses estar ("estoy de acuerdo"), and "contigo" is the tú form, for a friend or family member.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Depende de la situación." means "It depends on the situation"; Spanish uses "de" after depender, not "en".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Me siento un poco cansado hoy.
questions.explanation: "Me siento un poco cansado hoy." means "I feel a bit tired today"; sentirse needs "me", and a woman would say "cansada".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Estoy muy contento con los resultados.
questions.explanation: "Estoy muy contento con los resultados." means "I'm very happy with the results"; feelings take estar, and a woman would say "contenta".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Me preocupa el examen de mañana.
questions.explanation: "Me preocupa el examen de mañana." means "I'm worried about tomorrow's exam"; like gustar, the exam is the subject and "me" is the person who is worried.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Espero que todo salga bien." means "I hope everything turns out well"; "espero que" expresses a wish, so it takes the subjunctive "salga".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Ojalá pudiera ayudarte." means "I wish I could help you"; ojalá with the past subjunctive "pudiera" expresses a wish that is unlikely or impossible.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Es posible que llueva esta tarde.
questions.explanation: "Es posible que llueva esta tarde." means "It might rain this afternoon"; "es posible que" expresses uncertainty, so it takes the subjunctive "llueva".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Dudo que llegue a tiempo." means "I doubt he or she will arrive on time"; "dudo que" expresses doubt, so it takes the subjunctive "llegue".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Prefiero quedarme en casa." means "I'd rather stay home"; preferir is followed directly by an infinitive, here "quedarme" with the pronoun attached.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Me gustaría aprender a tocar la guitarra.
questions.explanation: "Me gustaría aprender a tocar la guitarra." uses "me gustaría" (the conditional of gustar) to say politely what you would like, and "aprender a" is always followed by an infinitive.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Si tuviera tiempo, viajaría más." describes an imaginary situation, so "si" takes the imperfect subjunctive ("tuviera") and the result takes the conditional ("viajaría").

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Cuando era niño, vivía en el campo.
questions.explanation: "Cuando era niño, vivía en el campo." uses the imperfect ("era", "vivía") because it describes an ongoing situation in the past, not a single completed event.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "Antes trabajaba en una oficina." The imperfect "trabajaba" with "antes" describes what you used to do in the past.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "Ahora trabajo desde casa." The present "trabajo" with "ahora" contrasts your current situation with how things used to be.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "He decidido cambiar de trabajo." The present perfect "he decidido" presents a recent decision that still matters now.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Todavía no he terminado el proyecto.
questions.explanation: "Todavía no he terminado el proyecto." uses "todavía no" with the present perfect "he terminado" to say something is still not finished.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Ya he leído ese libro." uses "ya" with the present perfect "he leído" to say you have already done something.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Nunca he estado en Argentina." uses "nunca" with the present perfect "he estado" to say you have never had that experience.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Siempre digo la verdad." uses "siempre" with the present tense to describe a habit, and "digo" is the irregular yo form of decir.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "A veces me equivoco." uses equivocarse (to make a mistake), which is reflexive, so it needs "me" before the yo form "equivoco".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Al final, todo salió bien." uses the preterite "salió" (from salir bien, to turn out well) to report how a finished situation ended.

units.title: Write It Yourself: Opinions and Reasons
units.description: Say it your own way — Opinions, reasons and comparisons, and more than one wording is right.

lessons.title: Write It Yourself: Opinions and Reasons 1
lessons.subtitle: Write it your own way

questions.prompt: Say you think it's a good idea.
acceptableAnswers: Creo que es una buena idea.
Pienso que es una buena idea.
questions.explanation: "Creo que es una buena idea." uses "creo que" to give an opinion, and an affirmative "creo que" is followed by the indicative ("es"); "Me parece una buena idea" says the same thing.

questions.prompt: Say that, in your opinion, he is right.
acceptableAnswers: En mi opinión, él tiene razón.
A mi parecer, él tiene razón.
Yo creo que él tiene razón.
questions.explanation: "En mi opinión, él tiene razón." uses "en mi opinión" for in my opinion, and Spanish says tener razón (to have reason) for to be right.

questions.prompt: Say you are not convinced by that argument.
acceptableAnswers: No estoy convencido por ese argumento.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "No estoy convencido por ese argumento." Opinions, reasons and comparisons, and more than one wording is right.

questions.prompt: Say this movie is more interesting than the other one.
acceptableAnswers: Esta película es más interesante que la otra.
Esta película es más interesante que la otra película.
La otra película es menos interesante que esta.
questions.explanation: "Esta película es más interesante que la otra." builds the comparison with "más" + adjective + "que", and "la otra" stands for "the other one".

questions.prompt: Say you prefer coffee to tea.
acceptableAnswers: Prefiero el café antes que el té.
Me gusta más el café que el té.
questions.explanation: "Prefiero el café al té." uses preferir with "a" before the second item, and a + el contracts to "al".

lessons.title: Write It Yourself: Opinions and Reasons 2
lessons.subtitle: Write it your own way

questions.prompt: Say it's better to leave early.
questions.explanation: "Es mejor salir temprano." gives general advice with "es mejor" + infinitive; no subject is needed because the advice applies to anyone.

questions.prompt: Say that in your opinion, it's too expensive.
acceptableAnswers: A mi juicio, es demasiado caro.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Según yo, es demasiado caro." Opinions, reasons and comparisons, and more than one wording is right.

questions.prompt: Say you find this book boring.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Me parece aburrido este libro." Opinions, reasons and comparisons, and more than one wording is right.

questions.prompt: Say she is probably right.
acceptableAnswers: Es probable que ella tenga razón.
questions.explanation: "Ella probablemente tiene razón." uses "tener razón" for "to be right"; if you start with "es probable que" instead, the verb changes to the subjunctive ("tenga").

questions.prompt: Say it's important to eat well.
questions.explanation: "Es importante comer bien." uses es importante followed by an infinitive, with no word for it, to state a general truth.

lessons.title: Write It Yourself: Opinions and Reasons 3
lessons.subtitle: Write it your own way

questions.prompt: Say it's necessary to book in advance.
questions.explanation: "Es necesario reservar con anticipación." uses "es necesario" + infinitive for a general need; "hay que reservar" means the same, and "con anticipación" is the usual Latin American way to say "in advance".

questions.prompt: Say you are happy with your results.
acceptableAnswers: Me siento contento con mis resultados.
Me siento contenta con mis resultados.
questions.explanation: "Estoy contento con mis resultados." uses "estar" because it describes a feeling, and the adjective agrees with the speaker, so a woman says "contenta".

questions.prompt: Say we are proud of our work.
acceptableAnswers: Nos sentimos orgullosos de nuestro trabajo.
questions.explanation: Pride is a feeling, so it takes "estar" plus "orgulloso" agreeing with "we", and "de" introduces what you are proud of: "Estamos orgullosos de nuestro trabajo."

questions.prompt: Say it's difficult to explain.
questions.explanation: "Es difícil de explicar." uses "difícil de" + infinitive because 'it' is the thing that is hard to explain; "Es difícil explicarlo" says the same thing.

questions.prompt: Say it's not that simple.
questions.explanation: "No es tan simple." uses "tan" + adjective to mean "that" or "so" simple; "sencillo" is a common synonym of "simple".

lessons.title: Write It Yourself: Opinions and Reasons 4
lessons.subtitle: Write it your own way

questions.prompt: Say you would like to change your mind.
questions.explanation: "Me gustaría" is the polite way to say "I would like", and "cambiar de opinión" is the set phrase for changing your mind: "Me gustaría cambiar de opinión."

questions.prompt: Say everything depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: "Todo depende de la situación." uses "depender de", so "depends on" is "depende de", never "depende en".

questions.prompt: Say that seems reasonable to you.
questions.explanation: "Parecer" works like "gustar": "me" shows whose opinion it is, and the adjective follows: "Eso me parece razonable."

questions.prompt: Say you doubt that's true.
acceptableAnswers: No creo que eso sea verdad.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Dudo que eso sea verdad." Doubt ("dudar", "no creer") triggers the subjunctive, so you need "sea" rather than "es".

questions.prompt: Say one must be patient.
questions.explanation: "Hay que ser paciente." uses "hay que" + infinitive, which states a general obligation with no specific subject, just like English "one must".

lessons.title: Write It Yourself: Opinions and Reasons 5
lessons.subtitle: Write it your own way

questions.prompt: Say we must make a decision.
questions.explanation: "Debemos tomar una decisión." uses "deber" + infinitive for "we must", and Spanish says "tomar una decisión" (not "hacer") for "make a decision".

questions.prompt: Say this is the best possible solution.
acceptableAnswers: Esta es la mejor solución posible.
Es la mejor solución que hay.
No hay mejor solución que esta.
questions.explanation: "Esta es la mejor solución posible." forms the superlative with "la mejor" before the noun, and "posible" goes after the noun, as in English "the best possible".

questions.prompt: Say you understand someone's point of view.
questions.explanation: "Entiendo tu punto de vista." uses "entender" in the yo form plus "punto de vista" for "point of view"; with someone you call usted, say "su punto de vista".

questions.prompt: Say you finally agree.
questions.explanation: "Finalmente estoy de acuerdo." uses "estar de acuerdo" for "agree" (always with estar), and "finalmente", "al final" or "por fin" all express "finally".

questions.prompt: Say the meeting was very productive.
questions.explanation: "La reunión fue muy productiva." uses the preterite "fue" for a finished event, and "productiva" is feminine to agree with "la reunión".

units.title: Conditional Mood
units.description: Hypothetical situations — Simple conditional for hypothetical statements and polite requests.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (viajar) por el mundo si tuviera dinero.
questions.explanation: The "si tuviera" clause sets up an imaginary situation, so the main verb takes the conditional, and "Yo" needs the ending -ía: "viajaría".

questions.prompt: Ella ___ (comprar) esa casa si pudiera.
questions.explanation: "Si pudiera" introduces an unreal wish, so the main verb is conditional, and "Ella" takes the third-person singular ending: "compraría".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (ir) contigo si tuviéramos tiempo.
questions.explanation: The "si tuviéramos tiempo" clause is hypothetical, so the result is conditional, and "Nosotros" takes -íamos added to the infinitive: "iríamos".

questions.prompt: ¿___ (poder) usted ayudarme, por favor?
questions.explanation: The conditional makes a request more polite, and "usted" takes the third-person singular form of poder: "Podría".

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (deber) descansar más.
questions.explanation: The conditional of deber gives soft advice ('you should'), and "Tú" needs the -ías ending: "deberías".

questions.prompt: Ellos ___ (querer) verte si estuvieran aquí.
questions.explanation: Querer has the irregular conditional stem "querr-", and "Ellos" takes the ending -ían, giving "querrían" after the imaginary "si estuvieran aquí".

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (decir) la verdad en tu lugar.
questions.explanation: "En tu lugar" asks you to imagine another situation, so the conditional is used; decir has the irregular stem "dir-", and "Yo" takes -ía: "diría".

questions.prompt: Él ___ (hacer) lo mismo en esa situación.
questions.explanation: The conditional expresses what he would do in that situation; hacer has the irregular stem "har-", and "Él" takes -ía: "haría".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (ser) más felices con más tiempo libre.
questions.explanation: The sentence imagines a hypothetical ("con más tiempo libre"), so ser takes the conditional, and "Nosotros" needs -íamos: "seríamos".

questions.prompt: ¿___ (gustar) a usted un café?
questions.explanation: "Le gustaría" fits because "a usted" is formal singular, so it takes the indirect pronoun "le", and the singular noun "un café" needs singular "gustaría". "Te" would be informal tú.
questions.example: ¿Le gustaría un café?

questions.prompt: Ella ___ (saber) qué hacer si lo pensara.
questions.explanation: The subject "Ella" is third person singular, so the conditional ending is "-ía": "sabría". The other forms belong to tú, nosotros and ellos.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (poder) terminarlo con más ayuda.
questions.explanation: The subject "Yo" takes the first-person singular conditional, which ends in "-ía": "podría". "Podrías" is for tú, "podrían" for ellos, "podríamos" for nosotros.
questions.meaning: I could, I would be able to

questions.prompt: Ellos ___ (venir) si los invitáramos.
questions.explanation: "Ellos" is third person plural, so the conditional of "venir" (irregular stem "vendr-") ends in "-ían": "vendrían".

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (tener) más éxito con más práctica.
questions.explanation: "Tú" takes the second-person singular ending "-ías", and "tener" has the irregular stem "tendr-": "tendrías".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (salir) antes si fuera posible.
questions.explanation: "Nosotros" takes the ending "-íamos", and "salir" has the irregular stem "saldr-": "saldríamos".

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (vivir) en otro país si pudiera.
questions.explanation: "Yo" takes the first-person singular conditional: the infinitive "vivir" plus "-ía" gives "viviría".

questions.prompt: Ella ___ (estudiar) medicina si tuviera la oportunidad.
questions.explanation: "Ella" is third person singular, so the infinitive "estudiar" plus "-ía" gives "estudiaría", matching the hypothetical "si tuviera la oportunidad".

questions.prompt: ¿___ (poder, tú) darme más información?
questions.explanation: The clue "(tú)" calls for the second-person singular form, which ends in "-ías": "Podrías". The conditional makes the request polite.

questions.prompt: Ellos ___ (preferir) quedarse en casa.
questions.explanation: "Ellos" is third person plural, so the infinitive "preferir" plus "-ían" gives "preferirían".

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (necesitar) más tiempo para decidir.
questions.explanation: "Nosotros" takes the ending "-íamos" added to the infinitive: "necesitaríamos".

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (cambiar) de trabajo si encontrara algo mejor.
questions.explanation: "Yo" takes the first-person singular conditional, so "cambiar" plus "-ía" gives "cambiaría", matching "si encontrara algo mejor".

questions.prompt: Él ___ (aceptar) la oferta sin dudarlo.
questions.explanation: The subject "Él" is third person singular, so the conditional takes the ending -ía: "aceptaría". The conditional expresses what he would do in a hypothetical situation.

questions.prompt: Tú ___ (disfrutar) mucho ese viaje.
questions.explanation: The subject "Tú" needs the second person singular conditional ending -ías: "disfrutarías". The other options are for él/ella, nosotros or ellos.

questions.prompt: Ella ___ (poner) más esfuerzo si le importara.
questions.explanation: "Ella" is third person singular, and poner has the irregular conditional stem pondr-, giving "pondría". The si-clause with "importara" signals a hypothetical result.

questions.prompt: Nosotros ___ (celebrar) si ganáramos.
questions.explanation: "Nosotros" takes the ending -íamos in the conditional: "celebraríamos". The clause "si ganáramos" sets up the hypothetical result.

units.title: Passive Voice
units.description: ser + past participle — Passive voice constructions common in formal/written Spanish.

questions.prompt: El libro ___ (escribir) por un autor famoso.
questions.explanation: In the passive, the participle agrees with the subject "El libro" (masculine singular), so ser takes "fue escrito". Feminine or plural forms don't match.

questions.prompt: La casa ___ (construir) en 1990.
questions.explanation: "La casa" is feminine singular, so the passive needs "fue construida" with a feminine participle. Masculine or plural forms would not agree.

questions.prompt: Las decisiones ___ (tomar) por el comité.
questions.explanation: "Las decisiones" is feminine plural, so both ser and the participle must agree: "fueron tomadas".

questions.prompt: El puente ___ (diseñar) por un ingeniero español.
questions.explanation: "El puente" is masculine singular, so the passive is "fue diseñado". The participle must agree with the bridge, not with the engineer.

questions.prompt: Los documentos ___ (firmar) ayer.
questions.explanation: "Los documentos" is masculine plural, so the passive is "fueron firmados", with both the verb and participle agreeing.

questions.prompt: La ciudad ___ (fundar) hace siglos.
questions.explanation: "La ciudad" is feminine singular, so the passive is "fue fundada", with a feminine singular participle.

questions.prompt: El premio ___ (otorgar) al mejor estudiante.
questions.explanation: "El premio" is masculine singular, so the passive is "fue otorgado". The participle agrees with the prize, not with "estudiante".

questions.prompt: Las reglas ___ (establecer) por el gobierno.
questions.explanation: "Las reglas" is feminine plural, so the passive needs "fueron establecidas", with plural ser and a feminine plural participle.

questions.prompt: El proyecto ___ (aprobar) por unanimidad.
questions.explanation: The passive is ser + past participle, and the participle agrees with the subject. "El proyecto" is masculine singular, so the past form is "fue aprobado".

questions.prompt: La carta ___ (enviar) la semana pasada.
questions.explanation: In the passive, the participle agrees with the subject. "La carta" is feminine singular, so the verb is "fue enviada".

questions.prompt: Los resultados ___ (anunciar) esta mañana.
questions.explanation: Both ser and the participle agree with the subject. "Los resultados" is masculine plural, so the form is "fueron anunciados".

questions.prompt: El edificio ___ (renovar) el año pasado.
questions.explanation: The passive uses ser + participle, agreeing with the subject. "El edificio" is masculine singular, so it takes "fue renovado".

questions.prompt: La novela ___ (traducir) a varios idiomas.
questions.explanation: The participle must agree with the subject in gender and number. "La novela" is feminine singular, so the form is "fue traducida".

questions.prompt: Los errores ___ (corregir) a tiempo.
questions.explanation: Ser and the participle agree with the subject. "Los errores" is masculine plural, so the form is "fueron corregidos".

questions.prompt: El evento ___ (organizar) por la universidad.
questions.explanation: In the passive, the participle matches the subject. "El evento" is masculine singular, so the form is "fue organizado".

questions.prompt: Las obras ___ (exhibir) en el museo.
questions.explanation: Ser and the participle agree with the subject. "Las obras" is feminine plural, so the form is "fueron exhibidas".

questions.prompt: El contrato ___ (firmar) por ambas partes.
questions.explanation: The participle agrees with the subject in the passive. "El contrato" is masculine singular, so the form is "fue firmado".

questions.prompt: La medicina ___ (descubrir) por accidente.
questions.explanation: Ser and the participle agree with the subject. "La medicina" is feminine singular, so the form is "fue descubierta".

questions.prompt: Los estudiantes ___ (seleccionar) cuidadosamente.
questions.explanation: The participle agrees with the subject. "Los estudiantes" is masculine plural, so the form is "fueron seleccionados".

questions.prompt: El informe ___ (publicar) el mes pasado.
questions.explanation: In the passive, ser and the participle agree with the subject. "El informe" is masculine singular, so the form is "fue publicado".

questions.prompt: La ley ___ (aprobar) por el parlamento.
questions.explanation: The passive uses ser + participle, and the participle agrees with the subject: "La ley" is feminine singular, so "fue aprobada".

questions.prompt: Los daños ___ (reparar) rápidamente.
questions.explanation: "Los daños" is masculine plural, so both the verb and the participle go plural and masculine: "fueron reparados".

questions.prompt: El plan ___ (rechazar) por el consejo.
questions.explanation: "El plan" is masculine singular, so the passive needs "fue rechazado" (singular verb, masculine participle).

questions.prompt: Las cartas ___ (leer) en voz alta.
questions.explanation: "Las cartas" is feminine plural, so the passive takes a plural verb and a feminine participle: "fueron leídas".

questions.prompt: El museo ___ (visitar) por miles de personas.
questions.explanation: "El museo" is masculine singular, so the passive is "fue visitado"; the other options have the wrong gender or number.

units.title: Formal vs. Informal Register
units.description: usted vs. tú — Formal register expressions, contrasted with informal equivalents.

questions.prompt: What is the formal ("usted") way to ask "¿cómo estás?" (how are you)? ___
questions.explanation: "¿cómo está usted?" uses the usted verb form "está" instead of the informal "estás", which is how Spanish marks polite address.

questions.prompt: What is the formal ("usted") way to ask "¿qué quieres?" (what do you want)?
questions.explanation: "¿qué desea usted?" swaps the informal "quieres" for the more polite verb "desear" in the usted form, the usual way to ask what someone wants in formal speech.

questions.prompt: What is the formal ("usted") way to say "can you help me (informal: ¿puedes ayudarme?)"? ___
questions.explanation: "¿podría ayudarme?" uses the usted form of "poder" in the conditional, which sounds extra polite, replacing informal "¿puedes ayudarme?".

questions.prompt: What is the formal ("usted") way to say "your" before a noun (informal: tu), as in "your car"?
questions.explanation: "su" is the possessive that goes before a noun with usted, replacing informal "tu" (su coche). "suyo" means "yours" and comes after the noun or stands alone.

questions.prompt: What is the formal ("usted") way to say "you (informal: tú)"? ___
bank: quedo a la espera de su respuesta
questions.explanation: "usted" is the formal pronoun that replaces "tú". It takes third-person verb forms, as in "usted está" instead of "tú estás".

questions.prompt: What is the formal ("usted") way to say "sit down please (informal: siéntate)"?
questions.explanation: "siéntese, por favor" is the usted command of "sentarse": the -e ending marks usted, and "se" attaches to the end, unlike informal "siéntate".

questions.prompt: What is the formal ("usted") way to say "come in (informal: entra)"? ___
questions.explanation: "pase usted" is the usted command of "pasar", the usual polite way to invite someone in, replacing informal "entra".

questions.prompt: What is the formal ("usted") way to say "excuse me, sir/madam"?
choices: quedo a la espera de su respuesta
questions.explanation: "disculpe, señor/señora" uses "disculpe", the usted command of "disculpar" (informal "disculpa"), plus a polite title to address a stranger.

questions.prompt: What is the formal ("usted") way to say "it's a pleasure to meet you"? ___
questions.explanation: it's a pleasure to meet you → es un placer conocerle. Formal register expressions, contrasted with informal equivalents.

questions.prompt: What is the formal ("usted") way to say "how may I help you?"?
questions.explanation: "¿en qué puedo servirle?" literally means "in what can I serve you?" and is the formal question staff use to offer help; the informal version is "¿en qué te puedo ayudar?".

questions.prompt: What is the formal ("usted") way to say "please wait a moment"?
questions.explanation: "espere un momento, por favor" uses "espere", the usted command of "esperar"; the informal form would be "espera".

questions.prompt: What is the formal ("usted") way to say "would you like anything else?"? ___
questions.explanation: "¿desea algo más?" uses the usted verb form "desea" to offer more service; a friend would say "¿quieres algo más?".

questions.prompt: What is the formal ("usted") way to say "I would appreciate your response"?
choices: quedo a la espera de su respuesta
questions.explanation: "agradecería su respuesta" uses the conditional "agradecería" (I would appreciate) with the formal possessive "su"; "quedo a la espera" means "I await" instead.

questions.prompt: What is the formal ("usted") way to say "please find attached"? ___
questions.explanation: "adjunto encontrará" (attached you will find) is the standard way to introduce an attachment in a formal email, using the usted form "encontrará".

questions.prompt: What is the formal ("usted") way to say "sincerely (formal letter closing)"?
questions.explanation: "atentamente" is the standard closing of a formal letter or email, written just before the signature; friends would close with "un abrazo" instead.

questions.prompt: What is the formal ("usted") way to say "dear sir or madam"? ___
questions.explanation: "estimado señor o señora" is the standard formal greeting at the start of a letter to an unknown reader, where a friend would get "querido" or "hola".

questions.prompt: What is the formal ("usted") way to say "at your service"?
questions.explanation: "a su disposición" literally means "at your disposal" and uses the formal possessive "su"; the informal version is "a tu disposición".

questions.prompt: What is the formal ("usted") way to say "thank you for your time"? ___
questions.explanation: "gracias por su tiempo" uses "su", the usted possessive; to a friend you would say "gracias por tu tiempo".

questions.prompt: What is the formal ("usted") way to say "I look forward to your reply"?
choices: quedo a la espera de su respuesta
questions.explanation: "quedo a la espera de su respuesta" (I remain awaiting your reply) is the set formal closing line for expecting an answer; "agradecería" would mean "I would appreciate".

questions.prompt: What is the formal ("usted") way to say "best regards"? ___
questions.explanation: "un cordial saludo" is the standard polite sign-off at the end of a formal letter or email, like "best regards". "Estimado señor o señora" opens a letter rather than closing it.

units.title: Advanced Connectors
units.description: Formal written Spanish — Connectors typical of formal writing and argumentation.

questions.prompt: How do you say "furthermore" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "además" adds another point to an argument, just like "furthermore"; "sobre todo" means "above all" and "siempre y cuando" means "as long as".

questions.prompt: How do you say "in this regard" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "al respecto" means "in this regard" or "about this" and points back to a topic already mentioned. "En vista de" means "in view of", and "en resumen" means "in summary".

questions.prompt: How do you say "with regard to" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "con respecto a" introduces the topic you are talking about, like "with regard to"; "cabe destacar que" means "it is worth noting that".

questions.prompt: How do you say "in conclusion" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "en conclusión" introduces the final point that sums up an argument; "en primer lugar" opens an argument and "por otra parte" adds a contrasting point.

questions.prompt: How do you say "in summary" in Spanish?
choices: por último pero no menos importante
questions.explanation: "en resumen" means "in summary" and introduces a short recap of the main points. "Al respecto" means "about that", "en vista de" means "in view of", and "por último pero no menos importante" means "last but not least".

questions.prompt: How do you say "on the one hand" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "por una parte" introduces the first of two points, like "on the one hand", and is usually answered by "por otra parte".

questions.prompt: How do you say "on the other hand (formal)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "por otra parte" introduces the second, contrasting point, like "on the other hand"; "por una parte" opens the first point.

questions.prompt: How do you say "given that" in Spanish? ___
bank: por último pero no menos importante
questions.explanation: "dado que" introduces a reason that is already known or accepted, like "given that" or "since".

questions.prompt: How do you say "provided that" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "siempre y cuando" sets a condition, like "provided that", and the verb after it goes in the subjunctive.

questions.prompt: How do you say "in view of" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "en vista de" means "in view of" and introduces the circumstance that justifies what follows.

questions.prompt: How do you say "as a result of" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "como resultado de" means "as a result of" and introduces the cause that led to a consequence.

questions.prompt: How do you say "in relation to" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "en relación con" means "in relation to" and links a statement to a topic, which is followed by a noun.

questions.prompt: How do you say "without a doubt" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "sin lugar a dudas" is a fixed expression for "without a doubt", used to stress that something is certain.

questions.prompt: How do you say "first of all" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "en primer lugar" means "first of all" and opens the first item in a list of points.

questions.prompt: How do you say "last but not least" in Spanish? ___
bank: por último pero no menos importante
questions.answer: por último pero no menos importante
questions.explanation: "por último pero no menos importante" introduces the final point while stressing that it matters as much as the others, like "last but not least".

questions.prompt: How do you say "above all" in Spanish?
choices: por último pero no menos importante
questions.explanation: "sobre todo" means "above all" or "especially" and highlights the most important point. "Por último pero no menos importante" means "last but not least".

questions.prompt: How do you say "in other terms" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: in other terms → dicho de otro modo. Connectors typical of formal writing and argumentation.

questions.prompt: How do you say "it is worth noting that" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cabe destacar que" literally means "it fits to highlight that" and introduces a point worth noting. "Sin lugar a dudas" means "without a doubt".

questions.prompt: How do you say "taking into account" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "tomando en cuenta" uses the gerund of "tomar" (to take) plus "en cuenta" (into account). It is the usual Latin American form of "taking into account".

questions.prompt: How do you say "in the same way" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "del mismo modo" means "in the same way" or "likewise" and adds a similar point. "Siempre y cuando" means "as long as".

units.title: Complex Prepositions
units.description: Multi-word prepositional phrases — Compound prepositional phrases common at intermediate to advanced level.

questions.prompt: Vamos a hablar acerca ___ este tema.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase meaning 'about' is "acerca de", so the blank takes "de".

questions.prompt: El regalo es ___ parte de todo el equipo.
questions.explanation: "De parte de" is the fixed phrase meaning 'on behalf of', so the blank takes "de".

questions.prompt: A pesar ___ la lluvia, salimos a caminar.
questions.explanation: "A pesar de" ('despite') is a fixed phrase that always takes "de" before the noun.

questions.prompt: Ella vive cerca ___ la estación.
questions.explanation: "Cerca de" ('near') always takes "de" before the place, so the answer is "de".

questions.prompt: El banco está enfrente ___ la farmacia.
questions.explanation: "Enfrente de" ('opposite, in front of') is followed by "de" before the noun.

questions.prompt: Trabajamos junto ___ el nuevo equipo.
questions.explanation: "Junto con" means 'together with', so the blank takes "con".

questions.prompt: Lo hice a través ___ un amigo.
questions.explanation: "A través de" ('through, by means of') is a fixed phrase ending in "de".
questions.meaning: of (in 'a través de': through, by means of)

questions.prompt: Él llegó antes ___ que empezara la reunión.
questions.explanation: The phrase "antes de que" always takes "de" before "que" to mean 'before'; "antes a" or "antes con" do not exist.

questions.prompt: Nos vemos después ___ la clase.
questions.explanation: "de" is correct here. Compound prepositional phrases common in intermediate-advanced Spanish.

questions.prompt: Ella se sienta al lado ___ la ventana.
questions.explanation: "Al lado de" means 'next to', and this phrase always links to the noun with "de" ("al lado de la ventana").

questions.prompt: El parque está detrás ___ mi casa.
questions.explanation: "Detrás de" means 'behind' and takes "de" before the noun ("detrás de mi casa").

questions.prompt: En cuanto ___ tu pregunta, no estoy seguro.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase "en cuanto a" means 'as for / regarding' and ends in "a" before "tu pregunta".

questions.prompt: Con respecto ___ eso, hablaremos mañana.
questions.explanation: "Con respecto a" means 'regarding' and the fixed phrase ends in "a" before "eso".

questions.prompt: Debido ___ la lluvia, llegamos tarde.
questions.explanation: "Debido a" means 'due to / because of' and always takes "a" before the cause ("debido a la lluvia").

questions.prompt: Todo salió bien gracias ___ tu ayuda.
questions.explanation: "Gracias a" means 'thanks to' and takes "a" before the person or cause ("gracias a tu ayuda").

questions.prompt: En lugar ___ quejarte, busca una solución.
questions.explanation: "En lugar de" means 'instead of' and takes "de" before the infinitive ("en lugar de quejarte").

questions.prompt: A causa ___ la lluvia, cancelaron el vuelo.
questions.explanation: "A causa de" means 'because of' and its last word is "de" before the cause ("a causa de la lluvia").

questions.prompt: Además ___ ser inteligente, es muy amable.
questions.explanation: "Además de" means 'besides / in addition to' and takes "de" before the infinitive ("además de ser inteligente").

questions.prompt: Frente ___ la casa hay un jardín grande.
questions.explanation: "Frente a" means 'facing / in front of' and takes "a" before the noun ("frente a la casa").
questions.meaning: to (in 'frente a': facing, in front of)

questions.prompt: Antes ___ salir, cierra la puerta con llave.
questions.explanation: The set phrase "antes de" + infinitive means 'before doing something'. Spanish uses "de" here, not "a" or "con".

units.title: Relative Pronouns
units.description: que, quien, cuyo — Relative pronouns linking clauses.

questions.prompt: El libro ___ leí es excelente.
questions.explanation: "que" is the basic relative pronoun for a thing ("el libro") that is the direct object of "leí". "Quien" is for people and "cuyo" means 'whose'.

questions.prompt: La mujer con ___ hablé es mi jefa.
questions.explanation: After a preposition ("con") with a person ("la mujer"), use "quien". Bare "que" is not used here and "cuyo" means 'whose'.

questions.prompt: El hombre ___ casa visitamos es mi tío.
questions.explanation: "cuya" means 'whose' and agrees with the thing possessed, "casa" (feminine singular), not with "hombre".
questions.meaning: whose (feminine singular, matches the thing owned)

questions.prompt: Los amigos ___ conocí son de Chile.
questions.explanation: "que" works for plural people ("los amigos") as the direct object of "conocí". "La que" is singular feminine and does not agree.

questions.prompt: La persona a ___ llamé no contestó.
questions.explanation: After the preposition "a" with a person ("la persona"), the relative pronoun is "quien". Bare "que" does not follow "a" here.

questions.prompt: El coche ___ compré es nuevo.
questions.explanation: "que" refers to the thing "el coche", the object of "compré". "Cuyo/cuya" would mean 'whose' and "quien" is for people.

questions.prompt: El museo ___ visitamos ayer es enorme.
questions.explanation: "que" is the plain relative pronoun for "el museo", the object of "visitamos". "La que" is feminine and does not agree with the masculine noun.

questions.prompt: El profesor ___ libro leímos es famoso.
questions.explanation: "cuyo" means 'whose' and agrees with the thing owned, "libro" (masculine singular), not with "profesor".

questions.prompt: Las chicas ___ vimos ayer son mis primas.
questions.explanation: "que" is the relative pronoun for "las chicas" as the object of "vimos". The "cuyo" forms mean 'whose' and need a noun right after them.

questions.prompt: El escritor ___ obras admiro nació en España.
questions.explanation: "cuyas" means 'whose' and agrees with the thing owned, "obras" (feminine plural), not with "escritor".

questions.prompt: La razón por ___ llegué tarde fue el tráfico.
questions.explanation: "la que" refers back to "la razón" (feminine singular) after the preposition "por". "El que" is masculine and "lo que" is neuter.
questions.meaning: which, that (feminine singular, after a preposition); also "the one that"

questions.prompt: El niño ___ juguete se rompió lloró.
questions.explanation: "cuyo" means 'whose' and agrees with the thing owned, not the owner: "juguete" is masculine singular, so "cuyo" fits.

questions.prompt: Los países ___ visitamos fueron interesantes.
questions.explanation: "que" is the plain relative pronoun for things; here it refers to "los países" and is the object of "visitamos", so no preposition or article is needed.

questions.prompt: La empresa para ___ trabajo es grande.
questions.explanation: After a preposition ("para") a relative pronoun for a thing needs an article: "la que" agrees with feminine "la empresa". Plain "que" cannot follow "para" here.

questions.prompt: El equipo ___ ganó celebró mucho.
questions.explanation: "que" is the subject of "ganó" and refers back to "el equipo"; no preposition is involved, so the simple relative "que" is used.

questions.prompt: La casa ___ ventanas son azules es mía.
questions.explanation: "cuyas" ('whose') agrees with the noun that follows it: "ventanas" is feminine plural, so "cuyas" is needed.

questions.prompt: Los estudiantes ___ estudian mucho aprueban.
questions.explanation: "que" is the subject of "estudian" and refers to "los estudiantes"; "quien" is singular and "cuyo/cuya" would mean 'whose', which doesn't fit.

questions.prompt: La actriz de ___ hablamos ganó un premio.
questions.explanation: After the preposition "de" with a person, "quien" ('whom') is used; "la actriz" is a person, and bare "que" cannot follow "de" here.

questions.prompt: El parque ___ está cerca es bonito.
questions.explanation: "que" is the subject of "está cerca" and refers to "el parque"; no possession or preposition is involved, so "cuyo/cuyas" and "quien" don't fit.

questions.prompt: Las noticias ___ escuché me sorprendieron.
questions.explanation: "que" is the object of "escuché" and refers to "las noticias" (things); "quien" is for people and "cuyo/cuya" would mean 'whose'.

questions.prompt: El médico ___ consulta visité es excelente.
questions.explanation: The doctor possesses the office, so we need 'whose': "cuya" agrees with the thing owned, "consulta" (feminine singular).

questions.prompt: La canción ___ cantamos es popular.
questions.explanation: "que" is the object of "cantamos" and refers to "la canción"; "la que" would need a preposition or no noun before it, and "cuyo/cuyas" means 'whose'.
questions.meaning: that, which (links a clause to a noun)

questions.prompt: Los vecinos ___ perro ladra mucho se mudaron.
questions.explanation: "cuyo" means 'whose' and agrees with the thing owned: "perro" is masculine singular, so "cuyo" (not "cuya") is correct.
questions.meaning: whose (masculine singular, matches the thing owned)

questions.prompt: La idea ___ propuso fue aceptada.
questions.explanation: "que" is the general relative pronoun for a thing and needs no preposition: it links "La idea" to the verb "propuso" (the idea that someone proposed). "cuyo/cuya" would mean 'whose' and need a noun right after them.

questions.prompt: El amigo con ___ viajé vive en Lima.
questions.explanation: After a preposition ("con") and referring to a person ("El amigo"), the standard relative is "quien" (or el que). Bare "que" is not used after "con" here, and "cuyo" means 'whose'.

units.title: Environment & Nature
units.description: The natural world — Environment and nature vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "environment" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "medio ambiente" is the standard Spanish term for the environment; it is two words and masculine: el medio ambiente.

questions.prompt: How do you say "nature" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "naturaleza" means nature, the natural world, and it is feminine: la naturaleza.

questions.prompt: How do you say "forest" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "bosque" is a forest, an area full of trees; it is masculine: el bosque.

questions.prompt: How do you say "habitat" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "hábitat" is spelled like the English word but needs an accent on the first a, and it is masculine: el hábitat.

questions.prompt: How do you say "river" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "río" means river; the accent on the í is required, and the word is masculine: el río.

questions.prompt: How do you say "ocean" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "océano" means ocean; it has an accent on the e and is masculine: el océano.

questions.prompt: How do you say "climate" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "clima" means climate; although it ends in -a it is masculine: el clima, as in el cambio climático.

questions.prompt: How do you say "pollution" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "contaminación" is the everyday word for pollution, as in la contaminación del aire; "polución" exists but is much less common.

questions.prompt: How do you say "recycling" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "reciclaje" means recycling and is masculine: el reciclaje de plástico.

questions.prompt: How do you say "energy" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "energía" means energy; the accent on the í is required, as in energía renovable.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sustainable" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "sostenible" means sustainable, as in desarrollo sostenible; in much of Latin America "sustentable" is also common.

questions.prompt: How do you say "species" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: English "species" is both singular and plural, but Spanish uses "especie" for one and especies for several.

questions.prompt: How do you say "planet" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Planet" is "planeta" in Spanish. Note that it is masculine (el planeta) even though it ends in -a.

questions.prompt: How do you say "resource" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Resource" is "recurso", a masculine noun, as in "recursos naturales" (natural resources).

questions.prompt: How do you say "drought" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "sequía" means "drought", a long period without rain. It comes from "seco" (dry) and carries an accent on the í.

questions.prompt: How do you say "wildlife" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Wildlife" is "fauna", the animals living in a region; "especie" means a single species, not wildlife as a whole.

questions.prompt: How do you say "ecosystem" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ecosistema" is the Spanish for "ecosystem". Like many words ending in -ma from Greek, it is masculine: "el ecosistema".

questions.prompt: How do you say "renewable" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "renovable" is the adjective for "renewable", as in "energía renovable". "Recurso" means "resource" and "reciclaje" means "recycling".

questions.prompt: How do you say "carbon" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "carbono" is the chemical element carbon, as in "dióxido de carbono". Note that "carbón" means coal.

questions.prompt: How do you say "biodiversity" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "biodiversidad" means "biodiversity". English "-ity" usually becomes "-idad" in Spanish, and these nouns are feminine: "la biodiversidad".

units.title: Gerund & Present Progressive
units.description: estar + gerundio — Present progressive constructions with irregular gerunds included.

questions.prompt: Ella está ___ (hablar) por teléfono.
questions.explanation: The present progressive is estar + gerund, so after "está" you need the -ando form of hablar: "hablando". "Hablado" is the participle, "hablar" the infinitive.

questions.prompt: Yo estoy ___ (comer) ahora mismo.
questions.explanation: "Estoy" plus "ahora mismo" calls for the present progressive, which uses the gerund of comer: "comiendo" (-er verbs take -iendo). The other forms are the infinitive, present and imperfect.

questions.prompt: Nosotros estamos ___ (escribir) un informe.
questions.explanation: After "estamos" the progressive needs a gerund, and -ir verbs form it with -iendo: "escribiendo". "Escribimos" and "escribíamos" are finite tenses, and "escribir" is the infinitive.

questions.prompt: Ellos están ___ (dormir) todavía.
questions.explanation: "Están" + gerund forms the progressive, and dormir changes its stem vowel in the gerund: o becomes u, giving "durmiendo". The other options are not gerunds.

questions.prompt: Tú estás ___ (leer) ese libro.
questions.explanation: After "estás" you need the gerund of leer. The ending -iendo between vowels changes to -yendo, so it is "leyendo" (not "leiendo").

questions.prompt: Yo estoy ___ (trabajar) en un proyecto.
questions.explanation: "Estoy" + gerund is the present progressive for an action in progress, and trabajar forms its gerund regularly with -ando: "trabajando". The other options are finite or infinitive forms.

questions.prompt: Ella está ___ (pedir) ayuda.
questions.explanation: The progressive "está" + gerund needs the gerund of pedir, which changes its stem e to i: "pidiendo". "Pide" and "pedía" are finite verbs, "pedir" is the infinitive.

questions.prompt: Nosotros estamos ___ (venir) hacia allá.
questions.explanation: After "estamos" you need the gerund of venir, whose stem changes e to i: "viniendo". "Venido" is the participle and "vinimos" a preterite.
questions.example: Mucha gente está viniendo a la fiesta.

questions.prompt: Ellos están ___ (decir) la verdad.
questions.explanation: The progressive "están" + gerund needs the gerund of decir, which is irregular (e becomes i): "diciendo". "Dicho" is the participle and "dicen" a present-tense form.

questions.prompt: Tú estás ___ (sentir) mucho dolor.
questions.explanation: "Estás" + gerund forms the progressive, and sentir has an irregular gerund with e becoming i: "sintiendo". "Sientes" is a present-tense form, not a gerund.
questions.example: Estoy sintiendo mucha presión en el trabajo.

questions.prompt: Yo estoy ___ (seguir) las instrucciones.
questions.explanation: After "estoy" the progressive needs a gerund, and seguir is stem-changing (e→i) in the gerund, so it becomes "siguiendo". "Seguido" is the participle, "seguir" the infinitive.

questions.prompt: Ella está ___ (repetir) la pregunta.
questions.explanation: The progressive "está + gerund" needs a gerund, and repetir changes e→i in the gerund: "repitiendo". "Repetido" is the participle and "repetir" the infinitive.

questions.prompt: Nosotros estamos ___ (construir) una casa.
questions.explanation: Verbs in -uir take y instead of i before the gerund ending, so construir becomes "construyendo" after "estamos".

questions.prompt: Ellos están ___ (destruir) el edificio viejo.
questions.explanation: Destruir ends in -uir, so the gerund ending -iendo becomes -yendo: "destruyendo". After "están" a gerund is needed, not the participle or infinitive.

questions.prompt: Tú estás ___ (creer) algo falso.
questions.explanation: When the stem ends in a vowel (cre-), the gerund ending -iendo turns -yendo, so creer gives "creyendo" after "estás".
questions.example: Sigues creyendo que es verdad.

questions.prompt: Yo estoy ___ (jugar) al tenis.
questions.explanation: "Estoy" needs a gerund, formed from jugar by replacing -ar with -ando: "jugando". "Jugado" is the participle and "juego" a conjugated verb.

questions.prompt: Ella está ___ (estudiar) para el examen.
questions.explanation: "Está" needs a gerund, formed from estudiar by replacing -ar with -ando: "estudiando". The participle and infinitive cannot follow "estar" here.

questions.prompt: Nosotros estamos ___ (viajar) por Europa.
questions.explanation: The progressive "estamos + gerund" needs viajar to end in -ando: "viajando". "Viajamos" is a finite verb and cannot follow "estamos".

questions.prompt: Ellos están ___ (correr) en el parque.
questions.explanation: Verbs in -er form the gerund with -iendo, so correr gives "corriendo" after "están". "Corrido" is the participle.

questions.prompt: Tú estás ___ (aprender) mucho.
questions.explanation: After "estás" a gerund is needed, and aprender (-er) takes -iendo: "aprendiendo". "Aprendes" is a present-tense form and cannot follow "estar".

questions.prompt: Yo estoy ___ (mirar) la televisión.
questions.explanation: "Estoy" plus a gerund expresses an action in progress; mirar (-ar) becomes "mirando". "Miro" and "mirar" cannot follow "estoy" here.

questions.prompt: Ella está ___ (preparar) la cena.
questions.explanation: The progressive "está + gerund" needs preparar (-ar) to end in -ando: "preparando". "Preparado" is the participle and "prepara" a finite verb.

questions.prompt: Nosotros estamos ___ (esperar) el autobús.
questions.explanation: The present progressive is estar + gerund, and "esperando" is the gerund of esperar (-ar verbs take -ando). "Esperado" is the participle, "esperar" the infinitive, and "esperamos" a conjugated form, none of which follows "estamos".

questions.prompt: Ellos están ___ (cantar) una canción.
questions.explanation: After "están" the present progressive needs a gerund, and "cantando" is the -ar gerund of cantar. "Cantado" is the participle, "cantar" the infinitive, and "cantan" a finite verb, so none of them can follow "están".

questions.prompt: Tú estás ___ (bailar) muy bien.
questions.explanation: "Estás" must be followed by a gerund to form the present progressive, and the gerund of bailar is "bailando". "Bailado" is a participle, "bailar" an infinitive, and "bailas" a conjugated form.

units.title: Subjunctive with Impersonal Expressions
units.description: es posible que, es necesario que... — Subjunctive triggered by impersonal expressions of necessity/possibility.

lessons.title: Subjunctive with Impersonal Expressions 1
lessons.subtitle: es posible que, es necesario que...

questions.prompt: Es posible que ___ (llover) mañana.
questions.explanation: "Es posible que" expresses possibility and triggers the subjunctive, so llover becomes "llueva". The indicative "llueve" and the imperfect "llovía" don't fit this trigger.

questions.prompt: Es necesario que tú ___ (terminar) el informe.
questions.explanation: "Es necesario que" requires the subjunctive, and with "tú" the present subjunctive of terminar is "termines". "Terminas" is indicative, and "terminen" is the ustedes/ellos form, which doesn't match "tú".

questions.prompt: Es probable que nosotros ___ (ganar) el partido.
questions.explanation: "Es probable que" takes the subjunctive, and for "nosotros" the present subjunctive of ganar is "ganemos". "Ganamos" is indicative, and "ganen" is the form for ellos/ustedes.

questions.prompt: Es probable que ellos ___ (venir) tarde.
questions.explanation: "Es probable que" triggers the subjunctive, and the subject "ellos" is plural, so venir becomes "vengan". "Venga" is singular and "vienen" is indicative.

questions.prompt: Es raro que ella no ___ (contestar) el teléfono.
questions.explanation: "Es raro que" expresses a reaction and takes the subjunctive, and with "ella" the form is "conteste". "Contesta" is indicative, and "contesten" is plural, which doesn't match "ella".

lessons.title: Subjunctive with Impersonal Expressions 2
lessons.subtitle: es posible que, es necesario que...

questions.prompt: Es mejor que ustedes ___ (descansar) hoy.
questions.explanation: "Es mejor que" calls for the subjunctive, and "ustedes" takes the -en ending for -ar verbs, giving "descansen". "Descansan" is indicative, and "descanses" is the tú form.

questions.prompt: Es dudoso que él ___ (saber) la respuesta.
questions.explanation: "Es dudoso que" expresses doubt and takes the subjunctive, and the subjunctive of saber for "él" is "sepa". "Sabe" is indicative, and "sepas" is the tú form.

questions.prompt: Es una lástima que tú no ___ (poder) venir.
questions.explanation: "Es una lástima que" expresses an emotional reaction and takes the subjunctive, and with "tú" poder becomes "puedas". "Puedes" is indicative, and "pueda" is the él/ella form.
questions.meaning: you can, you are able to

questions.prompt: Es fácil que nosotros ___ (perder) el tren.
questions.explanation: "Es fácil que" signals possibility and takes the subjunctive, and for "nosotros" perder becomes "perdamos" (no stem change in nosotros). "Pierdan" is the ellos form, and "perdemos" is indicative.
questions.example: Es posible que nosotros perdamos el tren.

questions.prompt: Es urgente que ella ___ (hacer) la llamada.
questions.explanation: "Es urgente que" expresses necessity, so the verb after "que" goes in the subjunctive; for "ella" the subjunctive of hacer is "haga".

lessons.title: Subjunctive with Impersonal Expressions 3
lessons.subtitle: es posible que, es necesario que...

questions.prompt: Es normal que los niños ___ (tener) miedo.
questions.explanation: "Es normal que" triggers the subjunctive, and "los niños" is plural, so tener becomes "tengan".

questions.prompt: Es difícil que él ___ (cambiar) de opinión.
questions.explanation: "Es difícil que" expresses doubt about likelihood, so it takes the subjunctive; with "él" the form is "cambie".

questions.prompt: Es esencial que nosotros ___ (revisar) el contrato.
questions.explanation: "Es esencial que" takes the subjunctive, and the subject "nosotros" requires the nosotros form "revisemos" (not the indicative "revisamos").

questions.prompt: Es conveniente que tú ___ (llamar) primero.
questions.explanation: "Es conveniente que" triggers the subjunctive, and the subject "tú" calls for the tú form "llames".

questions.prompt: Es lógico que ellos ___ (dudar) al principio.
questions.explanation: "Es lógico que" takes the subjunctive, and "ellos" needs the plural form "duden" (not indicative "dudan").

units.title: Subjunctive with Emotion
units.description: me alegra que, es una lástima que... — Subjunctive triggered by expressions of emotion.

lessons.title: Subjunctive with Emotion 1
lessons.subtitle: me alegra que, es una lástima que...

questions.prompt: Me alegra que tú ___ (estar) aquí.
questions.explanation: "Me alegra que" expresses emotion, so the next verb is subjunctive; for "tú" the subjunctive of estar is "estés".

questions.prompt: Me sorprende que ella ___ (saber) la verdad.
questions.explanation: "Me sorprende que" expresses a reaction, so it takes the subjunctive; for "ella" saber becomes "sepa".

questions.prompt: Siento que ustedes ___ (tener) que esperar.
questions.explanation: "Siento que" expresses feeling, so the subjunctive follows, and "ustedes" needs the plural form "tengan".

questions.prompt: A mis padres les encanta que nosotros ___ (poder) viajar juntos.
questions.explanation: "Les encanta que" expresses an emotion about someone else's action, so the verb after "que" goes into the subjunctive, and "podamos" is the nosotros form of poder.
questions.meaning: we can, we are able to (subjunctive)

questions.prompt: Le molesta que él siempre ___ (llegar) tarde.
questions.explanation: "Le molesta que" expresses annoyance, so the subjunctive follows; for "él" llegar becomes "llegue".
questions.example: Le molesta que él siempre llegue tarde.

lessons.title: Subjunctive with Emotion 2
lessons.subtitle: me alegra que, es una lástima que...

questions.prompt: Es triste que ellos ___ (irse) tan pronto.
questions.explanation: "Es triste que" expresses emotion, so it takes the subjunctive, and "ellos" needs the plural form "se vayan".

questions.prompt: Me preocupa que tú no ___ (dormir) bien.
questions.explanation: "Me preocupa que" expresses worry, so the verb after "que" goes in the subjunctive. With "tú" the present subjunctive of dormir is "duermas", not the indicative "duermes".

questions.prompt: Me gusta que ella ___ (ser) tan honesta.
questions.explanation: "Me gusta que" expresses a feeling, so the verb after "que" needs the subjunctive. For "ella" the present subjunctive of ser is "sea"; "es" is indicative and "seas" is the tú form.

questions.prompt: Nos alegra que ustedes ___ (venir) a la boda.
questions.explanation: "Nos alegra que" expresses joy, so the next verb takes the subjunctive. The subject "ustedes" is plural, so venir becomes "vengan"; "vienen" is indicative and "venga" is singular.

questions.prompt: Le sorprende que nosotros ___ (vivir) tan lejos.
questions.explanation: "Le sorprende que" expresses surprise, so the verb after "que" goes in the subjunctive. The subject is "nosotros", so vivir becomes "vivamos"; "vivimos" is indicative and "vivan" is the ustedes/ellos form.

lessons.title: Subjunctive with Emotion 3
lessons.subtitle: me alegra que, es una lástima que...

questions.prompt: Siento mucho que tú ___ (perder) tu trabajo.
questions.explanation: "Siento mucho que" expresses regret about something that already happened, so the perfect subjunctive is used. With "tú" it is "hayas perdido"; "has perdido" is indicative and "haya perdido" is the él/ella form.

questions.prompt: Me encanta que ellos ___ (celebrar) juntos.
questions.explanation: "Me encanta que" expresses a feeling, so the verb after "que" takes the subjunctive. The subject "ellos" is plural, so celebrar becomes "celebren"; "celebran" is indicative and "celebre" is singular.

questions.prompt: Es una pena que ella no ___ (poder) venir.
questions.explanation: "Es una pena que" expresses regret, so the verb after "que" must be subjunctive. With "ella" the form is "pueda"; "puede" is indicative and "puedan" is plural.

questions.prompt: Nos molesta que él siempre ___ (llegar) tarde.
questions.explanation: "Nos molesta que" expresses annoyance, so the verb after "que" goes in the subjunctive. With "él" the present subjunctive of llegar is "llegue"; "llega" is indicative and "llegues" is the tú form.

questions.prompt: Le alegra que nosotros ___ (estar) bien.
questions.explanation: "Le alegra que" expresses happiness, so the verb after "que" takes the subjunctive. The subject "nosotros" needs "estemos"; "estamos" is indicative and "esté" is singular.

units.title: Por vs. Para
units.description: Two prepositions, different uses — "Por" (cause, exchange, duration, means) vs. "para" (purpose, destination, deadline).

questions.prompt: Este regalo es ___ ti.
questions.explanation: Here the gift is intended for a recipient, and "para" marks the person something is meant for. "Por" would suggest cause or exchange, which doesn't fit "Este regalo es ___ ti".

questions.prompt: Caminamos ___ el parque (through it), mirando los árboles.
questions.explanation: "por" expresses movement through or around a place, so "caminamos por el parque" means we walked through the park; "para" would mean heading toward it.

questions.prompt: Pagué diez dólares ___ el libro.
questions.explanation: "Por" is used for exchange, what you give in return for something, so paying ten dollars "por el libro" takes "por". "Para" would express purpose or recipient instead.

questions.prompt: Salimos ___ Madrid mañana y llegamos allá el martes. (destino)
questions.explanation: "para" marks the destination of the trip: "salir para Madrid" means heading toward Madrid, and "llegamos allá el martes" confirms Madrid is where they are going.

questions.prompt: Estudio ___ ser doctor.
questions.explanation: "para" expresses purpose or goal: studying in order to become a doctor.

questions.prompt: Gracias ___ tu ayuda.
questions.explanation: "por" is used with "gracias" to give the reason you are thankful: "gracias por tu ayuda" is a fixed pattern.

questions.prompt: Necesito esto ___ el lunes.
questions.explanation: "para" marks a deadline: you need it by Monday, "para el lunes".

questions.prompt: Te mando los documentos ___ correo.
questions.explanation: "por" marks the means by which something is sent, so "por correo" means by mail; "para" would mark a purpose or recipient instead.

questions.prompt: Trabajó ___ tres horas.
questions.explanation: "por" expresses duration of time: worked "por tres horas" means for three hours.

questions.prompt: Este café es ___ mi madre.
questions.explanation: "para" marks the recipient: the coffee is intended for your mother.

questions.prompt: Ella no trabaja ___ dinero; trabaja porque le gusta.
questions.explanation: "por" expresses motive: she does not work out of a desire for money, but because she likes it.

questions.prompt: Llámame ___ teléfono.
questions.explanation: "por" expresses the means of communication: "llámame por teléfono" means call me by phone.

questions.prompt: Estudiamos ___ la noche.
questions.explanation: "por" is used in time-of-day expressions: "por la noche" means at night or in the evening.

questions.prompt: Este proyecto es ___ el viernes.
questions.explanation: "para" marks a deadline: the project is due by Friday, "para el viernes".

questions.prompt: Mañana salimos ___ (toward) la playa.
questions.explanation: "para" marks the destination you are heading to, so "salimos para la playa" means we leave for the beach; "por" would mean through or along it.

units.title: Indefinite & Negative Words
units.description: algo/nada, alguien/nadie... — Indefinite and negative pronouns/adverbs.

questions.prompt: ¿Hay ___ (something) en la caja? No, no hay nada.
questions.explanation: "algo" means 'something' and refers to a thing, which fits a question about what is in a box; "alguien" is for people, and the reply "no hay nada" answers an "algo" question.

questions.prompt: ¿Vino ___ (someone) a la fiesta? No, no vino nadie.
questions.explanation: "alguien" means 'someone' and is used for people; the answer "no vino nadie" confirms a person is asked about, while "algo" would mean a thing and "nunca" is not a pronoun.

questions.prompt: ¿Tienes ___ (some) plan para hoy? No tengo ninguno.
questions.explanation: "plan" is masculine singular, so the shortened form "algún" is needed before it; "alguna" is feminine and "alguno" is not used before a noun.

questions.prompt: Nunca como carne; ella ___ (neither) la come.
questions.explanation: "tampoco" means 'neither/not either' and adds a second negative to "Nunca como carne"; "también" would be positive and "nadie" is a person pronoun.
questions.example: Nunca como carne, y ella tampoco.

questions.prompt: Yo también voy; ella ___ (also) va.
questions.explanation: "también" means 'also' and agrees with the positive "Yo también voy"; "tampoco" would need a negative sentence before it.
questions.example: Yo voy a la fiesta y ella también.

questions.prompt: No tengo ___ problema con eso.
questions.explanation: "problema" is masculine singular, so the shortened "ningún" is used before it; "ninguno" stands alone without a noun and "ninguna" is feminine.

questions.prompt: ¿___ llegas tarde?
questions.explanation: "Siempre" means 'always' and fits the question "¿...llegas tarde?" asking if someone is habitually late; "Nunca" would mean 'never' and "Todavía" means 'still'.

questions.prompt: No, ___ (never) llego tarde.
questions.explanation: "nunca" means 'never' and follows the "No," answer to deny being late; "siempre" would contradict the "No," and "tampoco" needs a prior negative statement.

questions.prompt: Hay ___ (some) estudiantes en la clase.
questions.explanation: "estudiantes" is plural, so the plural form "algunos" is needed; "algún" is singular and "algunas" is feminine.

questions.prompt: No hay ___ (no) razón para preocuparse.
questions.explanation: "razón" is feminine singular, so the negative form "ninguna" is used after "No hay"; "ningún" is for masculine nouns and "ninguno" stands alone.

questions.prompt: ¿Conoces a ___ (someone) aquí?
questions.explanation: "alguien" means 'someone/anyone' and follows the personal "a" when asking whether you know a person; "algo" is for things and "nadie" is negative.

questions.prompt: No conozco a ___ (no one) en esta ciudad.
questions.explanation: "nadie" means 'no one' and works with "No conozco a" for a double negative about people; "nada" refers to things and "alguien" is positive.

questions.prompt: ¿Compraste ___ (something) en la tienda?
questions.explanation: The clue "something" calls for the indefinite pronoun "algo", which stands for an unspecified thing. "nada" is negative, "alguien" means a person, and "algún" must be followed by a noun.

questions.prompt: No compré ___ (nothing) hoy.
questions.explanation: After "No compré" Spanish uses a double negative, so the negative word "nada" (nothing) is needed. "algo" is positive and "nadie" refers to people, not things.

questions.prompt: ¿Tienes ___ (any) pregunta?
questions.explanation: "pregunta" is feminine singular, so the adjective must be "alguna". "algún" is only used before masculine nouns and "alguno" is the pronoun form.

units.title: Passive 'Se' Constructions
units.description: se vende, se dice, se necesita — Impersonal/passive 'se' constructions common in signs and announcements.

lessons.title: Passive 'Se' Constructions 1
lessons.subtitle: se vende, se dice, se necesita

questions.prompt: Se ___ (vender) esta casa.
questions.explanation: In passive "se" the verb agrees with the thing sold, "esta casa", which is singular, so we need "vende". "venden" would be plural and "vendes" is a "tú" form.
questions.meaning: is sold, is for sale (in "se vende")

questions.prompt: Se ___ (decir) que va a llover.
questions.explanation: "Se dice que..." is a fixed impersonal phrase meaning 'it is said that', and its verb stays singular: "dice". "dicen" is plural and "digo" is first person, which doesn't fit with "se".

questions.prompt: Se ___ (necesitar) empleados.
questions.explanation: The thing needed, "empleados", is plural, so the verb with passive "se" must be plural too: "necesitan". "necesitas" and "necesito" are "tú" and "yo" forms.

questions.prompt: Se ___ (hablar) español aquí.
questions.explanation: The thing spoken, "español", is singular, so the passive "se" verb is singular: "habla". "hablan" would be plural and "hablas" is a "tú" form.

questions.prompt: Se ___ (prohibir) fumar.
questions.explanation: With an infinitive like "fumar" as what is banned, the verb is singular: "prohíbe" ('smoking is prohibited'). "prohíben" is plural and "prohíbo" is a first-person form.

lessons.title: Passive 'Se' Constructions 2
lessons.subtitle: se vende, se dice, se necesita

questions.prompt: Se ___ (buscar) camarero con experiencia.
questions.explanation: The thing sought, "camarero", is singular, so passive "se" takes a singular verb: "busca". "buscan" is plural and "buscamos" is a "nosotros" form.
questions.example: Se busca mesero con experiencia.

questions.prompt: Se ___ (alquilar) apartamentos.
questions.explanation: The thing rented, "apartamentos", is plural, so the passive "se" verb must be plural: "alquilan". "alquila" is singular and "alquilamos" is a "nosotros" form.

questions.prompt: Se ___ (poder) pagar con tarjeta.
questions.explanation: The conjugated verb "puede" agrees with the infinitive "pagar" (what can be done), which counts as singular. "pueden" is plural and "podemos" is a "nosotros" form.

questions.prompt: Se ___ (permitir) el acceso solo a socios.
questions.explanation: The thing allowed, "el acceso", is singular, so passive "se" takes a singular verb: "permite". "permiten" is plural and "permitimos" is a "nosotros" form.

questions.prompt: Se ___ (recomendar) llegar temprano.
questions.explanation: The thing recommended is the infinitive clause "llegar temprano", which counts as singular, so impersonal 'se' takes the singular verb "recomienda".

lessons.title: Passive 'Se' Constructions 3
lessons.subtitle: se vende, se dice, se necesita

questions.prompt: La tienda se ___ (abrir) a las nueve.
questions.explanation: The subject "la tienda" is singular, so the verb with 'se' is third-person singular: "abre". "abren" would need a plural subject and "abrimos" means 'we open'.

questions.prompt: La biblioteca se ___ (cerrar) los domingos.
questions.explanation: The subject "la biblioteca" is singular, so the verb with 'se' is third-person singular: "cierra". "cierran" would need a plural subject and "cerramos" means 'we close'.

questions.prompt: Se ___ (aceptar) reservas online.
questions.explanation: In passive 'se' the verb agrees with the noun, and "reservas" is plural, so the verb must be plural: "aceptan".

questions.prompt: Se ___ (ofrecer) descuentos a estudiantes.
questions.explanation: The thing offered is "descuentos", which is plural, so the passive 'se' verb must agree in the plural: "ofrecen".

questions.prompt: Se ___ (requerir) identificación.
