questions.explanation: "identificación" is a singular noun, so passive 'se' takes the singular verb "requiere" (identification is required).

units.title: Si-Clauses (Hypothetical Present)
units.description: If I had..., I would... — Type-2 conditional: si + imperfect subjunctive, + conditional.

questions.prompt: Si yo ___ (tener) más dinero, viajaría más.
questions.explanation: The main clause uses the conditional "viajaría", so the si-clause needs the imperfect subjunctive: "tuviera"; the conditional or present cannot follow 'si' here.

questions.prompt: Si ella ___ (estudiar) más, aprobaría el examen.
questions.explanation: After 'si' in a hypothetical, with "aprobaría" in the result clause, use the imperfect subjunctive; for 'ella' that is "estudiara" ("estudiaran" is plural).

questions.prompt: Si nosotros ___ (vivir) cerca, nos veríamos más.
questions.explanation: The subject is "nosotros" and the result clause is conditional ("veríamos"), so the si-clause needs the 'nosotros' imperfect subjunctive with its accent: "viviéramos".

questions.prompt: Si ellos ___ (saber) la verdad, actuarían diferente.
questions.explanation: A hypothetical 'si' clause followed by the conditional "actuarían" takes the imperfect subjunctive; 'saber' is irregular, giving "supieran" for 'ellos'.

questions.prompt: Si tú ___ (poder), ¿qué harías?
questions.explanation: The subject is "tú" and the result clause is conditional ("harías"), so the si-clause takes the 'tú' imperfect subjunctive of 'poder': "pudieras".

questions.prompt: Si yo ___ (ser) rico, ayudaría a más gente.
questions.explanation: Being rich is a hypothetical state ('ser', not 'estar'), and with "ayudaría" in the result clause the si-clause takes the imperfect subjunctive: "fuera".

questions.prompt: Si ella ___ (querer), podría cambiar de trabajo.
questions.explanation: After "si" in a hypothetical, the verb takes the imperfect subjunctive, so "quisiera" fits, matching the conditional "podría" in the main clause. "quiera" is present subjunctive and "querría" is conditional, which cannot follow "si" here.

questions.prompt: Si nosotros ___ (tener) tiempo, iríamos contigo.
questions.explanation: The "si" clause needs the imperfect subjunctive, and the "nosotros" form of "tener" is "tuviéramos", matching the conditional "iríamos". "tuviera" is a singular form and "tendríamos" is conditional.

questions.prompt: Si tú me ___ (decir) la verdad, te ayudaría.
questions.explanation: With "tú", the imperfect subjunctive of "decir" is "dijeras", which goes after "si" before the conditional "ayudaría". "digas" is present subjunctive and "dirías" is conditional.

questions.prompt: Si ellos ___ (venir) antes, verían el atardecer.
questions.explanation: The subject "ellos" calls for the third-person plural imperfect subjunctive "vinieran" after "si", paired with the conditional "verían". "viniera" is singular and "viniéramos" is first-person plural.

questions.prompt: Si yo ___ (hacer) más ejercicio, me sentiría mejor.
questions.explanation: The subject "yo" takes the first-person singular imperfect subjunctive "hiciera" after "si", paired with the conditional "sentiría". "hicieras" is the "tú" form and "hicieran" is plural.

questions.prompt: Si ella ___ (estar) aquí, todo sería más fácil.
questions.explanation: The subject "ella" is third-person singular, so the imperfect subjunctive after "si" is "estuviera", matching the conditional "sería". "estuvieran" is plural and "estuviéramos" is "nosotros".

questions.prompt: Si nosotros ___ (poder), te ayudaríamos ahora mismo.
questions.explanation: The subject "nosotros" needs the imperfect subjunctive "pudiéramos" (with accent) after "si", paired with the conditional "ayudaríamos". "pudieras" is "tú" and "pudieran" is "ellos".
questions.meaning: we could, we were able to (if-clause form)

questions.prompt: Si tú ___ (querer), podríamos hablar hoy.
questions.explanation: With "tú", the imperfect subjunctive of "querer" is "quisieras", used after "si" before the conditional "podríamos". "quieras" is present subjunctive and "querrías" is conditional.

questions.prompt: Si ellos ___ (ser) más pacientes, entenderían mejor.
questions.explanation: After "si" with "ellos", "ser" takes the imperfect subjunctive "fueran", matching the conditional "entenderían". "serían" is conditional and "estuvieran" comes from "estar", which does not go with "ser pacientes" as a trait.

units.title: Business & Economy
units.description: The world of work and money — Business and economics vocabulary.

lessons.title: Business & Economy 1
lessons.subtitle: The world of work and money

questions.prompt: How do you say "economy" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "economía" is the Spanish word for "economy", a country's system of money, trade and production; "pérdida" means "loss" and "demanda" means "demand".

questions.prompt: How do you say "bankruptcy" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "bancarrota" (also "quiebra") is the state of being unable to pay what you owe; "deuda" is the debt itself and "impuesto" is a tax.

questions.prompt: How do you say "investment" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "inversión" is money put into something to earn a return, which is what "investment" means; "economía" is the economy and "exportación" is an export.

questions.prompt: How do you say "profit" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ganancia" means "profit", the money a business earns after costs. "Inversión" means "investment" and "oferta" means "supply" or "offer".

questions.prompt: How do you say "loss" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A financial loss is "pérdida" (feminine: la pérdida), the opposite of ganancia (profit); inversión means investment and oferta means supply or offer.

lessons.title: Business & Economy 2
lessons.subtitle: The world of work and money

questions.prompt: How do you say "budget" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A budget, a planned amount of money to spend, is "presupuesto" (masculine: el presupuesto); acción means share and pérdida means loss.

questions.prompt: How do you say "tax" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A tax paid to the government is "impuesto" (el impuesto, often plural: pagar impuestos); a subsidio is money the government gives, not money it collects.

questions.prompt: How do you say "inflation" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "inflación" is the general rise in prices, which is what "inflation" means; "bancarrota" is bankruptcy and "importación" is an import.

questions.prompt: How do you say "export" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "exportación" is the selling of goods to another country, which is what "export" means as a noun; "deuda" is debt and "presupuesto" is a budget.

questions.prompt: How do you say "import" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "importación" is the buying of goods from another country, which is what "import" means as a noun; "inflación" is inflation and "economía" is the economy.

lessons.title: Business & Economy 3
lessons.subtitle: The world of work and money

questions.prompt: How do you say "supply" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: In economics, supply as in 'supply and demand' is "oferta" (la oferta y la demanda); presupuesto means budget and deuda means debt.

questions.prompt: How do you say "demand" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "demanda" is how much people want to buy, as in "oferta y demanda" (supply and demand); "economía" is the economy and "inflación" is inflation.

questions.prompt: How do you say "stock (shares)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A share of a company is "acción" (las acciones de una empresa), the same word as 'action'; inversión means investment.

questions.prompt: How do you say "debt" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "deuda" is money you owe, which is what "debt" means; "demanda" is demand and "pérdida" is a loss.

questions.prompt: How do you say "subsidy" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "subsidio" is money the government gives to support a person or industry, which is what "subsidy" means; "impuesto" is a tax and "deuda" is a debt.

units.title: Politics & Government
units.description: Civic vocabulary — Politics and government vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "government" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "gobierno" is the group of people that runs a country, which is what "government" means; "constitución" is the constitution and "ciudadano" is a citizen.

questions.prompt: How do you say "president" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "presidente" is the head of state, like English "president"; "alcalde" is a mayor and "congreso" is the legislature.

questions.prompt: How do you say "election" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "elección" is an election (a national vote is usually the plural "elecciones"); "política" is politics and "gobierno" is government.

questions.prompt: How do you say "vote" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "voto" is the noun for a vote you cast (the verb is "votar"); "elección" is the election and "campaña" the campaign.

questions.prompt: How do you say "citizen" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ciudadano" is a citizen, a person who belongs to a country and has rights there; "ley" is a law and "senado" the senate.

questions.prompt: How do you say "law" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ley" is a law, a rule passed by a legislature; "referéndum" is a public vote and "democracia" a system of government.

questions.prompt: How do you say "congress" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "congreso" is the congress, the body that makes laws; "presidente" is the president and "ministro" a minister.

questions.prompt: How do you say "democracy" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "democracia" is democracy, government chosen by the people; "constitución" is the constitution and "voto" a vote.

questions.prompt: How do you say "policy" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "política" means both politics and a government's policy (plan of action); "ley" is a law and "alcalde" a mayor.

questions.prompt: How do you say "minister" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ministro" is a minister, the head of a government department; "gobierno" is the whole government and "democracia" a system of government.

questions.prompt: How do you say "campaign" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "campaña" is a campaign, the organized effort to win votes; "presidente" is the president and "política" is politics or policy.

questions.prompt: How do you say "constitution" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "constitución" is the constitution, a country's founding set of laws; "congreso" is the legislature and "referéndum" a public vote.

questions.prompt: How do you say "senate" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "senado" is the senate, the upper chamber of the legislature; "alcalde" is a mayor and "ley" a law.

questions.prompt: How do you say "mayor" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: The head of a city government is "alcalde" (alcaldesa for a woman); voto means vote and campaña means campaign.

questions.prompt: How do you say "referendum" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A "referéndum" is a direct vote by citizens on a single question; note the accent on the é, which English does not have.

units.title: Media & Journalism
units.description: News and reporting — Media and journalism vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "news" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: 'The news' is usually plural in Spanish, "noticias" (las noticias), and one news item is una noticia; titular means headline.

questions.prompt: How do you say "journalist" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A "periodista" is anyone who works as a journalist; a "corresponsal" reports from a particular place, and a "locutor" is a radio or TV announcer.

questions.prompt: How do you say "newspaper" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A newspaper is "periódico" (el periódico), and diario is also common in Latin America; audiencia means audience.

questions.prompt: How do you say "headline" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: The big title of a news story is "titular" (el titular); noticias means news and editor means editor.

questions.prompt: How do you say "article" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A newspaper or magazine "article" is "artículo" in Spanish; a "titular" is only the headline, not the whole piece.

questions.prompt: How do you say "correspondent" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A "corresponsal" is a journalist who reports from another city or country, for example "el corresponsal en Washington".

questions.prompt: How do you say "broadcast" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A radio or TV "broadcast" is a "transmisión", as in "la transmisión en vivo del partido"; "emisión" is also used.

questions.prompt: How do you say "report" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A journalistic report or feature is a "reportaje"; a "periodista" is the person who writes it and a "rueda de prensa" is a press conference.

questions.prompt: How do you say "editor" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: The person who prepares and revises texts for publication is an "editor" in Spanish too; a "lector" is a reader and a "locutor" is an announcer.

questions.prompt: How do you say "press conference" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A press conference is "rueda de prensa", and conferencia de prensa is also very common in Latin America; transmisión means broadcast.

questions.prompt: How do you say "source (of info)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Where information comes from is "fuente" (una fuente confiable, 'a reliable source'), the same word as 'fountain'; a corresponsal is a correspondent.

questions.prompt: How do you say "censorship" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Censorship is "censura" (la censura), from the verb censurar, 'to censor'; fuente means source and titular means headline.

questions.prompt: How do you say "publish" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "publicar" means to make a text available to the public, as in "publicar un artículo"; "censurar" means to censor and "transmitir" means to broadcast.

questions.prompt: How do you say "audience" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "audiencia" is the people who watch or listen to a programme; "noticias" means news and "reportaje" is a report or feature.

questions.prompt: How do you say "subscription" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "suscripción" is a subscription to a newspaper or service; note the Spanish spelling has no "b" (not "subscripción").

units.title: Art & Culture
units.description: The arts — Art and culture vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "painting" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "pintura" means painting, both the art and a painted work; "galería" is the place where paintings are shown.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sculpture" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "escultura" is a sculpture, a work carved or modelled in 3D; "artesanía" means crafts.

questions.prompt: How do you say "exhibition" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "exposición" is an art exhibition; "escultor" is a sculptor and "lienzo" is a canvas.

questions.prompt: How do you say "curator" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: In Latin America the person who selects and organizes an exhibition is a "curador" (in Spain, usually "comisario").

questions.prompt: How do you say "gallery" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: An art "gallery" is a "galería" in Spanish, as in "una galería de arte moderno"; note the accent on the í.

questions.prompt: How do you say "portrait" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A painting or photo of a person is a "retrato"; a "lienzo" is the canvas it may be painted on.

questions.prompt: How do you say "masterpiece" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "obra maestra" is literally a master work, an artist's finest piece; "pincel" is a paintbrush.

questions.prompt: How do you say "canvas" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: The cloth surface an artist paints on is a "lienzo", as in "pintó el paisaje sobre un lienzo grande".

questions.prompt: How do you say "paintbrush" (an artist's brush) in Spanish?
questions.explanation: An artist's brush for painting is "pincel". A hairbrush is a cepillo, and a broad brush for walls is a brocha.

questions.prompt: How do you say "tradition" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "tradición" means a custom passed down through generations; English -tion often becomes -ción in Spanish, as in "Es una tradición familiar."

questions.prompt: How do you say "heritage" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "patrimonio" is heritage, as in "patrimonio cultural" (cultural heritage); "curador" is a curator.

questions.prompt: How do you say "festival" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: festival → festival. Art and culture vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "performance" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "actuación" is a performance on stage by an actor or musician; "lienzo" is a canvas and "pintura" a painting.

questions.prompt: How do you say "craft" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "artesanía" means craft, handmade traditional work such as pottery or weaving; "tradición" just means tradition.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sculptor" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A person who makes sculptures is an "escultor" (feminine: escultora), as in "El escultor trabaja con mármol."

units.title: Health & Medicine (Advanced)
units.description: Medical vocabulary — Advanced health and medical vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "diagnosis" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "diagnóstico" is the doctor's identification of an illness, as in "El médico dio el diagnóstico ayer."

questions.prompt: How do you say "treatment" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "tratamiento" is the care or medicine given to cure an illness, as in "El tratamiento dura tres semanas."

questions.prompt: How do you say "surgery" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cirugía" is a medical operation; the related verb is "operar", as in "Necesita una cirugía de rodilla."

questions.prompt: How do you say "vaccine" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "vacuna" is the shot that protects you from a disease; the verb is "vacunar", as in "Me pusieron la vacuna contra la gripe."

questions.prompt: How do you say "infection" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "infección" is an illness caused by germs; English -tion becomes -ción, with an accent on the last syllable.

questions.prompt: How do you say "chronic" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "crónico" describes a condition that lasts a long time, the opposite of agudo (acute), as in "Tiene un dolor crónico de espalda."

questions.prompt: How do you say "inflammation" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "inflamación" is swelling and redness in part of the body; do not confuse it with infección, which is caused by germs.

questions.prompt: How do you say "recovery" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "recuperación" is the period of getting better after an illness or surgery; the verb is "recuperarse".

questions.prompt: How do you say "specialist" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "especialista" means "specialist", a doctor who focuses on one field; the same form is used for men and women (el/la especialista).

questions.prompt: How do you say "emergency room" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "sala de urgencias" is the hospital's emergency room; people often shorten it to "urgencias", as in "Lo llevaron a urgencias".

questions.prompt: How do you say "blood pressure" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "presión arterial" means "blood pressure" (literally "arterial pressure"), as in "El médico me midió la presión arterial".

questions.prompt: How do you say "side effect" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "efecto secundario" means "side effect", an unwanted reaction to a medicine; literally it is a "secondary effect".

questions.prompt: How do you say "immune system" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "sistema inmunológico" means "immune system", the body's defense against disease; "sistema nervioso" is the nervous system.

questions.prompt: How do you say "prescription" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "receta médica" is a doctor's prescription for medicine; "receta" on its own can also mean a cooking recipe, so "médica" makes the meaning clear.

questions.prompt: How do you say "anesthesia" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "anestesia" means "anesthesia"; note the Spanish spelling with "st" and no "h".

units.title: Probability Expressions
units.description: deber de, puede (ser) que, a lo mejor — Expressions of probability and conjecture.

lessons.title: Probability Expressions 1
lessons.subtitle: deber de, poder ser que, a lo mejor

questions.prompt: ___ de estar en casa ya.
questions.explanation: The probability phrase is "deber de + infinitive", so "Debe" de estar means "he/she must be". "Puede" does not take "de" before an infinitive.

questions.prompt: A lo ___, llega tarde.
questions.explanation: "A lo mejor" is a fixed phrase meaning "maybe", so "mejor" completes it. "bien" and "bueno" do not form this expression.
questions.example: A lo mejor llega tarde.

questions.prompt: Puede ___ que no venga.
questions.explanation: "Puede ser que" is the fixed expression for "it may be that" and takes the subjunctive "venga", so "ser" is right. "estar", "haber" and "hacer" do not form this phrase.
questions.meaning: to be; puede ser que: it may be

questions.prompt: ___ esté ocupado.
questions.explanation: "Probablemente" can be followed by the subjunctive, so it fits "esté". "Seguro que" and "A lo mejor" are followed by the indicative ("está"), so they don't fit here.

questions.prompt: Seguramente ___ (haber) mucho tráfico.
questions.explanation: "Seguramente" can take the indicative, and impersonal haber is always singular, so the answer is "hay". "haber" is the infinitive, and "hayan" is never used for 'there is/are'.

lessons.title: Probability Expressions 2
lessons.subtitle: deber de, poder ser que, a lo mejor

questions.prompt: Tal ___ mañana llueva.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression "tal vez" means "maybe", and it often takes the subjunctive, as in "llueva"; "tal caso" and "tal modo" are not expressions of probability, so the answer is "vez".

questions.prompt: Es posible que el perro ya ___ (perderse).
questions.explanation: "Es posible que" always triggers the subjunctive, and "ya" points to a completed event, so the perfect subjunctive "se haya perdido" is needed. "se ha perdido" and "se perdió" are indicative.

questions.prompt: Quizás ella ya lo ___ (saber).
questions.explanation: "Quizás" is followed here by the subjunctive, and the subject "ella" needs the third person singular, "sepa". "sepas" is for tú and "sepan" is plural.

questions.prompt: A lo mejor él no ___ (querer) venir.
questions.explanation: "A lo mejor" is always followed by the indicative, never the subjunctive, so "quiere" is right. "quiera" is the subjunctive trap and "quieren" is plural, not matching "él".

questions.prompt: Debe de ___ muy tarde ya.
questions.explanation: "Deber de" + infinitive expresses a guess, and telling the time uses ser, so "ser" fits: "It must be very late already."
questions.meaning: to be; debe de ser: must be

lessons.title: Probability Expressions 3
lessons.subtitle: deber de, poder ser que, a lo mejor

questions.prompt: Igual ella ___ (llegar) antes que nosotros.
questions.explanation: Colloquial "igual" meaning "maybe" takes the indicative, and "ella" needs the third person singular, so "llega". "llegue" is subjunctive and "llegan" is plural.

questions.prompt: Puede que él ___ (tener) razón.
questions.explanation: "Puede que" always takes the subjunctive, and "él" needs the third person singular, so "tenga". "tiene" is indicative and "tengan" is plural.

questions.prompt: Lo más seguro es que ella ___ (estar) en camino.
questions.explanation: "Lo más seguro es que" is followed by the subjunctive, and "ella" needs the third person singular, so "esté". "estés" is for tú and "estén" is plural.

questions.prompt: A lo mejor no ___ (recordar) la cita.
questions.explanation: "A lo mejor" is followed by the indicative, never the subjunctive, so the answer is "recuerda". "recuerde" is the subjunctive form, which this expression doesn't take.

questions.prompt: Seguro que ella ya ___ (terminar).
questions.explanation: "Seguro que" expresses certainty and takes the indicative, and "ya" points to a finished action by one person, so "terminó". "termine" is subjunctive and "terminaron" is plural.

units.title: Subjunctive with Doubt & Denial
units.description: No creo que, dudo que, niego que... — Subjunctive triggered by expressions of doubt or denial.

lessons.title: Subjunctive with Doubt & Denial 1
lessons.subtitle: No creo que, dudo que, niego que...

questions.prompt: No creo que ella ___ (venir) hoy.
questions.explanation: "No creo que" expresses doubt, so the verb goes in the subjunctive, and "venga" is the third-person singular form that agrees with "ella".

questions.prompt: Dudo que ellos ___ (saber) la respuesta.
questions.explanation: "Dudo que" expresses doubt, so the verb needs the subjunctive, and "sepan" is the plural form of saber that agrees with "ellos".

questions.prompt: No es verdad que él ___ (mentir).
questions.explanation: "No es verdad que" denies a statement, so the verb takes the subjunctive, and "mienta" is the third-person singular form for "él".

questions.prompt: Niego que nosotros ___ (tener) la culpa.
questions.explanation: "Niego que" expresses denial, so the verb is in the subjunctive, and "tengamos" is the "nosotros" form of tener.

questions.prompt: No pienso que tú ___ (estar) equivocado.
questions.explanation: "No pienso que" expresses doubt, so the subjunctive is required, and "estés" is the "tú" form of estar (with the accent).

lessons.title: Subjunctive with Doubt & Denial 2
lessons.subtitle: No creo que, dudo que, niego que...

questions.prompt: No parece que ___ (ir) a llover.
questions.explanation: "No parece que" expresses doubt about what is likely, so the subjunctive follows, and "vaya" is the subjunctive of ir in "vaya a llover".

questions.prompt: No es cierto que ella ___ (haber) llegado.
questions.explanation: "No es cierto que" denies certainty, so the subjunctive is needed; the present perfect subjunctive uses "haya" + participle for "ella".

questions.prompt: Dudamos que ellos ___ (poder) terminar a tiempo.
questions.explanation: "Dudamos que" expresses doubt, so the verb is subjunctive, and "puedan" is the plural form of poder agreeing with "ellos".

questions.prompt: No creemos que él ___ (decir) la verdad.
questions.explanation: "No creemos que" denies belief, so the subjunctive is used, and "diga" is the third-person singular form of decir for "él".

questions.prompt: No es seguro que nosotros ___ (ganar).
questions.explanation: "No es seguro que" expresses uncertainty, so the subjunctive is required, and "ganemos" is the "nosotros" form of ganar.

lessons.title: Subjunctive with Doubt & Denial 3
lessons.subtitle: No creo que, dudo que, niego que...

questions.prompt: No confío en que ellos ___ (cumplir) su promesa.
questions.explanation: "No confío en que" expresses lack of confidence, so the subjunctive follows, and "cumplan" is the plural form agreeing with "ellos".

questions.prompt: No es probable que ___ (nevar) esta semana.
questions.explanation: "No es probable que" expresses doubt, so the subjunctive is needed, and "nieve" is the subjunctive of nevar (e changes to ie).

questions.prompt: No creo que tú ___ (querer) hacerlo.
questions.explanation: "No creo que" expresses doubt, so the verb takes the subjunctive, and the subject "tú" needs the second-person form "quieras".

questions.prompt: Niegan que la empresa ___ (perder) dinero.
questions.explanation: "Niegan que" (they deny that) triggers the subjunctive, and "la empresa" is third-person singular, so the form is "pierda".

questions.prompt: No es evidente que ella ___ (saber) nadar.
questions.explanation: "No es evidente que" denies certainty, so the subjunctive is needed; "ella" takes the third-person form "sepa" (irregular subjunctive of saber).

lessons.title: Subjunctive with Doubt & Denial 4
lessons.subtitle: No creo que, dudo que, niego que...

questions.prompt: Dudo que él ___ (venir) mañana.
questions.explanation: "Dudo que" expresses doubt, so the subjunctive follows, and "él" takes the third-person form "venga".

questions.prompt: No creo que nosotros ___ (necesitar) más tiempo.
questions.explanation: "No creo que" expresses doubt, so the subjunctive is required; with "nosotros" the present subjunctive of necesitar is "necesitemos".

questions.prompt: No es verdad que ellos ___ (pagar) tanto.
questions.explanation: "No es verdad que" denies the statement, so the verb after it goes in the subjunctive: "paguen" (pagar changes g to gu before e).

questions.prompt: No creo que tú ___ (hacer) eso.
questions.explanation: "No creo que" expresses doubt, so the verb after it is in the subjunctive; the tú form of hacer is "hagas".

questions.prompt: No creo que ella ___ (poder) sola.
questions.explanation: "No creo que" expresses doubt, so the subjunctive follows, and "ella" takes the third-person form "pueda".
questions.example: No creo que ella pueda hacerlo sola.

lessons.title: Subjunctive with Doubt & Denial 5
lessons.subtitle: No creo que, dudo que, niego que...

questions.prompt: Dudamos que el plan ___ (funcionar).
questions.explanation: "Dudamos que" expresses doubt, so the subjunctive is needed, and "el plan" is third-person singular: "funcione".

questions.prompt: No es verdad que nosotros ___ (mentir).
questions.explanation: "No es verdad que" denies a fact, so the subjunctive is required; for "nosotros" the stem-changing verb mentir uses "mintamos" (e becomes i).

questions.prompt: No pienso que ustedes ___ (estar) listos.
questions.explanation: "No pienso que" expresses doubt, so the subjunctive is used, and "ustedes" takes the third-person plural form "estén" (with the accent).

questions.prompt: No creo que él ___ (ser) el culpable.
questions.explanation: "No creo que" expresses doubt, so the subjunctive is required, and "él" takes the third-person singular subjunctive of ser: "sea".

questions.prompt: No es seguro que ellos ___ (llegar) a tiempo.
questions.explanation: "lleguen" is right because "No es seguro que" expresses doubt and so takes the subjunctive, and the plural subject "ellos" needs the plural form (llegar → lleguen).

units.title: Advanced Personality Adjectives
units.description: Describing character — Advanced personality-trait adjectives.

questions.prompt: How do you say "ambitious" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: ambitious → ambicioso. Advanced personality-trait adjectives.

questions.prompt: How do you say "stubborn" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "terco" describes someone stubborn who won't change their mind; "ingenuo" means naive and "grosero" means rude.

questions.prompt: How do you say "generous" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: generous → generoso. Advanced personality-trait adjectives.

questions.prompt: How do you say "arrogant" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: arrogant → arrogante. Advanced personality-trait adjectives.

questions.prompt: How do you say "humble" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "humilde" means humble, someone who doesn't show off; "cortés" means polite and "exigente" means demanding.

questions.prompt: How do you say "reliable" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: reliable → confiable. Advanced personality-trait adjectives.

questions.prompt: How do you say "cautious" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cauteloso" means 'cautious': describing someone who acts carefully to avoid risks or mistakes.

questions.prompt: How do you say "curious" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "curioso" means 'curious': describing someone who wants to learn or find out about things.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sincere" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "sincero" means 'sincere': describing someone who says what they really think and feel; its opposite here is "hipócrita".

questions.prompt: How do you say "hypocritical" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "hipócrita" means 'hypocritical': describing someone who says one thing and does another, and it has the same form for masculine and feminine.

questions.prompt: How do you say "optimistic" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "optimista" means 'optimistic': describing someone who expects good outcomes, and it ends in -a for both masculine and feminine.

questions.prompt: How do you say "pessimistic" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "pesimista" means 'pessimistic': describing someone who expects bad outcomes, and it ends in -a for both masculine and feminine.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sensitive" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "sensible" means 'sensitive' (easily affected by feelings); careful, it is a false friend, and English 'sensible' is "sensato" in Spanish.

questions.prompt: How do you say "tolerant" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "tolerante" means 'tolerant': describing someone who accepts people and opinions different from their own.

questions.prompt: How do you say "rude" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "grosero" means 'rude': describing someone who behaves without manners; its opposite in the bank is "cortés".

questions.prompt: How do you say "polite" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cortés" means 'polite': describing someone with good manners, and it has the same form for masculine and feminine.

questions.prompt: How do you say "honest" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "honesto" means 'honest': describing someone who tells the truth, which is different from "confiable" ('trustworthy').

questions.prompt: How do you say "dishonest" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "deshonesto" means 'dishonest': it is "honesto" with the negative prefix des-, while "desleal" means 'disloyal'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "loyal" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: loyal → leal. Advanced personality-trait adjectives.

questions.prompt: How do you say "disloyal" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: disloyal → desleal. Advanced personality-trait adjectives.

questions.prompt: How do you say "competitive" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: competitive → competitivo. Advanced personality-trait adjectives.

questions.prompt: How do you say "relaxed, easygoing" (personality) in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "relajado" describes a relaxed, easygoing person who doesn't get stressed; the other words mean disloyal, generous and hypocritical.

questions.prompt: How do you say "demanding" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: demanding → exigente. Advanced personality-trait adjectives.

questions.prompt: How do you say "resourceful" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: resourceful → ingenioso. Advanced personality-trait adjectives.

questions.prompt: How do you say "naive" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: naive → ingenuo. Advanced personality-trait adjectives.

units.title: Legal & Civic Rights
units.description: Rights and civic vocabulary — Civic rights and legal-process vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "right (entitlement)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: right (entitlement) → derecho. Civic rights and legal-process vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "duty" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: duty → deber. Civic rights and legal-process vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "freedom of speech" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "libertad de expresión" is the right to say what you think; "libertad de culto" is freedom of religion.

questions.prompt: How do you say "privacy" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: privacy → privacidad. Civic rights and legal-process vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "equality" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: equality → igualdad. Civic rights and legal-process vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "discrimination" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: discrimination → discriminación. Civic rights and legal-process vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "injustice" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: The English ending -ice often becomes -icia in Spanish, so "injustice" is "injusticia", a feminine noun (una injusticia).

questions.prompt: How do you say "citizenship" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ciudadanía" is the legal status of being a citizen (ciudadano); here the English ending -ship matches the Spanish ending -ía.

questions.prompt: How do you say "immigration" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Spanish spells it "inmigración", with "nm" rather than "mm" and an accent on the final -ón; it means people moving into a country.

questions.prompt: How do you say "refugee" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A "refugiado" is a person who flees their country to seek protection (refugio); a woman is a "refugiada".

questions.prompt: How do you say "asylum" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "asilo" is the protection a country grants to someone fleeing persecution, as in pedir asilo (to ask for asylum). "apelación" is an appeal, and "derecho" is a right or law.

questions.prompt: How do you say "human rights" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "derechos humanos" puts the adjective after the noun, as Spanish usually does: "derechos" (rights) followed by "humanos" (human), both masculine plural.

questions.prompt: How do you say "protest" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "protesta" is the feminine noun for a public protest (la protesta); the related verb is "protestar".

questions.prompt: How do you say "petition" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A formal written request, often signed by many people, is a "petición"; the English ending -tion becomes -ción, with an accent.

questions.prompt: How do you say "jury" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: The group of citizens who decide a verdict in court is "el jurado"; a single member of it can also be called a "jurado".

questions.prompt: How do you say "witness" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A witness, the person who saw something and testifies about it, is "testigo"; the word is the same for a man or a woman (el/la testigo). "apelación" means appeal and "asilo" means asylum.

questions.prompt: How do you say "testimony" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "testimonio" is the statement a witness (testigo) gives in court; here the English ending -y becomes -io.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sentence (legal)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A judge's legal sentence or ruling is a "sentencia"; a grammatical sentence is an "oración", not a "sentencia".

questions.prompt: How do you say "appeal" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Asking a higher court to review a decision is an "apelación", from the verb "apelar"; lawyers "presentan una apelación".

questions.prompt: How do you say "plaintiff" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: The "demandante" is the person who files a lawsuit, called a "demanda"; the person being sued is the "demandado".

questions.prompt: How do you say "defendant" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: The "acusado" is the person accused of a crime and tried in court. In a civil lawsuit, the other party is usually called "demandado".

questions.prompt: How do you say "fine (penalty)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A "multa" is money you pay as a penalty for breaking a rule or law. Don't confuse it with "fianza", which is bail.

questions.prompt: How do you say "bail" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "fianza" is bail: money paid so an accused person can stay free while waiting for trial.

questions.prompt: How do you say "custody" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "custodia" is legal care of a child or of a person held by the police, as in "la custodia de los hijos" after a divorce.

questions.prompt: How do you say "verdict" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: The "veredicto" is the final decision of a jury or court, such as guilty or not guilty.

units.title: Emotional Intelligence
units.description: Communication and self-awareness — Emotional-intelligence and communication vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "empathy" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "empatía" is the ability to understand and share another person's feelings. Note the accent on the í.

questions.prompt: How do you say "self-esteem" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "autoestima" is how much you value yourself: "auto-" (self) plus "estima" (esteem).

questions.prompt: How do you say "assertiveness" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "asertividad" is expressing your needs and opinions clearly and respectfully, without being passive or aggressive.

questions.prompt: How do you say "resilience" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "resiliencia" is the ability to recover from difficulties and keep going.

questions.prompt: How do you say "conflict" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "conflicto" is a clash or serious disagreement between people; it is English "conflict" with a final -o added, like "contacto" and "efecto".

questions.prompt: How do you say "feedback" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "retroalimentación" is the usual Latin American term for feedback: comments on how someone is doing so they can improve.

questions.prompt: How do you say "criticism" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "crítica" is the noun for criticism, a negative judgement of someone's work or behavior. Its opposite is "elogio", praise.

questions.prompt: How do you say "praise" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "elogio" is the noun for praise, the positive words you give someone for their work or qualities (verb: elogiar).

questions.prompt: How do you say "active listening" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "escucha activa" is the fixed phrase for active listening: paying full attention and showing the speaker you understand. Note that escucha is a feminine noun here, hence activa.

questions.prompt: How do you say "body language" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "lenguaje corporal" is the set phrase for body language: what your posture, gestures and facial expressions communicate.

questions.prompt: How do you say "tone of voice" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "tono de voz" means tone of voice, how you sound when you speak (calm, sharp, warm), which can change how your words are received.

questions.prompt: How do you say "misunderstanding" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "malentendido" (mal + entendido, 'badly understood') is a misunderstanding, when two people take the same words differently.

questions.prompt: How do you say "apology" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "disculpa" is an apology, what you offer when you have made a mistake (pedir una disculpa = to apologize).

questions.prompt: How do you say "forgiveness" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "perdón" is forgiveness, what the hurt person grants (perdonar = to forgive); it is also used in pedir perdón, 'to ask for forgiveness'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "gratitude" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "gratitud" means gratitude, the feeling of being thankful; English nouns ending in -tude often end in -tud in Spanish.

questions.prompt: How do you say "vulnerability" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "vulnerabilidad" means vulnerability, being open to emotional hurt; English -ity usually becomes -idad in Spanish.

questions.prompt: How do you say "boundary" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A personal boundary is "límite", usually plural in the phrase poner límites (to set boundaries). "compromiso" means commitment, not boundary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "trust" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Trust is "confianza", as in tener confianza en alguien (to trust someone). "paciencia" is patience and "disculpa" is an apology.

questions.prompt: How do you say "betrayal" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Betrayal is "traición", the noun from traicionar (to betray), and it needs the accent on the ó. "confianza" is the opposite idea, trust.

questions.prompt: How do you say "reconciliation" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "reconciliación" means reconciliation, making peace again after a conflict; English -tion becomes -ción, with an accent on the ó.

questions.prompt: How do you say "patience" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Patience is "paciencia", spelled with -cia, as in tener paciencia (to be patient). "perdón" means forgiveness and "crítica" means criticism.

questions.prompt: How do you say "mindfulness" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Mindfulness is usually translated as "atención plena", literally 'full attention' to the present moment. "asertividad" is assertiveness and "lenguaje corporal" is body language.

questions.prompt: How do you say "self-awareness" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "autoconocimiento" (auto 'self' + conocimiento 'knowledge') is self-awareness, knowing your own emotions, strengths and limits.

questions.prompt: How do you say "motivation" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "motivación" means motivation, the drive that makes you act; English -tion becomes -ción, with an accent on the ó.

questions.prompt: How do you say "commitment" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "compromiso" means "commitment", a promise or obligation you take on. Careful: it is a false friend for "compromise", which is usually "acuerdo" or "término medio".

units.title: Housing & Real Estate
units.description: Renting and buying property — Housing and real-estate vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "rent" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: The money you pay to live in someone else's home is "alquiler"; in Mexico you will also hear renta. "hipoteca" is a mortgage, which is a loan to buy a home.

questions.prompt: How do you say "mortgage" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A home loan from a bank is "hipoteca". "tasación" is an appraisal of the home's value, and "inspección" is an inspection.

questions.prompt: How do you say "lease" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A "lease" is the legal agreement to rent a home, which is "contrato de arrendamiento"; in everyday Latin American speech you will also hear "contrato de alquiler".

questions.prompt: How do you say "tenant" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A "tenant" is the person who rents a home from its owner, which is "inquilino" in Spanish ("inquilina" for a woman).

questions.prompt: How do you say "landlord" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A "landlord" is the owner who rents the home out, so the word is "propietario"; the person renting from him is the "inquilino".

questions.prompt: How do you say "inspection" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "inspección" is the direct cognate of "inspection", here a check of the home's condition. Note the accent on the final -ón.

questions.prompt: How do you say "real estate agent" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "agente inmobiliario" is the person who sells or rents out properties; "inmobiliario" means "related to real estate".

questions.prompt: How do you say "property" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: In housing, "property" means a building or land someone owns, which is "propiedad" in Spanish.

questions.prompt: How do you say "neighborhood" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "vecindario" means the neighborhood, the area where you live and the people in it; "barrio" is a very common everyday synonym.

questions.prompt: How do you say "utilities" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Utilities" are basic services such as water, electricity and gas, called "servicios públicos" in Spanish.

questions.prompt: How do you say "square meters" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A home's size is measured in "metros cuadrados" (written m²); the adjective "cuadrados" comes after the noun and agrees with it.

questions.prompt: How do you say "down payment" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A "down payment" is the first payment when you buy a home, "pago inicial"; depending on the country you will also hear "enganche" (Mexico) or "cuota inicial".

questions.prompt: How do you say "appraisal" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: An "appraisal" is the official estimate of a property's value, which is "tasación" (from "tasar", to value).

questions.prompt: How do you say "renovation" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "renovación" is the Spanish cognate of "renovation": the work done to update or repair a home, as in "La casa necesita una renovación".

questions.prompt: How do you say "furnished" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "amueblado" describes a home that comes with furniture (from "mueble", furniture); its opposite is "sin amueblar".

questions.prompt: How do you say "unfurnished" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "sin amueblar" is "sin" (without) plus "amueblar" (to furnish), so it describes a place rented or sold with no furniture.

questions.prompt: How do you say "move in" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "mudarse" means to move to a new home; use "mudarse a" for the place you move into ("Me mudo a mi nuevo apartamento el lunes").

questions.prompt: How do you say "eviction" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Forcing a tenant to leave a home is "desalojo", from desalojar (to evict); Spain also uses desahucio. "renovación" means renovation.

questions.prompt: How do you say "homeowner" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "propietario de vivienda" is the person who owns the home they live in, unlike the "inquilino", who rents it.

questions.prompt: How do you say "condominium" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "condominio" is a building or complex where each unit is privately owned and common areas are shared, just like an English "condominium".

questions.prompt: How do you say "suburb" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: suburb → suburbio. Housing and real-estate vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "downtown" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "centro" (usually "el centro") is the main commercial heart of a city, which is what "downtown" means.

questions.prompt: How do you say "lease agreement" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A lease is "contrato de alquiler", the contract you sign to rent a home; contrato de arrendamiento is the more formal legal term. "hipoteca" is a mortgage, not a lease.

questions.prompt: How do you say "security deposit" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: security deposit → depósito de seguridad. Housing and real-estate vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "real estate market" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Real estate market" is "mercado inmobiliario": "inmobiliario" is the adjective for property and real estate, and it follows the noun "mercado" as Spanish adjectives usually do.

units.title: Connectors of Contrast & Concession
units.description: Advanced contrast connectors — Advanced connectors expressing contrast or concession.

questions.prompt: How do you say "even though" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "aunque" joins two clauses to mean "even though" ("Aunque llueve, salgo"), while "aun así" and "sin embargo" start a new idea meaning "even so" or "however".

questions.prompt: How do you say "despite the fact that" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: despite the fact that → a pesar de que. Advanced connectors expressing contrast or concession.

questions.prompt: How do you say "whereas" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: whereas → mientras que. Advanced connectors expressing contrast or concession.

questions.prompt: How do you say "on the contrary" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "por el contrario" introduces the opposite of what was just said ("No es caro; por el contrario, es barato"), while "por otro lado" only adds a different point.

questions.prompt: How do you say "as a result" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "como resultado" introduces a consequence, like "as a result"; the other options express contrast instead ("de todas formas" means "anyway").

questions.prompt: How do you say "nonetheless" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: nonetheless → no obstante. Advanced connectors expressing contrast or concession.

questions.prompt: How do you say "regardless of" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "independientemente de" means "regardless of" and is followed by a noun or a "que" clause ("independientemente de la edad").

questions.prompt: How do you say "for this reason" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "por esta razón" introduces a consequence of what was just said ("for this reason"); it explains a cause and does not show contrast.

questions.prompt: How do you say "granted that" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "si bien es cierto que" admits a point before you push back on it, like "granted that": Si bien es cierto que es caro, vale la pena.

questions.prompt: How do you say "on the other hand (by contrast)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "por otro lado" starts a new sentence that presents the opposite side, like "on the other hand"; "mientras que" means "whereas" and joins two clauses inside one sentence.

questions.prompt: How do you say "on top of that" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "además de eso" adds one more point to what you said ("on top of that"); it does not express contrast.

questions.prompt: How do you say "all the same" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "de todas formas" means the outcome doesn't change despite what was said, like "all the same"; "pese a" needs a noun after it, so it cannot stand alone here.

questions.prompt: How do you say "in contrast" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "en contraste" directly translates "in contrast" and sets two things side by side to show their difference.

questions.prompt: How do you say "notwithstanding" (before a noun, as in "notwithstanding the cost") in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "pese a" goes before a noun (pese al costo), just like "notwithstanding the cost"; "aun así" cannot be followed by a noun.

questions.prompt: How do you say "at the same time" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "al mismo tiempo" literally means "at the same time"; it links two things happening together and can also add a balancing point.

questions.prompt: How do you say "even so" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "aun así" means "even so": the result holds despite what was just said; "si bien" means "although" and must begin a clause.

questions.prompt: How do you say "albeit" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "si bien" means "albeit" or "although" and introduces a concession; "pese a" means "despite" and needs a noun after it.

questions.prompt: How do you say "in any case" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "en todo caso" is the standard way to say "in any case": whatever happens, this point stands.

questions.prompt: How do you say "either way" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "de cualquier manera" means "either way": whichever option happens, the conclusion is the same.

questions.prompt: How do you say "that said" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "dicho esto" means "that said": it accepts what was just said and then adds a contrasting point, unlike "de todas formas" (anyway).

questions.prompt: How do you say "having said that" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: having said that → habiendo dicho esto. Advanced connectors expressing contrast or concession.

questions.prompt: How do you say "in short" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "en definitiva" means "in short" and introduces a final summing-up of what was said.

questions.prompt: How do you say "all things considered" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: all things considered → considerando todo. Advanced connectors expressing contrast or concession.

questions.prompt: How do you say "in the end" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "al final" means "in the end" and introduces the final outcome after a process or a doubt.

questions.prompt: How do you say "ultimately" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "en última instancia" means "ultimately" and points to the final, deciding factor.

units.title: Speaking: Professional & Abstract Topics
units.description: Say it out loud — Professional and abstract topics to practise saying.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: El cambio climático afecta a todo el planeta.
questions.explanation: Say "El cambio climático afecta a todo el planeta." with the stress on "cli-MÁ-ti-co" and "pla-NE-ta".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: La economía global sigue siendo incierta.
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "La economía global sigue siendo incierta." Professional and abstract topics to practise saying.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Es fundamental proteger el medio ambiente.
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "Es fundamental proteger el medio ambiente." Professional and abstract topics to practise saying.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: La tecnología avanza más rápido que nunca.
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "La tecnología avanza más rápido que nunca." Professional and abstract topics to practise saying.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Muchas empresas apuestan por el trabajo remoto.
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "Muchas empresas apuestan por el trabajo remoto." Professional and abstract topics to practise saying.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: La educación es la base del desarrollo.
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "La educación es la base del desarrollo." Professional and abstract topics to practise saying.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: El gobierno anunció nuevas medidas económicas.
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "El gobierno anunció nuevas medidas económicas." Professional and abstract topics to practise saying.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: La inflación preocupa a los consumidores.
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "La inflación preocupa a los consumidores." Professional and abstract topics to practise saying.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Es importante fomentar la igualdad de oportunidades.
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "Es importante fomentar la igualdad de oportunidades." Professional and abstract topics to practise saying.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: La innovación impulsa el crecimiento empresarial.
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "La innovación impulsa el crecimiento empresarial." It means 'Innovation drives business growth'; "impulsa" (drives, boosts) is a common verb in business Spanish.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Debemos reducir nuestra huella de carbono.
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "Debemos reducir nuestra huella de carbono." It means 'We must reduce our carbon footprint'; "huella de carbono" is the standard term for carbon footprint.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: La inteligencia artificial cambiará muchos empleos.
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "La inteligencia artificial cambiará muchos empleos." It means 'Artificial intelligence will change many jobs'; "cambiará" is the future tense and is stressed on the last syllable.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Las energías renovables son el futuro.
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "Las energías renovables son el futuro." It means 'Renewable energy is the future'; note that Spanish uses the plural "energías" here.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: La comunicación efectiva es clave en el trabajo.
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "La comunicación efectiva es clave en el trabajo." It means 'Effective communication is key at work'; "clave" (key) does not change form after "es".

units.title: Write It Yourself: Multi-Clause Sentences
units.description: Say it your own way — Multi-clause sentences, and more than one wording is right.

questions.prompt: Say that when you finish work, you'll go for a walk.
acceptableAnswers: Cuando termine el trabajo, iré a caminar.
Cuando acabe el trabajo, saldré a caminar.
Iré a caminar cuando termine el trabajo.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Cuando termine el trabajo, iré a caminar." When "cuando" refers to the future it takes the subjunctive ("termine"), while the main clause uses the future ("iré").

questions.prompt: Say that if you have time, you could have lunch together.
acceptableAnswers: Si tienes tiempo, podríamos almorzar juntos.
Si tienes tiempo, podríamos comer juntos.
Podríamos almorzar juntos si tienes tiempo.
Si tiene tiempo, podríamos almorzar juntos.
questions.explanation: "Si tienes tiempo, podríamos almorzar juntos." uses the present after "si" for a real possibility and the conditional "podríamos" for a polite suggestion.

questions.prompt: Say that although it's difficult, you're going to try.
acceptableAnswers: Aunque es difícil, voy a intentarlo.
Aunque sea difícil, lo voy a intentar.
Voy a intentarlo aunque sea difícil.
questions.explanation: "Aunque es difícil, voy a intentarlo." uses the indicative because the difficulty is a known fact; "aunque sea" would treat it as hypothetical.

questions.prompt: Say that since it's raining, you'll stay home.
acceptableAnswers: Como está lloviendo, me quedaré en casa.
Ya que está lloviendo, me quedo en casa.
Me quedaré en casa porque está lloviendo.
Como está lloviendo, nos quedaremos en casa.
Ya que está lloviendo, nos quedamos en casa.
Nos quedaremos en casa porque está lloviendo.
questions.explanation: "Como está lloviendo, me quedaré en casa." puts "como" (since) first to give the reason, then the future "me quedaré". If "you" includes others at home, "nos quedaremos" is also right.

questions.prompt: Say that when you arrive, you'll call.
questions.explanation: "Cuando llegue, te llamaré." needs the subjunctive "llegue" because "cuando" refers to a future moment.

questions.prompt: Say that if we leave now, you think we'll arrive on time.
acceptableAnswers: Creo que si salimos ahora, llegaremos a tiempo.
Pienso que si nos vamos ahora, llegaremos a tiempo.
Si salimos ahora, creo que llegaremos a tiempo.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Creo que si salimos ahora, llegaremos a tiempo." A real condition uses "si" + present indicative ("salimos") with the future in the result ("llegaremos").

questions.prompt: Say she said she would come, but she didn't come.
acceptableAnswers: Ella dijo que vendría, pero no vino.
Dijo que iba a venir, pero no llegó.
Ella dijo que vendría y no vino.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Ella dijo que vendría, pero no vino." After a past reporting verb, "would come" becomes the conditional "vendría", and the preterite "no vino" states what actually happened.

questions.prompt: Say that even if it's expensive, you're going to buy it.
acceptableAnswers: Aunque sea caro, lo voy a comprar.
Incluso si es caro, lo compraré.
Lo voy a comprar aunque sea caro.
questions.explanation: "Aunque sea caro, lo voy a comprar." uses the subjunctive "sea" because "even if" leaves the price open or hypothetical.

questions.prompt: Say that as soon as you have news, you'll let me know.
acceptableAnswers: En cuanto tenga noticias, te aviso.
Tan pronto tenga noticias, te avisaré.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "En cuanto tenga noticias, te aviso." Time expressions like "en cuanto" referring to the future take the subjunctive ("tenga").

questions.prompt: Say it's necessary that you finish before tonight.
acceptableAnswers: Es necesario que termines antes de esta noche.
Hace falta que termines antes de esta noche.
Es necesario que termine antes de esta noche.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Es necesario que termines antes de esta noche." Impersonal expressions of necessity like "es necesario que" and "hace falta que" take the subjunctive, so you write "termines" (or "termine" for usted).

questions.prompt: Say you would like him to help you with this project.
acceptableAnswers: Quisiera que me ayudara con este proyecto.
Me gustaría que me ayudara con este proyecto.
Quisiera que me ayude con este proyecto.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Quisiera que me ayudara con este proyecto." A polite wish with "quisiera" or "me gustaría" followed by "que" takes the subjunctive, usually the imperfect "ayudara".

questions.prompt: Say you hope everything goes well.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Espero que todo salga bien." "Esperar que" expresses a wish, so it takes the subjunctive "salga".

questions.prompt: Say that since it was cold, we came home early.
acceptableAnswers: Como hacía frío, volvimos temprano a casa.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Como hacía frío, volvimos temprano a casa." "Como" at the start gives the cause; the imperfect "hacía" describes the background and the preterite "volvimos" gives the completed action.

questions.prompt: Say that as long as you agree, we can continue.
acceptableAnswers: Mientras estés de acuerdo, podemos continuar.
Siempre que estés de acuerdo, seguimos.
Podemos seguir mientras estés de acuerdo.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Mientras estés de acuerdo, podemos continuar." When "mientras" or "siempre que" means 'as long as', it sets a condition and takes the subjunctive "estés".

questions.prompt: Tell a friend: before leaving, check that everything is closed.
acceptableAnswers: Antes de salir, verifica que todo esté cerrado.
Antes de irte, revisa que todo esté cerrado.
Antes de salir, asegúrate de que todo esté cerrado.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Antes de salir, verifica que todo esté cerrado." "Antes de" is followed by an infinitive, and "esté" is subjunctive because you are asking someone to make sure of something.

questions.prompt: Say that after eating, we went for a walk.
acceptableAnswers: Después de comer, salimos a caminar.
Después de comer, fuimos a caminar.
Salimos a caminar después de comer.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Después de comer, salimos a caminar." "Después de" is followed by an infinitive ("comer"), and the preterite "salimos" tells what we did next.

questions.prompt: Say that although he is tired, he keeps working.
acceptableAnswers: A pesar de estar cansado, sigue trabajando.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Aunque está cansado, sigue trabajando." Use the indicative "está" after "aunque" because his tiredness is a known fact, not a possibility.

questions.prompt: Say since you insist, you accept.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Ya que insistes, acepto." "Ya que" introduces a known cause ("since"), so it takes the indicative "insistes"; tú fits someone close to you.

questions.prompt: Say that whatever happens, you'll be there for them.
acceptableAnswers: Pase lo que pase, estaré ahí para ellos.

Pase lo que pase, los voy a apoyar.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Pase lo que pase, estaré ahí para ellos." "Whatever happens" is the fixed pattern "pase lo que pase", which repeats the subjunctive verb.

questions.prompt: Say if you had known, you wouldn't have come.
acceptableAnswers: Si lo hubiera sabido, no habría venido.
Si lo hubiese sabido, no hubiera venido.
De haberlo sabido, no habría venido.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Si lo hubiera sabido, no habría venido." An impossible past condition uses "si" + pluperfect subjunctive ("hubiera sabido") with the conditional perfect ("habría venido").

questions.prompt: Say in Spanish: "Every time I see him, he talks about work."
acceptableAnswers: Cada vez que lo veo, habla del trabajo.
Cada vez que lo veo, me habla de su trabajo.
Siempre que lo veo, habla de trabajo.
questions.explanation: "Cada vez que lo veo, habla del trabajo." uses "cada vez que" with the present indicative because it describes a repeated, habitual fact, not a future event; "siempre que" works the same way.

questions.prompt: Say in Spanish: "The more I think about it, the more convinced I am."
acceptableAnswers: Cuanto más lo pienso, más convencido estoy.
Cuanto más lo pienso, más convencida estoy.
Mientras más lo pienso, más me convenzo.
Entre más lo pienso, más seguro estoy.
Entre más lo pienso, más segura estoy.
questions.explanation: "Cuanto más lo pienso, más convencido estoy." uses the paired structure "cuanto más..., más..." for 'the more..., the more...'; a woman would say "convencida".

questions.prompt: Say whether you like it or not, it has to be done.
acceptableAnswers: Te guste o no, hay que hacerlo.
Quieras o no, se tiene que hacer.
Aunque no te guste, hay que hacerlo.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Te guste o no, hay que hacerlo." 'Whether you like it or not' uses the subjunctive "te guste" followed by "o no", and "hay que" means 'it has to be'.

questions.prompt: Say although you're busy, you're going to help.
acceptableAnswers: Aunque estoy ocupado, voy a ayudar.
Aunque estoy ocupada, voy a ayudar.
Voy a ayudar aunque esté ocupado.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Aunque estoy ocupado, voy a ayudar." "Aunque" with the indicative "estoy" presents being busy as a real fact (use "ocupada" if you are female).

questions.prompt: Say once this is finished, we can leave.
acceptableAnswers: Una vez que esto termine, podemos irnos.
En cuanto esto termine, nos podemos ir.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Una vez que esto termine, podemos irnos." "Una vez que", "en cuanto" and "cuando" refer to a future moment here, so they take the subjunctive "termine".

questions.explanation: The audio says "El concejo municipal se reunió por la tarde." "Concejo" (town council) sounds like "consejo" under seseo, so the word municipal, not escolar, tells you which sentence you heard.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué escuchaste?
questions.audioText: La sima resultó ser más profunda de lo esperado.
choices: La sima resultó ser más profunda de lo esperado.
Sintió que el fuego lo iba a abrasar.
Desde arriba se veía toda la sima.
Nadie se atrevía a acercarse a la sima.
questions.answer: La sima resultó ser más profunda de lo esperado.
questions.explanation: The audio says "La sima resultó ser más profunda de lo esperado." Only this option contains más profunda, which also fits "sima" (a deep pit) rather than its sound-alike "cima" (a summit).

units.title: Past Subjunctive
units.description: Imperfect subjunctive mood — Imperfect subjunctive, used for hypotheticals and past wishes/doubts.

questions.prompt: Si yo ___ (tener) más tiempo, viajaría más.
questions.explanation: After "Si" in a hypothetical, with a conditional ("viajaría") in the result clause, the verb is imperfect subjunctive: "tuviera".

questions.prompt: Ella actuó como si ___ (saber) todo.
questions.explanation: "como si" (as if) introduces an unreal comparison and requires the imperfect subjunctive, so "supiera" is used; "supieras" is the tú form and doesn't fit "ella".

questions.prompt: Ojalá ___ (llover) mañana.
questions.explanation: "Ojalá" expresses a wish and takes the subjunctive; the imperfect "lloviera" presents the wish as less likely or hypothetical, while a present-subjunctive "llueva" would be the likely-wish form.
questions.meaning: it rained / would rain (past subjunctive of llover)

questions.prompt: Si tú ___ (estudiar) más, aprobarías el examen.
questions.explanation: The si-clause with "aprobarías" in the result needs the imperfect subjunctive, and the subject "tú" calls for the tú form "estudiaras".

questions.prompt: Nos pidió que ___ (llegar) temprano.
questions.explanation: "Nos pidió que" is a past request, so the verb after "que" goes in the imperfect subjunctive, and "nos" points to the nosotros form "llegáramos".

questions.prompt: Dudaba que él ___ (decir) la verdad.
questions.explanation: "Dudaba que" expresses past doubt and takes the imperfect subjunctive; with "él" the form is "dijera".

questions.prompt: Si nosotros ___ (poder), te ayudaríamos.
questions.explanation: In a hypothetical "Si" clause with the conditional "ayudaríamos", the verb is imperfect subjunctive, and the subject "nosotros" gives "pudiéramos" (with the accent).

questions.prompt: Ella esperaba que yo ___ (venir) a la fiesta.
questions.explanation: "Esperaba que" (past wish) takes the imperfect subjunctive, and the subject "yo" calls for the singular form "viniera".

questions.prompt: Si ella ___ (saber) conducir, iría en coche.
questions.explanation: A hypothetical "Si" clause with the conditional "iría" needs the imperfect subjunctive, and "ella" takes the third-person form "supiera".
questions.example: Si ella supiera manejar, iría en auto.

questions.prompt: Me gustaría que tú ___ (ser) más paciente.
questions.explanation: "Me gustaría que" (a conditional wish) is followed by the imperfect subjunctive, and "tú" gives "fueras".

questions.prompt: Si él ___ (querer), podría cambiar de trabajo.
questions.explanation: After "Si" in a hypothetical, with "podría" in the result clause, the verb is imperfect subjunctive: "quisiera"; "quiera" and "querría" are not used after "si" here.

questions.prompt: Actuaba como si nada ___ (importar).
questions.explanation: After "como si" Spanish needs the imperfect subjunctive, and the subject "nada" is third person singular, so the form is "importara".

questions.prompt: Ojalá ___ (ganar) nosotros el premio.
questions.explanation: "Ojalá" expressing a wish contrary to reality takes the imperfect subjunctive, and the subject "nosotros" requires the nosotros form "ganáramos".

questions.prompt: Si ustedes ___ (venir) antes, verían el atardecer.
questions.explanation: A hypothetical "si" clause with a conditional result ("verían") needs the imperfect subjunctive, and "ustedes" takes the ellos form "vinieran".
questions.meaning: you all came (past subjunctive of venir)

questions.prompt: Ella dudaba que nosotros ___ (terminar) a tiempo.
questions.explanation: "Dudaba" is past and triggers the imperfect subjunctive, and the subject "nosotros" requires the nosotros form "termináramos".

questions.prompt: Si nosotros ___ (ser) más organizados, terminaríamos antes.
questions.explanation: An unreal "si" clause with a conditional result ("terminaríamos") takes the imperfect subjunctive, and with "nosotros" that is "fuéramos".

questions.prompt: Nos habría gustado que tú ___ (quedarse).
questions.explanation: "Nos habría gustado que" calls for the imperfect subjunctive, and the subject "tú" needs the tú form with its pronoun: "te quedaras".

questions.prompt: Si ella ___ (hacer) más ejercicio, se sentiría mejor.
questions.explanation: A hypothetical "si" clause with "se sentiría" needs the imperfect subjunctive, and "ella" takes the third person singular form "hiciera".

questions.prompt: Esperábamos que ellos ___ (llegar) sin problemas.
questions.explanation: "Esperábamos que" is past and triggers the imperfect subjunctive, and "ellos" takes the third person plural form "llegaran".

questions.prompt: Si nosotros ___ (vivir) más cerca, nos veríamos más.
questions.explanation: An unreal "si" clause with the conditional "veríamos" needs the imperfect subjunctive, and "nosotros" gives "viviéramos".

questions.prompt: Actuó como si ___ (tener) miedo.
questions.explanation: "Como si" always takes the imperfect (or pluperfect) subjunctive, never the present or indicative, so "tuviera" is right.

questions.prompt: Si tú ___ (poder) elegir, ¿qué harías?
questions.explanation: The hypothetical "si" clause with the conditional "harías" needs the imperfect subjunctive, and "tú" takes the tú form "pudieras".

questions.prompt: Me sorprendió que ella ___ (decir) eso.
questions.explanation: "Me sorprendió que" is a past emotional reaction that takes the subjunctive in the imperfect, and "ella" requires the third person singular "dijera".

questions.prompt: Si ellos ___ (estar) aquí, todo sería más fácil.
questions.explanation: After "Si" in a hypothetical contrary to fact, Spanish uses the imperfect subjunctive, and the plural subject "ellos" needs the plural ending: "estuvieran".

questions.prompt: Ojalá ___ (poder) yo cambiar el pasado.
questions.explanation: "Ojalá" expressing an unreal wish takes the imperfect subjunctive, and the subject "yo" needs the singular form "pudiera".

units.title: Nuanced Vocabulary
units.description: Precise synonyms and register — Advanced vocabulary offering more precise alternatives to common words.

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to think (basic: pensar)"?
questions.explanation: "reflexionar" means to think carefully and deliberately about something, so it is the more precise, formal alternative to "pensar".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to say (basic: decir)"? ___
questions.explanation: "manifestar" means to state or express something openly, as in "Manifestó su desacuerdo", so it is the formal alternative to "decir".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to show (basic: mostrar)"?
questions.explanation: "evidenciar" means to show or make evident, often with proof or data, so it is the formal alternative to "mostrar".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to get (basic: conseguir)"? ___
questions.explanation: "obtener" means to get or obtain something, usually as a result of effort, so it is the formal alternative to "conseguir".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to help (basic: ayudar)"?
questions.explanation: "colaborar" means to help by working together with someone on a task, so it is the formal alternative to "ayudar".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to want (basic: querer)"? ___
questions.explanation: "desear" expresses wanting or wishing for something in a more polite, formal way, so it is the alternative to "querer".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "big (basic: grande)"?
questions.explanation: "considerable" describes a large size or amount in a formal register, as in "una suma considerable", so it replaces "grande".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "important (basic: importante)"? ___
questions.explanation: "trascendental" means extremely important, with far-reaching consequences, so it is a stronger, formal alternative to "importante".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to look at (basic: mirar)"?
questions.explanation: "observar" means to look at something carefully and attentively, so it is the more precise alternative to "mirar".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to address / talk about a topic (basic: hablar de)"? ___
questions.explanation: "abordar" is the formal verb for taking up or dealing with a topic, as in "Abordaremos el tema mañana"; "esclarecer" means to clarify and "observar" means to observe.

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to make better (basic: mejorar)"? ___
questions.explanation: "perfeccionar" means to improve something by refining it towards perfection, a more precise word than the everyday "mejorar".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to end (basic: terminar)"?
questions.explanation: "concluir" is the formal verb for bringing something to an end, as in "La reunión concluyó a las seis"; the other verbs mean to perfect, to try and to wish.

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to begin (basic: empezar)"? ___
questions.explanation: "iniciar" is the formal verb for starting something, as in "Iniciamos el proyecto en enero", a more formal choice than "empezar".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "problem (basic: problema)"?
questions.explanation: "inconveniente" is the polite, formal word for a problem or setback, as in "Tuvimos un inconveniente con el pedido".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "change (basic: cambio)"? ___
