questions.explanation: "transformación" names a deep or complete change, a more precise and formal noun than "cambio".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to understand (basic: entender)"?
questions.explanation: "comprender" means to understand fully and sounds more formal than "entender"; "esclarecer" means to clarify something for others.

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to explain (basic: explicar)"? ___
questions.explanation: to explain (basic: explicar) → esclarecer. Advanced vocabulary offering more precise alternatives to common words.

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "result / consequence (basic: resultado)"?
questions.explanation: "consecuencia" names the result that follows from an action or event, as in "Es una consecuencia de la crisis".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to try (basic: intentar)"? ___
questions.explanation: "procurar" means to make an effort to do something, as in "Procura llegar temprano", a more formal word than "intentar".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "opinion (basic: opinión)"?
questions.explanation: "criterio" is a person's considered judgement or opinion, as in "a mi criterio", a more formal word than "opinión".

units.title: Advanced Idiomatic Expressions
units.description: Sophisticated sayings — More advanced idiomatic expressions used in fluent, natural Spanish.

questions.prompt: What does "andarse por las ramas" mean? ___
bank: to lay one's cards on the table
questions.explanation: "andarse por las ramas" literally means wandering through the branches instead of going to the trunk, so it means "to beat around the bush": avoiding the main point.

questions.prompt: What does "poner el dedo en la llaga" mean?
questions.explanation: "Poner el dedo en la llaga" literally means 'to put your finger in the wound': you press exactly on the painful point, so it means "to hit a sore spot".

questions.prompt: What does "ser la gota que colma el vaso" mean? ___
bank: to be between a rock and a hard place
questions.explanation: "Ser la gota que colma el vaso" literally means 'to be the drop that makes the glass overflow': one last small thing makes it all too much, so it means "to be the last straw".

questions.prompt: What does "llevar la voz cantante" mean?
choices: to be the one in charge
questions.explanation: "Llevar la voz cantante" literally means 'to carry the singing voice', like the lead singer the others follow, so it means "to be the one in charge".

questions.prompt: What does "irse de la lengua" mean? ___
questions.explanation: "Irse de la lengua" pictures your tongue running away with you, so you say more than you should: "to let something slip".

questions.prompt: What does "estar entre la espada y la pared" mean?
choices: to be between a rock and a hard place
questions.explanation: "Estar entre la espada y la pared" pictures being trapped between a sword and a wall with no way out, so it means "to be between a rock and a hard place".

questions.prompt: What does "dorar la píldora" mean? ___
bank: to be between a rock and a hard place
questions.explanation: "Dorar la píldora" literally means 'to gild the pill', making something unpleasant easier to swallow, so it means "to sugarcoat something".

questions.prompt: What does "irse por las nubes" mean?
questions.explanation: "Irse por las nubes" literally means 'to go up into the clouds'; when said of prices, it means "for prices to skyrocket".

questions.prompt: What does "ver los toros desde la barrera" mean? ___
bank: to lay one's cards on the table
to be the one in charge
questions.explanation: "Ver los toros desde la barrera" means watching the bulls from behind the safe barrier of the ring, so it means "to watch from the sidelines" without taking any risk.

questions.prompt: What does "poner las cartas sobre la mesa" mean?
choices: to lay one's cards on the table
questions.explanation: "Poner las cartas sobre la mesa" means showing all your cards and hiding nothing, exactly like the English "to lay one's cards on the table".

questions.prompt: What does "salirse con la suya" mean?
choices: to be between a rock and a hard place
questions.explanation: In "salirse con la suya", "la suya" stands for 'his or her own will', so coming out with it means "to get one's own way".

questions.prompt: What does "tirar la casa por la ventana" mean? ___
bank: to lay one's cards on the table
questions.explanation: "Tirar la casa por la ventana" literally means 'to throw the house out the window', that is, to spend lavishly, so it means "to spare no expense".

questions.prompt: What does "hacer oídos sordos" mean?
choices: to lay one's cards on the table
questions.explanation: "Hacer oídos sordos" literally means 'to make deaf ears', that is, to ignore what you hear on purpose, so it means "to turn a deaf ear".

questions.prompt: What does "no dar el brazo a torcer" mean? ___
questions.explanation: Literally 'not to give your arm to be twisted', so "to refuse to back down" means to stay stubborn and not give in.

questions.prompt: What does "írsele a alguien la mano" mean?
questions.explanation: Literally 'the hand gets away from someone', as with too much salt, so it means "to overdo something" without meaning to.

questions.prompt: What does "quedarse de piedra" mean? ___
bank: to be the one in charge
questions.explanation: Literally 'to turn to stone', so "to be dumbfounded" means to be frozen with shock or surprise.

questions.prompt: What does "tener la sartén por el mango" mean?
questions.explanation: Holding the frying pan by the handle means you are the one who controls the situation, so the idiom means "to be in control".

questions.prompt: What does "pasar factura" mean? ___
questions.explanation: Literally 'to send the bill', so "to take its toll" describes something whose bad effects show up later, like stress or bad habits.

questions.prompt: What does "estar en el ajo" mean?
choices: to be between a rock and a hard place
questions.explanation: Literally 'to be in the garlic', it means "to be in on something", that is, to know about a secret or plan; it is mostly used in Spain.

questions.prompt: What does "dar la cara" mean? ___
bank: to lay one's cards on the table
questions.explanation: "Dar la cara" (literally 'to give the face') means showing your face and taking responsibility instead of hiding, so it means "to face the consequences".

units.title: Formal & Literary Register
units.description: Written and academic Spanish — Formal/literary sentence structures typical of academic or professional writing.

questions.prompt: Cabe ___ (to point out) que los resultados fueron positivos.
questions.explanation: "Cabe" in the formal phrase "cabe señalar que" (it should be noted that) is followed by an infinitive, so "señalar" is right and the conjugated or -ndo forms are not.

questions.prompt: Es menester ___ (to take into account) todos los factores.
questions.explanation: "Es menester" (it is necessary) is followed by an infinitive when the action is general, so the answer is "considerar", not a conjugated verb, gerund or participle.
questions.meaning: to consider, to take into account

questions.prompt: Huelga ___ (to say) que el proyecto fue un éxito.
questions.explanation: "Huelga decir que" is a fixed formal phrase meaning 'needless to say', and "huelga" is followed by the infinitive "decir".
questions.meaning: to say (huelga decir: needless to say)

questions.prompt: Conviene ___ (to highlight) la importancia del estudio.
questions.explanation: "Conviene" (it is advisable) is followed by an infinitive when the action is general, so "destacar" fits and the conjugated, participle and -ndo forms do not.

questions.prompt: No cabe ___ de que el plan funcionará.
questions.explanation: "No cabe duda de que" is the fixed phrase for 'there is no doubt that', and after "cabe" it needs the noun "duda", not a verb or adjective.
questions.meaning: doubt (no cabe duda: there is no doubt)

questions.prompt: Es preciso ___ la situación con cuidado.
questions.explanation: "Es preciso" (it is necessary) is followed by an infinitive for a general action, so the answer is "analizar".

questions.prompt: Resulta ___ que se necesita más inversión.
questions.explanation: "Resulta evidente que" states a fact, so it is followed by the indicative "se necesita"; "extraño", "dudoso" and "necesario" would require the subjunctive "se necesite". That is why only "evidente" fits.

questions.prompt: Se hace ___ revisar la propuesta. (necessary)
questions.explanation: "Se hace necesario" means 'it becomes necessary'; the clue (necessary) points to "necesario", and the impersonal construction takes the masculine form, not "necesaria".

questions.prompt: Cabe ___ que hubo cambios recientes.
questions.explanation: In the formal phrase "cabe + infinitive" (it is worth / fitting to), "cabe" is followed by the infinitive "mencionar", not a conjugated form, participle or gerund.

questions.prompt: Es de ___ (to suppose) que llegará una respuesta pronto.
questions.explanation: "Es de suponer que" is a fixed phrase meaning 'it is to be assumed that', and "de" is followed by the infinitive "suponer".

questions.prompt: Vale la ___ reconsiderar la estrategia.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is "valer la pena" (to be worth it), always with the singular "pena" to match the singular article "la"; "gana" and "suerte" do not form this phrase.
questions.meaning: pity, sorrow; trouble (vale la pena: it's worth it)

questions.prompt: No es de ___ que el proyecto tardara tanto.
questions.explanation: After the preposition "de", the fixed phrase "no es de extrañar" (it is no surprise) needs the infinitive "extrañar". Participles and gerunds do not fit this structure.
questions.meaning: to find strange, to surprise (no es de extrañar: it's no surprise)

questions.prompt: Es dable ___ (to assert) que el mercado ha cambiado.
questions.explanation: "Es dable" (it is possible) is followed by an infinitive, so the verb must be "afirmar". Conjugated forms, participles and gerunds cannot follow it.
questions.example: Es posible afirmar que el mercado ha cambiado.

questions.prompt: Conviene ___ (to stress) los puntos más relevantes.
questions.explanation: The impersonal verb "conviene" (it is advisable) is followed by an infinitive, so "subrayar" is the right form. A conjugated verb, participle or gerund does not fit here.

questions.prompt: Cabe ___ (to stress) la relevancia de este hallazgo.
questions.explanation: The formal impersonal "cabe" (it is appropriate to) is followed by an infinitive, so the correct form is "recalcar". Conjugated forms, participles and gerunds do not work after it.

questions.prompt: Es oportuno ___ (to mention) las limitaciones del estudio.
questions.explanation: The clue asks for "to mention", which is "mencionar"; after the impersonal "Es oportuno" Spanish uses the bare infinitive.

questions.prompt: Huelga ___ (to add) que se requiere más investigación.
questions.explanation: "Huelga" + infinitive means "it goes without saying", and the clue asks for "to add", which is "añadir".
questions.example: Cabe añadir que se requiere más investigación.

questions.prompt: Resulta ___ (relevant) revisar los datos disponibles.
questions.explanation: "Resulta" + adjective + infinitive means "it is ... to do", and the formal adjective for "relevant" is "pertinente".

questions.prompt: Es menester ___ (to clarify) los términos del acuerdo.
questions.explanation: "Es menester" (formal for "it is necessary") takes an infinitive, and the clue asks for "to clarify", which is "aclarar".
questions.example: Es necesario aclarar los términos del acuerdo.

questions.prompt: Cabe ___ (to conclude) que los objetivos se cumplieron.
questions.explanation: "Cabe" + infinitive means "it is fitting to", and the clue asks for "to conclude", which is "concluir".

units.title: Complex Sentence Connectors
units.description: Advanced discourse markers — Discourse markers for sophisticated argumentation and academic writing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "notwithstanding the above (formal)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "no obstante lo anterior" literally means "notwithstanding the above"; it is a formal concessive marker that introduces a point holding true despite what was just said.

questions.prompt: How do you say "insofar as" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "en la medida en que" means "insofar as" or "to the extent that" and limits a statement to a certain degree or condition.

questions.prompt: How do you say "inasmuch as (formal)" in Spanish? ___
bank: a la luz de lo anterior
questions.explanation: "en tanto que" is a formal connector meaning "inasmuch as"; it introduces the respect or reason in which a statement holds.

questions.prompt: How do you say "by the same token" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "de igual manera" means "in the same way" and adds a parallel point, just as "by the same token" does.

questions.prompt: How do you say "conversely" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "en cambio" introduces a contrasting idea at the start of a new clause, just like 'conversely' or 'on the other hand'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "that being said" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "dicho esto" means "that being said" and introduces a caveat or contrast after a statement.

questions.prompt: How do you say "in light of the above" in Spanish? ___
bank: a la luz de lo anterior
questions.answer: a la luz de lo anterior
questions.explanation: "a la luz de lo anterior" literally means "in the light of the above" and draws a conclusion from what has just been presented.

questions.prompt: How do you say "all things considered (formal)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "considerando todo lo anterior" (considering all of the above) is a formal way to say "all things considered" when summing up an argument.

questions.prompt: How do you say "be that as it may" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "sea como sea" uses the subjunctive of ser to mean 'however it may be', so it sets a point aside and moves on, like 'be that as it may'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "with that in mind" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "teniendo esto en cuenta" literally means "taking this into account" and is the standard way to say "with that in mind"; "no obstante" means "nevertheless".

questions.prompt: How do you say "in the final analysis" in Spanish?
choices: a la luz de lo anterior
questions.explanation: "en última instancia" literally means 'in the last instance' and introduces the final, deciding point, like 'in the final analysis'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "notwithstanding the foregoing" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "sin perjuicio de lo anterior" is the formal legal and academic way to say "notwithstanding the foregoing": it adds a point that holds regardless of what was just said.

questions.prompt: How do you say "along the same lines" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "en esta misma línea" literally means "in this same line" and is the standard academic phrase for "along the same lines", used to add a point in a similar vein.

questions.prompt: How do you say "for all intents and purposes" in Spanish? ___
bank: a la luz de lo anterior
questions.explanation: "a todos los efectos" literally means 'for all effects' and says something counts as true in practice, like 'for all intents and purposes'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "as a corollary" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "como corolario" introduces a conclusion that follows naturally from what was just said, the direct equivalent of 'as a corollary'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "by way of contrast" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "a modo de contraste" introduces an idea that is meant to contrast with what came before, just like "by way of contrast"; "de igual manera" means the opposite ("likewise").

questions.prompt: How do you say "in the strictest sense" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "en el sentido más estricto" is a word-for-word match for "in the strictest sense" and limits a term to its narrowest meaning; "en cambio" means "on the other hand".

questions.prompt: How do you say "paradoxically" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "paradójicamente" is the adverb from "paradoja" (paradox) and means "paradoxically"; note the accent on the ó.

questions.prompt: How do you say "by extension" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "por extensión" means "by extension" and applies an idea to a wider case; "a todos los efectos" means "for all intents and purposes".

questions.prompt: How do you say "in essence" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "en esencia" means "in essence" and sums up the core of an argument; "en tanto que" means "insofar as".

units.title: Compound Tenses
units.description: Pluperfect & future perfect — Pluperfect (had done) and future perfect (will have done) tenses.

questions.prompt: Cuando llegué, ella ya ___ (salir).
questions.explanation: "había salido" is correct here. Pluperfect (had done) and future perfect (will have done) tenses.

questions.prompt: Para el año próximo, yo ___ (terminar) mis estudios.
questions.explanation: "habré terminado" is correct here. Pluperfect (had done) and future perfect (will have done) tenses.

questions.prompt: Antes de la reunión, nosotros ya ___ (revisar) el informe.
questions.explanation: "habíamos revisado" is right because "nosotros" needs the "habíamos" form, and "antes de la reunión ... ya" places the reviewing before a past point, which calls for the pluperfect.

questions.prompt: Para mañana, ellos ___ (completar) el proyecto.
questions.explanation: "habrán completado" is right because "para mañana" sets a future deadline (future perfect), and "ellos" requires the "habrán" ending.

questions.prompt: Cuando llamaste, yo ya ___ (comer).
questions.explanation: "había comido" is right because eating happened before the past moment "cuando llamaste", which needs the pluperfect, and "yo" takes "había".

questions.prompt: Para el viernes, tú ___ (recibir) la respuesta.
questions.explanation: "habrás recibido" is right because "para el viernes" points to a future deadline (future perfect), and "tú" requires the "habrás" ending.

questions.prompt: Antes de mudarnos, nosotros ___ (vivir) allí diez años.
questions.explanation: "habíamos vivido" is right because "antes de mudarnos" refers to a time before another past event, which calls for the pluperfect, and "nosotros" takes "habíamos".

questions.prompt: Cuando desperté, el sol ya ___ (salir).
questions.explanation: "había salido" is right because the sun had already risen before the past moment "cuando desperté" (pluperfect), and "el sol" is singular.

questions.prompt: Para las ocho, ella ___ (llegar) a casa.
questions.explanation: "habrá llegado" is right because "para las ocho" sets a future deadline (future perfect), and "ella" takes the third-person singular "habrá".

questions.prompt: Antes del examen, yo ya ___ (estudiar) todo.
questions.explanation: "había estudiado" is right because studying came before the past event "el examen" (pluperfect), and "yo" takes "había".

questions.prompt: Para entonces, ellos ya ___ (decidir).
questions.explanation: "habrán decidido" is right because "para entonces" points to a completed action by a future time (future perfect), and "ellos" requires "habrán".

questions.prompt: Cuando abrí la puerta, el perro ya ___ (escapar).
questions.explanation: "había escapado" is right because the dog's escape happened before the past moment "cuando abrí la puerta" (pluperfect), and "el perro" is singular.

questions.prompt: Para el próximo mes, nosotros ___ (ahorrar) lo suficiente.
questions.explanation: "habremos ahorrado" is right because "para el próximo mes" sets a future deadline (future perfect), and "nosotros" takes the "habremos" ending.
questions.example: Para el próximo mes, nosotros habremos ahorrado lo suficiente.

questions.prompt: Antes de esa fecha, tú nunca ___ (viajar) al extranjero.
questions.explanation: "habías viajado" is right because "antes de esa fecha" refers to a time before a past point (pluperfect), and "tú" requires the "habías" ending.

questions.prompt: Cuando volví, ellos ya ___ (limpiar) la casa.
questions.explanation: "habían limpiado" is right because the subject "ellos" needs the third-person plural, and the pluperfect (había/habían + participle) shows the cleaning was done before "cuando volví".

questions.prompt: Para el próximo diciembre, yo ___ (publicar) el libro.
questions.explanation: "habré publicado" is right because "yo" takes "habré", and the future perfect marks an action that will be completed before a future deadline ("para el próximo diciembre").

questions.prompt: Antes de conocerte, yo ya ___ (mudarse) tres veces.
questions.explanation: "me había mudado" is right because "mudarse" is reflexive, so the pronoun "me" must match "yo", and the pluperfect fits an event before "antes de conocerte".

questions.prompt: Para las nueve de esta noche, la tienda ya ___ (cerrar).
questions.explanation: "habrá cerrado" is right because "la tienda" is singular third person and "para las nueve de esta noche" sets a future deadline, which calls for the future perfect.

questions.prompt: Cuando llegamos, la película ya ___ (empezar).
questions.explanation: "había empezado" is right because "la película" is singular and the film started before "cuando llegamos", so the pluperfect is needed, not the future perfect.

questions.prompt: Para el final del curso, los estudiantes ___ (aprender) mucho.
questions.explanation: "habrán aprendido" is right because "los estudiantes" is plural third person and "para el final del curso" points to something completed by a future date, so it takes the future perfect.

questions.prompt: Antes de esta noche, nunca había ___ (probar) ese plato.
questions.explanation: "probado" is right because after "había" the pluperfect needs the invariable past participle; "probada" and "probados" wrongly add agreement, and "probando" is a gerund.

questions.prompt: Para el próximo lunes, nosotros ___ (firmar) el contrato.
questions.explanation: "habremos firmado" is right because "nosotros" takes "habremos", and "para el próximo lunes" sets a future deadline that calls for the future perfect.

questions.prompt: Cuando te vi, yo ya ___ (terminar) el trabajo.
questions.explanation: "había terminado" is right because the subject is "yo" and the work was finished before the past moment "cuando te vi", which needs the pluperfect.

questions.prompt: Para entonces, ella ___ (cumplir) treinta años.
questions.explanation: "habrá cumplido" is right because the subject "ella" takes "habrá", and "para entonces" refers to a future point by which she will have turned thirty.

questions.prompt: Antes de irme anoche, ya ___ (apagar) las luces.
questions.explanation: "había apagado" is right because turning off the lights happened before another past moment ("antes de irme anoche"), which calls for the pluperfect.

units.title: Legal & Academic Vocabulary
units.description: Formal institutional terms — Legal and academic register vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "trial" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "juicio" is the word for a court trial, as in "El juicio comenzará mañana"; in everyday speech the same word also means "judgment" or "good sense".

questions.prompt: How do you say "guilty" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "culpable" means "guilty", as in "El juez declaró culpable al acusado"; "acusado" only means accused and "absuelto" means acquitted.

questions.prompt: How do you say "innocent" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "inocente" means "innocent", as in "El tribunal lo declaró inocente"; "absuelto" means acquitted, which is the court's decision rather than the state of being innocent.

questions.prompt: How do you say "judge" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "juez" is the person who presides over a court; "culpable" means "guilty" and "reglamento" means "regulation".

questions.prompt: How do you say "court" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "tribunal" is the court of law itself, as in "El caso llegó al tribunal"; "juicio" is the trial held there and "sentencia" is the ruling.

questions.prompt: How do you say "evidence" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: In a trial, the facts or documents shown to prove a claim are called "prueba", so it translates "evidence" ("evidencia" is also heard, but "prueba" is the standard legal term).

questions.prompt: How do you say "lawsuit" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A "demanda" is the legal action one person files in court against another, which is what "lawsuit" means.

questions.prompt: How do you say "regulation" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A "reglamento" is an official set of rules issued by an authority, which matches "regulation"; a "cláusula" is only one provision inside a document.

questions.prompt: How do you say "clause" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: A "cláusula" is a single provision inside a contract or law, which is what "clause" means.

questions.prompt: How do you say "prosecutor" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: The "fiscal" is the public official who brings criminal charges in court, so it translates "prosecutor"; beware, it is a false friend, because English 'fiscal' means related to public finances.

questions.prompt: How do you say "research" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "investigación" is the systematic study of a subject, which is the academic sense of "research".

questions.prompt: How do you say "thesis" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "tesis" is the central claim of a work or the long paper defended for a degree, matching "thesis"; it has the same form in the singular and plural.

questions.prompt: How do you say "argument" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "argumento" is a reasoned case made for a position, the academic and legal sense of "argument"; a quarrel is usually "discusión".

questions.prompt: How do you say "hypothesis" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "hipótesis" is a proposed explanation that research sets out to test, which is what "hypothesis" means.

questions.prompt: How do you say "methodology" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "metodología" is the set of methods a study uses, which is what "methodology" means.

questions.prompt: How do you say "citation" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: In academic writing, a "cita" is a quoted passage or a reference to a source, so it translates "citation"; in everyday Spanish it also means "appointment" or "date".

questions.prompt: How do you say "conclusion" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "conclusión" is the final point or closing section of an argument or paper, which is what "conclusion" means; note the accent on the ó.

questions.prompt: How do you say "peer review" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "revisión por pares" is the standard academic term for having experts in the same field evaluate a work before publication, which is exactly what "peer review" means.

questions.prompt: How do you say "academic" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "académico" is the Spanish adjective for "academic", relating to universities, study and scholarship; the other options mean regulation, trial and methodology.

questions.prompt: How do you say "scholarship" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "beca" is money given to a student for their studies, a scholarship; "cita" means a quotation or an appointment, not a scholarship.

units.title: Advanced Reported Speech
units.description: Direct to indirect speech — Tense-shifting when converting direct speech to indirect (reported) speech.

questions.prompt: Ella dijo: "Voy a venir." → Ella dijo que ___ a venir.
questions.explanation: "iba" is right because after the past "dijo que", the present "voy" shifts back to the imperfect "iba" in reported speech.

questions.prompt: Él dijo: "Tengo hambre." → Él dijo que ___ hambre.
questions.explanation: After the past-tense "dijo que", the present "tengo" shifts back to the imperfect, so the reported form is "tenía".

questions.prompt: Ellos dijeron: "Hemos terminado." → Ellos dijeron que ___ terminado.
questions.explanation: The present perfect "hemos terminado" becomes the pluperfect in reported speech after "dijeron que", so you need "habían" + terminado.

questions.prompt: Ella preguntó: "¿Vendrás mañana?" → Ella preguntó si ___ al día siguiente.
questions.explanation: The future "vendrás" shifts to the conditional when reported after the past "preguntó", and "si" introduces an indirect question, so "vendría".

questions.prompt: Él afirmó: "Es la verdad." → Él afirmó que ___ la verdad.
questions.explanation: The present "es" shifts to the imperfect after the past "afirmó que", giving "era"; it is a plain statement, so no subjunctive.

questions.prompt: Ellos comentaron: "Nos gusta viajar." → Ellos comentaron que les ___ viajar.
questions.explanation: "Nos gusta" shifts to the imperfect after "comentaron que", and the thing liked is the singular infinitive "viajar", so the verb is singular: "gustaba".
questions.meaning: was pleasing, liked (imperfect of gustar; les gustaba = they liked)

questions.prompt: Ella explicó: "No puedo ir." → Ella explicó que no ___ ir.
questions.explanation: The present "puedo" shifts to the imperfect after the past "explicó que", so the reported form is "podía".

questions.prompt: Él admitió: "Cometí un error." → Él admitió que ___ un error.
questions.explanation: The preterite "cometí" moves one step back to the pluperfect when reported after "admitió que", giving "había cometido".

questions.prompt: Ellos insistieron: "Queremos ayudar." → Ellos insistieron en que ___ ayudar.
questions.explanation: "Queremos" shifts to the imperfect after the past "insistieron en que", so the reported verb is "querían".

questions.prompt: Ella señaló: "El plan funcionará." → Ella señaló que el plan ___.
questions.explanation: The future "funcionará" becomes the conditional when reported after the past "señaló que", giving "funcionaría".

questions.prompt: Él prometió: "Volveré pronto." → Él prometió que ___ pronto.
questions.explanation: The future "volveré" shifts to the conditional after the past "prometió que", so the reported form is "volvería".

questions.prompt: Ellos negaron: "No sabíamos nada." → Ellos negaron que ___ nada.
questions.explanation: "Negar que" takes the subjunctive, and the past "sabíamos" is reported with the past subjunctive after the past "negaron", giving "supieran".

questions.prompt: Ella sugirió: "Deberíamos esperar." → Ella sugirió que ___ esperar.
questions.explanation: The conditional "deberíamos" stays conditional in reported speech, and the subject changes from "we" to "they", so it becomes "deberían".

questions.prompt: Él confesó: "Estoy nervioso." → Él confesó que ___ nervioso.
questions.explanation: Reporting a past verb ('confesó') shifts the present "Estoy" to the imperfect, and 'nervioso' is a state, so it takes estar: "estaba".

questions.prompt: Ellos anunciaron: "Ganamos el premio." → Ellos anunciaron que ___ el premio.
questions.explanation: The original "Ganamos" is a preterite, which becomes the pluperfect in reported speech after 'anunciaron': "habían ganado".

questions.prompt: Ella declaró: "Esto es importante." → Ella declaró que esto ___ importante.
questions.explanation: After the past 'declaró', the present "es" backshifts to the imperfect, and 'importante' describes a quality, so it stays ser: "era".

questions.prompt: Él respondió: "No lo entiendo." → Él respondió que no lo ___.
questions.explanation: The present "entiendo" becomes the imperfect after the past verb 'respondió': "entendía".

questions.prompt: Ellos advirtieron: "Habrá problemas." → Ellos advirtieron que ___ problemas.
questions.explanation: The future "Habrá" becomes the conditional in reported speech, and impersonal 'haber' stays singular: "habría" (not 'habrían').

questions.prompt: Ella recordó: "Debemos llegar temprano." → Ella recordó que ___ llegar temprano.
questions.explanation: "Debemos" means 'we must', so the reported verb stays plural ('they had to'), and the present shifts to the imperfect "debían"; singular "debía" would mean only she had to.
questions.meaning: they had to, were supposed to

questions.prompt: Él reconoció: "Necesito ayuda." → Él reconoció que ___ ayuda.
questions.explanation: The present "Necesito" (he speaking) becomes the imperfect third person singular after 'reconoció': "necesitaba".

questions.prompt: Ellos concluyeron: "El experimento falló." → Ellos concluyeron que el experimento ___.
questions.explanation: The preterite "falló" backshifts to the pluperfect in reported speech after 'concluyeron': "había fallado".

questions.prompt: Ella observó: "Algo cambió." → Ella observó que algo ___.
questions.explanation: The preterite "cambió" becomes the pluperfect, and singular 'algo' needs a singular verb: "había cambiado" (not 'habían').

questions.prompt: Él aseguró: "Todo está bien." → Él aseguró que todo ___ bien.
questions.explanation: "está bien" uses estar, and after the past 'aseguró' the present shifts to the imperfect: "estaba" (ser would not fit 'bien').

questions.prompt: Ellos repitieron: "No cambiaremos de opinión." → Ellos repitieron que no ___ de opinión.
questions.explanation: The future "cambiaremos" becomes the conditional after 'repitieron', and the subject 'ellos' requires the third person plural: "cambiarían".

questions.prompt: Ella subrayó: "Este punto es clave." → Ella subrayó que ese punto ___ clave.
questions.explanation: After the past 'subrayó', the present "es" shifts to the imperfect, and 'clave' is a quality, so ser is used: "era".

units.title: Subjunctive After Conjunctions
units.description: para que, a menos que, con tal de que — Subjunctive obligatorily triggered by certain conjunctions.

lessons.title: Subjunctive After Conjunctions 1
lessons.subtitle: para que, a menos que, con tal de que

questions.prompt: Te lo explico para que lo ___ (entender).
questions.explanation: "entiendas" is subjunctive because "para que" (so that) expresses purpose and always takes the subjunctive. The indicative "entiendes" and the future "entenderás" are not allowed after it.

questions.prompt: No saldremos a menos que ___ (dejar) de llover.
questions.explanation: "deje" is subjunctive because "a menos que" (unless) introduces a condition and always takes the subjunctive. "Deja" and "dejó" are indicative forms.

questions.prompt: Te ayudo con tal de que ___ (terminar) a tiempo.
questions.explanation: "termines" is subjunctive because "con tal de que" (provided that) states a condition and always takes the subjunctive. "Terminas" and "terminaste" are indicative.

questions.prompt: Estudia mucho antes de que ___ (ser) el examen.
questions.explanation: "sea" is subjunctive because "antes de que" (before) always takes the subjunctive, since the exam has not happened yet. "Es" and "será" are indicative.
questions.example: Vámonos antes de que sea demasiado tarde.

questions.prompt: Llámame en cuanto ___ (llegar).
questions.explanation: "llegues" is subjunctive because "en cuanto" refers to a future, not-yet-happened event after the command "Llámame". With a future meaning, "en cuanto" takes the subjunctive, not "llegas" or "llegaste".

lessons.title: Subjunctive After Conjunctions 2
lessons.subtitle: para que, a menos que, con tal de que

questions.prompt: Iré aunque ___ (llover).
questions.explanation: "llueva" is subjunctive because "aunque" with a hypothetical, uncertain event ("even if it rains") takes the subjunctive. The infinitive "llover" cannot follow "aunque" and "llovía" is a past form.

questions.prompt: Trabajamos sin que nadie nos ___ (decir) qué hacer.
questions.explanation: "diga" is subjunctive because "sin que" (without) always takes the subjunctive. The subject "nadie" needs a third-person form, so "diga" fits.

questions.prompt: Ahorra dinero para que ___ (poder) viajar.
questions.explanation: "puedas" is subjunctive because "para que" (so that) expresses purpose and always takes the subjunctive. "Puedes" and "podrás" are indicative.

questions.prompt: No firmes hasta que lo ___ (leer) todo.
questions.explanation: "leas" is subjunctive because "hasta que" looks ahead to something that has not happened yet ("don't sign until you've read it all"). "Lees" and "leíste" are indicative.

questions.prompt: Vendrá a menos que ___ (surgir) un problema.
questions.explanation: "surja" is subjunctive because "a menos que" (unless) introduces a condition and always takes the subjunctive. "Surge" and "surgirá" are indicative.

lessons.title: Subjunctive After Conjunctions 3
lessons.subtitle: para que, a menos que, con tal de que

questions.prompt: Hazlo bien de modo que no ___ (haber) errores.
questions.explanation: "haya" is present subjunctive because "de modo que" expresses a desired result (so that there are no mistakes) and takes the subjunctive. "Hay" is indicative and "hubiera" is imperfect, which clashes with the command "Hazlo".

questions.prompt: Espera aquí hasta que yo ___ (volver).
questions.explanation: "vuelva" is subjunctive because "hasta que" points to a future event not yet happened, and the subject is "yo". "Vuelvo" is indicative and "vuelvas" is the wrong person (tú).

questions.prompt: No lo firmes sin que un abogado lo ___ (revisar).
questions.explanation: The conjunction "sin que" always takes the subjunctive, and "un abogado" is third person singular, so the form is "revise".

questions.prompt: Seguiremos adelante siempre que ustedes ___ (estar) de acuerdo.
questions.explanation: "siempre que" meaning 'as long as' (a condition) takes the subjunctive, and "ustedes" requires the third person plural form "estén".

questions.prompt: Avísame cuando ___ (saber) los resultados.
questions.explanation: "cuando" takes the subjunctive when it refers to a future event, as in a request to be told later, so "sepas" (tú form of saber) is needed.

units.title: Past Hypotheticals
units.description: If I had had..., I would have... — Type-3 conditional: si + pluperfect subjunctive + conditional perfect.

lessons.title: Past Hypotheticals 1
lessons.subtitle: If I had had..., I would have...

questions.prompt: Si yo ___ (saber) la verdad, habría actuado diferente.
questions.explanation: The main clause "habría actuado" is a conditional perfect, so the "si" clause about the unreal past needs the pluperfect subjunctive: "hubiera sabido".

questions.prompt: Si ella ___ (estudiar) más, habría aprobado.
questions.explanation: After "si" in a hypothetical about the past, with "habría aprobado" in the result clause, Spanish uses the pluperfect subjunctive: "hubiera estudiado".

questions.prompt: Si nosotros ___ (salir) antes, no habríamos llegado tarde.
questions.explanation: The result clause "no habríamos llegado tarde" is a conditional perfect, so the "si" clause takes the pluperfect subjunctive with "nosotros": "hubiéramos salido".
questions.meaning: we had left, we had gone out

questions.prompt: Si ellos ___ (venir), habrían visto el espectáculo.
questions.explanation: An unreal past condition with "si" followed by "habrían visto" needs the pluperfect subjunctive in the third person plural: "hubieran venido".

questions.prompt: Si tú me lo ___ (decir), te habría ayudado.
questions.explanation: Because the result is "te habría ayudado", the "si" clause must be pluperfect subjunctive, and with "tú" that is "hubieras dicho".
questions.meaning: you had said, you had told

lessons.title: Past Hypotheticals 2
lessons.subtitle: If I had had..., I would have...

questions.prompt: Si yo ___ (tener) más tiempo, habría terminado el proyecto.
questions.explanation: The unreal past condition after "si" pairs with the conditional perfect "habría terminado", so the verb is pluperfect subjunctive: "hubiera tenido".

questions.prompt: Si ella ___ (llamar), habríamos ido a recogerla.
questions.explanation: "habríamos ido" is a conditional perfect, so the "si" clause about what she did not do takes the pluperfect subjunctive: "hubiera llamado".

questions.prompt: Si nosotros lo ___ (saber) antes, habríamos cambiado los planes.
questions.explanation: With "habríamos cambiado" in the result clause, the "si" clause needs the pluperfect subjunctive for "nosotros": "hubiéramos sabido".

questions.prompt: Si ellos ___ (escuchar), habrían entendido mejor.
questions.explanation: The result "habrían entendido" is a conditional perfect, so the "si" clause uses the pluperfect subjunctive for "ellos": "hubieran escuchado".

questions.prompt: Si tú ___ (llegar) a tiempo, no te habrías perdido nada.
questions.explanation: The past unreal "si" clause (you didn't arrive on time) needs the pluperfect subjunctive, so "hubieras llegado" fits; "habrías llegado" is the result-clause form and "habías llegado" is indicative.

lessons.title: Past Hypotheticals 3
lessons.subtitle: If I had had..., I would have...

questions.prompt: Si yo ___ (poder), te habría acompañado.
questions.explanation: After "si" in an impossible past condition (I couldn't go), use the pluperfect subjunctive "hubiera podido"; the main clause "habría acompañado" already carries the conditional.

questions.prompt: Si ella ___ (querer), habría venido con nosotros.
questions.explanation: The "si" clause describes something that didn't happen (she didn't want to), so it takes the pluperfect subjunctive "hubiera querido", not the indicative "había querido".

questions.prompt: Si nosotros ___ (revisar) el contrato, no habría problemas.
questions.explanation: A hypothetical past action inside "si" takes the pluperfect subjunctive, so "hubiéramos revisado" is right; "habríamos revisado" is conditional and cannot follow "si" here.
questions.meaning: we had reviewed, we had checked
questions.example: Si nosotros hubiéramos revisado el contrato, no tendríamos problemas.

questions.prompt: Si ellos ___ (avisar) antes, habríamos estado listos.
questions.explanation: The unreal past condition (they didn't warn us) requires "hubieran avisado", the pluperfect subjunctive, matched with "habríamos estado" in the result clause.
questions.meaning: they had given notice, they had warned

questions.prompt: Si tú ___ (insistir), habríamos cambiado de plan.
questions.explanation: "Si" plus a past event that didn't happen (you didn't insist) takes the pluperfect subjunctive "hubieras insistido"; the conditional perfect belongs in the other clause.

units.title: Confusable Verb Pairs
units.description: saber/conocer, pedir/preguntar, llevar/traer — Classic confusable Spanish verb pairs for English speakers.

questions.prompt: Which verb best fits "to know a fact"?
questions.explanation: "saber" is for knowing facts or information (Sé que llega mañana). "conocer" is for being familiar with people or places.

questions.prompt: Which verb best fits "to know/be familiar with a person or place"?
questions.explanation: "conocer" means being familiar with a person or place (Conozco Lima). "saber" is for facts and skills.

questions.prompt: Which verb best fits "to ask for something"?
questions.explanation: "pedir" means to request something (Pedí un café). "preguntar" means to ask a question.

questions.prompt: Which verb best fits "to ask a question"?
questions.explanation: "preguntar" means to ask a question or ask for information (Le pregunté la hora). "pedir" means to request an object or favor.

questions.prompt: Which verb best fits "to take/carry something (away to another place)"?
questions.explanation: "llevar" means to carry something away to another place; "traer" means to bring it toward the speaker, and "tomar" means to take hold of or grab it, not to carry it somewhere.

questions.prompt: Which verb best fits "to bring something (here)"?
questions.explanation: "traer" means to bring something toward where the speaker is (here). "llevar" means to take it away to another place.

questions.prompt: Which verb best fits "to leave (depart)"?
questions.explanation: "salir" means to leave in the sense of departing or going out (Salgo a las ocho). "dejar" is to leave something behind, and "quedarse" is to stay.

questions.prompt: Which verb best fits "to leave something behind"?
questions.explanation: "dejar" means to leave something or someone behind (Dejé las llaves en casa). "salir" and "irse" mean the person departs.

questions.prompt: Which verb best fits "to play an instrument"?
questions.explanation: Instruments take "tocar" (Toco la guitarra). Games and sports take "jugar".

questions.prompt: Which verb best fits "to play a game/sport"?
questions.explanation: Games and sports take "jugar" (Juego al fútbol). Instruments take "tocar".

questions.prompt: Which verb best fits "to look at"?
questions.explanation: "mirar" means to look at something (Mira el cuadro). "buscar" means to look for, and "parecer" means to look or seem.

questions.prompt: Which verb best fits "to look for"?
questions.explanation: "buscar" already means "to look for", so it needs no preposition (Busco mis llaves). "mirar" means to look at.

questions.prompt: Which verb best fits "to become (permanent change)"?
questions.explanation: "convertirse en" expresses a lasting change into something new (Se convirtió en médico). "ponerse" is for temporary changes of mood or state.

questions.prompt: Which verb best fits "to become (temporary/emotional)"?
questions.explanation: "ponerse" + adjective expresses a sudden, temporary change of mood or state, as in "se puso nervioso"; "volverse" suggests a lasting change, and "convertirse en" means turning into something.

questions.prompt: Which verb best fits "to realize"?
questions.explanation: "darse cuenta de" means to realize or notice something, as in "Me di cuenta de mi error"; "realizar" is a false friend that means to carry out.

units.title: Business & Negotiation
units.description: Formal negotiation vocabulary — Business negotiation vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "agreement" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "acuerdo" is an agreement, as in "llegar a un acuerdo" (to reach an agreement); "plazo" is a deadline and "ingresos" means income.

questions.prompt: How do you say "proposal" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "propuesta" is a proposal put forward, as in "presentar una propuesta"; "acuerdo" is the agreement that may follow, and "responsabilidad" means responsibility.

questions.prompt: How do you say "counteroffer" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A counteroffer is an offer made in reply to the other side's offer, and Spanish builds it the same way: contra- (counter) + oferta (offer) gives "contraoferta".

questions.prompt: How do you say "stakeholder" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "parte interesada" means a party with an interest in a deal or project, a stakeholder; "sociedad" means a company or partnership.

questions.prompt: How do you say "merger" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "fusión" is the joining of two companies into one, a merger; "incumplimiento" means a breach of contract.

questions.prompt: How do you say "acquisition" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Buying another company is an "adquisición" (note the -d- in adq-, missing in English); "accionista" is a shareholder and "propuesta" is a proposal.

questions.prompt: How do you say "deadline (contractual)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "plazo" is the time limit set for fulfilling an obligation in a contract, as in "el plazo vence el lunes".

questions.prompt: How do you say "terms and conditions" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "términos y condiciones" are the clauses a party must accept in an agreement; "ingresos" means revenue.

questions.prompt: How do you say "liability" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: In contracts, "responsabilidad" means legal liability, as in "responsabilidad limitada". In everyday use the same word also means responsibility.

questions.prompt: How do you say "shareholder" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "accionista" is a person who owns shares (acciones) in a company, a shareholder; "adquisición" means an acquisition.

questions.prompt: How do you say "arbitration" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Settling a dispute through a neutral third party is "arbitraje"; "acuerdo" is the agreement itself and "términos y condiciones" are terms and conditions.

questions.prompt: How do you say "negotiation" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: The process of discussing terms to reach a deal is "negociación" (spelled with c, not t, before -ión); "ingresos" means revenue and "adquisición" means acquisition.

questions.prompt: How do you say "partnership" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: In business, "sociedad" is a partnership or company formed by partners ("socios"). "Fusión" is a merger of two companies.

questions.prompt: How do you say "revenue" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: The money a company takes in is "ingresos", always plural in this sense; "accionista" is a shareholder and "contraoferta" is a counteroffer.

questions.prompt: How do you say "breach" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A breach of contract is a failure to fulfil it, from incumplir (to fail to comply), hence "incumplimiento"; "plazo" means deadline and "ingresos" means revenue.

units.title: Diplomatic Correspondence
units.description: Formal letter phrases — Phrases typical of formal/diplomatic written correspondence.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Dear Sir or Madam" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Dear Sir or Madam → Estimado señor o señora. Phrases typical of formal/diplomatic written correspondence.

questions.prompt: How do you say "I am writing to inform you" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Le escribo para informarle" uses "le", the formal usted pronoun, plus "para" + infinitive to state the letter's purpose, just like "I am writing to inform you".

questions.prompt: How do you say "With reference to your letter" in Spanish?
choices: Quedo a la espera de su respuesta
questions.explanation: "En referencia a su carta" matches "With reference to your letter"; "su" is the formal "your" used in official correspondence.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Please do not hesitate to contact me" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "No dude en contactarme" is a formal usted command (dudar → dude) that politely invites the reader to get in touch, like "Please do not hesitate to contact me".

questions.prompt: How do you say "I look forward to hearing from you" in Spanish?
choices: Quedo a la espera de su respuesta
questions.explanation: "Quedo a la espera de su respuesta" literally means "I remain awaiting your reply". It is the standard formal Spanish closing for "I look forward to hearing from you".

questions.prompt: How do you say "Yours faithfully" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Le saluda atentamente" is the standard closing formula of a formal Spanish letter, used where English writes "Yours faithfully" above the signature.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Enclosed please find" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Adjunto encontrará" means "attached you will find". It uses the formal usted future "encontrará" to point the reader to enclosed documents.

questions.prompt: How do you say "We regret to inform you" in Spanish?
choices: Gracias por su atención a este asunto
questions.explanation: "Lamentamos informarle" combines "lamentamos" (we regret) with "informarle" (to inform you, formal) to open bad news politely.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Thank you for your attention to this matter" in Spanish?
choices: Gracias por su atención a este asunto
questions.explanation: "Gracias por su atención a este asunto" thanks the reader formally ("su") for attending to "este asunto", this matter.

questions.prompt: How do you say "It would be greatly appreciated" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Se agradecería enormemente" uses the impersonal "se" with the conditional "agradecería" to say "it would be greatly appreciated" without naming who appreciates it.

questions.prompt: How do you say "In accordance with" in Spanish?
choices: Gracias por su atención a este asunto
questions.explanation: "De acuerdo con" means "in accordance with" and introduces the rule or agreement being followed; the other options are a letter opening and a thank-you line.

questions.prompt: How do you say "On behalf of" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "En nombre de" literally means "in the name of", which is how Spanish says "on behalf of" when you act or speak for someone.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Please find attached the requested documents" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Adjunto encontrará los documentos solicitados" is the formal formula for "please find attached": "adjunto" means attached, "encontrará" is the polite usted form of "you will find", and "solicitados" means requested.

questions.prompt: How do you say "We would like to schedule a meeting" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Nos gustaría programar una reunión" uses the conditional "nos gustaría" for the polite "we would like", and "programar una reunión" means "to schedule a meeting".

questions.prompt: How do you say "Kind regards" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Saludos cordiales" is the common courteous sign-off at the end of a letter or email, matching English "Kind regards".

units.title: Literary & Narrative Devices
units.description: Talking about storytelling — Vocabulary for discussing literature and narrative technique.

questions.prompt: How do you say "plot" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "trama" is the sequence of events in a story, its plot; "tema" is the underlying theme, and "antagonista" is a character.

questions.prompt: How do you say "character" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "personaje" is a person or figure in a story; "simbolismo" and "punto de vista" are narrative techniques, not people.

questions.prompt: How do you say "narrator" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "narrador" is the voice that tells the story; "flashback" is a time-shifting technique, and "ironía" is a literary device.

questions.prompt: How do you say "setting" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ambientación" is the time and place in which a story happens, its setting; "clímax" is the peak of the plot, and "personaje" is a character.

questions.prompt: How do you say "theme" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "tema" is the central idea a work explores, its theme; "tono" is the author's attitude, and "metáfora" is a figure of speech.

questions.prompt: How do you say "metaphor" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "metáfora" is the figure of speech that equates two things without "como"; "ironía" says the opposite of what is meant, and "flashback" is a jump back in time.

questions.prompt: How do you say "symbolism" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Using objects or images to stand for ideas is "simbolismo"; "presagio" is foreshadowing or an omen, and "trama" is the plot.

questions.prompt: How do you say "irony" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Saying or showing the opposite of what is expected is "ironía", written with an accent on the í; "protagonista" is the main character and "narrador" is the narrator.

questions.prompt: How do you say "foreshadowing" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: A hint of what will happen later in a story is a "presagio" (also called prefiguración); "metáfora" is a metaphor and "punto de vista" is point of view.

questions.prompt: How do you say "climax" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: The point of highest tension in a story is the "clímax", which needs an accent on the í; "trama" is the plot and "ironía" is irony.

questions.prompt: How do you say "protagonist" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "protagonista" is the main character of a story; unlike most -a nouns, it keeps the same form for men and women (el/la protagonista).

questions.prompt: How do you say "antagonist" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "antagonista" is the character who opposes the hero, the protagonista; like it, the word works for both genders (el/la antagonista).

questions.prompt: How do you say "tone" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "tono" is the author's attitude or mood in a text. Don't confuse it with "tema" (theme) or "trama" (plot).

questions.prompt: How do you say "point of view" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "punto de vista" is the literary term for the perspective a story is told from, as in "narrado desde el punto de vista del hijo"; "tono" is the attitude of the text and "metáfora" is a figure of speech.

questions.prompt: How do you say "flashback" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: In literary analysis a flashback is called "analepsis" (also "escena retrospectiva"); the anglicism "flashback" is common only in everyday speech.

units.title: Philosophy & Abstract Concepts
units.description: Abstract thought vocabulary — Philosophical and abstract-concept vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "existence" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: The fact of being or living is "existencia" (spelled with -cia, not -ce); "identidad" is identity and "ética" is ethics.

questions.prompt: How do you say "consciousness" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Awareness of oneself and the world is "conciencia", the same word Spanish uses for conscience (the variant consciencia also exists); "realidad" is reality and "virtud" is virtue.

questions.prompt: How do you say "truth" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "verdad" means truth (la verdad); "creencia" is something you believe, which may or may not be true, and "moralidad" is morality.

questions.prompt: How do you say "ethics" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ética" is the Spanish noun for ethics, the study of right and wrong; it is feminine (la ética), while "conciencia" means conscience and "duda" means doubt.

questions.prompt: How do you say "freedom" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "libertad" means freedom or liberty (la libertad de expresión); "sentido" is meaning and "ética" is ethics.

questions.prompt: How do you say "reality" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "realidad" is the Spanish word for reality, as in la realidad y la apariencia; "justicia" means justice and "conocimiento" means knowledge.

questions.prompt: How do you say "knowledge" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "conocimiento" means knowledge, from conocer (to know); "razón" is reason and "existencia" is existence.

questions.prompt: How do you say "belief" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "creencia" means belief, from creer (to believe); "verdad" is truth and "identidad" is identity.

questions.prompt: How do you say "reason" (the faculty of thinking) in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "razón" is reason as the human ability to think logically (la razón y la fe); a reason in the sense of a motive is usually "motivo".

questions.prompt: How do you say "doubt" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "duda" is the noun for doubt, as in sin duda (without a doubt); "verdad" means truth and "identidad" means identity.

questions.prompt: How do you say "identity" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "identidad" is the Spanish word for identity; English -ity often becomes -idad, and the word is feminine (la identidad).

questions.prompt: How do you say "meaning" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "sentido" is meaning in the philosophical sense, as in "el sentido de la vida"; for the meaning of a word, Spanish usually says significado.

questions.prompt: How do you say "virtue" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "virtud" is the Spanish word for virtue, a good moral quality (la paciencia es una virtud); "moralidad" is morality in general, not a single good quality.

questions.prompt: How do you say "justice" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "justicia" is the Spanish word for justice; English nouns ending in -ice often become -icia, and it is feminine (la justicia). "Razón" means reason and "conciencia" means conscience or awareness.

questions.prompt: How do you say "morality" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "moralidad" means morality; English nouns ending in -ity usually become -idad in Spanish, and they are feminine (la moralidad).

units.title: Science & Technology (Advanced)
units.description: Scientific vocabulary — Advanced science and technology vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "prototype" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "prototipo" means prototype; the English ending -type becomes -tipo, and the noun is masculine (el prototipo).

questions.prompt: How do you say "experiment" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "experimento" means a scientific experiment (el experimento); don't confuse it with "experiencia", which means experience.

questions.prompt: How do you say "data" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "datos" translates data and is plural in Spanish, as in "los datos muestran"; "algoritmo" is algorithm and "cuántico" is quantum.

questions.prompt: How do you say "algorithm" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "algoritmo" means algorithm; it is masculine (el algoritmo) and is spelled with a t, not th.

questions.prompt: How do you say "artificial intelligence" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "inteligencia artificial" means artificial intelligence; in Spanish the adjective comes after the noun, so the word order is the reverse of English.

questions.prompt: How do you say "molecule" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "molécula" means molecule; it is feminine (la molécula) and carries a written accent on the é because the stress falls on the third-to-last syllable.

questions.prompt: How do you say "gene" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "gen" means gene; it is masculine (el gen), and its plural is genes.

questions.prompt: How do you say "theory" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "teoría" means theory; the accent on the í shows that the stress falls on that vowel, so it is pronounced te-o-RÍ-a.

questions.prompt: How do you say "innovation" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "innovación" means innovation; English -tion becomes -ción with an accent on the ó, and the word keeps the double n.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sustainability" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "sostenibilidad" means sustainability, from sostener (to sustain); "avance" is a breakthrough or advance and "molécula" is molecule.

questions.prompt: How do you say "quantum" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cuántico" is the adjective quantum, as in "física cuántica" or "computación cuántica"; the other options are nouns meaning innovation and experiment.

questions.prompt: How do you say "neural network" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "red neuronal" means neural network: red is network and neuronal is neural, placed after the noun as Spanish adjectives usually are.

questions.prompt: How do you say "evidence (scientific)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "evidencia" is the data or findings that support a scientific claim; it is feminine (la evidencia), and "pruebas" is also common in this sense.

questions.prompt: How do you say "breakthrough" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "avance" is the usual word for a scientific breakthrough, as in "un gran avance en la medicina"; "simulación" is simulation and "gen" is gene.

questions.prompt: How do you say "simulation" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "simulación" means simulation; English -tion becomes -ción with an accent on the ó, and the noun is feminine (la simulación).

units.title: Word Formation
units.description: Prefixes and suffixes — Common Spanish prefixes/suffixes and the words they form.

questions.prompt: What does the word "rápidamente" mean?
questions.explanation: "rápidamente" is the adjective rápida (fast) plus the suffix -mente, which turns adjectives into adverbs, so it means "quickly".

questions.prompt: What does the word "felizmente" mean?
questions.explanation: "felizmente" is feliz (happy) plus the adverb suffix -mente, so it means "happily".

questions.prompt: What does the word "reconstruir" mean?
questions.explanation: The prefix re- means 'again', so re- + construir (to build) gives "to rebuild".

questions.prompt: What does the word "deshacer" mean?
questions.explanation: The prefix des- reverses an action, so des- + hacer (to do/make) gives "to undo".

questions.prompt: What does the word "inaceptable" mean?
questions.explanation: The prefix in- means 'not', so in- + aceptable gives "unacceptable".

questions.prompt: What does the word "imposible" mean?
questions.explanation: The prefix in- becomes im- before p and means 'not', so im- + posible gives "impossible".

questions.prompt: What does the word "educación" mean?
questions.explanation: The suffix -ción turns the verb educar into a noun naming the action or result, so it means "education".

questions.prompt: What does the word "organización" mean?
questions.explanation: The suffix -ción turns the verb organizar into a noun, so it means "organization", not the person (organizador) or the adjective (organizado).

questions.prompt: What does the word "panadería" mean?
questions.explanation: The suffix -ería names a shop where something is made or sold, so pan (bread) + -ería gives "bakery"; the baker is panadero.

questions.prompt: What does the word "librería" mean?
questions.explanation: The suffix -ería names a shop, so libro + -ería gives "bookstore"; a library is biblioteca and a bookseller is librero.

questions.prompt: What does the word "inútil" mean?
questions.explanation: The prefix in- means 'not', so in- + útil (useful) gives "useless".

questions.prompt: What does the word "prehistórico" mean?
questions.explanation: The prefix pre- means 'before', so pre- + histórico gives "prehistoric", meaning before written history.

questions.prompt: What does the word "subestimar" mean?
questions.explanation: "Subestimar" is "sub-" (under) + "estimar" (to estimate, to value), so it means "to underestimate".

questions.prompt: What does the word "sobrevivir" mean?
questions.explanation: "Sobrevivir" is "sobre-" (over, beyond) + "vivir" (to live), meaning to live through something, so it means "to survive".

questions.prompt: What does the word "imposibilidad" mean?
questions.explanation: "Imposibilidad" is "imposible" + the noun suffix "-idad" (English "-ity"), so it means "impossibility".

units.title: Advanced Idiomatic Expressions II
units.description: More sophisticated sayings — More advanced idiomatic expressions for fluent Spanish.

questions.prompt: What does "costar Dios y ayuda" mean?
questions.explanation: "costar Dios y ayuda" literally means to cost God and help, so it describes something so hard you need divine help; it means "to be extremely difficult", as in "Me costó Dios y ayuda terminarlo."

questions.prompt: What does "no tener nombre" mean?
choices: to take the bull by the horns
questions.explanation: "No tener nombre" literally means "to have no name": something so bad there is no word for it. So it means "to be outrageous", as in "Lo que hiciste no tiene nombre."

questions.prompt: What does "írsele el santo al cielo" mean?
questions.explanation: The image is your saint flying off to heaven: your mind goes blank. So "írsele el santo al cielo" means "to completely forget something" you were about to say or do.

questions.prompt: What does "ponerse las botas" mean?
choices: to deceive someone with a substitute
questions.explanation: ponerse las botas → to indulge oneself. More advanced idiomatic expressions for fluent Spanish.

questions.prompt: What does "estar en su salsa" mean?
questions.explanation: Someone "en su salsa" is like food in its own sauce, perfectly comfortable. So the idiom means "to be in one's element".

questions.prompt: What does "no pegar ojo" mean?
choices: to talk a mile a minute
questions.explanation: "Pegar ojo" means to shut your eyes and sleep, so "no pegar ojo" means "to not sleep a wink".

questions.prompt: What does "tomar el toro por los cuernos" mean?
choices: to take the bull by the horns
questions.explanation: Spanish uses the same image as English for facing a problem head-on: "to take the bull by the horns". In much of Latin America you will also hear "agarrar el toro por los cuernos".

questions.prompt: What does "importar un bledo" mean?
questions.explanation: A "bledo" is a worthless weed, so if something "te importa un bledo" it matters nothing to you. The idiom means "to not care at all".

questions.prompt: What does "estar hecho polvo" mean?
questions.explanation: Literally "to be turned to dust", "estar hecho polvo" means "to be exhausted", as in "Después del viaje estoy hecho polvo."

questions.prompt: What does "dar gato por liebre" mean?
choices: to deceive someone with a substitute
questions.explanation: The image is a seller passing off cat meat as hare. So "dar gato por liebre" means "to deceive someone with a substitute".

questions.prompt: What does "no tener abuela" mean?
questions.explanation: "No tener abuela" jokes that a person praises himself because he has no grandmother to do it for him, so it means "to be shamelessly self-praising".

questions.prompt: What does "ser el pan de cada día" mean?
questions.explanation: Literally "to be the daily bread", something you get every day, "ser el pan de cada día" means "to be a daily occurrence".

questions.prompt: What does "hablar por los codos" mean?
choices: to talk a mile a minute
questions.explanation: "Hablar por los codos" pictures someone so chatty they seem to talk even through their elbows, so it means "to talk a mile a minute".

questions.prompt: What does "írsele la mano" mean?
choices: to deceive someone with a substitute
questions.explanation: "Írsele la mano" means your hand gets away from you and adds too much, as in "Se me fue la mano con la sal", so it means "to overdo it".

questions.prompt: What does "poner los puntos sobre las íes" mean?
questions.explanation: "Poner los puntos sobre las íes" means dotting every i, leaving nothing vague, so it means "to spell things out precisely".

units.title: Register Shifting II
units.description: Colloquial to formal, part 2 — More colloquial-to-formal register pairs.

questions.prompt: What is the more formal way to say "to fix (everyday: arreglar)"?
questions.explanation: "reparar" is the formal verb for fixing something broken (reparar una máquina); "revisar" only means to check and "reponer" means to replace.

questions.prompt: What is the more formal way to say "to buy (everyday: comprar)"?
questions.explanation: "adquirir" is the formal verb for buying or obtaining, common in contracts and official notices; "vender" means to sell and "alquilar" means to rent.

questions.prompt: What is the more formal way to say "kid (colloquial: chamaco)"?
questions.explanation: "joven" is the neutral, formal word for a young person, while chamaco is colloquial Mexican Spanish; "anciano" is an old person and "empleado" an employee.

questions.prompt: What is the more formal way to say "boss (everyday: jefe)"?
questions.explanation: "superior" is the formal word for the person above you at work (mi superior inmediato); "compañero" is a colleague and "subordinado" someone below you.

questions.prompt: What is the more formal way to say "to fire someone (colloquial: echar)"?
questions.explanation: "despedir" is the standard, formal verb for ending someone's employment, while "echar" is the casual way to say the same thing.

questions.prompt: What is the more formal way to say "to hire (colloquial: darle chamba a alguien)"?
questions.explanation: "contratar" is the formal verb for taking someone on as an employee, while "darle chamba a alguien" is casual Latin American speech.

questions.prompt: What is the more formal way to say "to talk (colloquial: charlar)"?
questions.explanation: "conversar" is the more formal verb for having a talk, while "charlar" is the relaxed, everyday word; "discutir" means to argue or debate.

questions.prompt: What is the more formal way to say "money (colloquial: plata)"?
questions.explanation: "dinero" is the standard, formal word for money, while "plata" is the everyday Latin American slang; "sueldo" means salary.

questions.prompt: What is the more formal way to say "job (colloquial: chamba)"?
questions.explanation: "empleo" is the formal word for a job or post, used in official contexts, while "chamba" is casual Latin American slang.

questions.prompt: What is the more formal way to say "house (everyday: casa)"?
questions.explanation: "vivienda" is the formal, administrative word for a home, used in official and legal texts, while "casa" is the everyday word.

questions.prompt: What is the more formal way to say "car (everyday: carro)"?
questions.explanation: "vehículo" is the formal term used in official and legal texts, while "carro" is the everyday Latin American word for a car.

questions.prompt: What is the more formal way to say "to eat (everyday: comer)"?
questions.explanation: "alimentarse" is the formal way to talk about eating or taking in food, while "comer" is the everyday verb.

questions.prompt: What is the more formal way to say "to take a nap (colloquial: echarse una pestañita)"?
questions.explanation: "descansar" (to rest) is the neutral, polite way to refer to taking a short rest or nap, while "echarse una pestañita" is casual Latin American speech; the exact standard phrase would be "tomar una siesta".

questions.prompt: What is the more formal way to say "friend (colloquial: colega)"?
questions.explanation: friend (colloquial: colega) → compañero. More colloquial-to-formal register pairs.

questions.prompt: What is the more formal way to say "to leave (colloquial: pirarse)"?
questions.explanation: "marcharse" is the neutral, more formal verb for leaving; "largarse" is just as slangy as "pirarse" (Spain slang), and "quedarse" means to stay.

units.title: Advanced Discourse Markers II
units.description: Even more sophisticated connectors — Further advanced discourse markers for academic/formal Spanish.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to that end" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: to that end → con ese fin. Further advanced discourse markers for academic/formal Spanish.

questions.prompt: How do you say "in other words (formal)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: in other words (formal) → dicho de otra manera. Further advanced discourse markers for academic/formal Spanish.

questions.prompt: How do you say "more specifically" in Spanish?
choices: en la medida de lo posible
questions.explanation: "Concretamente" means "specifically", so "más concretamente" narrows a point down, just like "more specifically".

questions.prompt: How do you say "broadly speaking" in Spanish?
choices: si todo lo demás permanece igual
questions.explanation: "en términos generales" means "broadly speaking" and introduces a general statement before details or exceptions, for example "En términos generales, la medida fue bien recibida."

questions.prompt: How do you say "as previously mentioned" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "como se mencionó anteriormente" uses the impersonal se with the preterite to refer back to a point already made in the text, just like "as previously mentioned".

questions.prompt: How do you say "it follows that" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "de ello se desprende que" literally means "from this it emerges that" and introduces a logical conclusion drawn from what came before, like "it follows that".

questions.prompt: How do you say "against this backdrop" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: against this backdrop → en este contexto. Further advanced discourse markers for academic/formal Spanish.

questions.prompt: How do you say "on closer inspection" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "tras un análisis más detallado" means "after a more detailed analysis" and signals that a closer look changes or refines a first impression, like "on closer inspection".

questions.prompt: How do you say "all else being equal" in Spanish?
choices: si todo lo demás permanece igual
questions.explanation: "si todo lo demás permanece igual" literally means "if everything else stays the same" and is used to isolate one factor in an argument, like "all else being equal" (also written "en igualdad de condiciones").

questions.prompt: How do you say "in the absence of" in Spanish?
choices: en la medida de lo posible
questions.explanation: "en ausencia de" is followed by a noun, as in "en ausencia de pruebas", and means "in the absence of", with no article before "ausencia".

questions.prompt: How do you say "as a case in point" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "como caso ilustrativo" introduces a concrete example that proves the point just made, like "as a case in point"; "a modo de ejemplo" is a common alternative.

questions.prompt: How do you say "in due course" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "a su debido tiempo" means "at the proper time" and announces that something will happen later when appropriate, like "in due course".

questions.prompt: How do you say "with this in mind" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "con esto en mente" mirrors "with this in mind" and introduces an action based on what was just said; in natural Spanish you will also often hear "teniendo esto en cuenta".

questions.prompt: How do you say "insofar as possible" in Spanish?
choices: en la medida de lo posible
questions.explanation: "en la medida de lo posible" means "to the extent possible" and limits a commitment to what can realistically be done, like "insofar as possible".

questions.prompt: How do you say "likewise (by the same token)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "de igual modo" means "in the same way" and adds a point that parallels the previous one, like "likewise" or "by the same token".

units.title: Subjunctive in Relative Clauses
units.description: Nonexistent or indefinite antecedents — Subjunctive required when the antecedent is unknown, indefinite, or nonexistent.

questions.prompt: Busco a alguien que ___ (hablar) tres idiomas.
questions.explanation: "Alguien" is an unknown, unspecified person, so the relative clause takes the subjunctive, and "hable" is the third-person singular form agreeing with "alguien".

questions.prompt: No hay nadie que ___ (saber) la respuesta.
questions.explanation: After "no hay nadie que" the antecedent doesn't exist, so the subjunctive "sepa" is required instead of the indicative "sabe".

questions.prompt: Necesito un libro que ___ (explicar) esto bien.
questions.explanation: "Un libro" is any book you hope exists, not a specific one, so the clause takes the subjunctive; "explique" agrees with the singular "libro".

questions.prompt: ¿Conoces a alguien que ___ (poder) ayudarme?
questions.explanation: In a question about whether such a person exists, "alguien" is unspecified, so the subjunctive is used; "pueda" agrees with the singular "alguien".

questions.prompt: No existe ningún método que ___ (garantizar) el éxito.
questions.explanation: "Ningún método" negates the antecedent, so the relative clause takes the subjunctive, and "garantice" agrees with the singular "método".

questions.prompt: Buscamos una casa que ___ (tener) jardín.
questions.explanation: The house being sought is not yet identified, so the relative clause takes the subjunctive, and "tenga" agrees with the singular "casa".

questions.prompt: No hay nada que ___ (justificar) su comportamiento.
questions.explanation: "No hay nada que..." denies that anything exists, so the relative clause takes the subjunctive; its antecedent "nada" is singular, so the verb is third-person singular "justifique".

questions.prompt: Quiero un trabajo que me ___ (permitir) viajar.
questions.explanation: "Un trabajo que..." describes a job that may not exist yet, so the verb is subjunctive. The singular subject "trabajo" calls for "permita", not a plural or a tú form.
