questions.prompt: No conozco a nadie que ___ (vivir) allí.
questions.explanation: "No conozco a nadie que..." denies that such a person exists, so the clause takes the subjunctive. "Nadie" is singular, hence "viva".

questions.prompt: Necesitamos a alguien que ___ (conocer) el sistema.
questions.explanation: "Alguien que..." refers to an unspecified person we are still looking for, so the verb is subjunctive. "Alguien" is singular, giving "conozca".
questions.example: Necesitamos a alguien que conozca el sistema.

questions.prompt: ¿Hay algún restaurante que ___ (servir) comida vegana?
questions.explanation: In a question like "¿Hay algún restaurante que...?" we do not know whether such a place exists, so the subjunctive is used. "Restaurante" is singular, hence "sirva".

questions.prompt: No hay razón que ___ (explicar) su ausencia.
questions.explanation: "No hay razón que..." says no such reason exists, so the relative clause takes the subjunctive. The singular "razón" calls for "explique".

questions.prompt: Buscan un candidato que ___ (tener) experiencia.
questions.explanation: "Buscan un candidato que..." describes a candidate who is not yet identified, so the subjunctive is needed. "Candidato" is singular, giving "tenga".

questions.prompt: No hay nadie aquí que ___ (querer) ese puesto.
questions.explanation: "No hay nadie aquí que..." denies that anyone exists, so the verb must be subjunctive, not indicative "quiere". "Nadie" is singular, so "quiera".

questions.prompt: Quiero encontrar algo que me ___ (hacer) feliz.
questions.explanation: "Algo que..." refers to something not yet found, so the subjunctive "haga" is used rather than indicative "hace" or the past forms.

questions.prompt: No existe una solución que ___ (satisfacer) a todos.
questions.explanation: "No existe una solución que..." denies that such a solution exists, so the subjunctive is required, not indicative "satisface". "Solución" is singular, giving "satisfaga".

questions.prompt: Necesito a alguien que ___ (entender) el problema.
questions.explanation: "Alguien que..." is an unspecified person we need, so the verb is subjunctive. "Alguien" is singular, so "entienda", not "entiendan" or "entiendas".

questions.prompt: ¿Hay alguien que ___ (saber) tocar el piano?
questions.explanation: In a question like "¿Hay alguien que...?" we do not know if such a person exists, so the subjunctive "sepa" is used instead of "sabía", "supo" or "sabrá".

questions.prompt: No hay ningún plan que ___ (funcionar) perfectamente.
questions.explanation: After "No hay ningún plan que", the plan is non-existent, so Spanish needs the subjunctive; "funcione" is the third-person singular subjunctive of funcionar, agreeing with the singular "plan".

questions.prompt: Buscamos empleados que ___ (ser) responsables.
questions.explanation: "Buscamos empleados que..." describes people who are not yet identified, so the verb is subjunctive, and "sean" is the plural form agreeing with "empleados".

questions.prompt: No conozco ningún lugar que ___ (ofrecer) esto.
questions.explanation: "No conozco ningún lugar que..." denies that such a place exists, so the subjunctive is required, and "ofrezca" is the singular subjunctive of ofrecer agreeing with "lugar".

questions.prompt: Quiero un coche que ___ (consumir) poca gasolina.
questions.explanation: "un coche que..." refers to a car the speaker wants but has not chosen yet, so the subjunctive is needed, and "consuma" is the singular form agreeing with "coche".

questions.prompt: No hay evidencia que ___ (probar) su culpabilidad.
questions.explanation: "No hay evidencia que..." says no such evidence exists, so the verb is subjunctive, and "pruebe" is the singular form agreeing with "evidencia".

questions.prompt: Necesitamos una estrategia que ___ (resolver) esto.
questions.explanation: "una estrategia que..." describes a strategy we need but do not yet have, so the subjunctive is used, and "resuelva" is the singular form agreeing with "estrategia".

questions.prompt: ¿Existe algo que ___ (poder) cambiar su decisión?
questions.explanation: "¿Existe algo que...?" asks about something whose existence is uncertain, so the subjunctive is used, and "pueda" is the singular form of poder agreeing with "algo".

units.title: Nuanced Synonyms II
units.description: Even more precise vocabulary — Further advanced vocabulary offering more precise alternatives.

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to cause (basic: causar)"?
questions.explanation: "ocasionar" is the more formal synonym of "causar", typical of written Spanish for bringing about effects or problems (ocasionar daños); the other options mean to gather, to establish and to strengthen.

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to reduce (basic: reducir)"? ___
questions.explanation: "disminuir" means to make something smaller in amount, like "reducir", and is common in formal writing; "limitar" only sets a limit, and "incrementar" means the opposite.

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to increase (basic: aumentar)"?
questions.explanation: "incrementar" is the formal equivalent of "aumentar", typical of reports and news, as in "incrementar los precios" or "incrementar la producción".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to reveal (basic: mostrar)"? ___
questions.explanation: "revelar" is more precise than "mostrar" because it means to make known something that was hidden or secret, as in "revelar un secreto".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to demand (what one is owed) (basic: pedir)"?
questions.explanation: "reclamar" is more precise than "pedir" when you demand something you are entitled to, as in "reclamar sus derechos" or "reclamar una indemnización".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to avoid (basic: evitar)"? ___
questions.explanation: "eludir" is a formal way to say "evitar" when you dodge or evade something, as in "eludir una responsabilidad" or "eludir una pregunta".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to gather (people) (basic: reunir)"?
questions.explanation: "congregar" is a formal verb for bringing many people together in one place, as in "El concierto congregó a miles de personas".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to reject (basic: rechazar)"? ___
questions.explanation: "repudiar" is a stronger, more formal way to say "rechazar": it means to reject something firmly because you condemn it, as in "repudiar la violencia".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to support (basic: apoyar)"?
questions.explanation: "respaldar" is a more formal verb than "apoyar" for backing a person, plan or claim, as in "El gobierno respaldó la propuesta".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to achieve (a goal) (basic: conseguir)"? ___
questions.explanation: "alcanzar" is a more elevated verb than "conseguir" for reaching a goal or target, as in "alcanzar un objetivo" or "alcanzar un acuerdo".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to face (a problem) (basic: enfrentar)"? ___
questions.explanation: "afrontar" is the more formal verb for facing a difficulty head-on and taking responsibility for it, as in "afrontar una crisis".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to solve (a problem) (basic: arreglar)"?
questions.explanation: "solucionar" is more formal than the everyday "arreglar" when you mean finding a solution to a problem, as in "solucionar un conflicto".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to consider (a possibility) (basic: tener en cuenta)"? ___
questions.explanation: "contemplar" is a formal verb for taking a possibility or case into account, as in "La ley contempla varias excepciones".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to strengthen (basic: fortalecer)"?
questions.explanation: "robustecer" is a formal synonym of "fortalecer" that means to make something sturdier or more solid, as in "robustecer la economía".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to undermine (a right, a reputation) (basic: debilitar)"? ___
questions.explanation: "menoscabar" means to undermine or diminish something abstract, such as someone's rights, authority or reputation. That makes it a more precise, formal choice than the general "debilitar".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to emphasize (basic: enfatizar)"?
questions.explanation: "recalcar" means to stress a point by repeating or underlining it, as in "Recalcó la importancia del acuerdo". It is a more precise verb than "enfatizar".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to clarify (basic: aclarar)"? ___
questions.explanation: to clarify (basic: aclarar) → esclarecer. Further advanced vocabulary offering more precise alternatives.

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to summarize (basic: resumir)"?
questions.explanation: "sintetizar" means to condense ideas into their essential points. It is a more formal and precise verb than "resumir".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to expand, to broaden (basic: agrandar)"? ___
questions.explanation: "ampliar" means to broaden the size or scope of something, as in "ampliar un plazo" or "ampliar conocimientos". It is more precise than the everyday "agrandar".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to restrict (basic: restringir)"?
questions.explanation: to restrict (basic: restringir) → limitar. Further advanced vocabulary offering more precise alternatives.

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to enable (basic: permitir)"?
questions.explanation: "posibilitar" means to make something possible, as in "La beca posibilitó sus estudios". It is a more formal verb than "permitir".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to hinder (basic: dificultar)"? ___
questions.explanation: "obstaculizar" means to put obstacles in the way of something, such as progress or an investigation. It is a more formal verb than "dificultar".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to promote (basic: promover)"?
questions.explanation: "fomentar" means to actively encourage or stimulate something, such as reading, investment or dialogue. It is a more precise verb than "promover".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to establish (basic: establecer)"? ___
questions.explanation: "instaurar" means to set up something new, such as a system, a regime or a custom. It is a more formal verb than "establecer".

questions.prompt: What is a more precise/formal way to say "to postpone (basic: dejar para más tarde)"?
questions.explanation: "posponer" means to move an event or decision to a later time, as in "posponer la reunión". It is the precise verb for the everyday phrase "dejar para más tarde".

units.title: Political & Social Commentary
units.description: Discussing society — Vocabulary for political and social commentary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "public opinion" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "opinión pública" puts the adjective after the noun, as Spanish usually does, and the adjective agrees with the feminine noun "opinión", hence "pública".

questions.prompt: How do you say "social inequality" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "desigualdad social" is the standard term for unequal access to income, rights or opportunities. Note that the noun comes first and the adjective "social" follows it.

questions.prompt: How do you say "grassroots movement" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "movimiento de base" is the usual Spanish term for a grassroots movement, one that starts from ordinary citizens rather than from institutions.

questions.prompt: How do you say "policy reform" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "reforma de políticas" means changing existing policies; "reforma" is reform and "políticas" is policies (you will also hear "reforma de políticas públicas").

questions.prompt: How do you say "civic engagement" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "participación cívica" means taking part in public and community life; "activismo de base" is grassroots activism, a narrower idea.

questions.prompt: How do you say "socioeconomic status" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "estatus socioeconómico" is a person's combined social and economic standing; "nivel socioeconómico" is also common in Latin America.

questions.prompt: How do you say "marginalized community" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "comunidad marginada" is a community pushed to the edges of society; "marginada" agrees in the feminine with "comunidad".

questions.prompt: How do you say "systemic change" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cambio sistémico" is change to a whole system and its structures, not just to a single rule or policy.

questions.prompt: How do you say "collective action" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "acción colectiva" is action a group takes together toward a shared goal; "colectiva" agrees in the feminine with "acción".

questions.prompt: How do you say "public discourse" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "discurso público" is how issues are talked about in public debate; "opinión pública" is what people think, which is a different idea.

questions.prompt: How do you say "social cohesion" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cohesión social" is the bond that holds a society together; as in many Spanish phrases, the adjective "social" comes after the noun.

questions.prompt: How do you say "economic disparity" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "disparidad económica" is unequal distribution of income and wealth; "disparidad" directly matches English "disparity".

questions.prompt: How do you say "political polarization" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "polarización política" is the split of a society into opposing political camps; "política" agrees in the feminine with "polarización".

questions.prompt: How do you say "civil disobedience" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "desobediencia civil" is the deliberate, usually nonviolent refusal to obey a law as a form of protest.

questions.prompt: How do you say "grassroots activism" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "activismo de base" matches "grassroots activism" word for word; "movimiento de base" means a grassroots movement, the group rather than the activity.

questions.prompt: How do you say "social contract" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "contrato social" is the political-philosophy term (Rousseau's "El contrato social") for the implicit agreement between citizens and the state; the adjective follows the noun.

questions.prompt: How do you say "common good" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "bien común" means what benefits society as a whole; here "bien" is a noun meaning "good", and "común" carries a tilde on the final syllable.

questions.prompt: How do you say "public accountability" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: public accountability → rendición de cuentas pública. Vocabulary for political and social commentary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "institutional trust" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "confianza institucional" is the usual term for how much people trust institutions such as courts or government; "confianza" is feminine, and the adjective comes after it.

questions.prompt: How do you say "social mobility" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "movilidad social" describes people's ability to move up or down the social ladder; don't confuse it with "desigualdad social", which means inequality.

questions.prompt: How do you say "wealth gap" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: wealth gap → brecha de riqueza. Vocabulary for political and social commentary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "policy implementation" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "implementación de políticas" means putting policies into practice; Spanish uses "de" plus the plural "políticas" where English uses "policy" as a modifier.

questions.prompt: How do you say "civic duty" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "deber cívico" means an obligation a citizen has, such as voting; "deber" is a noun here ("duty"), unlike "participación cívica", which means taking part.

questions.prompt: How do you say "public welfare" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: public welfare → bienestar público. Vocabulary for political and social commentary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "social justice" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "justicia social" is the fair distribution of rights and opportunities in a society; in Spanish the adjective "social" follows the noun, whereas English puts "social" first.

units.title: Academic Writing Verbs
units.description: Verbs for scholarly writing — Verbs common in academic and scholarly writing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to argue (in writing)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "argumentar" means to make a reasoned case in writing; "criticar" means to criticize, and "discutir" usually means to argue out loud or quarrel.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to demonstrate" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: to demonstrate → demostrar. Verbs common in academic and scholarly writing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to postulate" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: to postulate → postular. Verbs common in academic and scholarly writing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to critique" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: to critique → criticar. Verbs common in academic and scholarly writing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to synthesize" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: to synthesize → sintetizar. Verbs common in academic and scholarly writing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to substantiate" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: to substantiate → fundamentar. Verbs common in academic and scholarly writing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to corroborate" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: to corroborate → corroborar. Verbs common in academic and scholarly writing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to refute" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: to refute → refutar. Verbs common in academic and scholarly writing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to elaborate (on)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: to elaborate (on) → profundizar en. Verbs common in academic and scholarly writing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to delineate" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: to delineate → delinear. Verbs common in academic and scholarly writing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to formulate" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "formular" means to put an idea, question or theory into words, as in "formular una pregunta", which matches "to formulate".

questions.prompt: How do you say "to interpret" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "interpretar" means to explain the meaning of data or texts, exactly like "to interpret"; the other verbs mean to outline, postulate and contextualize.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to derive (a conclusion)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "derivar" means to obtain or deduce one thing from another, as in "de estos datos se deriva una conclusión", which matches "to derive (a conclusion)".

questions.prompt: How do you say "to validate" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "validar" means to confirm that something is correct or sound, such as a hypothesis or a method; it is a regular -ar verb.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to challenge (an idea)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cuestionar" means to call an idea into question or challenge it, while "refutar" goes further and means to prove it wrong.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to underscore" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "subrayar" literally means to underline, and in academic writing it means to stress a point, just like "to underscore".

questions.prompt: How do you say "to juxtapose" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "yuxtaponer" means to place two ideas side by side to compare them; it conjugates like "poner" (yo yuxtapongo).

questions.prompt: How do you say "to contextualize" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "contextualizar" means to place an idea or event in its context; in the present subjunctive the z changes to c (contextualice).

questions.prompt: How do you say "to problematize" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: to problematize → problematizar. Verbs common in academic and scholarly writing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to extrapolate" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: to extrapolate → extrapolar. Verbs common in academic and scholarly writing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to conceptualize" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: to conceptualize → conceptualizar. Verbs common in academic and scholarly writing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to hypothesize" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Spanish usually expresses "to hypothesize" with the phrase "formular una hipótesis", which means to put forward a hypothesis.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to enumerate" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: to enumerate → enumerar. Verbs common in academic and scholarly writing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to categorize" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: to categorize → categorizar. Verbs common in academic and scholarly writing.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to differentiate" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: to differentiate → diferenciar. Verbs common in academic and scholarly writing.

units.title: Idiomatic Business Expressions
units.description: English business idioms, in Spanish — Idiomatic business/formal expressions.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to think outside the box" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "pensar fuera de la caja" is the common Latin American rendering of the English idiom and means to think creatively, beyond conventional ideas.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to be on the same page" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "estar en sintonía" means to be in tune or in agreement with someone, which is what "to be on the same page" expresses.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to touch base" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "ponerse en contacto" means to get in touch with someone, the closest everyday equivalent of "to touch base".

questions.prompt: How do you say "to keep someone in the loop" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "mantener a alguien informado" means to keep someone updated, which is what "to keep someone in the loop" means.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to go the extra mile" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: to go the extra mile → dar lo mejor de sí. Idiomatic business/formal expressions.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to hit the ground running" in Spanish?
choices: tener intereses propios en el asunto
questions.explanation: to hit the ground running → empezar con buen pie. Idiomatic business/formal expressions.

questions.prompt: How do you say "low-hanging fruit" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "tarea fácil de lograr" means a task you can achieve with little effort, the quick, easy win that 'low-hanging fruit' describes.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to move the needle" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "generar un impacto real" means to produce a noticeable, measurable result, which is what 'to move the needle' means in business.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to circle back" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "retomar el tema" means to come back to a subject later, which is what 'to circle back' means in a meeting.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to be a game changer" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cambiar las reglas del juego" means to transform completely how things are done, which is what a 'game changer' does.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to read between the lines" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "leer entre líneas" is the same image as in English: to understand the hidden meaning behind what is said or written.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to have skin in the game" in Spanish? ___
bank: tener intereses propios en el asunto
questions.answer: tener intereses propios en el asunto
questions.explanation: "tener intereses propios en el asunto" means to have a personal stake in the outcome, which is the idea of 'skin in the game'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to drop the ball" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cometer un descuido" means to make a careless slip, which is what you do when you 'drop the ball' on something you were responsible for.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to raise the bar" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "elevar el estándar" means to set a higher level of quality or expectation, which is what 'to raise the bar' means.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to take ownership" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "asumir la responsabilidad" means to accept responsibility for a task or result, which is what 'to take ownership' means at work.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to be in the pipeline" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "estar en proceso" means to be underway or being prepared, like a project that is 'in the pipeline' but not finished yet.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to think on one's feet" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "pensar rápido" means to react and decide quickly without preparation, which is 'thinking on your feet'; it is not about being creative like 'pensar fuera de la caja'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to get the ball rolling" in Spanish? ___
bank: tener intereses propios en el asunto
questions.explanation: "poner las cosas en marcha" means to start a process or project moving, which is what 'to get the ball rolling' means.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to cut to the chase" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ir al grano" literally means 'to go to the grain' and is used for getting straight to the main point without small talk, just like 'to cut to the chase'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to be on the fence" in Spanish? ___
bank: tener intereses propios en el asunto
questions.explanation: Someone 'on the fence' has not decided yet, and "estar indeciso" means exactly that: to be undecided between options.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to bite the bullet" in Spanish? ___
bank: tener intereses propios en el asunto
questions.explanation: 'To bite the bullet' means to face something unpleasant you cannot avoid, which is what "afrontar lo inevitable" expresses; "superar la crisis" means getting through a crisis, not accepting it.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to leave no stone unturned" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "no dejar piedra sin remover" mirrors the English image of leaving no stone unturned and means to try every possible way to find or achieve something.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to weather the storm" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: 'To weather the storm' means to get through a difficult period, and "superar la crisis" means to overcome or get through a crisis.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to be at a crossroads" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "estar en una encrucijada" uses the same image as the English, since an encrucijada is a crossroads, and means facing a decisive choice.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to turn the tide" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: 'To turn the tide' means to change the direction a situation is going, which is what "cambiar el rumbo" (to change course) expresses here.

units.title: Nuanced Discourse Connectors III
units.description: Further sophisticated connectors — Further advanced discourse markers.

questions.prompt: How do you say "insofar as it concerns" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: insofar as it concerns → en lo que concierne a. Further advanced discourse markers.

questions.prompt: How do you say "with the exception of" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: with the exception of → con la excepción de. Further advanced discourse markers.

questions.prompt: How do you say "in the same vein" in Spanish?
choices: en la medida de lo posible
en el gran esquema de las cosas
questions.explanation: in the same vein → en la misma línea. Further advanced discourse markers.

questions.prompt: How do you say "for lack of a better term" in Spanish? ___
bank: a falta de un término mejor
questions.answer: a falta de un término mejor
questions.explanation: for lack of a better term → a falta de un término mejor. Further advanced discourse markers.

questions.prompt: How do you say "in a manner of speaking" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: in a manner of speaking → por así decirlo. Further advanced discourse markers.

questions.prompt: How do you say "strictly speaking" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "en sentido estricto" is a word-for-word match for 'strictly speaking' and is used to apply a term in its most precise meaning.

questions.prompt: How do you say "loosely speaking" in Spanish?
choices: a falta de un término mejor
questions.explanation: "en sentido amplio" means 'in a broad sense', the opposite of 'strictly speaking', which matches 'loosely speaking'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "to put it another way" in Spanish? ___
bank: en la medida de lo posible
en el gran esquema de las cosas
questions.explanation: to put it another way → dicho de otro modo. Further advanced discourse markers.

questions.prompt: How do you say "needless to say" in Spanish?
choices: en la medida de lo posible
questions.explanation: "huelga decir" is the fixed formal phrase for 'needless to say', because 'holgar' here means to be unnecessary; "sea como fuere" means 'be that as it may'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "suffice it to say" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "baste decir" uses the subjunctive of bastar ("let it suffice") to introduce a point the speaker will not develop, just like "suffice it to say".

questions.prompt: How do you say "be it as it may" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: be it as it may → sea como fuere. Further advanced discourse markers.

questions.prompt: How do you say "without further ado" in Spanish?
choices: en la medida de lo posible
questions.explanation: "sin más preámbulos" literally means "without more preambles" and is used to start the main point at once, exactly like "without further ado".

questions.prompt: How do you say "that being the case" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "siendo así" is a gerund phrase meaning "it being so" and draws a consequence from what was just said, like "that being the case".

questions.prompt: How do you say "under these circumstances" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "en estas circunstancias" is the most natural way to say "under these circumstances"; Spanish usually prefers "en" here, although "bajo estas circunstancias" is also heard.

questions.prompt: How do you say "by virtue of" in Spanish? ___
bank: en la medida de lo posible
questions.explanation: "en virtud de" means "by virtue of" or "under" (a law or a reason) and is followed by a noun, as in "en virtud de la ley".

questions.prompt: How do you say "with a view to" in Spanish?
choices: a falta de un término mejor
questions.explanation: "con miras a" means "with a view to" and introduces a goal, followed by a noun or an infinitive, as in "con miras a mejorar".

questions.prompt: How do you say "in the interest of" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "en aras de" is a formal phrase meaning "in the interest of" or "for the sake of", as in "en aras de la claridad".

questions.prompt: How do you say "to the extent possible" in Spanish?
choices: en la medida de lo posible
questions.explanation: "en la medida de lo posible" literally means "in the measure of what is possible", the standard way to say "to the extent possible".

questions.prompt: How do you say "as things stand" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "tal como están las cosas" uses estar for the current state of affairs and means "as things stand".

questions.prompt: How do you say "in retrospect" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "en retrospectiva" means "in retrospect" and is used when judging a past event with what you know now.

questions.prompt: How do you say "on second thought" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "pensándolo bien" literally means "thinking it over well" and signals a change of mind, like "on second thought".

questions.prompt: How do you say "all told" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "en total" sums up a count or amount, like "all told" in "all told, we spent 200 dollars"; "en general" means "in general" instead.

questions.prompt: How do you say "by and large" in Spanish?
choices: en la medida de lo posible
questions.explanation: 'By and large' means 'overall, in most cases', which is what "en general" expresses when introducing a broad statement.

questions.prompt: How do you say "when all is said and done" in Spanish? ___
bank: en el gran esquema de las cosas
questions.explanation: "al fin y al cabo" means "when all is said and done" or "after all": it sums up a conclusion after weighing everything, while the other options mean "broadly speaking", "in these circumstances" and "in the grand scheme of things".

questions.prompt: How do you say "in the grand scheme of things" in Spanish?
choices: en el gran esquema de las cosas
questions.explanation: in the grand scheme of things → en el gran esquema de las cosas. Further advanced discourse markers.

units.title: Speaking: Idiomatic and Formal Phrasing
units.description: Say it out loud — Idiomatic and formal phrasing said aloud.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Huelga decir que este proyecto es fundamental.
questions.explanation: "Huelga decir que este proyecto es fundamental." means "Needless to say, this project is essential": "huelga decir que" is a formal way to introduce something obvious.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "Ni que decir tiene." Idiomatic and formal phrasing said aloud.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Le ruego que disculpe las molestias.
questions.explanation: "Le ruego que disculpe las molestias." means "Please excuse the inconvenience": "le ruego que" is a formal usted request and takes the subjunctive "disculpe".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Tenemos el placer de informarle de nuestra decisión.
questions.explanation: "Tenemos el placer de informarle de nuestra decisión." means "We are pleased to inform you of our decision", a set formula from formal letters that uses usted ("-le").

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Adjunto encontrará el documento solicitado." means "Please find attached the requested document", the standard formal email formula with usted ("encontrará").

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: En la medida de lo posible, haremos lo necesario.
questions.explanation: "En la medida de lo posible, haremos lo necesario." means "As far as possible, we will do what is needed": "en la medida de lo posible" is a formal hedge meaning "as far as possible".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Sea como fuere, debemos avanzar." means "Be that as it may, we must move forward": "sea como fuere" is a formal fixed phrase that keeps the old future subjunctive "fuere".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "No cabe duda de ello." means "There is no doubt about it": "no cabe duda" is a formal way to say something is certain, and "ello" means "it".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "No obstante, el problema persiste." means "Nevertheless, the problem persists": "no obstante" is a formal connector for contrast, like "sin embargo".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: A decir verdad, no lo sé.
questions.explanation: "A decir verdad, no lo sé." means "To tell the truth, I don't know": "a decir verdad" introduces a frank admission.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: En definitiva, fue una buena decisión.
questions.explanation: "En definitiva, fue una buena decisión." means "All in all, it was a good decision": "en definitiva" introduces a final summing-up.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Al fin y al cabo, eso no importa.
questions.explanation: "Al fin y al cabo, eso no importa." means "At the end of the day, that doesn't matter." "Al fin y al cabo" is a set idiom that sums up an argument and is always said as a fixed block.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Huelga decirlo." means "Needless to say." It comes from the formal verb "holgar" (to be unnecessary) and is used in careful speech or writing.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Le agradezco de antemano su confianza.
questions.explanation: "Le agradezco de antemano su confianza." means "Thank you in advance for your trust." It uses formal "le" and "su" (usted), and "de antemano" means "in advance."

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Quedamos a su entera disposición." means "We remain entirely at your service." It is a standard formal closing in business letters and emails, addressed with "su" (usted).

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Es cuestión de sentido común." means "It's a matter of common sense." Note that "cuestión de" takes no article here.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Dicho esto, hay que ser prudentes.
questions.explanation: "Dicho esto, hay que ser prudentes." means "That said, we need to be careful." "Dicho esto" is a formal connector that adds a caveat to what was just said.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Donde hay humo, hay fuego." means "Where there's smoke, there's fire." It suggests that a rumour usually has some truth behind it, much like "Cuando el río suena, agua lleva."

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Más vale tarde que nunca." means "Better late than never." "Más vale" (it's better) is a common opening for Spanish sayings.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Cada cosa a su tiempo." means "Everything in its own time." You say it to urge patience or to deal with one thing at a time.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Le agradecería que respondiera con prontitud.
questions.explanation: "Le agradecería que respondiera con prontitud." means "I would be grateful if you replied promptly." The conditional "agradecería" triggers the imperfect subjunctive "respondiera," a very polite formal request.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Le pedimos disculpas por las molestias ocasionadas.
questions.explanation: "Le pedimos disculpas por las molestias ocasionadas." means "We apologise for any inconvenience caused." It is a standard formal apology used by companies and services.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Es el mundo al revés." means "It's the world turned upside down." You use it when a situation is absurd or the opposite of what it should be.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: En una palabra, todo va bien.
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "En una palabra, todo va bien." Idiomatic and formal phrasing said aloud.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "Sin más preámbulos, comencemos." Idiomatic and formal phrasing said aloud.

units.title: Write It Yourself: Idiomatic and Formal Phrasing
units.description: Say it your own way — Write idiomatic and formal phrasing in your own words; more than one wording can be right.

lessons.title: Write It Yourself: Idiomatic and Formal Phrasing 1
lessons.subtitle: Write it your own way

questions.prompt: Say it goes without saying that this project is important.
acceptableAnswers: Ni que decir tiene que este proyecto es importante.
Huelga decir que este proyecto es importante.
Sobra decir que este proyecto es importante.
questions.explanation: "Huelga decir que este proyecto es importante." uses "huelga decir" (it goes without saying), a formal set phrase; "Sobra decir" also works, and "Ni que decir tiene" is heard more in Spain.

questions.prompt: Say that goes without saying.
questions.explanation: "Eso ni se pregunta." says something is so obvious that nobody needs to ask, which matches "that goes without saying"; "Huelga decirlo" is the more formal written version.

questions.prompt: Say please excuse this delay.
acceptableAnswers: Le ruego que disculpe este retraso.
Le pido disculpas por este retraso.
Disculpe usted este retraso, por favor.
questions.explanation: "Le ruego que disculpe este retraso." is a polite usted request: "rogar que" triggers the subjunctive "disculpe".

questions.prompt: Say we are pleased to inform you of our decision.
acceptableAnswers: Nos complace informarle de nuestra decisión.
Tenemos el gusto de comunicarle nuestra decisión.
Nos es grato informarle nuestra decisión.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Nos complace informarle de nuestra decisión." Idiomatic and formal phrasing, and more than one wording is right.

questions.prompt: Say please find attached the requested document.
acceptableAnswers: Le envío adjunto el documento solicitado.
Encontrará adjunto el documento que pidió.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Adjunto encontrará el documento solicitado." Idiomatic and formal phrasing, and more than one wording is right.

lessons.title: Write It Yourself: Idiomatic and Formal Phrasing 2
lessons.subtitle: Write it your own way

questions.prompt: Say we will do our best.
acceptableAnswers: Haremos lo que esté a nuestro alcance.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Haremos todo lo posible." Idiomatic and formal phrasing, and more than one wording is right.

questions.prompt: Say be that as it may, we must move forward.
acceptableAnswers: Como quiera que sea, tenemos que seguir adelante.
De todos modos, hay que avanzar.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Sea como sea, debemos avanzar." Idiomatic and formal phrasing, and more than one wording is right.

questions.prompt: Say there is no doubt about that.
acceptableAnswers: No hay ninguna duda al respecto.
Eso está fuera de toda duda.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "No cabe duda de eso." Idiomatic and formal phrasing, and more than one wording is right.

questions.prompt: Say the problem persists nonetheless.
acceptableAnswers: No obstante, el problema sigue ahí.
A pesar de todo, el problema continúa.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "El problema persiste sin embargo." Idiomatic and formal phrasing, and more than one wording is right.

questions.prompt: Say to tell the truth, I have no idea.
acceptableAnswers: La verdad, no tengo ni idea.
A decir verdad, no tengo idea.
Si le soy sincero, no tengo ni idea.
questions.explanation: "La verdad, no tengo ni idea." opens with "La verdad" for "to tell the truth" and uses "no tengo ni idea" for "I have no idea".

lessons.title: Write It Yourself: Idiomatic and Formal Phrasing 3
lessons.subtitle: Write it your own way

questions.prompt: Say all things considered, it was a good decision.
acceptableAnswers: Considerando todo, fue una buena decisión.
Bien mirado, fue una buena decisión.
En resumidas cuentas, fue una buena decisión.
Considerándolo todo, fue una buena decisión.
Teniéndolo todo en cuenta, fue una buena decisión.
questions.explanation: "Considerando todo, fue una buena decisión." opens with a phrase meaning "taking everything into account"; the more idiomatic form is "Considerándolo todo", and "Bien mirado" works too.

questions.prompt: Say in the end, it doesn't matter.
acceptableAnswers: Al fin y al cabo, no importa.
A fin de cuentas, no importa.
questions.explanation: "Al final, no importa." renders 'in the end'; "Al fin y al cabo" and "A fin de cuentas" are more idiomatic ways to say 'after all'.

questions.prompt: Say you would like to thank someone for their trust.
acceptableAnswers: Deseo expresarle mi agradecimiento por su confianza.
questions.explanation: "Quisiera agradecerle su confianza." uses the polite conditional-like "quisiera" for 'would like', and "agradecer" takes the thing being thanked for directly, without "por".

questions.prompt: Say we remain at your entire disposal.
acceptableAnswers: Estamos a su disposición para lo que necesite.
questions.explanation: "Quedamos a su entera disposición." is the standard formal closing: "quedar" expresses 'remain', and "su" addresses the reader as usted.

questions.prompt: Say that's a matter of common sense.
acceptableAnswers: Eso es cuestión de sentido común.
Es pura cuestión de sentido común.
questions.explanation: "Eso es cuestión de sentido común." uses "cuestión de" for "a matter of" and "sentido común" for "common sense".

lessons.title: Write It Yourself: Idiomatic and Formal Phrasing 4
lessons.subtitle: Write it your own way

questions.prompt: Say that said, we should remain cautious.
acceptableAnswers: Dicho lo cual, hay que tener cuidado.
questions.explanation: "Dicho esto, debemos ser cautelosos." uses "Dicho esto", the formal way to say 'that said', and "debemos" for 'we should'.

questions.prompt: Say there's no smoke without fire.
acceptableAnswers: Cuando el río suena, agua lleva.
Algo de cierto habrá cuando tanto se dice.
questions.explanation: "No hay humo sin fuego." matches the English word for word and is also said in Spanish; "Cuando el río suena, agua lleva" is the more traditional Spanish proverb with the same meaning.

questions.prompt: Say better late than never.
questions.explanation: "Más vale tarde que nunca." is the fixed Spanish saying; "más vale" means 'it is better', and "Mejor tarde que nunca" is a shorter everyday version.

questions.prompt: Say each thing in its own time.
questions.explanation: "Cada cosa a su tiempo." is the set saying for 'each thing in its own time', with "a su tiempo" meaning 'at its proper time'.

questions.prompt: Say things are getting worse.
acceptableAnswers: Las cosas van de mal en peor.
La situación empeora cada vez más.
questions.explanation: "Las cosas van de mal en peor." uses the idiom "ir de mal en peor", literally 'go from bad to worse', for things getting worse.

lessons.title: Write It Yourself: Idiomatic and Formal Phrasing 5
lessons.subtitle: Say it your own way

questions.prompt: Say you would be grateful if someone could reply quickly.
acceptableAnswers: Le quedaría muy agradecido si contestara pronto.
Le quedaría muy agradecida si contestara pronto.
questions.explanation: "Le agradecería que respondiera pronto." uses the polite conditional "agradecería", and "que" after it takes the imperfect subjunctive "respondiera".

questions.prompt: Say we apologize for the inconvenience caused.
acceptableAnswers: Le pedimos disculpas por las molestias ocasionadas.
Lamentamos las molestias que esto haya causado.
questions.explanation: "Le pedimos disculpas por las molestias ocasionadas." is the standard formal apology, with "Le" for usted and "las molestias" for 'the inconvenience'.

questions.prompt: Say this is the world turned upside down.
acceptableAnswers: Esto es el mundo al revés.
Este es un mundo al revés.
questions.explanation: "Esto es el mundo al revés." uses the fixed expression "el mundo al revés" for a situation where everything is upside down; the neuter "esto" refers to the whole situation.

questions.prompt: Say in a word, everything is fine.
acceptableAnswers: En una palabra, todo está bien.
En pocas palabras, todo marcha bien.
questions.explanation: "En una palabra, todo está bien." uses "En una palabra" for 'in a word' and "está bien" for a state of being fine; "En resumen, todo va bien" also works.

questions.prompt: Say we look forward to hearing from you.
acceptableAnswers: Quedamos a la espera de su respuesta.
questions.explanation: "Quedamos a la espera de su respuesta." is the standard formal closing for 'we look forward to hearing from you', using "su" for usted as business letters require.
